  sign-in or step-up (403 `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`, answered by the web
  re-authentication dialog). Narrowing a grant is unchanged.

### Security: minting a sensor key and revealing a leaked credential need a recent sign-in

- `POST /api/v1/sensors` and `POST /api/v1/sensors/{id}/regenerate-key` mint a
  persistent sensor key, and now require step-up, as creating an API key
  already did. Revoking, disabling and deleting a sensor stay one click.
- `POST /api/v1/credentials/{id}/reveal` (the plaintext of a leaked
  credential) now requires step-up. It stays audited.
- `PUT /api/v1/sensors/identity-policy` requires step-up when it allows
  bearer-key sensors again. Requiring key-bound identity stays one click.
- The web console prompts for re-authentication and retries the request,
  as for API keys.
- **Upgrade note:** API clients that call these routes with a user session
  get `403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED` unless the session signed in or stepped up
  (`POST /api/v1/auth/step-up`) in the last 10 minutes. `oct_` API keys
  never reached them (keys are read-only).

### Security: support access granted by the organization, time-boxed and audited

- Organization owners can grant one named platform support administrator read-only access to the organization's findings and assets for 1 to 72 hours (default 4), with a reason and an optional case reference (Settings > Access > Support access; owner with a recent re-authentication). Owners and admins see the history and revoke at once; every member sees the active grants.
- In the platform console, the named administrator opens a support session (with a step-up) and reads through it. Every read is checked on the server against the live grant (not revoked, not expired, same console session, granted scope) and is written to both the organization's audit log and the admin audit log before any data is returned. Support reads never include messages, code snippets, secret values, evidence or people's details, and never the assets of private programs.
- Owners are emailed when a grant is created or revoked and when a support session starts or ends.
- Upgrade note: additive migration (`support_grants`, `support_sessions`).
- A support overview and finding rows carry only what the grant's scopes open (no asset count or asset columns without the assets scope, no finding counts without the findings scope). The console user list, first owner create or recovery and identity provider creation, which never needed a grant, now write `admin_console.tenant_access` to the organization's audit log and email its owners before running.

### Security: a suppression rule's requester cannot clear its review flag

- Clearing the review flag of one's own rule is refused (403, audited as a
  denied `suppression_rule.reviewed`) unless the requester is the sole
  approver: the owner with no other approver and no recent approver change,
  with a reason and a fresh authenticator code, like approving their own
  rule. The web asks for the reason and the code in that case.

### Security: suppression rules name only assets the requester may see

- Creating an asset-bound suppression rule (which auto-closes that asset's
  findings) now requires a live asset of the organization that the requester
  may see; anything else answers 404 `Asset`. `suppression_rules.asset_id`
  references `assets(id)` without the tenant, so a rule could name another
  tenant's asset or an out-of-scope one (RFC-050 W8).
- Docs: the authorization matrix and `api/CLAUDE.md` no longer say expiring
  grants will never be built (owner decisions D4/A2 reversed that; RFC-050
  W22/W23), and the tenant-wide aggregates table is marked as debt to scope
  (D6), not a decision (RFC-050 W10).

### Security: system roles change only through the membership; the owner role is never granted by a role assignment

- The Roles API (`/users/{id}/roles`, `/users/{id}/roles/{roleId}`,
  `/roles/{roleId}/members/bulk`) and team role bindings now take custom roles
  only. Granting or removing `owner`, `admin`, `member` or `viewer` there is
  refused with a 400, the owner role included. Before, an owner could grant the
  owner role to a co-owner whose membership still read `admin`; the real owner
  could then not take it back, and the organization's owner counts missed them.
  A system role changes with the member's role
  (`PATCH /tenants/{tenant}/members/{id}`) and ownership with the ownership
  transfer. `PUT /users/{id}/roles` replaces custom roles and keeps the team
  role; it accepts an empty list.
- A database trigger refuses an owner role row unless the membership label is
  `owner`. Existing rows that already break this are left in place; list them
  with the query in `api/docs/architecture/authorization-matrix.md` ("Owner role
  without the owner membership") and resolve them per organization.
- Owner and admin counts, approver feasibility, notification recipients and the
  platform console read the effective role (`v_user_effective_role`) instead of
  the raw membership label. `tools/lint/rawrole` bans new raw label reads.
- Web: the Members page "Change roles" dialog now has a role-in-organization
  selector (administrator for the owner only) and lists custom roles; the role
  detail sheet of a team role no longer adds or removes members through the
  Roles API.
- A co-owner planted before this change (owner role row, membership label not owner) is removed by the real owner through the member role route, with a fresh step-up; the change is audited as `owner_role_drift_removed` (Critical).

Upgrade note: API clients that assigned `admin`, `member` or `viewer` through
`/users/{id}/roles` must use the member role route instead.

### Security: the data-flow endpoint applies the finding's own access gate

- `GET /api/v1/findings/{id}/dataflows` applies the same tenant, data-scope and pentest-campaign check as `GET /api/v1/findings/{id}`. Before, it called the service as an administrator and relied on the route guard alone. A caller who may not read the finding gets 404.

### Security: template-source clones over ssh connect only to the address that was checked

- A scanner-template source cloned over ssh was checked against the SSRF guard before the clone, but go-git then resolved the host again and dialled it itself. A DNS answer that changed in between (rebinding) could point the connection at an internal address.
- ssh clones and pulls now connect through the same guarded dialer as every other outbound request: it resolves the host once, refuses blocked answers, and connects only to the vetted address. https clones were already pinned this way.

### Security: privileged role grants, integration writes and loosened sign-in security are guarded

- Giving a user a privileged custom role they do not hold (direct grant, role replacement or bulk assign) now needs the acting administrator's recent re-authentication, and so does an edit that makes a directly-held custom role privileged. System paths (SCIM, SSO, invitation acceptance) are unchanged.
- Organization-wide scan configuration is owner and administrator only: a scan profile's quality gate and default flag, the tool settings (single and bulk) and deleting a secret-store entry. Members whose role carries the write permission now get 403.
- Connecting, changing, disabling or deleting an integration, creating a notification channel, changing a channel's settings and saving the SCIM group-to-role mapping need step-up re-authentication.
- Loosening sign-in security (administrators' two-factor requirement off, personal-account policy relaxed, approval of new single sign-on members off, a sign-in exception added) is graded High in the audit log, and every High or Critical security-settings change now sends an in-app notice to all owners and administrators naming who changed what.

### Security: the tenant web app carries nothing of the platform console

- `GET /api/version` no longer accepts the console's `admin_session` cookie; the
  console is its own app and answers its own version.
- The generated route gate map and authorization reference bundled into the
  tenant web app no longer list `/api/v1/admin/...` routes (the documentation
  pages keep them).
- Web CI fails a build whose tenant output (`.next/server`) contains console
  route ids or `api/v1/admin`.

### Security: a tenant-plane API refuses to start in production when its database role can write administrators

- With `OPENCTEM_PLANE=tenant` the API always checks its database role's
  privileges on `admin_users` (before, only when `DB_ADMIN_USER` was set), and
  in production refuses to start if `DB_USER` can write it or the check cannot
  run. Run the least-privilege bootstrap with `admin_user` (the db-roles job).
- A test walks the registered routes and fails if a tenant-plane process holds
  any `/api/v1/admin` route.

### Security: suspending or removing a member in one organization no longer signs them out of their other organizations

- Disable, offboard and SCIM deprovisioning used to revoke every session of the person. The person's other organizations were affected too: an administrator of one organization could sign a member of another out at will.
- The organization's own access is still cut at once:
  - membership checks on every request and at token exchange;
  - caches dropped and sockets closed;
  - the sessions its own identity provider signed in are revoked.
- Sessions that serve the person's other organizations stay.
- A person with no other organization left still loses every session.
- Erasing personal data still ends every session, and so do account-wide actions: a password reset, or a platform administrator disabling the account.

### Security: a tenant can no longer turn off TLS verification for its SMTP relay

- The email notification integration accepted `skip_verify: true`, which sent
  the tenant's SMTP username and password to a relay whose certificate was
  never checked (RFC-049 F-5). Creating or updating an email integration with
  `skip_verify: true` is now refused (400), and the flag is no longer stored.
- Integrations stored with `skip_verify: true` are read without it: delivery
  verifies the relay certificate, and a relay with a self-signed or private-CA
  certificate now fails delivery instead of sending the credentials unverified.
- The operator-level `SMTP_SKIP_VERIFY` for the system relay is unchanged.
- **Upgrade note:** a tenant whose relay uses a self-signed certificate must
  give it a certificate from a CA the API trusts (or the operator adds that CA
  to the API container).

### Security: the list of ticket trackers exempt from the claim rules is fixed

- Only verified Jira and GitHub webhooks are exempt from the person-only fix
  claim rules; the list is now private to the findings domain, so no other
  code can add a source at run time.

### Security: a report can no longer set a finding's ticket links

- The `work_item_uris` of an ingested finding (CTIS, and SARIF through it) are
  no longer stored as the finding's ticket links. The ticket sync acts on
  those links: it moved and commented on the linked issue, and a change of
  that issue moved the finding. A sensor or an imported file could point a
  finding at any issue of the organization's tracker, or block a real ticket
  ("already ticketed"). Only the platform (create ticket) or a person links a
  ticket now.

### Security: one secret redactor for Jira and GitHub tickets; private keys no longer leak into GitHub issues

- GitHub issue bodies removed only the header line of a private key, so the key body reached the issue. Jira and GitHub now share one redactor that removes the whole key block (also a block whose footer is cut off), JWTs, AWS `AKIA`/`ASIA` key ids, GitHub, Slack and Google tokens, bearer values and secret assignments.
- The mobilization brief and the campaign epic description are redacted, capped and encoded like finding text, so they cannot add links, mentions or macros to a ticket.

### Security: a request that outlives the request timeout can no longer crash the API

- When a handler set a response header after the request timeout (30 s by
  default) had fired, it wrote to the same header map as the timeout's 504
  response, from another goroutine. That concurrent map write is a fatal Go
  error: the whole API process exited and dropped every in-flight request. A
  member could trigger it, for example with concurrent dashboard overview
  calls on a large tenant.
- The timeout middleware now gives the handler its own header map. The map
  is copied to the response under the writer's lock on the handler's first
  write, and never after a timeout. Late headers and body are dropped, and the
  handler's context is still cancelled at the deadline.

### Security: changing an Impact tool option needs a recent re-authentication

- Setting an Impact (T1) tool option to a new value, in either the organization defaults or a sensor's settings, now asks for step-up re-authentication (`403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED`). Organization changes to an Impact option are audited at high severity.

### Security: the platform assigns each job's tier from the tool contract

- The grant check at dispatch now compares the sensor's tier ceiling with a tier the platform assigns from the tool contract the sensor reported (RFC-055 §6.3). It is the highest of:
  - the floor of the capability the job runs, or the catalog rule for a job without a capability;
  - the tier the tool's descriptor declares;
  - T2 for a declared side effect;
  - T2 for a tool the operator installed (origin `adapter`, unverified until it is classified).
- A tool's own tier can only raise the tier, never lower it below the capability's floor. A tool or capability the platform does not know stays T2.
- `sensor.ToolTrust` gives a tool's trust level: `builtin` or `unverified`.
- A sensor without a manifest is checked as before, by the catalog rule (one release train, TC12).

### Security: a sensor can no longer make its own tool "builtin" by claiming it

- A tool contract's `origin` is a sensor claim. The platform granted trust `builtin` and the capability's tier floor to any tool reporting `origin: builtin`, so an operator-installed tool with any name (including a catalog name the sensor does not ship, such as `zap`) could be classified builtin and run below T2.
- The claim is now honored only for the tools a released sensor compiles in (betterleaks, codeql, dnsx, httpx, katana, naabu, nuclei, nuclei-validate, semgrep, subfinder, trivy) and the SDK's `file-import`. Any other tool that claims it is unverified and T2, as an operator-installed tool is.
- Binding the claim to the signed release's descriptor digests is planned (RFC-060).

### Security: tool authorization per action on the one resource

- Reading the catalog needs `scans:tools:read`. Each include needs the permission of its former standalone route: `scans:tenant_tools:read`, and `scans:read` as well for `stats` (tenant-wide counts over every scan). One the caller may not read is left out and named in `meta.omitted_includes` (200, never a 403). Sensor names and zones in the availability still need `sensors:read`.
- `include` (one shared implementation, `internal/infra/http/include`) takes at most 3 known values; an unknown, nested or extra value is refused with `INVALID_INCLUDE`. `per_page` is capped at 100, and at 50 with availability or stats, which also cost 2 more read-limit tokens each. A response that took `include=` is `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.
- Tool settings never hold secrets: a config with a secret-shaped key or value is refused (400); credentials belong in the secret store, referenced by id. A config stored before this rule is masked on read.
- **Behaviour change:** config overrides (`PATCH /tools/{id}/settings` with `config`) need `scans:tools:write` (admins and owners by default), since they change what the sensors run. Members keep the on/off switch.
- **Behaviour change:** creating, changing and deleting custom tools and custom categories needs `scans:tools:write` / `scans:tools:delete` (admins and owners by default). Members, who held `scans:tenant_tools:write`, no longer create custom tools (whose install commands sensors run); they still switch tools on or off (`PATCH /tools/{id}/settings` with `is_enabled`, `PATCH /tools/settings`).
- A platform tool or category, or another organization's, answers 404 on `PUT`, `DELETE` and `PATCH …/settings`; the service resolves the tool by tenant and id. Changing a platform category used to answer 403 and reading a platform category that is not builtin answered 404.

### Security: a triggered run leaves out internal addresses when the organization has no scan zones

- Scan create refuses internal addresses (private, loopback, link-local,
  unspecified, carrier-grade NAT) outside a scan zone, but a run did not check
  again: asset-group members were never validated, and a direct target saved
  while a zone covered it stayed in the scan after the zone was deleted. A
  triggered run (manual, scheduled, automation, retry) now leaves such targets
  out when the organization has no zones, counts them
  (`internal_outside_zones_target_count`, a run warning) and refuses a run left
  with nothing (`INTERNAL_TARGET_OUTSIDE_ZONES`). With zones, zone routing
  already refused uncovered targets. Platform sensors never received internal
  targets.

### Security: a retest run follows the access rules of its finding

- A run about a finding exposes the finding's target and the check output. To
  read it, its tasks, its stages or its logs, the caller needs `findings:read`
  and the finding inside their data scope. Otherwise the answer is 404. The
  Runs list leaves these runs out for callers without `findings:read` or with a
  restricted data scope.

### Security: upstream error responses no longer reach errors, API answers or audit text

- Jira, DefectDojo, the GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket clients, OAuth and SSO put
  the third-party response body into their errors, which can reach API answers,
  audit entries and the console. They now return the provider and HTTP status
  only; a bounded, sanitized snippet of the body is logged at debug level
  (RFC-049 F-2). security-lint Rule 9 keeps it that way.

### Security: validation evidence no longer resolves a finding

- **A validation "not detected" keeps a `fix_applied` finding open**
  (RFC-040). The only proof that the target answered was
  `raw_meta.reachable`, which the sensor asserts about its own run, so a
  hostile or broken sensor could close any `fix_applied` finding. The verdict
  is still recorded on the finding; a retest (whose reachability probe the
  platform dispatches) or a `findings:verify` holder closes it. Downgrades of
  still-open findings to `validated_fixed` (which a person still closes) and
  reopen on "detected" are unchanged.

### Security: viewers no longer list stored scan credentials

- The built-in **Viewer** role (where every invitation, SSO and SCIM member
  starts) loses `scans:secret_store:read` (the list and details of stored scan
  credentials: names, kinds, descriptions, expiry) and
  `team:assignment_rules:read` (the member role never had it). Viewers lose the
  Secret store and Assignment rules pages; nothing else changes. Custom roles
  keep what their administrators gave them (migration 001420).
- The built-in roles now nest (viewer within member within administrator
  within owner), a unit test keeps them so, and a database test checks that
  the seeded grants match `permission.SystemRoles`, the list the role
  documentation is generated from.
- **Upgrade note:** a viewer who needs the secret store list gets it through a
  custom role with `scans:secret_store:read`.

### Security: wide trusted-proxy ranges are reported at startup

- A trusted proxy may set the client address the API believes (login rate limits, audit addresses, IP allowlists). Trusting a whole container network trusts every container on it, including a sensor running third-party tools.
- The API now logs a `SECURITY:` warning at startup, and `server -check-config` prints a warning, for each `SERVER_TRUSTED_PROXIES` or `SENSOR_MTLS_TRUSTED_PROXIES` range wider than 16 addresses (an IPv4 `/28`, an IPv6 `/124`). Nothing is refused.
- **Upgrade note:** replace a network range such as `172.18.0.0/16` with the gateway's and the web server's own addresses (give those containers fixed addresses, as the shipped Compose file does).

### Security: the console's Content-Security-Policy uses the deployment's origin

- Published web images were built with `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://app.openctem.io`, and the policy read it as a `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_*` literal, which Next.js replaces at build time: a self-hosted console could allow connections to that origin and ignore its own `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`. The policy now reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, `BACKEND_API_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_BASE_URL` at run time, release builds no longer bake an origin, and Docker Compose and the all-in-one image pass the platform URL to the console.

### Security: the web console checks CSRF on every write, before sign-in too

- Every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE the web server answers must come from the
  console's own origin (`Sec-Fetch-Site`, `Origin`, else `Referer`; a request
  with neither is refused) and echo the `csrf_token` cookie in `X-CSRF-Token`.
  Otherwise it gets `403 CSRF_INVALID` and nothing runs. Before, the web
  routes let a request through when it had no `csrf_token` cookie, and the
  `/api/v1` proxy checked nothing itself, so a page on another site could
  sign a visitor into the attacker's account (login CSRF) through
  `/api/v1/auth/login`.
- The pre-session steps are covered: sign-in, registration, forgot, reset and
  set password, invitation acceptance, second-factor steps, team selection
  and SSO/OAuth start (Server Actions, checked in `src/proxy.ts`), the
  `/api/v1` and `/api/v1/admin` proxies and the `/api/auth/*` routes. Every
  page now sets the `csrf_token` cookie when the browser has none, and the
  browser sends it on every same-origin write, Server Actions included.
- Upgrade: a browser tab opened before the upgrade has no `csrf_token`
  cookie; its first write is refused and a page reload fixes it. Scripts that
  post to the web server (not the API) must send `Origin` and the pair; API
  clients that call the API with a token are not affected.
- Client error reports are sent with a keepalive `fetch` instead of
  `navigator.sendBeacon`, which cannot carry the header.

### Security: path- and method-aware scope exclusions with a testing mode

- A `path` exclusion is now a web rule: a host pattern, a segment-aware path prefix and the methods it blocks
  (migration 001290 migrates existing `path` rows, for example `/api/v1/*` to host `*` + prefix `/api/v1`; two old
  rows that read as the same rule are merged into the one in effect).
- It is enforced at dispatch (URL targets under it are excluded), in the job (`web_scope.deny_paths`, or GET/HEAD only
  for a method-scoped rule) and at ingest (endpoints under it are recorded excluded-untested with the exclusion).
  A path rule never excludes a whole host.
- `PUT /api/v1/scope/exclusions/{id}/testing` sets `blocked`, `read_only` (GET, HEAD) or `allowed` with an optional
  deadline (at most 90 days): exclusion approval permission and step-up, audited, administrators notified. It never
  widens scope beyond the organization's own in-scope assets. Design: RFC-056, contract in RFC-054 §6.2.
- **Upgrade note:** a web step whose sensor does not support `web_scope` fails when a path exclusion applies to its
  host; update the sensor.

### Security: the web API proxy re-encodes path segments

- The `/api/v1/*` proxy in the web app joined the decoded path segments as they were, so a `%3F` or `%23` inside a segment became a query string or fragment on the backend URL, and a `%25` was decoded twice. Each segment now has `%`, `?` and `#` percent-encoded again before the request is forwarded; every other character is forwarded as before. Traversal (`..`, `\`) was already refused.

### Security: the web API proxy never shares one person's refreshed session with another

- The web server's `/api/v1` proxy refreshed expired access tokens behind a lock keyed by the organization id from the `app_tenant` cookie. A request that arrived while another member's refresh was in flight received that member's new access token and rotated refresh token as its own cookies. The tenant cookie is set by the client, so anyone who knew an organization id could collect a signed-in member's session by sending requests with a made-up refresh cookie; two members of one organization whose tokens expired together could also swap sessions.
- The lock is now keyed by the caller's own refresh token (with the organization), so only parallel requests of one session share a refresh.

### Security: the console's API proxy keeps the API's security headers

- The web console forwards `/api/v1/*` to the API.
- Until now it dropped the API's `Content-Security-Policy` (`default-src 'none'`), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Content-Disposition` headers on every answer that was not a binary file, so a non-JSON answer could render on the console's own origin with no policy. Examples are an HTML report, or a file built from scan data.
- The proxy now forwards those headers on every answer, including streamed files, which also keep their attachment disposition.

### Security: path exclusions bind every web job, not only workflow steps

- A quick scan, a single-scanner scan (scheduled or retried included), a
  zone batch and a command created through the API ran crawl, template and
  web application tools without the job's web scope, so a host's excluded
  paths (for example `/admin`) were requested. Every command now passes one
  guard when it is stored: a job whose tool requests web paths gets the
  deny paths of its own organization's path exclusions, or is refused when
  they cannot be read.
- A nuclei validation or retest on a host with a path exclusion is refused
  (`WEB_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED`): the sensor cannot keep such a job to a web
  scope yet.

### Security: names that resolve only through a wildcard DNS record are never scanned actively or confirmed automatically

- A finished dnsx resolution with the wildcard-DNS filter on marks the names it was given and did not report: they resolve only through a wildcard record of their zone (or not at all). A later filtered resolution that reports a name clears its mark.
- The active-probe gate refuses a marked name, and a service or URL on it, with the new refusal code `wildcard_only` until a person confirms the asset or the mark clears. A scope entry covering the name no longer lets probes reach it.
- The scope join (auto-confirmation of discovered names under a permanent scope entry) never confirms a marked name.
- Migration `asset_wildcard_dns`: a new, empty table; nothing existing changes until the next filtered resolution finishes.

### Security: workflow scans reach platform sensors only under the same checks as single scans

- The steps of a workflow scan used to follow the workflow's own sensor
  preference. When that preference was `platform`, the steps of a scan of an
  asset group or of internal targets could be queued for shared platform
  sensors. A scan set to `platform` was also never checked.
- A workflow scan now follows the scan's `sensor_preference`, decided when it
  is triggered:
  - `platform` is refused (400 `PLATFORM_SENSOR_REFUSED`) for asset groups,
    internal targets, unproven targets and tenants without platform access,
    as it is for single scans;
  - `auto` may use platform sensors only when none of these applies, and then
    only for steps whose tool no tenant sensor has;
  - `tenant` and "run on tenant sensors only" keep every step on the tenant's
    sensors.
- The decision is kept in the run (`sensor_routing`). A routing value sent in
  the trigger context is ignored.

### Security: scan-zone preview no longer resolves names a tenant may not scan

- `POST /api/v1/scan-zones/preview` resolved every target hostname with the platform's own DNS resolver, without checking the target first, and returned the answers. On a cloud deployment, the platform's resolver knows internal names, for example private hosted zones and cluster DNS. So any member with `scan_zones:read` could map the platform's internal network. Private answers also appeared in the reason text.
- The preview now runs the same act-scope check as scan creation first. A target with no scope entry covering it, or outside the member's data scope, is refused without any lookup.
- An answer is shown only when it is public, or when it lies inside the zone the target routed to. Reasons never quote an address.
- **Behaviour change:** scan-zone routing resolves hostnames with `SCAN_ZONE_RESOLVER`, either `system` or `host[:port]`. When it is unset, self-service installs (`TENANT_CREATION_MODE=self_service`) use the public resolver `1.1.1.1:53`, and every other install keeps the platform's own resolver.
- **Upgrade note:** on a self-service install, the API must be able to reach the configured resolver on port 53. Hostnames that resolve only through the platform's internal DNS no longer route to a zone there.

### Behaviour change: the platform console signs in on its own

- The console's sign-in page asks for the administrator's email and password (same account, password and lockout), then the console's authenticator code. It no longer starts from the tenant `/login` session: `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/session` is removed and `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/login {email, password}` replaces it. A wrong password and an unknown email answer the same 401; only a local password account can pass.
- Signing out of the console ends only the console session, not the tenant sign-in.
- The console's web proxy never forwards the tenant refresh token.
- **Upgrade note:** administrators sign in once more on `/admin/login` with their email and password; nothing else changes for them.

### Behaviour change: platform administrators act as read-only until they elevate

- With `ADMIN_ELEVATION=required` (the default), a console session acts as read-only. To change anything, the administrator elevates the session (`POST /api/v1/admin/auth/elevate`: a role no higher than their own, 15 to 60 minutes, a reason, and a fresh authenticator code); the elevation is audited at high severity and ends on request or when the time is up. The console shows a bar to elevate or end. Another session of the same administrator stays read-only.
- `GET /api/v1/admin/auth/validate` now returns `role` (what the session acts as), `max_role` and `elevated_until`.
- Migration 002813 adds `admin_sessions.elevated_role`, `elevated_until`, `elevation_reason` (nullable, no backfill).
- **Upgrade note:** administrators press Elevate before making changes. `ADMIN_ELEVATION=off` keeps the old behaviour (each administrator acts as their own role from sign-in).

### Behaviour change: finding approvals follow the approval policy (tiers by risk, two approvers, step-up, asset owners excluded)

- Accepting the risk of a high finding (severity high, P1, a validated exploit, EPSS at or above 0.5, or a medium finding on a crown-jewel or internet-exposed asset) needs an approver from the security pool who re-authenticated in the last 10 minutes; a critical finding (severity critical, P0, KEV) needs two such approvers by default. Low and medium acceptances still need one other person. RFC-111.
- The owners of a finding's asset (user owners and members of owner groups) can no longer approve its false positive or accepted risk, and never decide a false positive alone.
- `POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/approve` can answer 200 with the request still `pending` (`approvals_collected` < `approvals_required`), 403 `APPROVER_NOT_ELIGIBLE` with `details.reason`, 409 `NO_ELIGIBLE_APPROVER`, or 403 `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`. Each refusal is audited `finding_approval.approval_refused`; each partial approval `finding_approval.signed`.
- `settings.finding_approvals.policy` (PUT `/api/v1/organization/settings/finding-approvals/`): tier per kind and class, security pool group, exclude assignee, step-up for every tier, class caps, decision deadline, EPSS threshold. It can only add constraints above the platform floors; a relaxing change takes effect 24 hours later. An organization with only two people that needs to accept critical risks can set `accepted.critical` to `security`.
- `GET /api/v1/findings/{id}/approvals/policy?status=accepted` explains how a request would be decided (tier, reasons, eligible approvers, cap).
- Migrations `002841_approval_policy_signoffs` (+ `002842` validate) and `002843_finding_activity_approval_signed` (+ `002844` validate): nullable columns and NOT VALID checks, then a separate validation; no long locks.

### Behaviour change: suppression rules need a reason code and follow the approval policy

- `POST /api/v1/suppressions` requires `reason_code` (a false-positive justification for `false_positive` rules, an accepted-risk reason for `accepted_risk` and `wont_fix`) and a `description`. Responses carry `reason_code`, `tier`, `approvals_required` and `approvals_collected`. RFC-111.
- A rule's tier comes from the worst open finding it matches: a false-positive rule over high or critical findings, or an accepted-risk rule over high findings, needs an approver from the security pool with a recent re-authentication; an accepted-risk rule over critical findings needs two approvers. Owners of the matched findings' assets cannot approve.
- `POST /api/v1/suppressions/{id}/approve` can answer 200 with the rule still `pending` (more approvals needed), 403 `APPROVER_NOT_ELIGIBLE`, 409 `NO_ELIGIBLE_APPROVER` or 403 `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`. Editing a pending rule voids earlier approvals.
- Migrations `002872_suppression_rule_policy` (+ `002873` validate): nullable columns and NOT VALID checks; the rule audit trail accepts `signed`.
- Approving your own suppression rule is possible only as the sole active person of the organization (an owner, with a reason and a fresh authenticator code). Taking the approve permission from the other members no longer opens it; with another active person the policy refuses the requester.
- A rule that matches more open findings than the approval cap (10,000) is refused as too broad: its tier and the asset owners of its matches are judged on every finding it matches, not a sample.

### Behaviour change: imports and integrations update criticality, owner and classification

- Before, the first value written stayed forever. Now an import or an integration (DefectDojo sync) updates these attributes on assets nobody locked. A person's create or edit is a lock until released on the asset page.
- **Upgrade note:** the migration turns the values people set into locks (assets created by a person, and attributes changed by a person in the asset history), so nothing a person set changes at upgrade.

### Behaviour change: observation order and sensor clocks

- A source's value is replaced only by an observation it made strictly
  later; same-time replays and older reports are ignored and counted in
  `openctem_asset_attribute_observations_total`. A re-sighting of the same
  value refreshes its time at most once an hour.
- A sensor report's timestamp is clamped between the time its job was
  handed to the sensor and its arrival, for every use of it.
- Two equally trusted sources that disagree no longer flip the value back
  and forth: the value the asset shows stays and the conflict is shown.
  Sources of different trust disagreeing is no longer flagged as a conflict.
- Values whose deciding source passed its TTL move to the next fresh source
  within a day, without waiting for a new report.

### Behaviour change: asset classes no longer carry an external mapping hint

- `GET /api/v1/asset-types` no longer returns `jupiterone` on each class. Nothing in OpenCTEM read it; the class `id`, `label`, `lens` and `types` are unchanged. The `jupiterone` key is no longer accepted in `configs/asset-types.yaml`.
- The Vulnerability Management Essentials module preset describes its target persona without naming other products.

### Behaviour change: asset property names follow one convention

- Booleans are `is_<state>` / `has_<thing>`, timestamps `<event>_at`, lists plural; the registry generator refuses a key that breaks this (RFC-042 §6.3.10, architecture page "Property names").
- 22 boolean keys, 3 timestamps and one duration were renamed (`mfa_enabled` → `has_mfa`, `encrypted` / `encryption_enabled` → `is_encrypted`, `publicly_accessible` → `is_public`, `last_login` → `last_login_at`, `max_session_duration` → `max_session_duration_seconds`, …). The old names stay accepted on every write path and are folded into the new key.
- Scanner spellings fold too: `os` → `os_name`, `web_server` → `server`, `self_signed` → `is_self_signed`.
- Network devices gain `vendor`, `model`, `firmware_version`, `management_ip` and `serial_number`; HTTP services `chain_status_codes`.
- Migration `001333` folds the old names in stored assets (idempotent; its down is a no-op because a fold is not reversible).
- **Upgrade note:** API clients and saved filters that read the old key names must read the new ones; writes with the old names keep working.

### Behaviour change: one key per asset property, from the type registry

- The asset type registry (`api/configs/asset-types.yaml`, served by `GET /api/v1/asset-types` as `properties` and `common_properties`) declares every property key once: English and Vietnamese labels, display format, synonyms and, for keys such as `port`, the classes that may hold them (RFC-042 §6.3.9).
- An asset's addresses are stored only as `ip_addresses`. Ingest, `POST`/`PUT /api/v1/assets` and CSV import fold `ip`, `ips`, a plain `ip_address` string, `resolved_ip`, `resolved_ips` and `addresses` into it (and `nameserver`, `technology`, `san` into their plural keys). The domain DNS flattening writes `ip_addresses` instead of `resolved_ip`/`resolved_ips`.
- A port reported on a domain, subdomain, host or IP address is stored as that asset's `host:port/proto` open-port service with an `exposes` edge, not as a property of the domain. REST and import refuse such a key with 400.
- A domain's addresses also become `resolves_to` edges to IP assets for every report that may change the domain; a repeated sighting refreshes the edge's `last_verified`.
- Scope exclusions, IP correlation, relationship inference and the IP lookups read addresses through one helper, under the canonical key and every synonym.

### Behaviour change: asset risk scores use a likelihood-impact model

- The default risk model is now risk = findings score × exposure factor ×
  criticality factor × (1 − compensating-control reduction). The worst
  severity tier sets the findings score with diminishing returns per extra
  finding (500 low findings stay below one high); a finding in CISA KEV, with
  EPSS ≥ 0.5 or a known exploit counts one severity up. Unknown exposure and
  "not rated" criticality are not treated as safe; a crown jewel counts as
  critical. An asset with no open finding scores 0.
- Organizations on the built-in settings (legacy or default preset) move to the
  new default preset; an organization that chose another preset keeps it and
  can switch under Settings > Risk scoring. Every asset is rescored after the
  migration (`asset_risk_model`).
- Compensating controls now lower the score, and linking, unlinking, failing
  or expiring a control rescores its assets.
- Business units and asset groups refresh their average risk score after every
  rescore of a member asset; a business unit's finding counts now count open
  findings only (they included resolved ones).

### Behaviour change: asset IP addresses, technologies and open ports are tracked per source

- Each source keeps its own record of every IP address, technology and open
  port it reported, with when it last saw it (RFC-069 §13). An element is
  removed from a source's contribution only when the same source observes the
  same coverage again without it: a port scan of the same port range on the
  same address, a DNS resolution of the same name. A partial scan no longer
  closes ports outside its range, and a top-N or default port scan closes
  only what an earlier scan with the same setting found.
- The asset shows the union of the trusted sources that reported within
  their TTL (the per-class source rules). Another source still reporting a
  port keeps it open; a source past its TTL stops counting on the daily
  re-resolution.
- Ingest no longer overwrites `ip_addresses` or unions `technologies`
  forever on existing assets, and no longer closes ports by "the same kind
  of scan".
- The asset timeline records added and removed elements with the source and
  scan run; a change that undoes the previous one within an hour folds into
  it. Re-sightings record nothing.
- Migration `asset_attribute_set_elements` adds the table (no backfill:
  existing values stay until a source that covers them reports).

### Behaviour change: asset source precedence per attribute class

- Source precedence is now a ranked list per attribute class (identity,
  network, software, ownership, cloud tags, lifecycle) with a default list
  the classes inherit. A row names a kind or one source (`scan:nmap`), with
  its own TTL and a trust switch. New source kind `feed` for passive and
  published feeds.
- `GET/PUT /api/v1/organization/settings/asset-reconciliation` take
  `{"default": [...], "classes": {...}}`; `GET` also lists the sources that
  reported the organization's assets. `POST …/preview` shows what a policy
  would change before saving.
- Demoting a connector source needs step-up re-authentication. After a save
  the organization's assets are re-resolved in the background; changed
  values appear in the asset timeline.
- **Upgrade note:** settings saved in the previous shape (`precedence`,
  `ttl_days`) are ignored and the defaults apply; set them again under
  Settings > Asset sources. A migration (`asset_source_kind_feed`) widens the
  source kind check.

### Behaviour change: CTIS technical blocks are stored as flat asset properties

- Ingest, REST create/update and CSV import move a CTIS technical block's facts (`technical.certificate`, `.domain`, `.ip_address`, `.service`) to the asset type's flat property keys and drop the block (RFC-042 §6.3.10 item 6). `properties.certificate.not_after` is now `properties.not_after`, `properties.domain.registrar` is `properties.registrar`, a service's port is `properties.port`, and so on; renamed fields: `fingerprint` → `fingerprint_sha256`, `self_signed` → `is_self_signed`, `expired` → `is_expired`, `tls` → `has_tls`, `auth_required` → `is_auth_required`, service `name` → `service` (open port) or `server` (HTTP service).
- A domain's DNS records also give `dns_record_types`, `cname_target` and the A/AAAA addresses in `ip_addresses`. REST no longer writes the off-schema `record_type`, `ttl` and `dns_record_count`.
- A service's `tls: false` is no longer recorded (an unmeasured report sends the same value); `tls_cert_*`, `extra_info` and `auth_methods` are not kept.
- Migration `001340` promotes the blocks stored before (idempotent; its down is a no-op).
- **Upgrade note:** API clients reading `properties.<block>.<field>` read the flat key instead.

### Behaviour change: technologies are no longer an asset property

- The technologies detected on an asset live only in the asset technologies list (RFC-112). Set
  reconciliation writes them there (one per name: when two tools report different versions, the
  better version is shown) and `assets.properties.technologies` is no longer written or read.
- Asset responses (`GET /api/v1/assets`, `/assets/{id}`, `/assets/{id}/full`) embed `technologies`
  (name, version, category): at most 20 per asset on a list, all of them on one asset.
- `properties.technologies` and its synonym `technology` are dropped on every asset write; the
  `asset-technology-backfill` job removes the stored key from existing assets in batches. Tags are
  never removed (a tag carries no origin); new reports no longer add technologies as tags.
- Upgrade note: API clients that read `properties.technologies` read `technologies` instead.

### Behaviour change: automations no longer offer triggers and actions that never run

- The `finding_updated` and `webhook` triggers never fired (nothing called
  them). They are no longer offered, and creating, editing or switching on an
  automation that uses them returns 400 `UNSUPPORTED_WORKFLOW_FEATURE`.
- The `trigger_pipeline` action ran a scan workflow outside any scan, with no
  targets, scope gate or scan history. It is refused the same way; an
  automation runs a saved scan with `trigger_scan`. The executor also refuses
  to run any refused action type still stored in an automation.
- Migration 001212 switches off every active automation that still uses a
  refused trigger or action. The automation stays readable and lists the
  refused types in `unsupported_features`; replace the node to switch it on.
- **Upgrade note:** none; the migration runs with the others.

### Behaviour change: scope entries record their authorization source

- `POST /scope/targets` takes `authorization_source` (`ownership` by default, or `self_attestation`); `program` is refused (`PROGRAM_ENTRY_VIA_PROGRAMS`). Responses carry `authorization_source` and `program_id`.
- Widening a program entry on the Scope routes (activate, tier, expiry, reason, discovery) answers `409 PROGRAM_MANAGED`; deactivating and deleting still work.

### Behaviour change: findings seen only on a feature branch are not counted as exposure

- A finding first seen on a branch that does not count (not the default, a
  protected, a `main` or a `release` branch) is marked `branch_only`
  (migration 001138). The findings list, stats, groups and export leave it out
  unless the request filters on `branch_only`, a branch, a scan or ids
  (`branch_only=true` lists them); SLA escalation skips it; new-finding
  workflows (notifications, ticket rules) and regression follow-ups do not run
  for it. Dashboards, the executive summary, MTTR, program and CTEM cycle
  metrics, risk snapshots, asset, group and business unit finding counts and
  the threat model leave it out too. The CI gate, the run and the branch
  pages are unchanged.
- When a counting branch sees it, or its branch starts to count, the mark is
  cleared and its SLA clock starts then (the deadline keeps its length,
  measured from that time). Its workflows run then. `first_detected_at` keeps
  the first sighting, so the CI gate's notion of "new" is unchanged.
- The CI gate's findings link adds `branch_only=true` for a run on a branch
  that does not count.
- A branch-only finding no branch still shows (deleted, or merged and no
  longer scanned) becomes `not_observed` (`branch_expired`) through the finding
  lifecycle job, with an activity entry.
- A repository with no known default branch hides nothing. Findings response:
  new `branch_only` flag. See `docs/architecture/branch-only-findings.md`.

### Behaviour change: a remediation campaign completes only when its findings are fixed

- A campaign is done when every finding is closed and at least one is verified fixed (`resolved`). Auto-complete no longer fires for a campaign whose findings were all accepted, marked false positive or duplicate.
- Completing a campaign that is not done through `PATCH /api/v1/remediation/campaigns/{id}/status` answers 400 unless the request sets `close_with_open_members: true`; the console asks first and the audit row records `manual_with_open_members`. Responses carry `verified_count`.
- A Jira epic moved to Done completes its campaign only when the campaign is done.
- Restored: a completed campaign can be reopened (`status: active`), and a campaign in validation goes back to active when the validation fails.
- A campaign's due date only moves earlier: a later date or clearing it is refused.

### Behaviour change: capabilities are one resource, /api/v1/capabilities

- `GET /api/v1/capabilities` lists the platform capabilities and the
  organization's own custom ones, with `source=platform|custom`, `category`,
  `q`, `page` and `per_page` (max 100), and `include=usage` (tool and sensor
  counts). `GET /api/v1/capabilities/{id}?include=usage` also names the tools
  and sensors. The usage needs `scans:tenant_tools:read`; without it the
  include is left out and listed in `meta.omitted_includes`. Sensor names
  need `sensors:read`.
- Custom capabilities are created, changed and deleted at `POST /api/v1/capabilities`
  and `PUT`/`DELETE /api/v1/capabilities/{id}`, with `scans:tools:write` /
  `scans:tools:delete` (owner and admin), as custom tools are. A member could
  do this before with `scans:tenant_tools:write`.
- Changing or deleting a platform capability or another organization's
  custom capability answers 404 (it answered 403). The repository update
  and delete are now scoped to the organization as well.
- **Removed:** `GET /api/v1/capabilities/all`, `GET /api/v1/capabilities/by-category/{category}`,
  `GET /api/v1/capabilities/{id}/usage-stats`, `POST /api/v1/capabilities/usage-stats`
  and `/api/v1/custom-capabilities[/{id}]`.
- **Upgrade note:** clients move to the routes above (`/all` is the list with
  `per_page=100`; `by-category` is `category=`; usage is `include=usage`).

### Behaviour change: findings only a stale CI pipeline reported become not observed

- Within 15 minutes of the upgrade, the CI alert job moves open findings whose only source is a CI pipeline that is stale or archived to not observed (`source_stale`), audited per pipeline (`ci_pipeline.stale_source_findings`). They are not resolved and reopen on the next sighting.

### Behaviour change: a secret already on the default branch no longer blocks every pull request

- The CI gate still fails any run that adds a committed secret, and every
  default-branch run while a secret is open. A secret already open on the
  default branch is now a non-blocking `secret_pre_existing` note on pull
  request and other branch runs, so one historic secret does not block every
  pull request until it is triaged (RFC-077 G-9, owner decision 2). Without a
  default-branch baseline every secret counts as new and fails.

### Behaviour change: CI runners below the minimum supported version are refused

- A CI job whose runner reports a sensor version below `SENSOR_MIN_VERSION` now gets `403 RUNNER_OUTDATED` at the OIDC exchange (after its token verified and was admitted); the refusal is audited (`ci_run.token_refused`, reason `runner_outdated`). Before, the run was accepted and its pipeline only shown as degraded.
- A client that reports no sensor version is still admitted.
- **Upgrade note:** pipelines pinned to an old sensor image must update it before `SENSOR_MIN_VERSION` is raised.

### Behaviour change: a GitHub pull request run's branch is `pull/<n>`

- The CI/CD runs list shows `pull/<n>` for a GitHub pull request instead of its head branch. A trust
  configuration's `refs` rule no longer matches a pull request by its head branch name (a name the author
  chooses); list `refs/pull/*` to admit pull requests by ref.

### Behaviour change: CI runners v0.3.0 and later only

- openctemio/ci v0.3.0 is the CI runner release the console's snippets pin, and the oldest one the platform accepts (`CI_RUNNER_LATEST_VERSION` and `CI_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` default to v0.3.0). A pipeline on v0.2.0 or older is refused with `403 RUNNER_OUTDATED`. Those releases read scanner configuration and ignore files from the scanned tree, which could hide findings.
- The GitHub snippet keeps granting `security-events: write`: the v0.3.0 reusable workflow's scan job still asks for it, and GitHub does not start a called job that asks for more than its caller grants.
- `403 RUNNER_OUTDATED` now tells the job exactly what to change. It names the runner's version, the minimum, and the line to pin, in each form: GitHub `uses: openctemio/ci/.github/workflows/scan.yml@v0.3.0` or `openctemio/ci@v0.3.0`, the GitLab `include` URL, or the image tag for other CI systems. Before, it said "update the sensor image".
- The how-to guides pin v0.3.0.

### Behaviour change: a secret found by CI on a non-fork branch is an organization finding with a rotation task

- A secret a CI run finds on any non-fork branch (pull requests included) is now an organization finding at once instead of staying hidden as seen only on a branch, and a remediation task "Rotate <secret type>" is opened for it. The task is per secret identity: the same credential in other repositories or branches joins the open task, never a second one. Fork runs raise nothing.
- Only secrets that are not validated false and not matched by a generic or heuristic rule page: they block the gate and open a task. A hard-coded password hit or a dead secret follows the policy's severity and modes like any finding, so it no longer blocks every pipeline.
- Added: remediation action origin `system` (migration `remediation_action_origin_system`).
- Security: the validity a CI upload reports for a secret is no longer stored or trusted by the gate, and generic rules are matched against an explicit list of scanner rule ids. A secret rotation task is opened at most once per action at a time: a concurrent run joins the existing task.

### Behaviour change: address ranges are scanned live hosts first

- New `target_options.cidr_mode` value `liveness`, the default of a new scan with an address range when it can run it (a single-scanner scan, or a workflow with a Host discovery step). The ranges go to Host discovery and passive lookups only; the port scan and the steps after it get the live hosts found plus the addresses the inventory already holds in the ranges (RFC-088 step 6).
- A scan saved before keeps sweeping every address until it is edited. An explicit `sweep` is now stored as chosen. An explicit `liveness` on a workflow without Host discovery is refused (`LIVENESS_NEEDS_HOST_DISCOVERY`).
- The Network starter workflow starts with a Host discovery step; copies made before keep their steps. A run of names settles Host discovery without a command.
- The platform names the probe ports of every host discovery job (80, 443, 22, 3389, 8080, 8443 unless the step sets `ports`).
- New Scan: the address ranges choice offers "Find live hosts first" (en, vi).

### Behaviour change: a trusted collector's reports are an integration source

- A report from a collector sensor of the organization at trust level `trusted` (and push ingest in effect) is recorded as source kind `integration` for attribute reconciliation, named by its tool (`ldap`, `vcenter`, …), instead of `scan`. Its owner, criticality and exposure claims are therefore used like an integration's under the organization's reconciliation policy; a person's decision still wins. An untrusted collector, or a collector of another organization, stays a scan source, so its owner claim is dropped as before.

### Behaviour change: one software inventory with a dependency graph

- Packages are catalog products (package URL identity) with versions; where
  an asset uses one is a package link (`asset_software`, source `package`)
  with its relationship (direct or transitive), dependency scope, manifest
  path, licenses and the channel that reported it. Every parent of a package
  is kept (`asset_software_edges`), so all introduction paths are known.
- A report or SBOM is a snapshot of the manifests it names: packages it no
  longer lists at those paths are removed.
- `findings.component_id` now references `software_versions(id)`.
- **Upgrade note:** destructive migration; stop the API during the deploy
  (old code reads the dropped `components` and `asset_components` tables).
  Existing rows are copied per organization; the old shared description and
  homepage are not copied.

### Behaviour change: an unset APP_ENV means production; AUTH_PROVIDER defaults to local

- The API (and every image built from it, the all-in-one included) treats an
  unset `APP_ENV` as `production`, so a container started without configuration
  gets every production check (secrets, TLS to Postgres and Redis, Secure
  cookies, rate limits) and refuses to start without them, instead of running in
  development mode. `AUTH_PROVIDER` defaults to `local` (it was `oidc`).
- A secret that still holds example-file text (`openssl rand -hex 32`,
  `<CHANGE_ME...>`, `your-super-secret-...`) is refused at start-up in every
  environment, with a message naming the variable.
- New `server -check-config`: validates the configuration from the environment
  and exits (0 valid, 1 invalid) without connecting to anything; no secret is printed.
- `api/.env.example` now holds working development values (it held the literal
  `openssl rand -hex 32` as the encryption key, which stopped the API).
- **Upgrade note:** a development setup that relied on the old default must set
  `APP_ENV=development` (the shipped `.env.example` and `docker-compose.dev.yml`
  already do). A deployment that relied on `AUTH_PROVIDER` defaulting to `oidc`
  must set `AUTH_PROVIDER=oidc`.

### Behaviour change: emails and authenticator apps name the brand, not `APP_NAME`

- Emails and the two-factor issuer label now use `BRAND_NAME` (default
  `OpenCTEM`). `APP_NAME` names the service in logs only. Installations that
  set `APP_NAME` to rename the product set `BRAND_NAME` instead.

### Behaviour change: web-scoped nuclei jobs wait for a confined sensor

- A nuclei step with a web scope (a path exclusion on its host) carries `required_features: ["net.confined@1"]`. The claim offers it only to a sensor whose own report lists `net.confined@1` (sensor v0.19.0 or later, running with its seccomp profile); a capability declared by an administrator never counts. Other sensors leave it queued, and the run page says why (`not_confined`), instead of failing it with `WEB_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED` on an unconfined sensor.
- A step whose jobs need a confined sensor is refused when it is queued with the new code `NO_CONFINED_SENSOR` (class `placement`, never retried) when the organization has no active sensor that reports it.
- **Upgrade note:** until a sensor runs v0.19.0 with `--security-opt seccomp=…/sensor.json`, web-scoped nuclei steps fail with `NO_CONFINED_SENSOR`. Other steps are unchanged.

### Behaviour change: confirming an asset as ours adds its exact scope entry

- While scan approval is Off or On, a person who confirms a domain, subdomain
  or public address as the organization's (review queue, review by rule
  "accept selected", or the asset's Ownership tab) now also adds the scope
  entry for exactly that name. Scans can reach it without a second step in
  the scope dialog.
- The entry goes through the scope service: guardrails, the deny list, one
  re-authentication for the batch (nothing is saved without it), one notice
  to the administrators and an audit event per entry. Entries carry the
  origin `confirmed_asset`. The answer names each entry, so Undo is an
  ordinary entry delete.
- Never added: anything wider than the name, a name an entry already covers,
  a private or internal name, or a service, certificate or web endpoint.
  Nothing is added for a caller without the scope write permission.
- Under Strict, confirming still records ownership only. The organization
  can turn the behaviour off with the new scope setting
  `confirm_adds_to_scope` (default on). Assets confirmed earlier are not
  backfilled.
- Upgrade note: migration `scope_origin_confirmed_asset` widens the origin
  check on `scope_targets`. It is safe on populated tables.

### Behaviour change: connector assets are in scope by default

- After a successful Tenable.sc connector sync, the public names and
  addresses it synced get their exact scope entries (origin `connector`), so
  scans may reach them. A new per-connector switch, `assets_in_scope`
  (default on), turns this off. Entries already added stay and are listed on
  the Scope page.
- Each connector's first successful sync only notifies the administrators
  that its assets will be added from the next sync. Later syncs add them,
  with an audit event per entry and one notice per sync.
- Never added: wildcards or ranges, private names, services, certificates or
  hosts, names already in scope, or anything while scan approval is Strict.
- Upgrade note: migration `scope_origin_connector` widens the origin check on
  `scope_targets`. It is safe on populated tables.

### Behaviour change: legal links, legal pages and security.txt are set in the admin console

- Console > System > Legal sets the terms and privacy links of the sign-in and sign-up pages, whether the built-in legal pages are served and their values, and the `/.well-known/security.txt` contact and policy (`GET`/`PUT /api/v1/admin/settings/legal`, super admin with a fresh authenticator code, audited). The web console reads them from the public `GET /api/v1/legal`; changes show within a minute, without a redeploy.
- **Removed:** the web console no longer reads `LEGAL_TERMS_URL`, `LEGAL_PRIVACY_URL`, `LEGAL_PAGES_ENABLED`, `LEGAL_ORGANIZATION_NAME`, `LEGAL_SERVICE_NAME`, `LEGAL_CONTACT_EMAIL`, `LEGAL_WEBSITE_URL`, `LEGAL_DOCS_URL`, `LEGAL_ADDRESS`, `LEGAL_JURISDICTION`, `LEGAL_EFFECTIVE_DATE`, `SECURITY_CONTACT`, `SECURITY_POLICY_URL`, `SECURITY_TXT_ENABLED`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_TERMS_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVACY_URL`. **Upgrade note:** enter their values in the console after upgrading; until then the defaults apply (OpenCTEM contacts, no links, legal pages off).

### Behaviour change: platform e-mail is set in the admin console

- The platform's SMTP server is set in the admin console, System > E-mail (`GET`/`PUT /api/v1/admin/settings/email`, super admin with a fresh authenticator code, audited without the password). The password is encrypted with `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and never returned. "Send a test e-mail" sends to the acting administrator's own address only. A change applies without a restart.
- **Removed:** `SMTP_ENABLED`, `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_FROM`, `SMTP_FROM_NAME`, `SMTP_TLS`, `SMTP_SKIP_VERIFY`, `SMTP_TIMEOUT`. Startup refuses them with a hint. `SMTP_BASE_URL` (the link base) stays.
- Headless installs: `bootstrap-admin` stores `BOOTSTRAP_SMTP_HOST` (with `_PORT`, `_USER`, `_PASSWORD`, `_FROM`, `_FROM_NAME`, `_STARTTLS`) as the platform e-mail setting when none is stored.
- **Upgrade note:** before upgrading, note your SMTP settings, remove the `SMTP_*` lines (except `SMTP_BASE_URL`), and enter the settings in the admin console after the upgrade (or run `bootstrap-admin` with `BOOTSTRAP_SMTP_*`).

### Behaviour change: environment values lock or default the moved settings

- `CAPTCHA_TURNSTILE_SECRET`/`_SITE_KEY`, `DEPLOYMENT_REGION` and any of `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` still work and pin their setting: the console shows it as locked. `STORAGE_TENANT_QUOTA_MB` is the default until the console stores one.
- `SIGNUP_MODE=open` in production no longer refuses to start without CAPTCHA keys in the environment: open sign-up stays closed at runtime until a CAPTCHA is configured (or `SIGNUP_CAPTCHA=off-i-understand` is set).
- AI triage is always available for organizations that use their own key; a request in platform AI mode is refused with a clear message until a platform provider is on.
- **Upgrade note:** nothing to do. Existing environment values keep working; remove them to manage the settings in the console. No migration.

### Behaviour change: the crown-jewel flag is the assets.is_crown_jewel column

- **The crown-jewel flag is the `assets.is_crown_jewel` column** (owner
  decision O5). It was written into `properties.is_crown_jewel`, while the
  scoping summary read the column, so the two disagreed. Migration 000778
  backfills the column from the property (JSON `true` or the string `"true"`,
  any case; anything else reads as false), removes the key from properties
  and makes the column `NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE`. Priority classification, the
  attack-path graph, exposure chains, threat models, the executive
  dashboard, the crown-jewel filter and dedup merge (a merged crown jewel
  keeps the flag) read the column; asset responses carry `is_crown_jewel`.
  Only `PATCH /assets/{id}/crown-jewel` writes it: assets:write, the asset in
  the caller's data scope (404 otherwise), audited. `is_crown_jewel` stays a
  reserved key, so a create, update, import or sensor report cannot set it
  through properties. **Upgrade note:** a crown jewel marked by a pod of the
  previous release while the migration runs must be marked again.

- **`POST /api/v1/assets` for an asset that already exists is a 409** (owner
  decision O4). A name, or an address the name correlates to (IP/hostname),
  that matches an asset of the organization used to merge the request into
  that asset; it now creates and changes nothing. The 409 carries
  `details.existing_asset_id` only when that asset is in the caller's data
  scope; otherwise it is the same generic conflict for every match, so it
  reveals nothing about an asset the caller cannot see. Another
  organization's assets never match. The web offers to open the existing
  asset. Sensor ingest and the SCM repository import
  (`POST /api/v1/assets/repository`) keep their merge paths. **Upgrade
  note:** an API client that relied on the create upserting must handle the
  409 (update the named asset) or send its data through ingest.

- **Tenable rolling coverage of private addresses needs a scan zone.**
  The coverage dispatcher now applies scan create's private-range policy:
  a private address is dispatched only when a scan zone of the tenant
  covers it (and the pinned sensor, if any, is in that
  zone). Tenants that rotated internal assets without zones see those
  assets skipped (logged) until they add a zone.

- **`*.example.com` means the subdomains of example.com, not example.com
  itself.** The scope matcher used to let a wildcard domain pattern match the
  bare name too, which is not what the pattern says (RFC-042 §6.13, F17).
  `**.example.com` means the same as `*.example.com`. Matching ignores case
  and a trailing dot, and compares names in their IDNA form
  (`*.bücher.example` matches `shop.xn--bcher-kva.example`). The web's scope
  preview already matched this way. Both directions change:
  - **Scope targets:** a target `*.example.com` no longer puts
    `example.com` in scope (coverage counts, `POST /scope/check`, overlap
    warnings). This only narrows scope. Existing targets are not rewritten:
    add `example.com` as its own target if the apex should stay in scope.
  - **Exclusions:** an exclusion `*.example.com` no longer excludes
    `example.com` from scans. So that nothing excluded today is scanned
    tomorrow, migration 000292 adds an apex sibling (`example.com`, same
    type, status, approval and expiry) for every existing domain/subdomain
    exclusion written `*.x` or `**.x`, except rejected ones and names that
    already have their own row. The siblings have `created_by =
    system:migration-000292` and a reason naming the wildcard row; the down
    migration removes exactly those. New wildcard exclusions cover
    subdomains only: request the apex separately.

- **Organizations are created by the platform administrator by default.**
  `TENANT_CREATION_MODE` now defaults to `admin_only` (was `self_service`).
  Signed-in users can no longer create organizations themselves
  (`POST /api/v1/auth/create-first-team` and `POST /api/v1/tenants` return
  403); the administrator creates them in the console or with
  `bootstrap-admin -org-*`. Existing organizations and memberships are
  unaffected. To keep self-service creation (SaaS or trial installs), set
  `TENANT_CREATION_MODE=self_service` (Helm: `api.tenantCreationMode=self_service`).
  Any value other than `self_service` is treated as admin-only.

### Behaviour change: dispatch uses every tool the sensor reports

- The declared list was set when a sensor was created and went stale (a sensor reporting nine tools still had four declared), and it narrowed dispatch, so a tool installed later never got jobs. Dispatch, the v2 result tool gate, the manifest policy echo and the generated install configs now use the installed tools the sensor reports.
- To narrow a sensor's tools, edit its grant (`sensor_grants.tools`, RFC-052). Dispatch already enforces the grant.
- A sensor that has never reported its tools gets no tool jobs and may not push results until it reports them. That was already true for dispatch; now it also holds for the result gate. Sensors from v0.9.0 report their tools on every heartbeat. Fleet health flags a connected sensor without reported tools as `no_tools`.

### Behaviour change: every closed finding records why it closed and how that was proven

- A closed finding now carries a `closure_reason` and, when resolved, a
  `verification`, replacing `resolution_method` (removed). Resolved:
  `fixed`, `mitigated`, or `obsolete_asset` / `obsolete_source` /
  `obsolete_rule` (it went away without a fix). False positive: the five VEX
  `not_affected` justifications, `detection_error`, `test_or_example_code`.
  Accepted: `risk_accepted`, `compensating_control`, `wont_fix`,
  `no_fix_available`. Duplicate: `duplicate`, `correlated`. Verification:
  `covered_scan`, `retest`, `source_reported`, `vex_statement`,
  `security_review`, `attested`, `none`. Both are in the finding API response.
- **Requesting a false positive or an accepted risk now needs a reason**:
  `POST /findings/{id}/approvals` takes `closure_reason` (required); the web
  request dialog asks for it. The approval applies that reason. A resolve
  (`PATCH /findings/{id}/status`, bulk) may name `closure_reason`
  `fixed` (default) or `mitigated`.
- **MTTR counts remediations only**: findings resolved because their asset,
  source (a retired CI pipeline) or rule (the license policy no longer flags
  the package) went away are left out of MTTR, the risk snapshot's
  closed-today, the executive summary and the risk velocity fix count.
- Existing closed findings are backfilled from what `resolution_method`
  recorded; everything else becomes `unknown` (never guessed), and a resolved
  finding of unknown reason still counts in MTTR as before.
- Migrations `002270_finding_closure_columns` (columns), `002271_finding_closure_backfill`
  (batches of 1000 rows, each committed), `002272_finding_closure_trigger` (trigger and
  CHECK `NOT VALID`), `002273_finding_closure_validate`, `002274_finding_closure_drop_resolution_method`.
- **Upgrade note:** the migration drops `findings.resolution_method`; stop the
  API while it runs (old code reads that column).

### Behaviour change: VEX not_affected statements (INGEST_VEX)

- A finding with a VEX `not_affected` statement and a justification is counted and audited (`ingest.vex_dry_run`) by default. With `INGEST_VEX=enforce`, an open, non-human finding of a command-bound report becomes `false_positive` with the justification as its resolution (`ingest.vex_applied`). `off` only stores the statement.

### Behaviour change: every finding status change follows the lifecycle

- The finding lifecycle is now enforced on every write path. Moves a person may make are `ValidStatusTransitions`; the moves only the platform makes on evidence (a covered scan, a retest, a source mitigation, a VEX statement, an approved suppression rule, a stale source or expired branch, a regression reopen) are listed once in `PlatformStatusTransitions`.
- Automated SQL writes (coverage and default-branch auto-resolve, source-mitigated resolve, VEX not_affected, stale-source and branch expiry, regression reopen, suppression lift and re-link) take their from-states from the domain lifecycle; a list that drifts stops the server at start.
- Bulk status changes (bulk update, verify or reject by filter, approval) change only findings whose current status may move to the target; a finding that changed since the request is left alone.
- A retest whose decision is not a lifecycle move is refused and rolled back.
- Requesting or approving a false positive or accepted disposition is refused (400) when the finding's current status cannot move there. An expired risk acceptance reopens the finding only while it is still accepted.
- Triage (confirm) is refused for a finding that cannot move to confirmed (for example fix_applied).
- `open` was never a finding status; SQL filters no longer list it.

### Behaviour change: one finding status set for every source

- Pentest findings use the statuses every finding uses: `remediation` is now `in_progress`, `retest` is `fix_applied`, `verified` is `resolved` (how it was closed is `resolution_method = retest_verified`), `accepted_risk` is `accepted`. `draft` and `in_review` stay as the pentest pre-publication states. The pentest lifecycle is `vulnerability.PentestStatusTransitions` (one map for the legacy and unified paths).
- The API refuses the retired values (and `open`) with a 400 in status changes, pentest finding updates and list filters; nothing is mapped silently. The OpenAPI status enums list the canonical set.
- Pentest campaign stats are keyed `in_progress_count`, `fix_applied_count`, `resolved_count`, `false_positive_count`, `accepted_count` (were `remediation_count`, `retest_count`, `verified_count`, `false_positives`, `accepted_risks`).
- Finding stats `by_status` gains `fix_applied`, `validated_fixed` and `not_observed`; `open_count` is new + confirmed + in_progress (+ draft, in_review).
- The web console has one status registry (labels in English and Vietnamese, category, color); the findings filter groups statuses by category, each status once.
- Migration `001378` maps stored alias values (and `open`) in findings, pentest findings, approvals and retests, and adds a CHECK on the canonical set to `findings.status` and `pentest_findings.status`. It is idempotent.
- **Upgrade note:** API clients that send `remediation`, `retest`, `verified`, `accepted_risk` or `open` as a finding status must send the canonical status.

### Behaviour change: secret findings are fingerprinted with their own key, FINGERPRINT_KEY

- The fingerprint of a reported secret (and the key CI jobs hash raw secrets with) is now derived from `FINGERPRINT_KEY` instead of `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so rotating the encryption key no longer changes a secret's identity. `FINGERPRINT_KEY` is required outside `APP_ENV=development` (at least 32 characters, never printed). **Existing installs:** set it to the current `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` value before upgrading; every stored fingerprint stays valid. Never rotate it. See `docs/deployment/encryption-key-rotation.md`. `deploy/setup.sh` generates one for new installs.

### Behaviour change: the Compose gateway runs as non-root from the openctem-gateway image

- `api/deploy/docker-compose.yml` runs the gateway from
  `ghcr.io/openctemio/openctem-gateway` (Caddy with the standard and layer4
  modules, built with the release's Go) as uid/gid 1000, with no capability
  and `no-new-privileges`. It binds 443 through the namespaced sysctl
  `net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0`. Before, it ran as root from
  `caddy:2.11.4-alpine`. The image is set with `GATEWAY_IMAGE` /
  `GATEWAY_VERSION` (default: `OPENCTEM_VERSION`).
- Upgrade: the new one-shot `gateway-init` service changes the owner of the
  `gateway-data` / `gateway-config` volumes and `./ca` to 1000:1000 before
  the gateway starts, so `docker compose up -d` keeps certificates, the
  internal CA and the ACME account. Without it, run once:
  `docker compose run --rm --no-deps --user 0 --entrypoint chown gateway -R 1000:1000 /data /config /ca`.
  The gateway refuses to start on root-owned data and prints that command
  (`api/docs/deployment/docker.md`, "Gateway user").
- The `openctem-gateway` image itself now runs as uid 1000.

### Behaviour change: discovered assets join the inventory at once; scope still decides what is scanned

- What a scan or CT logs find outside every permanent scope entry is now stored as `discovered` and listed in the inventory at once, instead of waiting outside it in the review queue (RFC-054 §15).
- A discovered asset gets passive checks only unless an active scope entry covers it: scans refuse it with `no_entry`. Exclusions, rejections and the deny list still win.
- New scope setting `review_before_inventory` (default off) keeps the old review gate for organizations that want it.
- Dashboards, attack-surface counts and the CT watch list count only attributed assets (new asset filter `attributed`); the asset filter `approved` now includes `discovered`.
- Upgrade: migration `inventory_first_discovered` moves automatic `needs_review` records to `discovered` (a person's decisions are untouched); down restores them.

### Behaviour change: invite anyone, to any role, unless the organization restricts invitations

- People outside the organization (personal addresses, other companies' domains, unverified work domains) may now be invited to any role but owner. They no longer join as viewers only, and their access no longer has to end in 90 days (RFC-095 §4, amending RFC-058).
- New security settings (owner, step-up, audited): `invitees` (`any` by default, `verified_domains`, `allow_list`) and `external_access_end_required` (off by default; on restores the mandatory end of access, 90 days by default and 365 at most, for outside people no organization manages). An organization with `allowed_domains` set reads as `allow_list`.
- Inviting or giving an outside person a role above member (admin, full data access, or member, team, role, API key or settings administration) needs the inviter's recent re-authentication, and that member must prove a second factor every time a token is minted for the organization. A trust with their home organization still caps them at its `max_role`; full data access never reaches them through a team.
- Outside members may create API keys unless an active trust forbids it, never beyond their end of access.
- Invitation refusals carry codes: `INVITEE_NOT_ON_VERIFIED_DOMAIN`, `INVITEE_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, `INVITATION_NO_LONGER_VALID`, `PERSONAL_ACCOUNTS_BLOCKED`.

### Behaviour change: inbound Jira changes follow the finding rules for every linked finding

- An inbound Jira status change now goes through the finding service (transition map, pentest and approval gates, tenant scope) with the Jira integration as the recorded actor and the Jira account that moved the issue in the note and the timeline, instead of writing one finding row directly. Only a verified Jira or GitHub ticket move is exempt from the person-only claim rules; other integrations are not.
- Every finding linked to the issue is moved, not one arbitrary finding. "Done" is a fix claim: the findings take the legal steps to `fix_applied`, with a proof-of-fix re-check queued for each; nothing is closed from a ticket. "In Progress" walks the legal steps too (also back from `fix_applied`).
- Findings the rules keep where they are (closed, pentest, ...) are listed with the reason in one comment on the issue, not repeated within an hour.
- Done on a campaign's epic marks the campaign's findings fixed; it no longer completes the campaign (a campaign completes when its findings are verified closed).
- Migration `002642_findings_work_item_uris_gin` adds a partial GIN index on `findings.work_item_uris` (built concurrently).

### Behaviour change: per-organization limits replace plans
