- The core no longer has plans. An organization is unlimited and may use every module unless the instance operator (or, on a hosted service, its control plane) set a limit or a module deny for that organization. A self-hosted install with default settings has no limits anywhere.
- New organizations created by a person themselves start with the instance's **self-service default limits** (Console > System > Limits, `GET/PUT /api/v1/admin/settings/limits`, super admin with a fresh authenticator code). Empty by default. The same setting holds `orgs_per_user`, the per-person cap on self-service organizations (unlimited by default). The limits are written in the transaction that creates the organization.
- Migration 002890 (`per_organization_limits`) keeps every organization's caps: the limits of its plan become operator limits with the reason "migrated from plan", and modules its plan left out become module denies. Plans, plan defaults and the plan to module map are dropped.
- Over a limit only new additions are refused; nothing is deleted. A denied module keeps read access for 30 days.
- **Self-service sign-up requires starting limits.** With sign-up in `self_service` (`SIGNUP_MODE=open` or the console policy), the API refuses to start and the console refuses to switch to self-service until starting limits are configured: a saved console setting, `SELF_SERVICE_START_LIMITS` (a JSON object of limits, or `unlimited`), or the internal entitlements API.

### Behaviour change: saved scans are never switched to live hosts first on their own

- Editing a scan with address ranges keeps its CIDR mode: an edit that names no mode keeps the stored one, so a scan saved before live hosts first existed keeps sweeping. Before, an edit switched it to live hosts first when its workflow had Host discovery.
- The edit form shows a saved scan without a mode as sweeping, with an inline "Live hosts first (recommended)" suggestion that switches with one click when the scan can run it.
- The scan detail page shows the same suggestion as a non-blocking hint for sweeping scans whose scanner or workflow can find live hosts first; switching needs scans write.
- The scan details describe a live hosts first scan as such (it was shown as "swept whole").

### Behaviour change: migrations start from one baseline (RFC-053)

- The 395 migrations up to 001146 are replaced by `migrations/001146_baseline.up.sql`, the schema and built-in rows they produced, generated and verified by `scripts/squash-migrations.sh`. A fresh install applies one file; the resulting database is the same (schema byte-identical, grants of the least-privilege app role identical).
- A database at migration 001146 or later upgrades as usual. A database older than 001146 is refused before anything changes, by the migrations image, the all-in-one image and the API's startup check, with instructions.
- **Upgrade note:** before deploying this release, run the migrations of the last release before the baseline (git tag `pre-baseline-001146`), so the database is at 001146. Back up first.

### Behaviour change: only a proven scan run closes repository findings

- **Default-branch auto-resolve needs a clean, bound run** (owner
  decision O11). A scan closes a repository finding only when a
  protocol v2 run **bound to a command** completed with exit code 0, every
  report of the run completed with nothing rejected, quarantined or in error,
  the reports are an explicitly `full` scan of the default branch, and the
  finding was last seen by the same tool **under the same scan profile**
  (the blinding guard still applies). Before, any full default-branch report
  closed what it left out, even when the scanner had failed or ran a
  narrower ruleset.
- **Never closes now:** a report without a command (CI runner or collector,
  also in `warn` mode), a tenant upload (SARIF, CTIS, Nessus) and any
  protocol v1 report. They still create and update findings, and the
  per-branch occurrence sweep is unchanged. Findings they leave open close on
  the next clean bound run that saw them, by retest, or by a
  `findings:verify` holder.

### Behaviour change: the coverage SLO gate on closing a cycle is an organization setting

- Whether a CTEM cycle below the validation coverage SLO can be closed is now each organization's policy: owners and admins switch it on the Cycles page (`GET`/`PUT /api/v1/organization/settings/cycles`, `enforce_coverage_slo`, audited as `tenant.cycle_policy_updated`). Default off: the cycle closes and the shortfall is logged, as before.
- The platform-wide `CTEM_ENFORCE_COVERAGE_SLO` environment variable is removed; startup refuses it with a hint. **Upgrade note:** if you set it to `true`, unset it and switch the policy on for the organizations that want the gate.
- A policy that cannot be read refuses the close (500) instead of guessing.

### Behaviour change: deleting an organization waits 14 days, and owners can cancel

- An owner's `DELETE /api/v1/tenants/{tenant}` now answers 202 with
  `deletion_due_at` instead of deleting at once. The organization is closed to
  every credential from that moment (the same gate as a suspension) and the
  `organization-delete` worker deletes it when the 14 days end.
- Any active owner can cancel until then from the sign-in page
  (`POST /api/v1/auth/organization-deletion/cancel`, refresh-token
  authenticated); everything works again as before.
- Console > Organizations: "Delete now" (super_admin, fresh authenticator code,
  reason, critical admin audit) deletes an organization at once, whatever its
  status. It needs a second super admin's approval (four-eyes, action
  `organization.purge`, target `tenant:<id>`) when approvals are on.
- Migration `002915_organization_deletion_grace` adds the `pending_deletion` status
  and the `deletion_requested_at`, `deletion_requested_by` and
  `deletion_due_at` columns.

### Behaviour change: pentest campaigns with published findings are archived, not deleted

- Deleting a pentest campaign deleted all its findings, retests and reports,
  even findings the organization had already acted on. A campaign with
  published findings (any status other than draft, in review, false
  positive or duplicate) is now refused with 409 and a message to archive it
  instead; campaigns with only unpublished findings can still be deleted.
- New campaign status `archived`, reachable from completed or canceled and
  back to completed (unarchive). An archived campaign is read-only and left
  out of the campaign list unless `include_archived=true` or
  `status=archived` is asked for; the console's status filter shows it.

### Behaviour change: pentest reports are stored when generated and can be marked delivered

- A generated pentest report is stored (in the organization's rows, at most
  50 MiB) and its download returns the stored bytes: a report no longer
  changes when the campaign's findings change afterwards. The report shows
  `stored` and the SHA-256 of its bytes. Reports created before this change
  answer 409 on download; generate them again.
- The campaign lead can mark a stored report delivered
  (`POST /api/v1/pentest/reports/{id}/deliver`, audited
  `pentest_report.delivered`); a delivered report cannot be deleted. The
  console shows a Delivered badge and a Mark delivered action.
- Migration `pentest_report_snapshots` adds the stored-file table and the
  delivery columns.

### Behaviour change: pentest campaigns get a reporting phase

- New campaign status `reporting` between testing (`in_progress`) and remediation (`completed`). Testing no longer goes straight to `completed`: the lead finishes testing (`reporting`), then delivers the report (`completed`). Existing campaigns keep their status; no data moves (migration `002071_pentest_reporting_phase`, which also adds `pentest_campaigns.hold_from_status` and check constraints on the campaign and retest statuses).
- Delivering the report needs every draft and in-review finding decided; the reason override for them is gone. The completion sign-off is given during reporting (it was during testing) and is cleared when the campaign goes back to testing. The sign-off override for org owners and admins stays.
- Findings by phase, enforced on the server (editor and import): none in planning, lead and testers in testing, lead and reviewers in reporting (audited), none on hold, in remediation, canceled or archived.
- Phase changes: the campaign lead, or an org owner or admin who is a member of the campaign. An admin outside the team gets 403. Reopening testing on a delivered campaign needs a `reason` (10 characters or more). An on-hold campaign resumes only the phase it was paused in, and cannot be canceled while on hold.
- Campaign members get a `campaign_status_change` notification on every phase change.

### Behaviour change: a pipeline save validates its workflow graph

- Saving a pipeline (create, full save, or adding, editing or deleting a step) now checks the steps as a graph against the scan capability contracts. Before, an edge between incompatible steps (for example subfinder → katana: hostnames into a URL crawler), a cycle or a dependency on a missing step was stored, and the run silently fed the step the scan's own targets instead.
- A refused save returns `422 VALIDATION_FAILED`. Every problem is anchored to a step or a connection in `details.errors`, and an incompatible connection names the capability that would connect it ("insert HTTP probe"). A connection to or from a tool without a contract (a tenant tool) is a warning: it orders the steps and passes no data.
- `POST /api/v1/pipelines/verify` (`pipelines:write`) checks a draft and stores nothing.
- Deleting a step removes it from the other steps' dependencies. Every seeded system template passes the check.
- **Upgrade note:** an existing pipeline whose graph is invalid keeps running as before, but it must be fixed before its next save.

### Behaviour change: notification channels send a minimal message unless they opt in

- A channel with "Include details" off now sends only the event type, severity
  and a link, with no finding title, asset name or body. Before, the switch
  was stored but ignored and every message carried full details.
- Only channels created after this upgrade default to off. Existing channels
  that never saved a value (no stored setting) keep sending full details: the
  migration sets them to on explicitly, and `include_details` is now NOT NULL.
  A channel that was saved with the switch off now really sends the minimal
  message. The add and edit dialogs explain it (en, vi).

### Behaviour change: the verified-domain requirement for platform sensors is a console setting, off by default

- New platform setting in Console > System > Platform scanning: "Require a
  verified domain before platform sensors scan a target". Default **off**:
  assets come from many sources, and the organization's scope entry is the
  authorization, so no scan, preflight or scope view is blocked with
  "Proof needed". On: jobs reach platform sensors only for targets at or under
  a verified domain of the organization, and intrusive (T2) probes need one
  on any sensor (RFC-054 §8.1). A public multi-tenant cloud should turn it on.
- Changing it needs a super admin, a fresh console authenticator code and a
  reason; it is written to the admin audit log at critical severity and the
  other platform administrators are emailed. An unreadable stored value
  counts as on.
- The scope gate, exclusions, the platform deny list, scan zones for private
  addresses and tier ceilings do not depend on it and stay in force.
- **Removed:** the environment variable `SCOPE_ACTIVE_PROOF` and its `all`
  mode. Startup refuses a set `SCOPE_ACTIVE_PROOF` with a hint; remove it and
  turn the setting on in the console when the install is a public cloud.
  Upgrading a self-service install that relied on the old `platform_sensors`
  default: turn the setting on after the upgrade.

### Behaviour change: unknown reachability is no longer read as unreachable

- A finding whose asset has unknown exposure and no attack path, threat path or scanner reachability flag (a dependency in a repository with no deployment data, for example) is now classified with reachability **unknown** instead of "not reachable". Its priority reason says so ("critical severity; reachability unknown …"), never "not reachable from attacker perspective".
- Exploitation evidence now raises such a finding to P1 even without reachability evidence: a CISA KEV CVE, EPSS of 50% or more, or EPSS of 10% or more on a critical or high asset. Before, these stayed at P2 because unknown counted as unreachable. A finding with only a high severity stays at P2 until reachability is known.
- An isolated asset still counts as unreachable; an internal-only asset (private or restricted) now names that in the reason.
- The finding drawer and page show a "Reachability unknown" risk signal, and every risk-signal label is translated.
- Existing findings take the new class and reason at the next reclassification sweep.

### Behaviour change: program identification is gated on a reported capability, not the SDK version

- A job that carries a bug-bounty program's headers or User-Agent goes only to a sensor that reports `http.identity@1`: its tools send the job's identification on every request. Before, any sensor whose SDK was v0.19.0 or later got it. The platform no longer judges a sensor by its SDK version (RFC-094, decision O2).
- **Upgrade note:** update sensors to a release that reports `http.identity@1` (openctemio/sensor#275 and later) before deploying this; until then, jobs on program targets that require identification wait (fail closed), and a claim by id answers `PROGRAM_RULES_UNSUPPORTED`.

### Behaviour change: a network range is cut around its exclusions instead of being skipped

- A scan or workflow-run target that is an address range (CIDR or `a-b`)
  and overlaps an active address, range or CIDR exclusion used to be skipped
  whole: a /16 with one excluded address was not scanned at all. The target
  gate now subtracts the exclusions and the built-in deny list exactly and
  dispatches the rest as the fewest prefixes that hold it; the excluded
  addresses are never sent. The run's warnings name every cut range and how
  many addresses were left out (RFC-088).
- A range with nothing left is excluded (refused `deny_list` when only the
  deny list removed it). A range target wider than 2^16 addresses is refused
  on every path, including those that skip the scan target validator. More
  than 4 096 pieces in one dispatch is refused with `RANGE_TOO_FRAGMENTED`
  (merge scattered exclusions into wider ones).
- No migration and no operator step.

### Behaviour change: a group or campaign resolve never closes findings

- `status: "resolved"` on `POST /findings/remediation-groups/{key}/resolve`
  and `POST /remediation/campaigns/{id}/resolve` is refused (400), even with
  `findings:verify`: each finding is closed by its own evidence (a covered
  scan, a retest or a reviewer on the finding). The campaign response changes
  from `{resolved}` to the result above.
- Any bulk fix claim now queues the proof-of-fix re-check.

### Behaviour change: active stages skip names that have not resolved for a week

- Port scans, HTTP probes, templates and other active stages now take a host name only while the platform holds evidence from the last 7 days that it resolves (its DNS, HTTP, TLS or port observations). Older names are left out (`not_resolving`) and their DNS is checked again through the automatic enrichment; names the platform knows nothing about are still handed to the sensor. Passive stages (DNS resolution, discovery) still take them (RFC-088 decision A5).
- A single-scanner run records how many names it left out (`not_resolving_target_count`, a warning) and is refused with `NO_RESOLVING_TARGETS` when nothing is left.

### Behaviour change: resolving a finding needs findings:verify

- **Members can no longer close findings as resolved** (owner
  decision O12). Moving a finding to `resolved` now needs
  `findings:verify` from every status, `fix_applied` included, on every path:
  `PATCH /findings/{id}/status`, `POST /findings/bulk/status`,
  `POST /findings/remediation-groups/{key}/resolve` and remediation campaign
  resolve. Before, a Member (`findings:fix_apply` + `findings:bulk_update`)
  could mark findings `fix_applied` and then bulk-close them with no
  checklist and no proof of fix. Without the permission these calls now
  answer **403** and change nothing. Members keep `fix_applied`; a retest, a
  verified scan or a security reviewer closes the finding. The web hides
  "Resolved" from people without the permission. Give `findings:verify` to a
  custom role if a team should keep closing findings by hand.
- **Every human resolve records how and by whom.** The single, bulk, group
  and campaign paths stamp `resolution_method` (`security_reviewed` when the
  finding's verification checklist is complete, `admin_direct` otherwise) and
  `resolved_by`, and the bulk path now writes a status-change activity per
  finding. Any move away from `resolved` clears `resolution_method`.
- The unused, unguarded `VulnerabilityService.BulkUpdateFindingStatus` was
  removed.

### Behaviour change: a retest that does not match no longer resolves a finding by itself

- Retest outcomes are now `confirmed_fixed`, `not_reproduced`, `still_vulnerable` and `inconclusive` with a `reason_code` (`unreachable`, `blocked`, `auth_changed`, `server_error`, `endpoint_mismatch`, `template_changed`, `no_result`, `error`). Migration 001242 renames earlier rows: `fixed` becomes `not_reproduced`, `still_present` `still_vulnerable`, `unknown` `inconclusive`; no finding status changes.
- A confirmed fix needs the re-run's own evidence: a request to the finding's endpoint (its matched-at) that got an answer that is not a block, an auth failure or a server error, and the template the finding was last seen with. A plain "not detected" on a host that answers is `not_reproduced` and changes nothing.
- A confirmed fix moves the finding to `validated_fixed` ("Verified fixed — awaiting confirmation") for a person with `findings:verify` to close. Set `auto_resolve: true` in `PUT /api/v1/organization/settings/retest` to resolve it directly (audited).
- Each attempt's request and response are kept as masked finding evidence and shown under the retest ("View evidence"); retest reasons and announcements never carry URL parameter values or detected secrets.
- Each retest returns `run_kind: "retest"`, its `check_command_id` and the `sensor_id` that ran it (stored when it settles), so an attempt links to its command and sensor.
- **Upgrade note:** sensors report attempt evidence from sensor releases with nuclei `-ms` retests; until then nuclei retests read `not_reproduced` instead of fixed.

### Behaviour change: Researcher is a role template, not a built-in role

- The built-in roles are owner, admin, member and viewer. Researcher (RFC-065) is now the `researcher` role template (RFC-095).
- Migration `role_template_library` gives every organization that used the built-in Researcher role (a member held it, or a pending invitation offered it) its own custom Researcher role with the same grants, and moves every assignment and invitation to it; nobody's permissions change. Organizations that never used it no longer see it. `researcher` is no longer a reserved role slug.
- **Upgrade note:** an API client that referenced the Researcher role id `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000005` must use the organization's own Researcher role (`GET /api/v1/roles`).

### Behaviour change: a scan run's deadline is a policy cap, not a 1 h default

- A scan has no max duration unless its owner sets one. Scans that carried
  the old 1 h column default (3600 s) lose it; any other value is kept. A
  run is then bounded by the workflow's timeout or the platform's 24 h cap,
  and slow but alive work is kept going by its commands' leases.
- Every run records why its deadline is what it is (`deadline_reason`:
  `scan_max_duration`, `workflow_max_duration`, `platform_cap`, or `legacy`)
  and the run API returns it.
- A step is no longer dispatched when less time is left before the run's
  deadline than its tool needs to do anything useful: it fails
  `DEADLINE_TOO_CLOSE` and its targets join the run's unfinished targets
  (rolled over to the next scheduled run) instead of being started and
  canceled seconds later.
- Setting `timeout_seconds` to 0 on a scan update clears its max duration.

### Behaviour change: a SAST finding is keyed on the code it flags, not on the engine

- The SAST identity no longer uses the tool name or the engine's own fingerprints (SARIF `primaryLocationLineHash`, Semgrep `matchBasedId/v1`). It is the rule, the repository path and the hash of the flagged code, from the snippet or from the producer's CTIS `snippetHash/v1`. Running the same rules on another engine keeps every finding and its triage, and a job that forges an engine fingerprint can no longer take over a finding marked false positive.
- A finding without its code is keyed on its start line, computed by the platform, instead of the producer's own fingerprint. The first report that carries the code re-keys it to the code key; its status and history stay.
- A SARIF finding with no snippet now gets a new finding when its line moves. Producers should include the region snippet, or the `snippetHash/v1` partial fingerprint.

### Behaviour change: scope entries need approval only under Strict scan approval

- New organization setting **Scan approval**: Off (default), On or Strict
  (RFC-073). Owner only, with step-up re-authentication and a reason;
  approval rules (intensity, tools, asset tags, criticality, crown jewels,
  selectors, blast radius, schedule, sensor placement, zone) with Light,
  Standard and Strict presets. `GET/PUT /api/v1/organization/settings/scan-governance`.
- In Off and On a scope widening takes effect without a second person (the
  RFC-054 §7 approvals and the sole-owner self-approval apply in Strict
  only). Step-up, the dry run, member requests, exclusions, ownership proof,
  the deny list, audit and notifications are unchanged in every mode.
  Entries already pending stay pending until approved or withdrawn.
- The platform approval policy now governs scan approval:
  `/api/v1/admin/settings/scan-approval-policy` and
  `/api/v1/admin/tenants/{id}/scan-approval-policy` replace the
  `scope-policy` routes; the body field is `policy` (`tenant_controlled`,
  `off`, `on`, `strict`). Migration `001881` renames
  `tenants.scope_approval_policy` to `scan_approval_policy`.
- **Upgrade note:** an organization override of `disabled` becomes `off`;
  `required` and `tenant_controlled` overrides and a stored platform default
  are cleared (organizations start Off and their owner chooses). To keep
  approvals for an organization, its owner sets Strict, or a platform
  administrator forces `strict`.

### Behaviour change: a wildcard target no longer refuses an active scanner

- `*.example.com` with nuclei, httpx or another active tool used to be refused (`WILDCARD_TARGET`); it is now a selector. `WILDCARD_TARGET` now refuses a wildcard whose root is a public suffix, a shared provider apex or a denied name, and a pattern in an active tool's `scanner_config.targets`. A run whose selectors cannot be read from the inventory is refused with `TARGET_SELECTOR_UNAVAILABLE`.

### Behaviour change: pausing a scan turns its schedule off, not "Run now"

- A paused scan can still be run by hand (`POST /scans/{id}/trigger`). Scheduled runs, retries and automation triggers still need the scan active. A disabled scan runs for nobody. A refused trigger is recorded as a blocked run with `SCAN_NOT_TRIGGERABLE`.

### Behaviour change: a scheduled scan without an active owner is paused, and an administrator takes ownership

- A scheduled scan whose owner is missing (the account was deleted) is now paused at its first refused run (`SCAN_HAS_NO_OWNER`), like one whose owner left (`SCAN_OWNER_INACTIVE`); before, it stayed active and was refused at every due run. The organization's owners and administrators get one in-app notice per scan.
- Resuming such a scan is refused until it has an active owner. New: `POST /api/v1/scans/{id}/take-ownership` (owners and administrators; the caller's act scope must cover the scan's targets; audited as `scan_config.owner_taken`). The scan response has `owner_state` (`ok`, `missing`, `inactive`) and the scan page shows a banner with a "Take ownership" button.
- A scheduled scan can no longer be created without an owner (`SCAN_OWNER_REQUIRED`).
- **Upgrade note:** scheduled scans that are already ownerless pause at their next due run and notify the administrators; take ownership and resume the ones to keep.

### Behaviour change: a scan step whose targets were unreachable is no longer "completed, 0 results"

- A sensor now reports per-target reach with each command result
  (`metadata.reach`, `unreached_targets`; RFC-089). When the sensor reached
  none of a step's targets (no route, a firewall refused it, every attempt
  timed out, the names did not resolve) and found nothing, the step **fails**
  with the new code `TARGET_UNREACHABLE` instead of completing with zero
  results, which read as "nothing exposed". When it missed only some targets,
  the step and the run end **partial** with a per-class summary.
- Users will see failed or partial steps (and runs) where they used to see
  completed runs with no results. The cause is where the scan ran from: route
  the targets to a sensor that can reach them (a zone, or another sensor).
- `TARGET_UNREACHABLE` is never retried automatically. Sensors that send no
  reach summary keep today's outcome; their failure text such as "network is
  unreachable" or "no route to host" is now classified as `TARGET_UNREACHABLE`
  instead of a retryable `COMMAND_FAILED`, and a sensor may send the code in a
  structured fail (`POST /api/v2/sensor/commands/{id}/fail`).
- The reach data is sensor-supplied: counts are clamped, at most 20
  unreached targets are kept per task, and every string is cleaned to one
  bounded line. No migration.

### Behaviour change: scans outside their windows wait instead of being refused or skipped

- Jobs outside their windows are deferred at the claim to the next opening; a job of a run step with targets inside and outside is split, the open targets go now. Waiting no longer counts against the job's expiry or the run's deadline, and the unclaimed-run reaper leaves such runs alone.
- A manual run during a blackout starts and waits (formerly `409 SCAN_FREEZE_ACTIVE`). A scheduled run with nothing open is deferred to the next opening; a scheduled run outside a program's testing windows is no longer skipped.
- A target whose windows never open refuses the run with `409 SCAN_WINDOW_NEVER_OPENS`.
- When a window closes under a running job, it may continue for the policy's grace (default 15 minutes; program windows none), then it goes back to the queue for the next opening and its sensor is told to stop.
- Held jobs no longer fill the claim window: before, 100 jobs outside a program's testing window could keep every other job of the organization from being handed out.

### Behaviour change: scan workflows and scan runs are named the same at every layer

- "Pipeline" now means a CI pipeline only. The graph of steps a Scan runs is a **scan workflow**, and one execution of a Scan is a **scan run** with **steps** (and sensor **tasks**).
- API: `/api/v1/pipelines` is now `/api/v1/scan-workflows` and `/api/v1/pipeline-runs` is now `/api/v1/scan-runs` (tasks, task logs, stages, cancel). The old paths return 404; there are no aliases.
- JSON: `pipeline_id` is `scan_workflow_id` (scans, scan runs, previews, run filters), `pipeline_run_id` is `scan_run_id`, `step_run_id` is `scan_run_step_id`, the scan list's `pipeline_name` is `scan_workflow_name` and the scan stats `pipelines` counts are `scan_runs`. The `scan_completed` automation event carries `scan.scan_workflow_id`.
- Permissions: `integrations:pipelines:{read,write,delete}` are `scans:workflows:{read,write,delete}`, mapped one to one in system and custom roles, API key scopes and licenses (migration 001285). Reading and cancelling scan runs needs `scans:read` / `scans:write`, like the rest of the Scans area. The module `scan_pipelines` is `scan_workflows`.
- Audit: new entries use `scan_workflow.*`, `scan_workflow_step.*` and `scan_run.*`; entries written before the upgrade keep their `pipeline_*` actions (the audit chain is never rewritten).
- Database (migration 001285): `pipeline_templates` → `scan_workflows`, `pipeline_steps` → `scan_workflow_steps`, `pipeline_runs` → `scan_runs`, `step_runs` → `scan_run_steps`, with their columns, indexes, constraints, RLS policies and trigger, renamed in place. Queued commands keep reporting to their run: their payload keys are rewritten in the same migration.
- **Upgrade note:** run the migrations before the new API starts. Scripts or API keys that call `/api/v1/pipelines` or `/api/v1/pipeline-runs` must switch to the new paths and field names.

### Behaviour change: scan workflows live under Scans; automations at /automations

- The console's Scans page has three route tabs: **Scans** (`/scans`), **Runs** (`/scans/runs`) and **Workflows** (`/scans/workflows`). The workflow editor is `/scans/workflows/{id}`. Each tab is its own page with one list, so links to a page of runs or workflows are plain URLs.
- Scan workflows left Mobilization: the "Scan Pipelines" sidebar row is gone, and the scan workflow list drops its "Recent runs" and "Visual builder" tabs (the Runs tab and the editor cover them). Creating a workflow needs `scans:workflows:write`.
- Event automation is **Mobilization > Automations** at `/automations`.
- The old `/pipelines`, `/pipelines/{id}/builder`, `/workflows` and `/scans?tab=runs` pages are removed with no redirect. The command palette still finds the Workflows tab when you search "pipeline" or "builder".
- **Upgrade note:** update bookmarks to the new paths.

### Behaviour change: scope changes left waiting for approval take effect where approvals are off

- Scope entries and exclusions still pending in an organization whose scan approval mode is Off or On (created before approvals of scope changes were limited to Strict) are put into effect by the new hourly `scope-pending-settle` controller. Each row goes through the job signer's ledger before it is saved and is audited (`scope_target.activated` / `scope_exclusion.activated`, actor `system`, reason `approvals_not_required`); administrators get one notification per organization. Strict organizations, and any whose mode cannot be read, keep their pending rows. No migration rewrites rows (a SQL update would bypass the signer's ledger).
- Activating such a pending entry or exclusion puts it into effect at once outside Strict.
- The Approvals tab and the "Waiting for approval" strip item are shown only while the organization requires approvals or something still waits. The In scope list now shows pending entries, and the Out of scope list pending and rejected exclusions, each with its status pill.

### Behaviour change: members request scope targets instead of creating them

- A member with `attack_surface:scope:write` but without
  `attack_surface:scope:approve` can no longer add a permanent scope target.
  They request a one-off entry for one name or address, with a reason, and an
  administrator approves it.
- **Upgrade note:** existing scope targets are unchanged (active, permanent,
  `t1`). A deactivated target is re-activated by an administrator.

### Behaviour change: an active scope entry lets scans reach a pending name

- A discovered name or address that automation left waiting for review
  (`needs_review` or `candidate`) can now be scanned when an active scope
  entry of the tenant covers it, a one-off entry included. Before, the
  pending record refused before any scope check, so adding a one-off entry
  for such a name never helped.
- The record stays pending and the asset does not join the inventory; only
  the entry authorizes the probe. Once the entry expires the record refuses
  again.
- A person's decision still wins: a state a person set (sent back to review,
  dependency, monitor only, rejected), a rejected parent name and a scope
  exclusion keep refusing whatever entry covers the name.
- A service or URL never gets more than its host: when the host asset is
  rejected, a dependency, monitor only or sent back to review by a person,
  probes of its services and URLs are refused with the host's state.

### Behaviour change: approving a scope entry confirms the names it covers at once

- The scope join (names waiting for review that a permanent scope entry
  covers join the inventory) now runs after every committed change that can
  confirm a name, not only after create and activate: an entry approved
  (the usual path for a new wildcard), an entry in effect updated, an
  exclusion deleted, deactivated or shortened. It runs from the scope
  service, so review rules and later automations get it too, debounced and
  serialized per tenant. Pending entries, rejections and new exclusions
  trigger nothing.

### Behaviour change: names a scope target or seed covers are confirmed without review

- A discovered name (Certificate Transparency or a tenant scan) that an active,
  permanent domain scope target (`x`, `*.x`) or a root-domain seed covers is
  confirmed into the inventory with the new rule `matches_scope_target`
  (RFC-054 §4.3). An IP address is confirmed only when an IP, range or CIDR
  scope entry contains it. Exclusions, tombstones and rejected parent names
  still win; a person's decision is never changed.
- Removing the scope target keeps the asset and its findings; active scanning
  of it stops at once.
- **Backfill:** at start-up (and every 6 h) the API re-evaluates automatic
  `needs_review`/`candidate` records against the current scope targets and
  seeds, tenant by tenant, and confirms the covered ones; each run that
  confirms names is audited as `asset.attribution_auto_confirmed`. Live had
  10 such names under `*.example.co.uk`.

### Behaviour change: scope entries and exclusions need no approval outside Strict scan approval

- In the Off (default) and On scan approval modes, a member with `attack_surface:scope:write` adds or widens a scope entry directly (step-up re-authentication kept) instead of sending a request, and a new scope exclusion is in effect at once, recorded with its creator as `approved_by`. Extending an exclusion keeps it in effect, and taking one out of effect no longer needs a second person. Only Strict keeps member requests and the exclusion review (RFC-073 §6, RFC-054 §13).
- Pending entries and exclusions left from the old flow are not activated: they stay on the Approvals tab to approve or reject, or their requester removes them and adds them again.
- An unknown scan approval mode now counts as Strict for scope entries (fail closed).
- The scope dialogs follow the mode: no request or approval wording outside Strict (en and vi).

### Behaviour change: scope responses name people and say where an entry came from

- Every actor field of a scope entry or exclusion (`created_by`,
  `approvals[].approver`, `rejected_by`, an exclusion's `approved_by`) is now
  an object: `{"kind": "user", "id", "name"}`, `{"kind": "user", "id",
  "former_member": true}` or `{"kind": "system", "code"}` (for example
  `upgrade_wildcard_split` instead of `system:migration-000292`). Names come
  only from the organization's current members; no e-mail is returned.
  **Upgrade note:** API clients that read `created_by` as a string read
  `created_by.id` now.
- New `origin` on entries and exclusions (migration `001244`): `manual`,
  `request`, `import`, `review_rule`, `refusal_fix`, `seed`,
  `seed_migration` or `system`, set by the path that created the row.
  Existing rows are `manual`, rows the platform wrote are `system`.

### Behaviour change: seeds are scope entries; only scope entries authorize scans

- Root-domain seeds are folded into scope entries (migration `001262`).
  Each seed became the permanent entry `*.<domain>`
  (`origin: seed_migration`, `t1`, in effect), unless an active permanent
  wildcard entry already covered it; nothing that was allowed before is
  refused after. `GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/easm/seeds` are removed: add
  a root domain as a scope entry (`POST /api/v1/scope/targets` with
  `*.example.com`).
- Scope entries gain `discovery` (default on): names under a permanent domain
  entry are discovered (Certificate Transparency, DNS checks) and join the
  inventory. One-off and non-domain entries never discover. Turning discovery
  on needs `attack_surface:scope:approve` and step-up, and notifies the
  administrators.
- A verified domain is proof of control only (SC2): it marks the entries at or
  under it as verified and is what platform sensors and intrusive checks
  require, but it no longer authorizes a scan by itself. Every `easm`
  verified domain that no entry covered became an entry `*.<domain>`, so
  nothing is lost; a domain verified for SSO sign-in got no entry.
- Web: the Seeds tab of Scoping › Scope is replaced by **Domain proof**
  (`/scope?tab=proof`). The old `/settings/integrations/verified-domains`
  redirect is removed (no redirects for moved pages).
- **Upgrade note:** API clients that used `/api/v1/easm/seeds` create scope
  entries instead. No action is needed for existing seeds.

### Behaviour change: a scope entry's tier ceiling is enforced on every dispatch; intrusive workflow steps need proof

- A scope entry authorizes probes up to its `max_tier`; a root-domain seed or
  verified domain up to t1 (RFC-054 §4.2). A target covered only below the
  probe's tier is now refused with `tier_exceeds` everywhere: scan create and
  quick scan answer `TARGET_OUT_OF_SCOPE` (fix `raise_tier` with the entry's
  id and the needed `tier`), a scan run leaves the target out with a warning
  (`TIER_EXCEEDS` when nothing is left), a workflow step leaves it out of that
  step, and pipeline runs, chained hops, coverage, validation and
  `POST /scope/check` refuse it. The probe's tier is the tool's highest stage
  tier (`zap` t2; `nuclei`, `httpx`, `naabu` t1; discovery and code tools
  t0); a tool the catalog does not know counts as t1.
- A workflow step whose tool is intrusive (t2) is handed only the run's
  targets at or under a verified domain; with none left it fails with
  `STEP_TARGETS_REFUSED` before any sensor sees it (RFC-054 §8.1).
- **Upgrade note:** existing entries are t1, so nothing changes for them. An
  entry an approver set to t0 now authorizes passive discovery only; raise it
  to t1 in Scoping > Targets to keep active scans of its names.

### Behaviour change: scope entry tier ceilings apply only in Strict scan approval

- In the Off and On scan approval modes a scope entry is a list of targets (with exclusions): its `max_tier` no longer refuses a probe; the scan's intensity and the approval rules decide how hard it probes. Coverage, exclusions, the deny list and ownership proof for intrusive steps are unchanged. Strict keeps the ceilings (RFC-073 §6).
- The job signer's ledger holds each organization's tier ceilings (`set_tier_ceilings`, snapshot `tier_ceilings_off`): leaving Strict is accepted by the signer before the mode is saved (a refusal keeps Strict), entering Strict narrows after, every scope widening carries the state, and a sync can only turn the ceilings back on. Turning them off needs the `SIGNER_LEDGER_T2_MIN_APPROVALS` floor.
- Upgrade: existing ledgers keep the ceilings on until an organization's next scope widening or mode change (the signer is the stricter side meanwhile). To bring every organization in step at once, run `server -signer-ledger-export` and import it into the stopped signer with `ledger import -replace`.

### Behaviour change: `*.example.com` in scope now covers `example.com` too

- A domain scope target or exclusion `*.x` (and `**.x`) now covers `x` itself
  as well as every name below it (RFC-054 §4.1). Scanning `example.com` with
  only `*.example.com` in Scoping is no longer refused. An exact `x` still
  covers only `x`.
- To keep the subdomains in scope without the apex, add an exclusion of exactly
  `x`; the exclusion carves out the apex and nothing else.
- Exclusions use the same matcher: an exclusion `*.x` now also excludes `x`.
- **Upgrade note:** existing `*.x` scope targets start covering their apex on
  deploy (live had 3 wildcard targets, one without its own apex entry). Review
  them in Scoping › Targets and add an apex exclusion where the apex is not
  yours.

### Behaviour change: scoring changes recompute open findings from that moment; closed findings stay frozen

- Every asset risk score and finding priority now stores the scoring version it was computed with (`assets.risk_version`, `findings.priority_version`). A version is a `scoring_changes` row: one per platform model version and one per change of a tenant's risk scoring settings, priority rules or SLA policies, recorded by database triggers (migration 002220).
- A change queues the affected assets in the new durable `finding_priority_queue` in the same transaction; the `finding-priority` worker recomputes the priority and SLA deadline of their **open** findings, tenant-fair. Closed findings are no longer reclassified: they keep the class and deadline they had when closed, so closed-period metrics no longer change after the fact.
- The recompute now re-reads EPSS and KEV from the catalogs, so intel that changed since a finding was ingested is applied.
- New findings, reopens, severity changes, asset criticality, exposure and crown-jewel changes, and business unit and service changes queue the asset. The 12-hour whole-tenant sweep and the in-memory queue are removed; a daily reconcile (and one at start-up) queues stale findings at once and the rest behind events.
- Metrics: `openctem_finding_priority_queue_depth`, `..._queue_oldest_seconds`, `..._checked_total`, `..._changed_total`.
- **Upgrade note:** none. After deploy the start-up reconcile recomputes every open finding once in the background.

### Behaviour change: self-service organizations get no limits, and the idle policy is opt-in per organization

- Organizations people create themselves (create-first-team, `POST /api/v1/tenants`) are no longer put on the Free plan. They start with no limits, like every other organization, and one person may create more than one. A self-hosted install with self-service sign-up on no longer caps new organizations at 5 seats and 500 assets on its own.
- The idle-organization policy (reminder, read-only, deletion due) used to apply to every Free organization. It now applies only where a platform administrator turned it on for that organization: `PUT /api/v1/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/idle/policy` `{enabled, reason}` (ops_admin+, reason required both ways, audited). It is off by default.
- Removed: `PUT /api/v1/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/idle/exemption` and the `exempt*` fields of `GET .../idle` (now `policy_enabled`, `policy_reason`, `policy_set_at`). Off is the default, so an exemption is no longer needed. The audit action `tenant.idle_exemption_changed` is now `tenant.idle_policy_changed`.
- Migration 002440 (`idle_policy_opt_in`) turns the policy off for every existing organization and returns every organization to `active`, so none stays read-only.
- **Upgrade note:** stop the API while the migration runs (it drops the exemption columns). An operator who wants the idle policy for some organizations turns it on per organization after the upgrade.

### Behaviour change: the API's internal sensor listener moves to port 9443

- The API's sensor protocol v3 listener (`SENSOR_MTLS_LISTEN_ADDR`) defaults to `:9443` instead of `:8443`, and the gateway passes sensor connections to `api:9443` (`SENSOR_MTLS_UPSTREAM`). Port 8443 now means only the platform console's site. Sensors are unaffected: they dial port 443 and the gateway routes them by ALPN inside the stack network.
- **Upgrade note:** only a deployment that publishes or proxies the API's sensor listener itself (a separate port, an SNI passthrough, your own TCP proxy) changes its target from `:8443` to `:9443`, or sets `SENSOR_MTLS_LISTEN_ADDR=:8443` and `SENSOR_MTLS_UPSTREAM=api:8443` to keep the old port. The Compose overlay `docker-compose.sensor-passthrough.yml` already uses 9443.

### Behaviour change: each sensor product is judged against its own release line

- The platform knows several sensor products: the scanning sensor and the Tenable.sc connector, listed in `versions.yaml` and built into the API. A sensor is compared with its own product's latest and minimum release. Before, every sensor was compared with the scanning sensor's, so a connector at v0.1.0 showed as "version unsupported". A sensor that reports no product counts as the scanning sensor. A custom sensor built on sdk-go gets no update or unsupported verdict; its compatibility is the protocol and the capabilities it advertises.
- The SDK release is informational. The SDK minimum is gone: `sdk_status` `unsupported` and the health reason `sdk_unsupported` are replaced by `advisory` and `sdk_advisory`, for SDK releases with a published security advisory (`versions.yaml` `sdk.advisories`). The Prometheus alert `SensorSdkUnsupported` is now `SensorSdkAdvisory` (`openctem_sensors_sdk{status="advisory"}`).
- `GET /sensors/stats` returns the product catalog (`products`) and `sdk_advisories` in place of `latest_version`, `min_version` and `sdk_min_version`. Sensor responses add `product`, `product_known`, `product_latest_version` and `product_min_version`. `GET /admin/operations` returns `sdk_advisories` in place of `sdk_min_version`.
- `GET /sensors/{id}/config-templates` takes `?product=` (a catalog product id) and renders that product's install snippets, pinned to its latest image. By default it renders the snippets of the product the sensor reports, or the scanning sensor's. The Tenable.sc connector has docker run and Compose snippets.

### Behaviour change: sensor transport status moved to Console > Operations

- The sensor transport status (protocol v3 mode, gRPC self-probe state, endpoint and reason) is installation infrastructure: it is now part of `GET /api/v1/admin/operations` (`sensor_transport`, platform admins only) and shown on Console > Operations as a calm note in plain language, with a link to the transport docs, only when an operator can change something.
- Removed `GET /api/v1/sensors/transport`: organization members no longer see the platform's gRPC endpoint or probe reason on the Sensors page.
- Sensor detail: the transport line labels HTTPS as "HTTPS" and explains each sensor fallback reason (including `platform_unreachable`) in plain words, with the reason code in a tooltip; the text is translated (en, vi).

### Behaviour change: sensor protocol v3 picks its bindings by itself

- `SENSOR_TRANSPORT_V3_ENABLED` is retired (startup refuses it). `SENSOR_TRANSPORT_V3` is `auto` by default: the HTTPS binding (`/api/v3/sensor`) is always served, so key-bound sensors move to protocol v3 at their next hello with no configuration; `off` serves no v3 and sends every sensor back to v2 at its next call.
- The gRPC binding listens once the sensor CA loads and a public host is known (`SENSOR_PUBLIC_HOST`, else `sensors.<host>:<port>` of the platform URL when its host is a DNS name). A self-probe dials that host through the gateway every minute and verifies the server certificate against the sensor CA; hello names the gRPC endpoint only while the probe passes, so a gateway without passthrough, a closed port or a wrong name leave sensors on the HTTPS binding instead of sending them to an endpoint that cannot work.
- `GET /api/v1/sensors/transport` (`sensors:read`) reports the mode and the gRPC binding's state, endpoint and reason; metrics `openctem_sensor_transport_grpc_advertised` and `openctem_sensor_transport_grpc_probe_total{result}`.

### Behaviour change: informational findings get no SLA and no priority or risk weight

- Informational findings (severity `info`, or `none` = CVSS 0.0) get no SLA
  deadline by default. An SLA policy's `info_days` of `0` now means "no SLA for
  informational findings" and is the default for new policies; a positive
  value opts back in. The priority class no longer hands an informational
  finding a deadline. Migration 001180 moves policies still on a shipped
  default info window (90 or 365 days) to `0` and clears the deadline of open
  informational findings whose effective policy has no info SLA, so they stop
  counting as SLA breaches.
- Informational findings are classified P3 and skip the ownership floor,
  unless the CVE is in CISA KEV. A tenant priority rule can still raise them.
- The count-based asset risk score no longer adds points for informational
  findings (eight technology detections used to cap the finding component).
- **Upgrade note:** a tenant that wants a deadline for informational findings
  sets the info window of its SLA policy again after upgrading.

### Behaviour change: SLA is always on

- SLA is now a core module. Every finding carries an SLA deadline that the findings
  list, dashboards, My Work, exports, reports and escalation use, but switching the
  SLA module off only hid the policy page and made the policy reads
  (`/api/v1/sla-policies`, `/api/v1/assets/{id}/sla-policy`) answer
  `MODULE_NOT_ENABLED` while SLA badges stayed visible. The SLA toggle is gone from
  Settings > Modules; reading and editing policies still needs the SLA permissions.
- Migration 001442 marks the module core and removes the organizations' SLA overrides.

### Behaviour change: SLA deadlines only tighten when a priority or policy changes

- When an open finding's priority rises, its deadline becomes min(old deadline, now + the new class's SLA). It used to be recomputed from the detection date, which set a deadline already in the past (an instant breach) for a late escalation.
- A priority drop no longer extends the deadline, and an overdue finding stays overdue. Before, the drop moved the deadline later and could turn `overdue` back into `on_track`.
- An SLA policy edit now applies to open findings from the change time, tighten-only: a shorter policy pulls deadlines in, a longer one only affects new findings. Closed findings keep their deadline.
- Every tightening writes a `sla_deadline_tightened` entry on the finding's timeline, with both deadlines, both classes and the reason.
- The database enforces the rule for every writer: an update that would move an open finding's deadline later, or clear it, keeps the stored deadline, so a stale full-row write or a recompute that read the row before a tightening cannot extend it. Only the regression restart and the end of a risk acceptance start a new, later clock.
- Upgrade note: the `finding_activities` activity-type constraint is re-added `NOT VALID` and validated by a separate migration, so the large table is not scanned under an exclusive lock.

### Behaviour change: approving a suppression rule closes the open findings it matches

- Approving a suppression rule now also gives the organization's open findings
  that the rule matches its disposition (`false_positive`, or `accepted` for an
  accepted-risk or won't-fix rule; resolution `suppressed`), in the same
  transaction as the approval. Before, only findings first seen after the
  approval were suppressed. Findings already decided, resolved or reported by
  a person (pentest, manual, bug bounty, red team) are left alone; an
  accepted-risk rule leaves work in progress alone.
- One approval changes at most 10 000 findings; the response
  (`applied_findings`, `capped`), the rule's audit entry and the audit log
  carry the count, and each finding gets an activity naming the approver.
  Deleting the rule or its expiry reopens them as before.
- New `GET /api/v1/suppressions/{id}/preview` (`findings:suppressions:approve`)
  returns how many open findings an approval would close; the console's
  approval dialog shows it.

### Behaviour change: approved suppression rules without an end now expire

- **Upgrade note:** since migration `suppression_rule_end_backfill`, an approved suppression rule that had no end date expires 90 days after the deploy that ran the migration, and the findings it suppressed reopen then (with a new SLA clock where they were accepted risks). Operators: review the rules flagged "Review" in Exceptions and submit a new rule before that date for any suppression that must continue.

### Behaviour change: every suppression rule has an end date

- A suppression rule ends at most 365 days ahead; a rule created without an end gets 90 days, and the end can no longer be removed. Renewal is a new rule, approved again.
- Migrations 002310–002313 add the review flag (`review_flagged_at`, `review_reason`) and a 90-day default for `expires_at`, give every existing rule without an end 90 days from the upgrade (pending and approved ones are flagged for review and show a "Review" badge), then add and validate `chk_suppression_rules_expires_at_set`.
- **Upgrade note:** rules that never expired before now expire 90 days after the upgrade, and the findings they suppress reopen then unless a new rule is approved. Review the flagged rules in Exceptions.

### Behaviour change: a scan no sensor can run is refused at trigger time

- A trigger (manual, scheduled or quick scan) is refused with `NO_SENSOR_FOR_TOOL` when its scanner, or the tool of one of its workflow steps, has no online sensor that may run it. A zone-pinned scan is judged on that zone's sensors. These jobs used to be queued and expire unclaimed. The error body's `details` name the tool, the step and the sensor counts.
- The trigger refusal codes `NO_SENSOR_FOR_TOOL`, `NO_SENSOR_AVAILABLE`, `TOOL_NOT_FOUND`, `TOOL_DISABLED` and `TOOL_NOT_SCANNER` are now returned in the error `code` instead of `BAD_REQUEST`.

### Behaviour change: unclassified assets get low-impact active checks behind platform guardrails

- An inventory asset that no scope entry covers and nobody excluded or
  rejected is no longer passive only: it now gets low-impact active checks
  (common ports at a low rate, HTTP GET of `/` and `/.well-known/*`, TLS and
  tech fingerprinting, nuclei info templates tagged tech or exposure). New
  scope setting `unclassified_scans`: `low_impact` (default), `off` (the old
  rule) or `full`; the Strict scan approval mode forces `off`. Changing it
  needs scope approve and step-up and is audited (RFC-054 §16).
- Platform guardrails keep an unclassified asset passive whatever the
  setting: addresses in CDN, shared-hosting or cloud networks, addresses with
  no network data, shared hosting, and names under none of the
  organization's domains (refusal code `guardrailed`). Its exact scope entry
  makes it scannable.
- A port scan of a name reaches only the web ports (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
  while an address the name resolves to is not in scope and may not be
  probed on its own, or nothing is known about its addresses (code
  `web_ports_only`); this also applies to names in scope.
- At claim, a job on unclassified targets that goes beyond the low-impact
  profile is clamped to it (or its unclassified targets are left out when it
  mixes them with in-scope ones). Port settings are now read from both
  `config` and `scanner_config`.

### Behaviour change: nuclei validations and retests keep to the web scope instead of being refused

- A nuclei validation (`validate`) or retest (`retest`) whose target host has a path exclusion now carries the organization's `web_scope`, like a scan, instead of being refused with `WEB_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED`. The platform writes the scope; a value in the caller's payload is replaced.
- Such a job requires `net.confined@1` (`required_features`): only a sensor that itself reported it is offered the job. A sensor reports it from v0.19.0, the release whose validation and retest paths keep to the scope (sdk-go v0.25.0), so an older sensor, which would drop the scope, never takes it. Other sensors leave it queued (`not_confined`).
- When the organization has no active sensor that reports `net.confined@1`, the job is refused when it is created with `NO_CONFINED_SENSOR`, and nothing is queued.
- A validation or retest of any other web tool on such a host is still refused with `WEB_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED`. Jobs on hosts without a path exclusion are unchanged.

### Behaviour change: crawled URLs are web endpoints under their origin, not assets

- A crawl (CTIS 1.6 `endpoints[]`, or a legacy `discovered_url` asset) now writes the web surface
  sub-inventory: one row per origin, method and path template in `web_endpoints`, and the parameter
  names in `web_endpoint_params` (migration 001270). No `discovered_url` asset, attribution record or
  graph node is created per URL any more; the origin's `http_service` asset is created when missing.
- Query values, user info and fragments are never stored, and token-like path segments are templated
  and masked before storage.
- A command-bound report writes endpoints only under origins its targets cover; endpoints land only on
  an origin asset the report may change. Only a tool whose stage reports endpoints (web crawl, web
  application scan) and whose declared contract names `endpoint` may write them.
- Caps: 5,000 active endpoints and 500 scripts per origin, 100 parameters per endpoint.
- A crawl step chained into a template scan now hands it the origin, not every crawled URL.
- Design: RFC-056.

### Behaviour change: the Sensors page lists sensors only; CI pipelines live on CI/CD

- The Sensors page no longer has the All / Daemon / Runner switch, the "CI pipelines fresh" metric or CI pipeline rows, and its "Needs attention" counts sensors only. CI pipelines, their runs and coverage are on the CI/CD page alone.
- When the organization has active CI pipelines and the caller may read them, Sensors shows one line, "N CI pipelines report through CI/CD", with the number of failing gates linking to that filter.
- With no sensor yet, Sensors explains what a sensor is. It offers "Pair a sensor" first, and "Install with an API key" where the organization allows bearer keys. It also notes that scanning repositories from CI needs no sensor.
- Old links to `/sensors?mode=runner` (and an open pipeline, `&pipeline=<id>`) now go to the same view on CI/CD.

### Removed: plaintext audit sink destinations and the Bearer token

- `ADMIN_AUDIT_SINK_TOKEN` is replaced by `ADMIN_AUDIT_SINK_SECRET`: at least 32 bytes, required for an `https://` sink, and used as an HMAC-SHA256 key (the receiver verifies `X-OpenCTEM-Signature`); a Bearer header is no longer sent.
- `syslog+tcp://` and `syslog+udp://` are removed: the API refuses to start with them. Use `syslog+tls://`.
- **Upgrade note:** an API configured with `ADMIN_AUDIT_SINK_TOKEN`, `syslog+tcp://` or `syslog+udp://` must be reconfigured before upgrading.

### Removed: AUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_COOKIE_NAME, AUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_COOKIE_NAME, AUTH_TENANT_COOKIE_NAME

- The session cookies are always `auth_token`, `refresh_token` and `app_tenant`, the names the web console and the gateway use. A custom name reached the API only, which split the session between the three.
- Startup refuses the three variables with a hint. **Upgrade note:** delete them from your environment if set.

### Removed: the per-type asset pages

- `/assets/hosts`, `/assets/domains`, `/assets/certificates`, `/assets/ip-addresses`, `/assets/services`, `/assets/websites`, `/assets/apis`, `/assets/mobile`, `/assets/containers`, `/assets/networks`, `/assets/cloud-accounts`, `/assets/storage`, `/assets/databases`, `/assets/identity` and `/assets/repositories` (the list), and the redirect-only routes `/assets/all`, `/assets/http-services`, `/assets/open-ports`, `/assets/web-applications`, `/assets/discovered-urls`, `/assets/iam-roles`, `/assets/iam-users`, `/assets/service-accounts`, `/assets/serverless`, `/assets/cloud-resources` and `/assets/vpcs` are gone, with no redirect. Every asset type is a filter of the one inventory: `/assets?types=host`, `/assets?types=identity&sub_type=iam_user`.
- **Upgrade note:** bookmarks to the old pages answer 404; open `/assets` and pick the type, or use `/assets?types=<type>`.

### Removed: the bootstrap-tenant command

- `bootstrap-tenant` (raw SQL, unaudited, ignored `TENANT_CREATION_MODE`) is
  no longer built or shipped in the image. Use
  `bootstrap-admin -org-name … -org-owner-email …`.
- `sla.Service.CreateDefaultTenantPolicy`, which nothing called.

### Removed: `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME`

- The page title now comes from `BRAND_NAME` on the API; the web variable is
  no longer read.

### Removed: the scans:tenant_tools:delete permission (migration 001179)

- Nothing checks it any more (tool settings have no delete; custom
  capabilities are deleted with `scans:tools:delete`), so it is removed from
  the catalog and from the owner and admin roles. No role loses access to
  anything. The rows are archived and the down migration restores them.

### Removed: legacy component endpoints and permission

- `GET /api/v1/components/stats`, `/ecosystems`, `/vulnerable`, `/licenses`
  (use `summary`, facets and list filters) and `POST /api/v1/components`,
  `PUT/DELETE /api/v1/components/{id}` (the inventory is written by sensors,
  CI and SBOM import). The permission `assets:components:delete` is removed;
  it gated nothing else.

### Removed: the program feed admin routes

- `GET /api/v1/admin/program-feed` and `PUT /api/v1/admin/program-feed/local-bundle` had no console page and are removed until one uses them. The stored local-bundle switch stays off, so a `PROGRAMFEED_LOCAL_BUNDLE_DIR` bundle is not imported. **Upgrade note:** none; no migration.

### Removed: the asset_sources table

- Migration 001076 drops `asset_sources`. Nothing ever wrote it (its
  repository was never constructed); production held 4 hand-made rows from one
  day with no source id and no contributed data. Its only reader, the asset
  lifecycle worker, now uses `assets.discovery_source` and `assets.last_seen`.
  The asset merge no longer moves its rows.
- Upgrade in one step. The down migration recreates the empty table.

### Removed: the assets.owner_id column (migration 001056)

- `assets.owner_id` and its two indexes are dropped. Asset owners live in
  `asset_owners` since migration 000340; no code reads the old column.
- **Upgrade note:** upgrade from a release before the owner model change in
  one step (migrate, then restart every API pod). Old pods still running during
  a rolling update would fail asset queries until they are replaced.

### Removed: retired and never-read columns (migration 001483)

- Migration 001483 drops `users.federated_issuer` and `users.federated_subject` (moved to `user_identities` by 001306, empty since), `tenants.members_without_group_see` and its CHECK (retired by decision D2; pinned to `nothing` by 000910), `admin_credentials.password_hash` and `password_changed_at` (the console signs in with the linked account plus TOTP; the stale console password hash is deleted with the column), `event_types.default_severity` and `licenses.is_osi_approved`, `is_fsf_libre`, `is_deprecated`, `limitations` (never read).
- `sensors.type` no longer accepts `agent` (the pre-rename name) or `platform`; the API already refused both and no row holds them.
- The migration stops with an error, instead of silently dropping it, if any other constraint or index uses one of these columns.
- **Upgrade note:** one step, no code change needed. Run the migration explicitly; `air` does not run migrations.

### Removed: database objects nothing used

- Migration 001059 drops objects that had no reader or writer, all verified
  empty or unreferenced: the `deprecated` schema and its seven quarantined
  tables (000213), `webhook_deliveries` (outbound webhooks never delivered;
  the `webhooks` table stays for now), the views `v_assets_domain_summary`,
  `v_assets_http_services` and `v_assets_ip_summary`, and ten functions with
  no caller (`user_has_permission`, `get_user_permissions`,
  `user_has_full_data_access`, `expire_scope_exclusions`,
  `expire_suppression_rules`, `cleanup_old_audit_logs`,
  `can_tool_scan_asset_type`, `get_compatible_asset_types`,
  `refresh_access_for_direct_owner_add/_remove`). The down migration
  recreates them as they were.
- **Upgrade note:** none for the application. An external script or report
  that queried one of these views or functions directly stops working.

### Removed: tool run statistics that were always zero, and four tables nothing wrote (migration 001491)

- `GET /api/v1/tools` and `GET /api/v1/tools/{id}` no longer accept `include=stats` or `days`: the statistics came from `tool_executions`, which no code path ever wrote, so every tool always showed zero runs. `include=stats` now answers 400 like any unknown include. The web console never requested it.
- Migration 001491 drops `tool_executions`, `component_licenses` (the shared component-to-license junction; license reports read `asset_components.license`), and `attack_paths` / `attack_path_nodes` (attack paths are computed on demand; only the demo seed ever wrote them). The demo component seed no longer writes the junction.
- **Upgrade note:** one step. A client that sent `include=stats` must drop it. Run the migration explicitly; `air` does not run migrations.

### Removed: rollback ledgers of finished data migrations (migration 001481)

- Migration 001481 drops twelve tables that past data migrations kept only so their own down migrations could put rows back: `access_control_removed_archive`, `asset_type_input_map`, `asset_type_legacy_codes`, `asset_types_legacy_removed`, `asset_type_reclassifications`, `asset_properties_pre_001185`, `easm_ct_rekey_001018`, `granular_permission_backfill`, `technique_applicability_rekey_ledger`, `technique_applicability_subtype_moves`, `legacy_templates_backup_001322` and `legacy_template_steps_backup_001322`, plus the function `asset_type_normalise_batch`. Nothing in the application reads them.
- A new unit test refuses a migration that creates a backup, ledger or archive table unless a later migration drops it or an allowlist entry with an expiry date covers it, so such tables do not pile up again.
- **Upgrade note:** one step, no code change needed. The rows are rollback data only; they are not restored by the down migration (it recreates the tables empty), so a down migration of 001322, 001286, 001185, 001184 or 001179 run afterwards restores nothing. Take the usual pre-upgrade backup if you may need them. Run the migration explicitly; `air` does not run migrations.

### Removed: twelve seeded platform settings nothing read

- Migration 001079 deletes the system-wide rows 000036 seeded into
  `settings` (registration_enabled, email_verification_required, mfa_enabled,
  password_min_length, session_timeout_hours, max_sessions_per_user,
  api_rate_limit_per_hour, max_file_upload_mb, audit_log_retention_days,
  default_timezone, default_language, support_email) and the typed value
  columns only they used. No code read them; the real controls are the
  environment settings (`AUTH_ALLOW_REGISTRATION`, `AUTH_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH`,
  ...) and the per-organization settings.
- The `settings` table stays for the per-tenant file storage configuration.
- Upgrade in one step. The down migration restores the columns and rows.

### Removed: unused rule-management and finding-data-source tables

- Migration 001092 drops `rules`, `rule_sources`, `rule_bundles`,
  `rule_overrides`, `rule_sync_history` and `finding_data_sources`. They were
  empty and never wired: no route, permission or worker used them. The
  matching Go repositories, the `rule` domain package and the unused rule
  service are removed. Custom scanner content stays in template sources and
  scanner templates. The down migration recreates the tables.

### Removed: the declared tool list on a sensor (`sensors.tools`)

- The `tools` field is gone from `POST /api/v1/sensors`, `PUT /api/v1/sensors/{id}` and the sensor response, and `capability_mismatch.tools_not_installed` is gone with it. The tools dispatch uses are in `effective.tools`; what the sensor reported is in `reported.tools`. The web console drops the tool-limit picker (Edit sensor, the install review) and the "installed but not allowed" notices.
- Migration 001149 drops `sensors.tools` and redefines the generated `effective_tools` as the reported installed tools (`COALESCE(reported_tool_names, '{}')`).
- **Upgrade note:** re-adding the stored generated column rewrites the `sensors` table under a short exclusive lock. The table holds one row per sensor, so this takes milliseconds. The old declared lists are not kept; the down migration restores an empty column.

### Removed: the retired outbound webhooks table

- Migration 001069 drops `webhooks`. The outbound webhooks feature never
  delivered anything; its API and permissions went in 001032. The table only
  held configuration rows of that removed feature (3 on production, created on
  one day and never used); they are dropped with it.
- Encryption-key rotation (`cmd/rekey`) no longer rewraps
  `webhooks.secret_encrypted`, and the sensor-rename upgrade check no longer
  counts event names in it.
- Upgrade in one step: no configuration change. The down migration recreates
  the empty table; the dropped rows are not restored.

### Removed: five environment variables that switched nothing

- `APP_DEBUG`, `GRPC_PORT`, `LOG_SKIP_HEALTH`, `AI_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS` and `AUTH_ALLOW_REGISTRATION` were read (or, for `AUTH_ALLOW_REGISTRATION`, only warned about) but changed no behaviour: no debug mode, no gRPC listener on 9090, health requests are never logged, AI triage runs on the job queue, and sign-up is the console's sign-up policy.
- Startup now **refuses to run** while one of them is set, and the error says what to do instead, the same way it refuses the retired `AGENT_*` names.
- The API image no longer advertises port 9090; it advertises the sensor protocol v3 listener (8443).
- `api/.env.production.example` is removed: nothing referenced it and it drifted from `api/deploy/.env.example`, the production example the Compose stack uses.
- **Upgrade note (one step):** delete these five lines from your `.env`, compose file or chart `extraEnv` before upgrading.

### Removed: the older auto-resolve and reopen repository methods

- `FindingRepository.AutoResolveStale`, `AutoResolveStaleByAssets` and
  `AutoReopenByFingerprint` are removed. Nothing called them; they closed
  findings with a weaker rule (no coverage proof) than the coverage
  auto-resolve and reopened with a narrower one than the scan re-detection
  that replaced them.
- The findings state tabs (Open, Fixed, Dispositioned, All), their
  descriptions and the drawer's status, severity and assignee toasts are now
  translated (en and vi).

### Removed: the finding statuses validated_fixed and not_observed

- Whether the scanner still reports a finding is now `observation`
  (`present` / `stale`), and whether a re-check reproduces it is `validation`
  (`reproducible` / `not_reproducible`). Both are fields beside the status, in
  the finding response and as list filters. A finding keeps its work status
  when it goes stale or a re-check no longer reproduces it.
- `status=validated_fixed` / `status=not_observed` (filters, saved views,
  `PATCH /status`) now answer 400 and name the replacement filter
  (`validation=not_reproducible`, `observation=stale`). Stored saved views and
  campaign filters are rewritten by the migration.
- A retest that confirms a fix without `retest.auto_resolve` no longer moves
  the finding; it stamps `validation = not_reproducible` and the finding waits
  in its status for a person (or a covered scan) to close it. The validation
  engine's downgrade works the same way.
- Feature-branch and branch-only expiry, a stale CI source, template drift and
  the software matcher mark findings stale instead of changing their status;
  any sighting makes them present again. A covered scan can now resolve a stale
  finding.
- Migrations `002530_finding_status_dimensions_column` (the column, a catalog
  change), `002531_finding_status_dimensions` (row moves first, the status CHECK
  replaced last and NOT VALID), `002532_finding_status_dimensions_validate`: findings in a retired status go
  back to the status they had before (from their timeline, else `confirmed`)
  with a timeline entry; live had none.

### Removed: workflow settings that never did anything

- Workflow `triggers` (manual, schedule, webhook, on asset discovery) were
  stored and never acted on. Schedules belong to scans, and events belong to
  Automations. `notify_on_complete`, `notify_on_failure`,
  `notification_channels` and `retry_failed_steps` were never applied either.
  All five are gone from the API, the domain and the console.
- The per-step "Retries" field is no longer offered in the builder: step
  retries are not applied yet.

### Removed: the OIDC `POST /api/v1/auth/token` stub

- With `AUTH_PROVIDER=oidc` the route no longer exists (404): the identity
  provider issues tokens, and the stub never issued one. `GET /api/v1/auth/info`
  still returns the provider endpoints.

### Removed: the tenant-wide Jira webhook route and secret endpoints

- `POST /api/v1/webhooks/incoming/jira?tenant=`, `GET /api/v1/integrations/jira/webhook-secret` and `POST /api/v1/integrations/jira/webhook-secret/rotate` are removed (the secret could be read back at any time). Use `GET /api/v1/integrations/{id}/jira-webhook`, `POST /api/v1/integrations/{id}/jira-webhook/secret/rotate` and `PUT /api/v1/integrations/{id}/jira-webhook/secret`.
- **Upgrade note:** a Jira webhook pointed at the old URL (`/api/v1/webhooks/incoming/jira?tenant=...`) now gets 404 (it was refused before as well); create it again with the integration's new URL and secret (Settings > Integrations > Ticketing > Inbound webhook).

### Removed: plan endpoints and fields

- `GET/PUT /api/v1/admin/settings/plans`, `GET/PUT /api/v1/admin/settings/plan-modules`, `GET/PUT /api/v1/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/plan`, `PUT/DELETE .../plan/overrides/{key}`, `PUT/DELETE .../modules/{module_id}/grant` and `GET /api/v1/organization/plan`.
- The `plan` field of `GET /api/v1/users/me/tenants` (and the session bootstrap) and of `GET /api/v1/tenants/{id}`, and the `plan` column and filter of `GET /api/v1/admin/tenants` (each row now has `limits_apply`).
- Replaced by `GET /api/v1/organization/limits` (owners and admins: the limits that apply, usage and unavailable modules; `applies: false` when nothing applies), `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/limits[/{key}]` and `PUT/DELETE /api/v1/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/modules/{module_id}/deny`.
- The error code of an addition over a limit is now `LIMIT_REACHED` (was `PLAN_LIMIT`), and the metric `openctem_plan_limit_refusals_total` is now `openctem_limit_refusals_total`.
- **Upgrade note:** an installation running self-service sign-up must set `SELF_SERVICE_START_LIMITS` (for example `unlimited`) or save limits in the console before upgrading, or the API will not start. Stop the API while migration 002890 runs (it renames and drops tables). API clients that read `plan` or call the plan endpoints must move to the limits endpoints.

### Removed: down-migration ledger tables

- Migration 001147 drops `priority_rule_safety_report` and `role_permissions_admin_only_stripped`. They recorded what migrations 000942 and 000945 changed, for their down migrations, which the baseline replaced; no code read them.
- `scripts/preflight-migrate.sh` and `make migrate-preflight` are removed: their only checks were for migrations 000170 and 000171.

### Removed: module switches that switched nothing

- Migration 001524 deletes the retired or inactive modules (billing, licensing, platform,
  subscription, usage, policies, scope, secrets, sources, webhooks,
  integrations.webhooks) and the ones that gated nothing: `vulnerabilities`, `commands`
  and `remediation_tasks` (the remediation pages now follow `remediation`, like their
  API). Their organization overrides are removed.
- Sensors, groups, API keys, notification settings, integrations and
  integrations.notifications are core: the toggle API already refused to switch them off,
  and the settings page showed a switch that failed on save.

### Removed: organization-chosen product bundles

- `GET/POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenant}/settings/modules/bundles` and the Products card are
  removed: packaging is the plan's. Onboarding offers one optional starting set (a preset,
  applied once). No organization had a bundle subscription; migration 001968 clears the
  setting.

### Removed: the API's own .nessus parser and its two upload routes

- `POST /api/v1/assets/import/nessus` (hosts only, no caller) and `POST /api/v1/assets/import/nessus-findings` are removed, with the parser and converter behind them. A `.nessus` export is uploaded to `POST /api/v1/findings/import`, which converts it with the shared ctis importer, like every other format. Settings → Vulnerability scanners now uses that route (with `min_severity=low`, as before).
- What the import keeps is equal or richer: every CVSS version with its vector, VPR, EPSS, typed vulnerability ids, CWEs, advisories, KEV and exploit maturity, one finding per compliance check (they used to collapse into one per plugin), host identity hints (FQDN, NetBIOS, MACs, OS CPE). Findings stored by earlier uploads keep their identity (host, CVE or plugin, port) and are updated, not duplicated.
- The scan policy is never read, and plugin output and compliance values are redacted of accounts, passwords, tokens and community strings; the removed converter copied plugin output as is.
- **Upgrade note:** a script that posted raw XML to `/assets/import/nessus-findings` posts the file as multipart part `file` to `/findings/import` (one file up to 100 MiB, or a ZIP of several). `session_id` and `tool` are gone: the import record is the producer, the tool is `nessus`. Neither route ever auto-resolved findings.

### Removed: inert plan checks

- The unwired single-sign-on plan check on trusted organizations (`ErrPlanLacksSSO`) and the AI triage plan checks that always allowed. Nothing was enforced by them.
- The `make assign-plan` and `make list-plans` targets (they used tables that no longer exist); `make list-tenants` lists organizations only.

### Removed: the API-only and web-only production Compose files

- `api/docker-compose.prod.yml`, `web/docker-compose.prod.yml`,
  `web/docker-compose.prod-simple.yml` and `web/nginx/` are removed. The API-only
  file could not start in production (it disabled Redis TLS, which production
  refuses), and three partial production layouts drifted from the supported one.
- **Upgrade note:** deploy with `api/deploy/docker-compose.yml` (the whole stack
  behind one HTTPS port), the all-in-one image, or the Helm chart.

### Removed: deprecated pentest campaign lead/team columns

- A pentest campaign's team is its member list (`pentest_campaign_members`, one role per user).
  Migration `001544` drops the deprecated `pentest_campaigns.lead_user_id` and `team_user_ids`
  copies, which nothing wrote any more. A campaign with no member row at all first gets its lead
  and team from those columns, limited to users who are members of the campaign's tenant; a
  campaign that already has members is left as it is.
