### Added: see and disconnect connected AI applications

- My account, Connected applications lists the AI applications (MCP clients)
  you connected in the organization: what they may read, when they were
  connected and last used, and from where. Disconnecting ends access at once.
- Settings, AI access (MCP) gains the organization policy editor and, for
  owners and administrators, every connection in the organization with a
  disconnect. The page now leads with connecting through the browser (no key
  to copy); API keys remain for scripts.
- The platform console lists every AI application with its usage (counts
  only) under System, AI applications, and operators can block one
  everywhere (audited).
- API: `/api/v1/mcp-access/my-connections`, `/api/v1/mcp-access/connections`,
  `/api/v1/admin/mcp-clients` (RFC-062 §12).

### Added: MCP clients discover how to authenticate

- `POST /api/v1/mcp` answers a missing or invalid credential with
  `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=…, scope=…`, and the API serves
  the OAuth Protected Resource Metadata of the MCP endpoint (RFC 9728) at
  `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/v1/mcp` and
  `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (RFC-062). The resource and issuer
  come from `APP_URL`; without it nothing changes.
- **Upgrade note:** the gateway sends `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource*`
  to the API; update a custom reverse proxy the same way.

### Added: AI applications connect to the MCP server with OAuth

- OpenCTEM is now the OAuth 2.1 authorization server of its MCP endpoint
  (RFC-062): authorization server metadata, `/oauth/authorize`,
  `/oauth/token`, `/oauth/revoke`, and a consent page (`/oauth/consent`)
  where a signed-in person sees the application, where it is published, where
  the browser returns, the organization and the access, and approves or
  refuses. An MCP client needs only the endpoint URL.
- Authorization code with PKCE S256 and a resource indicator; applications
  identify with a Client ID Metadata Document (fetched without redirects,
  public addresses only) or a client registered in advance.
- Access tokens last 10 minutes and are bound to one person, one
  organization, one application and the MCP endpoint; refresh tokens rotate,
  and presenting a used one revokes the connection. On every request the
  token can do at most what its scopes allow and the person still holds;
  suspension or removal ends it at once. A call another scope would allow
  gets an `insufficient_scope` challenge.
- Every consent, token issue, reuse and revocation is audited; tool-call
  audit rows name the application and connection.
- Migration `001381_mcp_oauth`.
- **Upgrade note:** the gateway sends `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`
  and `/oauth/authorize`, `/oauth/token`, `/oauth/revoke` to the API; update a
  custom reverse proxy the same way. `APP_URL` must be the public `https`
  origin. `oct_` keys keep working.

### Added: find your pentest campaigns and your work from an AI client

- New MCP tools `list_campaigns` and `my_work` (permission `pentest:campaigns:read`, pentest module). `list_campaigns` lists the campaigns you are a member of with your role, the phase, TLP, dates, finding counts and the next action for your role; filters `phase`, `role`, `search`, `include_archived`; paged. `my_work` lists your active campaigns that need something from you: drafts, findings assigned to you, reviews, retests, or for a client the published findings still open.
- Membership is a SQL filter: a tenant administrator who is not a member sees none of a campaign. A client gets published counts only.

### Added: AI applications can add finding comments, each confirmed by you

- First MCP write tool, `add_finding_comment` (scope `mcp:findings.comment`,
  permission `findings:comment`): an internal comment, never sent to
  integrations (RFC-062).
- Nothing changes until the person who connected the application confirms
  the exact comment in OpenCTEM at `/mcp/confirm/<id>`; the confirmation is
  bound to the connection, the tool and the arguments, lasts five minutes
  and is used once. API keys cannot run write tools.
- Write scopes are off by default: an organization enables them by listing
  `mcp:findings.comment` in its MCP policy. Applications ask for the scope
  only when they need it (`insufficient_scope` step-up).
- Audited: `mcp_action.requested`, `mcp_action.confirmed`,
  `mcp_action.refused`. Migration `001487_mcp_action_confirmations`.

### Added: `repomerge` merges duplicate repository assets

- One repository could be two assets: repository import named it `org/repo` and CI `github.com/org/repo`, or
  a rename or transfer made CI create a second asset while the first kept the findings, branches, gate policy
  and coverage expectation. `repomerge` (in the API image as `/app/repomerge`) finds such groups per tenant
  (same repository id on the same host, `host/path` with `path` on that host, a CI pipeline whose runs are on
  another asset) and merges each into its oldest asset through the asset merge: findings, branches, baseline,
  gate policy, expectations, pipelines and runs move; the kept asset takes the current `host/path` name.
- **Upgrade note:** run `repomerge` (a read-only dry run printing aggregate counts), then `repomerge -apply`.
  It is idempotent and tenant-scoped; no migration.

### Added: count discovered assets in metrics on request

- Dashboards, attack-surface counts and the EASM summary and change feed count the attributed inventory by default; `include_discovered=true` on `/dashboard/*`, `/attack-surface/*`, `/easm/summary` and `/easm/changes` counts discovered assets too (RFC-054 §15.6). It changes counts only.
- The Attack surface overview has an "Include discovered assets" switch and shows how many discovered assets are passive only.

### Added: 30 days of read-only access after losing a module

- When an organization loses a module (its plan changes, the plan's modules are narrowed, a
  platform administrator denies it, or a trial grant expires), it keeps read access for 30
  days: pages and GET exports work, changes are refused with `MODULE_NOT_ENABLED` reason
  `read_only_grace`, and the module's jobs, automations and MCP tools stop at once. The
  module's pages show "Read-only until <date>", Settings > Modules shows the same badge, and
  Console > Organizations > Plan > Modules lists it as "Read-only" with the end date.
- Getting the module back ends the grace; after 30 days it is off (`not_entitled`). Data is
  never deleted.
- Migration 001969 adds `tenant_module_grace`.

### Added: modules per plan, with grants for trials and add-ons

- A plan now decides which modules its organizations may use: Console > System > Plans >
  Plan modules (super admin, fresh authenticator code). Until it is saved every plan
  includes every module, so nothing changes on upgrade.
- One organization can be granted a module beyond its plan (a trial with an expiry, an
  add-on) or denied one: Console > Organizations > Plan > Modules (ops admin and up; granting,
  denying and removing each need a reason and a fresh authenticator code; admin audit log). Changes, and a change of plan, apply at once on every API
  replica.
- An organization cannot switch on a module its plan does not include; Settings > Modules
  shows it as "Not in your plan". A page of such a module says so, and
  `MODULE_NOT_ENABLED` carries reason `not_entitled`. If the entitlement cannot be read, the
  gate answers 503 rather than opening (fail-closed).
- Migration 001968 adds `tenant_module_grants`.

### Added: network devices are matched by address within the organization

- A reported network device (network asset of a device sub-type: firewall, router, switch, load balancer, VPN gateway, wireless controller, access point, IDS/IPS) that no identifier or exact name matched is matched to the organization's existing network device that is named by or records one of its addresses, so a device that one collector names by its hostname and another by its management address is one asset.
- The IP trust window of host matching applies; two devices with the address are ambiguous (no match, a dedup review). Segments (subnets, VLANs, …) and hosts or address assets are never matched this way, and the lookup is scoped to the organization.

### Added: New Scan review step

- New Scan ends with a Review step: what runs, the targets and their scope verdict, where it runs, when (with the next runs), the workflow preview and the zone routing, each with an Edit link. Start is disabled with the reason while a target is refused, a workflow step cannot start or something is missing; Remove them drops refused targets in one click.
- Schedule offers Save without running: the scan is saved and started later from its page.

### Added: opengrep as a SAST tool

- `opengrep` is a known built-in tool. It has a platform tools row (migration `opengrep_tool`), it is an implementation of the `sast.code` stage next to semgrep (semgrep stays the default), it takes capability jobs, it counts as passive in scan intensity, and its findings are classified as SAST even when a report names no capability.
- Findings carry over from semgrep: a finding a semgrep run stored is the finding the first opengrep run of the same rules reports, with the same row and triage, re-keyed to the version-2 identity. Integration test `sast_engine_change_test.go`; this needs sensors and ci reporting with the ctis `opengrep` format.
- Scan profile tool choices list Opengrep. Their descriptions are translated (en, vi); the unused `TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS` export is removed.

### Added: operator metrics for alerting on the running platform

- `/metrics` (token-gated by `METRICS_TOKEN`, never routed by the gateway) now also reports:
  `openctem_panics_recovered_total{where}`, `openctem_log_records_total{level,component}` (WARN/ERROR,
  counted before sampling), `openctem_auth_login_failures_total{reason}`,
  `openctem_automation_runs_total{status}`, `openctem_automations_auto_paused_total`,
  platform-wide gauges (`openctem_sensors{kind,health}`, `openctem_sensors_config_health`,
  `openctem_sensors_sdk`, `openctem_commands{state}`, `openctem_command_oldest_pending_seconds`,
  `openctem_scan_runs_open`, `openctem_scan_runs_past_deadline`, `openctem_outbox_entries{status}`,
  `openctem_outbox_oldest_pending_seconds`, `openctem_schema_version{source}`, `openctem_schema_dirty`,
  `openctem_build_info`, `openctem_ops_collector_up`) and the connection pool (`go_sql_*`).
- The platform-wide gauges are read with a few aggregate queries at most every 30 seconds, whatever the
  scrape rate. Labels carry no tenant, user, sensor or run identity.

### Added: operator monitoring stack with Telegram and Slack alerts

- `deploy/observability/`: a compose profile (`observability`) with Prometheus, Alertmanager,
  node-exporter, cAdvisor, the Postgres and Redis exporters and synthetic probes, plus optional Grafana
  (`grafana` profile) with an overview dashboard. It joins the stack's network and publishes nothing on a
  public interface.
- About 50 alert rules (API and web availability, 5xx rate, latency, panics, error log bursts, schema
  behind/dirty, sensors offline or impaired, stuck command queue and scan runs, ingest and outbox lag,
  automation auto-pauses, audit chain breaks, login failure spikes, rate-limit spikes, Postgres, Redis,
  disk, memory, OOM kills, container restarts, TLS expiry, backups), each with a runbook in
  `docs/operations/monitoring.md`, routed to Telegram and/or Slack with grouping, inhibition and resolved
  messages.
- The Postgres exporter connects as a `pg_monitor`-only role (`deploy/observability/postgres/monitor-role.sql`).
- **Upgrade note:** to use it, set `METRICS_TOKEN` on the API, create the monitor role and follow
  "Install (Docker Compose)" in `docs/operations/monitoring.md`. Nothing changes for installs that do not.

### Added: the organization's layer of its scan tools' HTTP settings (RFC-060 §4.1)

- Settings > Security can set a User-Agent for the organization's scan tools (`tool_http_user_agent`) and refuse tools that skip TLS verification (`forbid_tool_insecure_tls`).
- The platform puts them in every scan job it hands a sensor (`http_policy`), as they are at delivery. It replaces any value a command's creator set.
- They only narrow: the sensor's local policy decides first (sdk-go `core.OrgHTTPPolicy`).
- Allowing insecure TLS again is audited at high severity.
- A delivery fails (fail closed) when the organization's policy cannot be read.
- Sensors before the matching sdk-go release ignore the field.

### Added: how-to for marking things out of scope and how it reaches sensors

- `api/docs/how-to/mark-out-of-scope.md`: exclusions, "Not ours", entries and
  archive compared; exclusion kinds; the six places an exclusion is enforced
  (dispatch gate and range cut, `payload.exclusions`, `web_scope` deny paths,
  the claim-time re-check, the signer ledger, ingest); what unclassified
  assets get; where to see what was left out.

### Added: Transfer ownership on the Members page

- The owner picks "Transfer ownership..." on a member's row. A dialog shows whether the member qualifies (active, two-factor on, not managed by another organization), lets the owner choose what they become, and asks for confirmation when an outside member would become internal.
- While a transfer is open, the owner sees who was asked and can cancel it. The member asked sees what changes and can accept (after signing in again) or decline. English and Vietnamese.

### Added: transfer ownership of an organization

- The owner can hand the organization to an existing member: `POST /api/v1/organization/ownership-transfer` (owner, step-up). The member must be an active person with two-factor authentication on and not managed by another organization; an outside member nobody manages becomes internal after the owner confirms it. The owner chooses what they become (administrator by default, or member or viewer).
- The member accepts with their own step-up within 72 hours (`POST .../approve`) or declines (`POST .../reject`); the owner can cancel (`DELETE`). Acceptance re-checks everything in one transaction and ends with exactly one owner. Both people are emailed at each step; the audit log records the request, the transfer (critical), cancellations and declines.
- The error for changing the owner's role now points to Transfer ownership.
- Migration `002206` adds the `tenant_ownership_transfers` table (new and empty; no operator step).

### Added: passive discovery and continuous-discovery building blocks

- Two starter workflows (migration `passive_discovery_workflows`): **Passive
  discovery** (subdomains from passive sources, then DNS through recursive
  resolvers; nothing sent to the target hosts) and **Probe new assets** (port
  scan and HTTP probe, no discovery step) (RFC-071).
- `target_options.new_since_last_run`: a `*.example.com` selector takes only
  the assets that came into scope since the scan's previous successful run
  (attribution confirmed since then, or first seen since then without a
  record); never needs_review, candidate or rejected names. The first run
  takes every such asset.

### Added: passive RDAP and ASN lookups in the Passive discovery workflow

- New T0 scan stages `lookup.rdap` (registrar, registrant organization, name servers and registration dates of a root domain, from its registry's RDAP service) and `lookup.asn` (origin autonomous system, holder and announced range of an address or network, from the public-domain IPtoASN dataset), run by the sensor's built-in `rdap` and `asn` tools. Both declare the `egress-proxy` network: they never send anything to the target hosts, so a passive scan may run them.
- Migration `001967_passive_lookup_tools`: platform tool rows `rdap` and `asn`, and two steps in the "Passive discovery" starter template (RDAP lookup of the roots, ASN lookup of the resolved addresses; template version 2). Tenant copies made earlier keep their steps.
- A network a sensor report creates (the ranges an autonomous system announces) gets an attribution record like an internet-facing name: needs_review from a scan, candidate from an unsolicited report. Existing networks are unchanged.
- `rdap` and `asn` are built-in sensor tools for the tool-trust check.
- ctis is pinned to the commit with `lookup.rdap@1` and `lookup.asn@1`.
- **Upgrade note:** needs a sensor with the `rdap` and `asn` tools (sensor PR "passive rdap and asn tools"). Until a sensor that has them is online, the two new steps of a Passive discovery run wait and then time out; the other steps run as before.

### Added: upload the pentest campaign's authorization letter from the console

- The campaign lead uploads or replaces the signed authorization letter on the
  campaign's Engagement card, in the creation wizard (Scope and rules) and in
  the dialog Start opens when the organization requires a letter and none is
  linked. Members download it; clients do not see it.
- The letter must be a PDF, PNG or JPEG file (type sniffed at upload);
  linking another type answers 400.
- Campaign responses carry `authorization_required` (the organization's
  "require an authorization letter to start" setting).

### Added: checks and an optional sign-off before a pentest campaign is completed

- Completing a pentest campaign is refused (409) while findings are still in
  draft or in review, unless the caller gives a reason (`override_reason`,
  audited with high severity). Before, those findings silently never reached
  the client.
- Optional completion sign-off policy per campaign: how many distinct
  members, holding one of the listed campaign roles (lead, reviewer,
  client), must sign off before the campaign can be completed. Off by
  default. Set at creation or with
  `PUT /api/v1/pentest/campaigns/{id}/completion-policy`; members sign off
  with `POST /api/v1/pentest/campaigns/{id}/signoff` (withdraw with
  `DELETE`). A lead cannot weaken the policy once testing has started; only
  an organization owner or admin can, and only they can complete without the
  sign-offs (with a reason). Reopening clears the sign-offs. Every sign-off,
  withdrawal, policy change and override is audited.
- `GET /api/v1/pentest/campaigns/{id}/completion` shows what completing
  would leave behind (draft, in-review and open findings, reports, sign-offs).
- Migration `002053_pentest_completion_signoff` adds the policy columns and
  the `pentest_campaign_signoffs` table.
- Design: RFC-085.

### Added: pentest test-credentials vault and ticket links (Jira epic)

- Campaigns store test credentials encrypted with the application key: the
  list shows labels only; revealing one is a separate call for campaign
  leads, testers and reviewers who are members, audited with high severity
  and recorded on the credential. Archiving the campaign deletes them.
  Endpoints under `/api/v1/pentest/campaigns/{id}/secrets`. `cmd/rekey`
  re-encrypts them on key rotation.
- Campaigns carry up to five ticket links (`PUT /api/v1/pentest/campaigns/{id}/links`):
  https only, no credentials, query and fragment dropped; Jira links must be
  issue links on the organization's connected Jira site.
- With Jira connected, the lead searches issues
  (`GET .../jira/issues?q=`) and creates tickets for the campaign's open
  published findings as children of the linked epic (`POST .../jira/tickets`).
- Migration `002056_pentest_campaign_vault_refs` adds `pentest_campaign_secrets`
  and `pentest_campaigns.external_refs`.
- Design: RFC-086.
- Console: the campaign overview shows "Test credentials" (team only: add,
  reveal for 30 seconds with copy, delete) and "Tickets" (link chips in the
  header; the lead searches Jira, adds links and creates tickets under the
  epic). English and Vietnamese.

### Added: organization methodology checklists for pentest campaigns

- Checklist templates are organization data (RFC-087): built-in templates (OWASP WSTG 4.2, OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 Level 1 and Level 2, OWASP API Security Top 10 2023, OWASP MASVS 2.1.0, PTES phases, a cloud configuration baseline, and the 38-item OWASP Top 10 web checklist campaigns used until now) and the organization's own: create, clone, edit with versions, archive.
- Import and export as CSV, JSON or YAML (`/api/v1/pentest/checklist-templates`), with a sample file, row-level validation errors, a dry run, a 2 MiB limit and formula-safe CSV export.
- A campaign runs one or more checklists, by default, for each of its target types (RFC-086), the organization's templates for that target or the built-in default; the lead adds, removes and upgrades them (with a diff), and the lead and testers record results, notes, assignees, linked findings and evidence links, one item or many at once (`/api/v1/pentest/campaigns/{id}/checklists`).
- Reports: checklist coverage in the HTML and PDF reports and new tags for organization report templates (`checklists`, `checklist_summary`, `checklist_sections`, `checklist_failed_items`).
- New permission `pentest:checklists:manage` (owners and admins) manages templates.
- Migration `002057_pentest_checklists` moves each campaign's `metadata.checklist` results into a checklist of the built-in `owasp-top10-web-2021` template and removes the metadata key; its down migration puts them back.

### Added: methodology checklists in the web console

- Settings > Pentest methodology > Checklists: browse built-in and organization checklist templates, view and export them, and (with `pentest:checklists:manage`) create, clone, edit, import with row-level problem lists and sample files, and archive.
- The New campaign dialog preselects the checklists for the campaign type.
- The campaign Checklist tab runs every checklist of the campaign: progress per checklist and section, search and filters, results, notes, assignees, linked findings, evidence links, bulk changes, a draft finding from a failed item, and add, remove and upgrade (with a diff) for the lead. The fixed 38-item list defined in the console is gone.

### Added: a client role on pentest campaigns

- A campaign member can now have the `client` role: the tested
  organization's people read the campaign, its team and its published
  findings, read-only. They never see drafts or findings in peer review on
  any surface (campaign findings, pentest findings list, generic findings
  list and groups, single reads, retests, evidence), and get no stats,
  finding counts, exports, reports, campaign attachments or report-writing
  tools. Clients cannot be assigned findings. The console offers the role
  when adding or changing a member and shows clients a notice.

### Added: Word reports from organization templates embed evidence screenshots

- Markdown values rendered through `{@…}` in an organization's Word template
  now embed the screenshots a finding cites when they are evidence of that
  finding or its campaign (same rules and limits as the HTML and PDF
  reports), scaled to at most 6 inches wide. Other images show their alt
  text; the template's own parts stay untouched.

### Added: pentest findings stay fixable and retestable after testing is complete

- A completed pentest campaign keeps remediation open: findings can move
  between published statuses (in progress, fix applied, resolved, reopened,
  accepted, false positive) and retests can be recorded, without reopening
  the campaign. New findings, edits, deletions and draft/review moves stay
  locked; canceled and archived campaigns refuse both.
- `POST /api/v1/pentest/findings/{id}/request-retest` marks a
  published finding as fixed and ready for retest. Allowed for the campaign
  lead, reviewer, client, and the tester who owns the finding; recorded on
  the finding timeline and in the audit log; the assignee and author are
  notified.
- Each pentest retest keeps the finding status before and after it
  (`prior_status`, `result_status`). Migration `002052_pentest_retest_status_change`
  adds the two columns; retests recorded earlier have neither.
- Fixed: submitting a pentest retest silently dropped its timeline entry
  (the activity type was not an allowed value); it is now recorded as
  `retest_completed`.
- Design: RFC-085.

### Added: pentest reports render finding Markdown and embed evidence screenshots

- HTML and PDF reports render the Markdown findings are written in
  (paragraphs, lists, code blocks, bold, italic, links) instead of printing
  it raw. All text is escaped; only http(s) and mailto links are kept.
- Screenshots a finding references from its evidence are embedded in the
  report. An image is embedded only when it is evidence of that finding (or
  its retests or campaign) in the same organization and a real PNG, JPEG or
  GIF within the size limits; anything else shows its alt text. The report
  option `include_evidence=false` leaves images out.

### Added: organizations can render pentest reports through their own Word template

- Owners and admins upload a .docx report template
  (`POST /api/v1/pentest/report-templates`), written in Word with a small tag
  language: values (`{campaign.name}`), loops and conditions
  (`{#findings}…{/findings}`, `{^findings}…{/findings}`), Markdown blocks
  (`{@description}`) and list items (`{.}`). Tags may sit in paragraphs, table
  rows or inline; tags Word splits across runs are handled.
- The upload is checked: macro-enabled files, VBA projects, ActiveX,
  embedded objects, external links other than hyperlinks, DOCTYPE/ENTITY
  declarations, unsafe part names, oversized or zip-bomb files and misplaced
  tags are refused with a message; tags the report data does not have are
  returned as warnings. At most 20 templates per organization.
- A template can be previewed with fictional sample data, and a starter
  template is downloadable. A campaign report with `format: "docx"` and
  `options.template_id` renders through the template (labels in English or
  Vietnamese, as the template declares). Uploads and deletions are audited.
- Templates are stored in the organization's rows (migration
  `pentest_report_templates`) and erased with the organization; another
  organization's template answers 404 everywhere. Design: RFC-076; reference:
  `api/docs/architecture/pentest-report-templates.md`.

### Added: pentest duplicates and inconclusive retests

- The lead or a reviewer marks a draft or in-review finding as a duplicate of another finding of the same campaign: `PATCH /api/v1/pentest/findings/{id}/status` `{"status":"duplicate","duplicate_of":"<id>"}`; `{"status":"draft"}` undoes it. Finding responses carry `duplicate_of`.
- Retest result `inconclusive` (unable to verify) with a reason in the notes; the finding stays fix applied.
- Report templates: `campaign.status` can be `reporting`, new `campaign.status_label`, retest `status_label` for `inconclusive` (en, vi).

### Added: pentest console asks before status changes, shows completion checks and sign-offs, and lets clients request retests

- Every campaign status change that is not routine asks first (put on hold,
  complete, reopen, archive, cancel). Completing shows the checks: findings
  left in draft or review (a reason is needed to complete anyway), sign-offs
  n of N with names, open findings that stay in remediation, reports
  generated and delivered. Refusals show the API's reason instead of a
  generic error.
- Status actions show only for the campaign lead and organization admins.
  A completed campaign can be reopened from its page.
- Campaign pages show a "testing complete, remediation open" banner and a
  completion sign-off card (sign off, withdraw, the lead's policy editor);
  the create dialog sets the sign-off policy.
- "Request retest" on a finding (client, lead, reviewer, the tester who owns
  it) and as a bulk action on the findings list. On a completed campaign,
  retests and remediation status changes stay available.
- Retest history shows the finding status before and after each retest.
- English and Vietnamese text for all of the above.

### Added: a settings panel for each step in the pipeline builder

- Clicking a step opens its settings: the capability (with its versioned id and tier), how it picks its tool (any tool, preferred tools in order, or one tool), the capability's standard settings, retries and timeout.
- The settings form is built from the capability contract served by `GET /api/v1/scans/stages`, so only the contract's settings can be entered. Values are checked as you type (types, allowed values, bounds, port lists), and the panel names the tools that cannot run the step with its settings.
- A step whose tool has no capability contract says so and keeps its own settings.
- The unused step edit panel is removed.

### Added: typed connections in the pipeline builder

- Each step in the pipeline builder shows its capability, its tier and the port types it takes and gives, as served by `GET /api/v1/scans/stages`. A step without a contract (a tenant tool) says that it runs on the scan's targets and takes no data from earlier steps.
- Dragging a connection checks it as you drop. Incompatible ports, a loop, and derived targets into an intrusive (T2) step are refused with a plain reason. When the catalog has an adapter, the message offers **Insert step**, which adds the adapter step (for example an HTTP probe between subdomain discovery and a web crawl) and rewires the two.
- The builder checks the draft with `POST /api/v1/pipelines/verify` while you edit. It shows each problem on its step and blocks Save while the workflow has errors. A save the API refuses shows its issues on the steps.
- The connection rules and typed handles live in a shared `components/flow` kit for both canvases.

### Added: pipeline steps pick their tool by capability (auto, prefer, pin)

- A pipeline step names a capability and picks its tool in one of three ways. **auto** takes any implementation, with the catalog default first. **prefer** (`prefer_tools`) tries an ordered list. **pin** (`tool`) runs one tool only. Each tool in a prefer list must implement the step's capability, and a step cannot both pin a tool and list tools to prefer. Migration 001176 adds `pipeline_steps.prefer_tools`.
- Step settings follow the capability contract. Standard params are checked against their type, allowed values and bounds on every save, and each tool receives them under its own config key (for example naabu's `top_ports` for `top_n`). A tool that does not take a param the step sets is skipped, with the reason, so the value is never dropped silently. A pinned tool's own settings go under `x.<tool>`, or as plain keys on a pinned step.
- A queued step run records the capability it ran (`step_runs.capability`, for example `scan.ports@1`) and the tool the planner picked.
- The API adds `prefer_tools` and `tool_selection` on steps, and `capability` on step runs.

### Added: a queued scan task says why it waits

- `GET /api/v1/scan-runs/{id}/tasks/{task_id}/placement` (`scans:read`) explains a queued task: what holds it whatever the sensor (scan window, busy host, expired), how many of the organization's sensors may take it and how many of those are busy, and each reason that keeps it from the others (zone, tool, capability, grant, intensity, local policy, private targets, opt-ins, refusals). Callers who also have `sensors:read` get each sensor's verdict; platform scanning is never broken down into sensors.
- The explanation reads the claim's own SQL predicates and dispatch gate, and a database test keeps it in agreement with the poll. Details in `docs/architecture/placement.md`.

### Added: a findings plan limit

- New plan limit `findings` (Console > System > Plans, and per organization
  in Console > Organizations > Plan). Unlimited on every plan by default; an
  operator sets it to stop one organization's sensors from growing the shared
  database without bound.
- Ingest admits new findings up to the limit and refuses each one over it
  with a per-item error; assets, the other findings and re-sightings of
  existing findings are still stored. Manual create and import answer 403
  `PLAN_LIMIT`.
- Findings are counted only while a findings limit applies, and a check of
  any unlimited key no longer counts usage, so organizations without the
  limit pay nothing for it. No migration.

### Added: plans and limits for organizations

- Organizations are on a plan (Free, Pro, Enterprise) that caps members, assets, sensors, API keys, CI trusts and invitations a day. Platform administrators edit the plan defaults in Console > System > Plans (super admin, fresh authenticator code, audited critical, other administrators emailed) and set per-organization overrides with a reason and an optional expiry (ops_admin+, audited).
- Lowering a limit never removes anything; new additions over it are refused with 403 `PLAN_LIMIT` and the organization is flagged over limit. Refusals are counted in `openctem_plan_limit_refusals_total`.
- A self-service organization starts on Free; one person owns at most one Free organization by default. Organizations created before this change are Enterprise (no limits). Migration 001325 (two new, empty tables).
- Organization owners and admins see the plan and usage at `GET /api/v1/organization/plan`.

### Added: plan limits enforced on every creation path

- Members (invitation accept, SSO and federated sign-up, SCIM, administrator-created users), invitations a day, assets (create and ingest), sensors (create, registration, pairing), API keys and CI trusts are checked against the organization's plan when the row is inserted. Over the limit: 403 `PLAN_LIMIT` with what the plan allows and what is used.
- Ingest over the asset limit refuses the whole batch with that error and counts it in `openctem_plan_limit_refusals_total`; assets that already exist are always updated.
- Organizations without a plan (all organizations created before plans) are unaffected.

### Added: plan pages in the console and in organization settings

- Console > System > Plans edits the plan defaults (super admin, authenticator code). Console > Organizations > Plan changes an organization's plan and sets per-organization limits, with an over-limit badge.
- Settings > Organization > Plan & usage shows owners and admins their plan, what they use and what is allowed (English and Vietnamese).

### Added: platform content packs with stable and canary channels (RFC-061 K2)

- `/api/v1/admin/content-packs`:
  - a super admin uploads a pack, or imports an upstream release by https URL with its required sha256 (checked before parsing, fetched through the SSRF guard);
  - revokes a pack;
  - points the `stable` or `canary` channel of a name at a pack.

  Any admin reads. Every write needs a reason and a fresh console authenticator code (`totp_code`) and is audited with the reason.
- Platform packs are signed with the platform content key, kept apart from organization packs (migration 001568), and readable by every organization at `/api/v1/platform-content-packs` (`scans:content:read`).
- Upstream lint leaves out the files that fail it instead of refusing the release:
  - refused template protocols, self-contained templates, unsafe regexes and non-template YAML are left out;
  - templates with attack payloads in their requests are kept as T2.
- Revoking a pack moves its channels back to the previous good pack.

### Added: private bug-bounty programs

- A program can be entered by hand or imported from a file: the platform CSV export, a Burp Suite target scope (JSON) or any CSV with a column mapping. The link to the program is optional. A Burp host expression becomes a scope entry only when it names exactly one host or one domain and its subdomains; anything wider is shown and never imported. RFC-065 §15.
- Programs are private by default. A private program, its scope, rules and terms are visible only to its members and the organization owners (others get 404), and each person accepts its terms and confidentiality before seeing them (`POST /api/v1/programs/{id}/attest`); changed terms ask everyone again. Every view of a private program is audited, and the scope list leaves out the entries of private programs the caller may not see.

### Added: bug-bounty program assets are kept apart from the organization's own

- Assets a bug-bounty program lists or covers are linked to it (`asset_program_links`, source programfeed, program-manual or program-import) and carry system tags the platform derives (`bug-bounty`, `source:…`, `platform:…`, `program:<platform>:<slug>`, `program-unattested`); no request can change them. RFC-065 §16.5.
- An asset the organization already had stays its own and only gains the link; an asset that came after the program and that no own scope entry covers is program-only. Dashboards and CTEM program metrics leave program-only assets and their findings out by default (`include_program_assets=true` includes them).
- The inventory gets a "Bug bounty" view (`program_assets=only|exclude`); tag filters also match system tags; the asset page shows a "Program target" badge with the program and whether its terms are accepted.

### Added: more CTEM program metrics on Program Health

- `GET /api/v1/dashboard/program-metrics` (and Insights > Program Health)
  adds four metrics computed from data the platform already stores, each
  tenant-scoped, with `null` (shown as "—") when there is no sample:
  - `mttv`: time from detection to the first conclusive validation of P0/P1
    findings, with the count still waiting for validation;
  - `time_to_owner_internet_facing`: time from discovery to the first owner of
    new internet-facing assets, with the count still without an owner;
  - `cycle_completion`: CTEM cycles closed by their end date, and the mean
    charter success-criteria completion at close;
  - `control_coverage`: critical and crown-jewel assets whose EDR, MFA or
    logging attribute is false or not recorded (a snapshot of the inventory).
- Program Health metric texts are translated (en, vi). No migration.

### Added: programs sync their scope from the program source (RFC-065)

- `PUT /api/v1/programs/{id}/source` (step-up): `program_api` reads the researcher API of the platform that runs the program (HackerOne structured scopes, with your own API token, encrypted and never returned) and `program_file` reads a scope file the program publishes over https on its own domain. Migration 001610.
- `POST /api/v1/programs/{id}/sync` and a controller every 6 hours read the source through the outbound guard. What the source removes stops at once; new out-of-scope items become program exclusions; what it adds waits as pending terms until a member accepts them (`GET /pending`, `POST /pending/apply` with step-up). A closed or vanished program is suspended. Syncs that narrow or suspend are audited (`bounty_program.synced`).

### Added: program targets go through the standard asset ingest

- Every time a bug-bounty program scope is applied, its in-scope targets are ingested as assets of the program organization through the standard CTIS ingest: names, addresses and networks, a host and a service asset per listed port, a web application or API for a URL with a path, mobile apps and repositories (which no entry covers and which are never scanned). Executables, hardware, smart contracts and AI models stay program targets without an asset.
- Followed public programs ingest with source kind feed (run = feed sequence, observed at the record last change); imported and pasted programs with source kind import. Dedup, attribute reconciliation and the change timeline apply; an identical re-import writes nothing. The report opens no exposure.
- Migration 001970 records which assets are a program targets (bounty_program_target_assets); they count as program assets for links, system tags and the program group data scope.

### Added: per-target program qualifiers

- Program targets keep and show what the program says about each: bounty eligibility, maximum severity, environment, testing instructions, prerequisites and trust (published, listed by the platform, inferred). They never authorize anything.

### Added: web pages for letters of authorization, program sync and testing windows

- Scoping > Scope > **Letters**: upload a signed letter of authorization (PDF, PNG or JPEG, up to 10 MB, valid for at most two years), see whether each letter is in effect or ends soon, download it, and revoke it (scope approvers). RFC-065 §13.
- A program page shows its **scope source** (pasted, the platform researcher API, or a scope file on the program domain), the last sync and its error, and a **Sync now** button. The API token is write-only. RFC-065 §14.
- New scope found by a sync is shown for review and goes into effect only when someone accepts the new terms.
- The program form takes **testing windows**, one per line (`mon-fri 09:00-17:00 Europe/Paris`). RFC-065 §12.

### Added: Programs in the web console

- Scoping > Scope gains a **Programs** tab (shown with `attack_surface:programs:read`, so a researcher without scope access still finds it): the program list, an import page (details, rules, pasted scope or CSV, preview of what the import creates, attestation of the previewed terms) and a program page (attestation, rules, entries, program exclusions with overlaps with the organization own scope, re-import, suspend, reactivate, end). RFC-065.

### Added: follow public bug-bounty programs from a signed program feed

- The platform imports the signed public program feed (`PROGRAMFEED_DIR`, `PROGRAMFEED_ROOT_KEY_ID`) into a catalog: pinned root, key set never rolled back, newer sequence only, the delta only on top of the applied sequence, file hashes and sizes checked, every record validated. It never calls the bug-bounty platforms. RFC-065 §16.
- `GET /api/v1/programs/catalog` lists the catalog; `POST /api/v1/programs/subscriptions` follows a program: its entries are created inactive and nothing is scanned actively until a member accepts the terms (`POST /api/v1/programs/{id}/reactivate`).
- A feed target is never permission to test: only targets the program published become entries; targets the feed inferred are suggestions a member confirms (`POST /api/v1/programs/{id}/targets/approve`), which asks for a new acceptance.
- Feed changes reach followed programs: removals apply at once; new targets, changed rules or terms take the entries out of effect until the terms are accepted again (administrators are notified); a closed, paused or dropped program is suspended.
- An operator can import its own local-only program bundle (`PROGRAMFEED_LOCAL_BUNDLE_DIR`, output of `programfeed build --local-only`). It is off until a platform administrator enables it in the console with a reason and an authenticator code (audited); its records stay on the platform, keep their provenance, and every target is a suggestion until a follower confirms it.

### Added: the layer4 gateway image is published

- Releases publish `ghcr.io/openctemio/openctem-gateway` (the `api/deploy/gateway` Caddy with the layer4 module). With `OPENCTEM_SENSOR_GATEWAY=alpn` it lets sensors use gRPC with mutual TLS on port 443 next to the web UI; operators no longer build it themselves.

### Added: preview of a quick scan before it starts

- `POST /api/v1/scans/quick/preview` (`scans:write` and `scans:execute`) shows, per typed target, the known assets a wildcard or range covers, how many names the run would scan and how many it leaves out by reason, and a few sample names. It uses the run's own expansion and scope checks as the caller (tenant, data scope, exclusions, deny list, caps) and creates nothing. A wildcard with no known name carries an offer to run subdomain discovery on its apex.
- The Quick Scan dialog shows it under "Review selection", and words refused wildcards in user terms (English and Vietnamese).

### Added: accept remediation suggestions, and the opt-in auto-join rule

- Accept a suggestion as it is or edited first (title, findings to remove, other owners per partition, a
  tighter deadline): a new group creates the fix and one task per owner, a join adds the findings to the owner's
  task, a task route creates a task under the existing fix. Findings that closed or joined another task since
  are left out and reported; removed findings are not proposed for that fix again. Bulk accept up to 50
  suggestions at once.
- Auto-join, opt-in per fix and for exact fixes only (package upgrade, secret rotation): new findings with the
  fix's key join the owner's open or in-progress task without a suggestion, at most 200 a day; never into a task
  in verification; it never changes a finding's status. Turning it on needs access to every asset.
- API: `POST /api/v1/remediation/suggestions/{id}/approve`, `POST /api/v1/remediation/suggestions/approve`,
  `GET`/`PATCH /api/v1/remediation/actions/{id}`. Migration `remediation_action_auto_join`.

### Added: the Remediation console (fix plan, suggestions inbox, tasks, task detail)

- Remediation now opens on a **Fix plan** (tasks and suggestions ranked by risk left), with **Suggestions**
  (review inbox with "why" explanations, keyboard review and bulk accept), **Tasks** (saved views, table or board)
  and **Campaigns** (the former Remediation page, now at `/remediation/campaigns`).
- The task page shows the fix steps to copy, progress, the findings grouped by asset (a windowed list that stays
  fast with thousands of findings), and lets a person move findings (palette with compatibility warnings or drag
  and drop, with undo), split, mark the task fixed, hold or cancel it, and read its timeline.
- **Behaviour change:** campaign pages moved from `/remediation` and `/remediation/{id}` to
  `/remediation/campaigns` and `/remediation/campaigns/{id}`; old links are not redirected.
- The API's 409 answers for a finding already in another task and for a move that needs confirmation also carry
  `details.finding_ids` / `details.warnings`.

### Added: "Tracked in task" on findings

- The finding drawer and the finding page show the remediation task the finding is tracked in, with the task's
  state and deadline and a link to the task. Shown only to members who can read remediation tasks, and only for
  tasks inside their data scope.

### Added: mark a remediation task fixed; regressions open a linked task

- "Mark fixed" on a task claims the fix of each of its open findings: each goes to fix applied through the same
  rules as the findings list (a note, `findings:fix_apply`, the asset owner's own findings), and a proof-of-fix
  re-check is queued per finding. Nothing closes: each finding closes on its own evidence, and the task is done
  once every finding is closed and at least one was verified fixed. Findings not updated are listed with the
  reason. API: `POST /api/v1/remediation/tasks/{task_id}/resolve`.
- A finding that reopens after its task is done no longer reopens the task: it moves to a new task
  ("Regression: …", same fix and owner) linked to the done one.

### Added: the ticket comment hook for remediation task moves

- Moving findings between remediation tasks, splitting, merging and detaching now report each stored move to a
  tracker hook with the comment text for each task touched (finding counts and task titles only, never finding
  names). The task ticket integration posts these comments on the tasks' issues once it is connected.

### Added: move findings between remediation tasks, split and merge tasks

- Move findings from one task to another, or out of any task (back to the suggestions pool, not proposed for
  that fix again). A different fix, a different owner, a task in verification or emptying the source needs the
  person's confirmation (preview shows the warnings); a closed task, another organization or findings outside
  the caller's access are refused. An emptied task is archived with a note; every finding and both tasks record
  the move; versions guard concurrent changes, and the reverse move undoes it.
- Split some findings into a new task of the same fix (another owner if named); merge tasks of the same fix.
- API: `POST /api/v1/remediation/moves`, `POST /api/v1/remediation/moves/preview`,
  `POST /api/v1/remediation/tasks/{task_id}/splits`, `POST /api/v1/remediation/tasks/{task_id}/merges`.

### Added: a Tasks tab on My Work

- My Work has a Tasks tab: the open remediation tasks assigned to you or to one of your groups, earliest
  deadline first, with state, progress and deadline, and a link to the full Tasks list. Shown to members who can
  read remediation tasks. The My Work page is now translated (English, Vietnamese).

### Added: "Accept as owner" in the suggestions inbox

- Members without remediation write access see "Accept as owner" on suggestions that add findings to a task or
  create a task for an owner; the server accepts it only for their own tasks and assets.

### Added: asset owners accept their own remediation suggestions

- A member without `findings:remediation:write` can accept, as it is, a suggestion that adds findings to a task
  assigned to them (or to one of their groups) or creates a task for them, when every finding is in their data
  scope and on an asset they own as primary or secondary owner. Starting a new fix, editing a suggestion,
  leaving findings out and auto-join still need write access. The audit event records `as_owner`.
- `POST /api/v1/remediation/suggestions/{id}/approve` is now gated on `findings:remediation:read`; the service
  enforces the rest (403 otherwise).

### Added: remediation suggestions

- The platform proposes remediation groups from the remediation keys (one package upgrade, one leaked secret,
  one specific solution): one suggestion per fix, its findings split by the asset's primary owner, ranked by
  risk reduced. Nothing is created until a person accepts; a key that already has an action yields "join this
  task" or "new task for this owner" proposals instead.
- Lifecycle: dismiss with a reason (held until the suggestion changes materially), snooze (up to 180 days),
  reopen; suggestions expire when their findings close. At most 50 new suggestions are shown per organization
  per day; reviewers get one daily digest notification (event `remediation_suggestions_digest`).
- API `/api/v1/remediation/suggestions` (list, stats, run, get, members, snooze, reject, reopen) in the
  remediation module. A restricted member sees only their findings of a suggestion and may not decide on one
  with others. Design: RFC-098 §5. Migration `remediation_suggestions` (three new tables).

### Added: remediation tasks

- A remediation task groups the findings one fix closes, with one owner (a user and/or a group) and one
  deadline. Its state (open, in progress, verifying, done, closed without a verified fix, on hold, canceled,
  archived) is derived from its findings; it is done only when every finding is closed and at least one was
  verified fixed. The deadline is the earliest open finding's SLA deadline, tightened (never extended) by a
  manual deadline or the campaign's due date.
- A finding is the primary member of at most one active task and may be a related member of others; every
  change is on the task's timeline and the finding's activity.
- API: `/api/v1/remediation/tasks` (list, create, get, change, members, timeline) in the remediation module.
  A restricted member sees and changes tasks through their data scope only. Design: RFC-098.
- Every link from the new tables to a tenant row (finding, campaign, group, task) is a composite
  `(tenant_id, ...)` foreign key, so the schema refuses a cross-tenant link. Migration
  `findings_tenant_id_unique` builds the unique `(tenant_id, id)` index on findings it needs
  (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, the table stays writable).
- Migrations `remediation_tasks` (four new tables, plus a unique `(tenant_id, id)` on
  `remediation_campaigns`), `remediation_task_activity_type` and
  `remediation_task_activity_type_validate` (the finding activity CHECK re-added `NOT VALID`, then
  validated without blocking writes).

### Added: administrators are told when a renamed repository no longer matches its CI trust configuration

- When a repository is renamed on its code host and no CI trust configuration admits the new name, its uploads are refused. The organization's owners and administrators now get an in-app notification and an e-mail with the old and new name and a link to the trust settings. The trust configuration itself is never changed by the platform. One alert per repository and new name per day.

### Added: report template check, tag reference and three starter templates

- `POST /api/v1/pentest/report-templates/verify` lists every problem in a Word
  template without storing it, and `GET …/{id}/issues` re-checks a stored one:
  each issue names the part (body, header, footer) and the paragraph text and
  suggests the fix (the missing `{/x}`, the closest known tag for a typo, the
  loop an item field belongs in, `{@x}` for a Markdown field). Upload runs the
  same check and refuses a template with an error, saying how many problems
  there are.
- `GET /api/v1/pentest/report-templates/reference` answers every value a
  template can read (type, description in English or Vietnamese, example, tag
  to paste) and the sample data; it is generated from the same data model the
  renderer uses.
- Starter templates: `standard` (cover, table of contents, severity table,
  findings with evidence, remediation plan, appendix), `executive` (one page)
  and `technical` (one finding per page), with named Word styles and a header
  and footer; `GET …/starter?variant=`.
- New built-in labels for templates: `labels.contents`, `overview`,
  `appendix`, `methodology`, `team`, `name`, `role`, `client`, `contact`,
  `period`, `prepared_for`, `key_findings`, `no_key_findings`,
  `remediation_plan`, `details`, `reported`, `cvss`, `severity_ratings` and
  `<severity>_desc`.

### Added: report template help in the console

- Settings › Pentest methodology › Report templates has a searchable tag
  reference (click a tag to copy it, download the sample data as JSON), a
  choice of three starter templates and a link to the template guide.
- Picking a file to upload checks it at once and lists every problem with
  where it is and how to fix it; saving waits until the errors are fixed.
  Preview also re-checks the stored template.

### Added: an address in the review queue says why it waits and how to fix it

- An IP address (or a service on one) stays in review even when every name
  that resolves to it is in scope: names never grant their addresses
  (RFC-054 §4.3). Its row in `GET /api/v1/easm/candidates` now carries:
  - `resolved_from`: the in-scope names that resolve to it (within the
    caller's data scope);
  - `network`: the ASN and organization already held for it, whether it is
    shared CDN or cloud space, and whether the organization matches;
  - `hint: ip_needs_ip_entry`;
  - `fixes` the caller may take through the normal scope entry path: add the
    address, add the /24 or /48 around it (only when the ASN organization
    matches and the space is not shared), or, for a member, request a one-off
    entry. Shared CDN or cloud addresses get no fix.
- Evidence from a sensor shows the sensor's name (`source_label`) instead of
  its id; a platform sensor shows as "platform sensor", and another
  organization's sensor is never named.

### Added: review by rule for the attribution review queue

- `GET /api/v1/easm/candidates/suggestions` groups the pending review items
  into candidate scope rules: wildcards at each label level up to the
  registrable domain (`*.dev.example.com.vn`, `*.example.com.vn`; never a
  public suffix) and /24 or /48 address ranges (never shared, CDN or cloud
  provider space, which is listed for one-by-one review), with the items each
  covers, the items exclusions or rejections keep out, ownership hints and a
  strength (RFC-054 §6.7).
- `POST /api/v1/easm/candidates/rules/preview` shows exactly what an action
  would change; `POST /api/v1/easm/candidates/rules` applies it:
  `accept_rule` creates a scope entry through the normal path (guardrails,
  step-up, approvals, notification) and confirms the covered items once it is
  in effect; `accept_selected` confirms only the chosen items; `reject_rule`
  requests an exclusion and rejects the covered items. Every change is
  audited.

### Added: RFC-078 passkeys and account security notices (proposed)

- Design for passkeys (WebAuthn) as a second factor, as the step-up proof and
  as the platform-admin console factor (replacing its separate TOTP store),
  then passwordless sign-in; and for emails on a sign-in from a new device,
  2FA enabled, passkey added or removed, and API key created. Nothing is
  built yet.

### Added: versioned role templates with updates you review, and role summaries

- New templates: CI integrator, sensor operator, researcher and bug-bounty triager (16 in all). Each template has a version.
- `POST /api/v1/roles` takes `template_id`; the role records the template, its version and its permissions at that version. A later template change never changes the role: role responses show the difference (`template`), and `POST /api/v1/roles/{id}/template/apply` applies it within your own grants, keeping the role's own edits.
- Role and template responses carry `summary`: a risk tier (low, medium, high, critical), the reasons and what the role views or changes per area, so the console no longer shows a bare permission count.

### Added: role templates for the people in a CTEM program

- `GET /api/v1/roles/templates` (`team:roles:read`) lists twelve starting
  points for a custom role: program lead, security analyst, vulnerability
  manager, remediation owner, AppSec engineer, scan operator, validation
  engineer, external tester, threat intelligence analyst, risk approver,
  auditor and executive viewer.
- A template grants nothing. A role is created from it with the usual
  `POST /api/v1/roles`, so the grant ceiling applies: nobody can build a role
  above their own permissions. Tests keep separation of duties (the requester
  never approves, the fixer never verifies, the scope writer never approves).

### Added: coverage gaps on scan run tasks

- A sensor that could not fully cover some hosts of a task (the host stopped
  answering and its breaker gave it up, it kept rate-limiting the scan at the
  lowest rate, or it blocked the scan; RFC-074) reports them in the command
  result (`coverage_gaps`, `coverage_gaps_total`). The task completes, the
  step and the run end partial with code `COVERAGE_GAPS`, and the run's task
  list shows the hosts and the reason, so such a host is no longer read as
  "no findings". Batched steps count the gaps of every completed batch.
- The list is sensor-supplied: parsed defensively, unknown reasons dropped,
  at most 20 entries per task, every string cleaned to one bounded line;
  a platform sensor's detail text is redacted as its other messages are.

### Added: a run's tasks count the targets the sensor's confinement could not reach

- A run task's `egress_refused_targets` counts the targets of a completed task that its sensor's network confinement kept the tool from reaching (ctis outcome `failed` with class `egress_refused`). The run page shows "could not reach N targets" for them instead of "produced nothing". The count comes from the sensor, is read only for completed tasks, and is never more than the task's own targets.
- ctis is updated so the platform accepts the `egress_refused` class: such a target is settled, not handed out again as unfinished.

### Added: a timeline for every run

- Each change of a sensor task (queued, claimed, started, refused, requeued,
  completed, failed, canceled, expired) is recorded with its attempt number,
  its sensor and the reason. A trigger on `commands` writes the record, so
  every writer is covered. Migration `001305` (`command_events`). Records are
  kept 30 days by the `command-event-retention` controller.
- `GET /api/v1/scan-runs/{id}/events` returns a run's timeline, oldest first,
  at most 2000 records. It needs `scans:read`, and a retest run also needs the
  finding to be readable. A platform scanning task never names its sensor, and
  its text is masked.

### Added: runs and the scan preview say which exclusions left targets out

- A scan run records the targets its organization's exclusions left out
  (whole, or a range scanned without its excluded addresses) with the
  matching exclusion, up to 50; `GET /scan-runs/{id}` returns them as
  `dispatch.excluded` and the scan preview as `targets.excluded_detail`. The
  run page and the preview list them as "N targets left out by exclusions"
  with links to Scoping > Out of scope.

### Added: a run step says how many targets the sensor's target guard refused

- A run task's `guard_refused_targets` counts the targets its sensor's target guard refused and never ran (a blocked or unresolvable address, an unsafe target): the entries of the result's `refused_targets` with rule `target_guard`. The sensor refuses per target, so one bad target no longer fails the task; the run page says "N targets refused by the sensor's target guard" on the step instead. The count comes from the sensor and is never more than the task's own targets.

### Added: a run's live map

- `GET /scan-runs/{id}/map` (`scans:read`) returns the run drawn on the
  workflow version it executes: each step's state (pending, waiting for a
  sensor, running, succeeded, partial, failed, skipped, canceled) with its
  reason and error class, chunks by state, findings, planned inputs and
  outputs by asset type, and each dependency with what the upstream step
  produced. Output counts cover only the assets the caller may see; a run
  of another organization, or a retest of a finding outside the caller's
  scope, is not found.

### Added: the run map compares with the previous run

- Each step on the run map shows what is new and what is gone compared with
  the previous finished run of the same scan, and the map warns about a
  finished step that produced nothing (no asset and no finding).
- Opening a step lists what it produced, new ones first:
  `GET /api/v1/scan-runs/{id}/outputs?step_key=` (`scans:read`, up
  to 50 assets, only those in the viewer's data scope).

### Added: the run map updates live

- A run that changes (a step started, finished or was queued, the run
  settled or was canceled) tells the run page over the websocket channel
  `run:{id}`, at most once a second; the page refreshes the map, the run and
  its tasks at once instead of on its next poll. Subscribing needs
  `scans:read` and a run the viewer may read (a retest also needs its
  finding in the viewer's scope); the notice carries no data.

### Added: a step panel on the run map

- Clicking a step of the run map opens its panel: its state and why it
  waits or failed, its error, what it produced by asset type and its own
  tasks, each with its logs. Clicking the step again closes it.

### Added: the run map on the run page

- A run's sheet shows its live map: the workflow version the run executes,
  as stages or as a graph, each step coloured by its state with why it
  waits or failed, its chunks, outputs and findings, and each dependency
  labelled with what flowed along it. It refreshes while the run is live
  and replaces the previous workflow overlay, which drew the current
  workflow instead of the run's version.

### Added: the run page says why a task waits and how to fix a failed step

- A queued task has a "Why waiting?" toggle: how many sensors can take it and how many are busy, each reason that keeps it from the others with its fix and a link to the page that applies it, and (with `sensors:read`) each sensor's verdict. It reads `GET /api/v1/scan-runs/{id}/tasks/{task_id}/placement` only when opened.
- A failed step in the run map shows its error code, its class, what it means and the fix, with a link. Every error code and placement reason has English and Vietnamese text; a test fails on a code without one.

### Added: the run page shows a timeline

- A run now shows when each of its tasks was queued, picked up, refused,
  handed back, started and how it ended, with the reason. Platform scanning
  tasks never name their sensor.
- A task still queued after 5 minutes is called out as waiting for a sensor,
  with what to check.

### Added: every run says who or what started it

- Runs in `GET /api/v1/scan-runs`, `GET /api/v1/scan-runs/{id}` and the scan
  run reads now include `trigger`: `{type, id, run_id, label}`. `type` is
  `user`, `schedule`, `automation`, `api`, `webhook`, `asset_discovery` or
  `system`. It names the person (with a display name), the automation and the
  automation run behind the run, or the scan for a scheduled run.
- Before this, a run an automation started read "manual", and the Runs list
  showed the raw trigger type. The "Triggered by" column now reads the person's
  name, "Automation", "Schedule" or "Platform".

### Added: retests on the Runs page

- Scans › Runs filters by kind (scans, quick scans, retests); system runs stay
  hidden. A retest run is named "Retest" and links to its finding. The CSV
  export has a Kind column.
- A finding's retest has a "View run" link that opens the run (its tasks and
  their logs) at `/scans/runs?run=<id>`. The link is shown only to users with
  scans:read. The run page leaves out stages and dispatch for runs that execute
  no scan workflow.

### Added: asset owners as scan approvers (design and model)

- RFC-073 §10 designs asset owners as approvers: each owner approves the part of a scan's targets they own, a fallback group approves the rest. The model (`approver_source`, `fallback_group_id`, owner parts) is in place; saving a rule with `asset_owners` is refused until the request and gate paths enforce it.

### Added: scan approval rules by requester, origin and business hours

- Approval rule conditions `requester_roles`, `requester_group_ids`, `origins` (`ui`, `api_key`, `service_account`, `mcp`, `ci`, `system`) with `trusted_service_account_ids`, and `hours` (weekly windows in the organization's or a named timezone, catching scans outside or inside them; daylight saving follows the wall clock) (RFC-073 §4.1).
- The origin comes from the authentication method; a trusted service account is exempt only when it is one of the organization's service accounts. Unknown requester, origin or time is caught, and a failed lookup refuses the run.

### Added: scan approval requests and the run gate

- When scan approval is On or Strict, a scan the organization's rules catch
  runs only under an approval of its current definition (targets and
  selectors, intensity, tools or workflow, schedule, sensor placement and
  zone). Runs of an approved definition need nothing more; a change needs a
  new approval with the diff shown. Manual, scheduled, quick and retried
  runs all pass the gate (a scheduled run without approval is recorded as
  blocked). RFC-073 §8.
- New permission `scans:approve` (owners and administrators). Routes:
  `POST /api/v1/scans/approval-preview`, `GET/POST /api/v1/scans/{id}/approval`,
  `POST /api/v1/scans/{id}/emergency-run` (owner or administrator, step-up,
  1-24 hours, audited critical), `GET /api/v1/scan-approvals`, and
  `approve`, `reject`, `self-approve` (sole owner with an authenticator
  code), `remind`, `cancel`. The scan list returns `approval_status`.
- Migration `001921` adds `scan_approval_requests` and the permission.

### Added: scan approval rule tester

- `POST /api/v1/organization/settings/scan-governance/test` (owner or administrator) evaluates a proposed rule set against the organization's saved scans (at most 200) without saving it: the scans it would hold for approval, those only monitor rules catch, and how many scans each rule catches (RFC-073 §4.3).

### Added: scan approval in the web console

- Settings > Scanning > Scan approval: the mode (owner), presets, and
  turning rules on, off or into monitor mode (RFC-073).
- New Scan: the review step says when the scan needs approval and by whom,
  asks for the justification or change ticket the rules need, and saves
  and submits it ("Submit for approval").
- Scans > Approvals: the requests with what each scan would do and what
  changed since the last approval; approve, reject, approve your own scan
  with an authenticator code when no other approver exists, remind,
  withdraw. The scan list shows "Awaiting approval".

### Added: scan capability contracts (typed ports, standard params, versions)

- Each scan stage is now a versioned capability (`scan.ports@1`) with a contract: input and output **port types** from a closed set of ten (`root_domain`, `hostname`, `ip`, `cidr`, `service`, `url`, `repository`, `container_image`, `cloud_account`, `finding`), standard params with types and bounds, and the fields a report must carry. Each implementation maps the params it accepts to the tool's own config key.
- An adapter table names the capability that turns one port type into another (for example `hostname → url`: `probe.http`). The workflow editor offers it on an incompatible connection.
- Taxonomy v1 lists 22 capabilities. Nine are planned, with a contract and no implementation yet: they are served with `available: false` and are never routed.
- `GET /api/v1/scans/stages` serves the contracts, the implementations (with `batch` and `params`), `port_types` and `adapters`. Existing fields are unchanged.
- Whether a tool takes a target list per task now comes from the catalogue instead of a hardcoded scanner map. Behaviour is unchanged.

### Added: create a scan from inventory assets by id

- `POST /api/v1/scans` accepts `asset_ids`: the server scans each asset by its inventory name, checked like any typed target (act scope, ownership, proof, tier). An asset the creator may not scan, another organization asset or an unknown id refuses the request without saying which. At most 1,000 targets and assets together.

### Added: scans of `*.example.com` and CIDRs follow the inventory at every run

- A wildcard domain in a scan's targets is resolved at the start of every run to the apex and every domain or subdomain asset the inventory holds at or under it, so a scheduled scan also scans the names found since its last run (RFC-068). Subdomain discovery (subfinder) still takes the apex only.
- A CIDR target can be swept as before (default) or, with `target_options.cidr_mode = inventory`, replaced at each run by the address assets the inventory holds inside the range.
- `target_options` on `POST /scans` and `PUT /scans/{id}`: `cidr_mode`, `seen_within_days` (0–365), `include_stale`. Archived assets are never taken; stale ones only on request; at most 5 000 assets per selector, the most recently seen first.
- Every expanded target goes through the dispatch gate as the inventory asset it is (exclusions, ownership, act scope, tier, private ranges); a selector authorizes nothing.
- `GET /scan-runs/{id}` reports what each selector added (`dispatch.target_expansion`); `GET /assets?in_cidr=` lists the address assets inside ranges; metrics `scan_target_selector_expansions_total` and `scan_stage_targets_skipped_total`.
- Migration `001640_scan_target_options` adds `scans.target_options` (constant default, no rewrite).

### Added: scan freeze windows in the console

- Settings, Policies, Scan freeze windows lists, creates, edits and deletes the organization-wide windows (one-off or weekly, in a chosen time zone); each scan zone has its own windows from the zone list (Freeze windows), and a zone held by a window shows Frozen.
- A banner on Scans and on Scan zones names the active windows and when they end.
- Run now during a window: members holding `scans:freeze:override` are asked whether to start the scan anyway (audited); others are told why it did not start.

### Added: scan freeze windows

- Organization-wide or per-zone windows (one-off, or weekly in an IANA time zone) in which no active (T1/T2) scan work is dispatched: `/api/v1/scan-freeze-windows` (read with `scans:read`, manage with `sensors:zones:write` / `sensors:zones:delete`). Passive work and ingest continue.
- Enforced at claim time for every command path (trigger, pipeline steps, direct commands, validation, coverage and EASM dispatch); scheduled runs are deferred to the window's end; other triggers answer `409 SCAN_FREEZE_ACTIVE` unless the caller sends `override_freeze` and holds the new permission `scans:freeze:override` (owner and admin; audited).
- Migration `001115` (new table, two `freeze_override` columns with a default, one permission). See `docs/architecture/scan-zones.md#freeze-windows`.

### Added: scan intensity (passive, active, intrusive)

- Every scan has an `intensity`, the ceiling of what its runs may send toward
  the targets: `passive` (no packets from the sensors to the targets),
  `active` (non-intrusive probing) or `intrusive` (RFC-071). It is on scan
  create, update, quick scan, import/export and the scan and run responses.
- A scanner or workflow step above the intensity is refused when the scan is
  saved (`INTENSITY_EXCEEDED`); at run time such a step is skipped with its
  reason and never dispatched; the claim refuses a job whose tier, or the tier
  the sensor's tool contract gives it, is above.
- Existing scans get the tier they already probe at (migration
  `scan_intensity`); nothing changes behaviour.

### Added: end-to-end test of a scan's life in the console

- A Playwright spec creates a single-scanner and a workflow scan in the New Scan wizard, edits each (name, targets, max duration) from its page, runs it and opens the run, so a broken Edit can no longer pass unnoticed. The e2e seed's sensor gets a tier ceiling that lets active workflow steps be saved.

### Added: the scan list carries each scan's latest run and workflow name

- `GET /scans` and `GET /scans/{id}` return `last_run`: the scan's latest run with its real state (running with `progress` 0-100, completed, partial, failed, blocked with `refusal_code` and message, ...), its times and task counts. They also return `pipeline_name` for a workflow scan. Both are read in two batch queries per page, scoped to the caller's tenant.

### Added: never-run one-off scans are archived after 30 days

- A new job (`one-off-scan-archive`, every 6 hours, one replica) archives ad-hoc scans that never had a run and are older than 30 days. An archived scan is disabled, left out of every scan list (also with one-off scans shown), and kept with its runs and audit trail; it is never deleted. Each archive is audited in the scan's tenant (`scan_config.disabled`, metadata `archived: true`).
- Migration 001154 adds `scans.archived_at`.

### Added: the scope check says where a scan would run; save a scan with only its allowed targets

- `POST /scope/check` returns `routing`: where a scan of the targets would
  run (`tenant`, `platform` or `waits`), why, and which of the
  organization's own sensors would take it. In auto mode, with the platform
  setting "Require a verified domain before platform sensors scan a target"
  on, unverified targets run on the organization's own online sensor instead
  of being reported as "Proof needed"; only without one do they need proof
  (RFC-054 §6.4).
- A `zone_none` refusal of a hostname lists the private addresses it resolved
  to (`resolved`), when the platform may show them.
- An intrusive probe's `proof_required` refusal no longer offers "use your
  own sensor" (it would not help).
- `POST /scans` takes `skip_refused_targets`: the scan is saved with only
  the targets the scope check allows; the others are recorded with their
  refusal codes in `skipped_targets` on the scan and on every run (never sent
  to a sensor). Nothing the gate refuses is saved or scanned.

### Added: a workflow scan run shows its steps as a graph

- The scan run panel shows a workflow run as a graph. Each step shows its status, the capability and tool it ran, how many targets it took in and was handed, the reasons targets were left out, its findings and its error. The graph is read-only and refreshes while the run is live.
- The graph is built from the run's own step records (which keep their name, tool and capability after the workflow changes) and from `GET /pipeline-runs/{id}/stages`. The workflow's dependencies draw the edges. Nothing is computed in the browser.
- The run's stage lanes take their labels from the capability catalog the API serves, instead of a copy kept in the web app.

### Added: refused triggers are recorded as blocked runs

- A trigger refused before anything is dispatched (scope gate, freeze window, unavailable tool or sensor, no target, paused scan, platform routing, sensor policy) is recorded as a run with status `blocked`, its `refusal_code` and message, visible in the scan's run list. It is terminal and never retried. Skipped scheduled occurrences (previous run still active) stay audit entries.
- `GET /scans` and `GET /scans/{id}` return `blocked_runs`; runs return `refusal_code`.
- Migration 001157 adds `blocked` to the run status constraint, `pipeline_runs.refusal_code` and `scans.blocked_runs`.

### Added: save a scan to start when its scope is approved
- `POST /api/v1/scans` takes `start_when_scope_approved`. When every direct target the scope gate refuses is covered by a scope entry that waits for approval, the scan is saved without a run and starts on its own, as the person who asked, once the entry comes into effect (created active, approved, self-approved or activated). Every gate runs again at that start; any other refusal still refuses the create. The response says `starts_when_scope_approved`. A wait lapses after 30 days. Migration `001727` (`scan_scope_waits`).
- New Scan offers "Create scan, start when scope is approved" when the only thing blocking its targets is a pending approval, and keeps the wizard's state when the user leaves it (for example to approve or verify) and opens it again.

### Added: starter scan workflows (Discover, Discover + Vuln, Web app, Network, Code / CI)

- Five system workflows are built from capability steps, so the platform picks an available tool for each step (migration 001201):
  - **Discover**: subdomains → DNS → HTTP probe;
  - **Discover + Vuln**: adds ports and vulnerability templates;
  - **Web app**: probe → crawl → templates;
  - **Network**: ports → probe → templates;
  - **Code / CI**: secrets, static analysis, dependencies and IaC.
- Each one passes the workflow graph check, and a platform tool resolves for every step. Like every system workflow, they are read-only and copied into an organization on use.
- The new-scan wizard starts with **What to run**: a single check, one of the starter workflows (with its steps), or another of the organization's workflows. This replaces the Single/Workflow switch under Advanced options.
- The presets they replace (Subdomain Enumeration, Port Scanning, Full Reconnaissance, Continuous Monitoring, and the two inactive web and API presets) are deactivated, not deleted. Scans and copies made from them keep working.
- A pipeline step stored without a description no longer fails to load its workflow.

### Added: scan window policies (when scans may touch which targets)

- Allow windows (scan the selected targets only inside them) and blackout windows (never inside them), selected by asset tags, asset groups, asset types, criticality, business units, scope entries, scan zones and bug-bounty programs; weekly slots and dated one-offs in an IANA time zone; all tools, active and intrusive, or intrusive only; a grace for running work; optional rate and concurrency caps. RFC-067, `docs/architecture/scan-windows.md`.
