- `/api/v1/scan-window-policies` (read with `scans:read`, manage with the new `scans:windows:manage`), `POST /api/v1/scan-window-policies/preview`, `POST /api/v1/scan-windows/preview` (why a target or asset cannot be scanned now and when it can), `/api/v1/scan-window-overrides`.
- Bug-bounty program testing windows are evaluated with the policies; no override ever lifts them.
- Emergency override: suspends one or every policy for 15 minutes to 24 hours with a reason and a current authenticator code (`scans:windows:override`, owner and admin); audited and notified to every owner and administrator.
- Run tasks carry `window_hold` and runs `window_waits`; the zone routing and workflow previews carry `windows`.

### Added: preview of a workflow scan before it starts

- `POST /api/v1/scans/workflow-preview` (`scans:write`) shows what a workflow scan would do, before it is saved or started. It creates nothing:
  - per step: the capability and tier, the tool the planner picks, and its sensor status (ready, sensors offline, no sensor);
  - the targets: zone routing and scope exclusions, with at most 20 samples;
  - a freeze window active now.
- It uses the trigger's code. A step the trigger would refuse (`NO_SENSOR_FOR_TOOL`) carries the same code and message, and `blocking` is true when a trigger with these settings would be refused (a test checks this parity).
- The new-scan wizard shows the preview for a workflow scan on its last step.
- A workflow that is neither the organization's own nor a system workflow is not found.

### Added: scope entries name their approvers; reminders; an owner without another approver can approve

- A scope entry waiting for approval now says how many approvals it still needs and who can give them (owners, administrators and members with the scope approval permission, never the requester). Names are shown to people who may see the organization's members; everyone else sees the count.
- The approvers are told in-app, by email and on the organization's notification channels. "Remind approvers" (`POST /api/v1/scope/targets/{id}/remind`) sends the request again, at most once an hour per entry.
- When nobody else can approve an entry (an organization with a single owner), the owner who requested it can approve it with a reason and a code from their authenticator app (`POST /api/v1/scope/targets/{id}/self-approve`). It is audited at high severity and every administrator is told. Nothing is approved automatically.
- Migration `001615` adds `scope_targets.approval_reminded_at` and the `self_approved` and `reason` columns of `scope_target_approvals`.

### Added: add many scope entries in one request

- `POST /api/v1/scope/targets/bulk` (`attack_surface:scope:write`) adds up to 200 permanent scope entries at once: a pasted list, a selection of inventory assets, or the targets a scan refused. Each item follows the rules of a single add (platform guardrails, duplicates, the Strict request and approval rules, the job signer's ledger before the database write) and is audited on its own; a caller who adds entries directly re-authenticates once for the batch, and the administrators get one notice for the batch instead of one per entry. Every item answers `created`, `exists` (the organization's existing entry) or `refused` (code and message). RFC-054 §14.

### Added: `POST /scope/check` checks inventory assets by id

- The dry run of the active-probe gate now also takes `asset_ids` (at most
  200 targets and assets together). Each asset is checked by its name, as a
  scan of it would be, and its result carries `asset_id` (RFC-054 §6.4).
- An asset outside the caller's data scope, another organization's, deleted
  or unknown answers `out_of_data_scope` with its id only, whichever it is:
  the check reveals no asset name and no existence.
- `targets` is no longer required when `asset_ids` is sent.

### Added: what the scope join did, and what it would do

- Create, approve, activate and update of a scope entry answer
  `join: {confirmed_count, assets_filter: {covered_by}}`;
  `GET /api/v1/assets?covered_by=<entry id>` lists the assets confirmed
  through that entry.
- `POST /api/v1/scope/targets/preview` `{target_type, pattern}` answers
  `{would_confirm}`.
- Both counts cover only the assets the caller may see. Each run that
  confirms names writes one system audit event
  `asset.attribution_auto_confirmed`.

### Added: Repository scope entries judge repository assets

- A repository asset now gets a scope verdict (in scope through the entry that covers it, or out of scope) instead of "Scope entries do not apply to this kind of asset".
- Repository entries have one canonical form (lower case, no scheme or `.git`): `host/namespace/repo`, `host/namespace/*` (every repository below the namespace, subgroups included) or `host/*` (a whole self-hosted host). Matching is per path segment: `gitlab.com/acme/*` never covers `gitlab.com/acme-evil/app`. Repository exclusions use the same matcher.
- Security: on a code host many organizations share, only repository entries judge repositories: a domain entry such as `github.com` claims nobody's repositories. On a self-hosted host, an entry for the host covers its repositories.
- Security: a whole-host entry on a code host shared by many organizations (github.com, gitlab.com, bitbucket.org and others, `pkg/domain/scope/public_code_hosts.txt`) is refused with `SHARED_CODE_HOST`; name a namespace there. Operators add hosts with `SCOPE_PUBLIC_CODE_HOSTS_EXTRA`. The deny list applies to code hosts.
- "Add to scope" on a repository asset proposes a repository entry.

### Added: a hashed scope snapshot for every scan run

- When a scan run starts, the authority its targets relied on (the covering entries with their authorization source, program and tier; those programs with their accepted terms hash and program exclusions; the count of uncovered targets) is stored canonically with its SHA-256, one body per distinct hash (migration 001495 tables). `GET /api/v1/scan-runs/{id}/scope-snapshot` returns it to callers who may see the run and hold `scope:read` or `programs:read`. RFC-065.

### Added: long intrusive (T2) scope entries are confirmed periodically, or fall back to T1

- An active T2 entry that lasts beyond its attestation period (every 90 days by default; an owner sets 30 to 180) is confirmed by an owner, administrator or scope approver: "Keep T2 for <pattern>?" arrives in-app, by email and on the organization's channels, and the Approvals tab offers "Keep T2" (`POST /api/v1/scope/targets/{id}/attest`).
- Without a confirmation within 14 days the entry falls back to non-intrusive (T1) probes. It is never removed; raising it to T2 again is an ordinary widening that needs an approval. The downgrade is audited (`scope_target.t2_downgraded`) and announced to every administrator.
- `t2_attestation_days` joins the owner-only `PUT /api/v1/scope/settings/intrusive`. Active T2 entries answer an `attestation` object.
- Migration `001620` adds `attested_at`, `attested_by` and `attestation_requested_at` to `scope_targets`. Existing T2 entries start their first period from their approval.

### Added: trend charts mark scoring changes; risk snapshots record their scoring versions

- `risk_snapshots` gets `risk_version` and `priority_version`: the scoring versions the day's numbers were computed with. Past snapshots are never recomputed.
- `GET /dashboard/risk-trend` points carry their versions and the scoring changes that took effect there (`scoring_changes`: date, kind, source, summary). Listed changes are the organization's own and platform model versions.
- The dashboard's priority charts draw a dashed line at each change and explain it ("Scoring changed on <date> (<what>): values before and after are not directly comparable").

### Added: security overview and audit log export

- `GET /api/v1/organization/security-overview` (owners and administrators with `settings:read`) returns a score and 13 posture checks: sign-in, people, credentials, scanning and organization. The console shows them in Settings > Security overview.
- `GET /api/v1/audit-logs/export?format=csv|jsonl` (`audit:read`) downloads the audit log with the list's filters, newest first, up to 50,000 rows (`X-Export-Truncated: true` when more match). CSV cells that start with a formula character are neutralised. Each export is itself recorded as an `audit_log.exported` event. The audit log page has an Export button.
- No migration and no upgrade step.

### Added: content delivery to sensors by digest

- New sensor routes under `/api/v2/sensor/content`:
  - `desired`: the organization's active packs, the platform's stable packs, and the revoked digests. It has an ETag; `If-None-Match` answers 304 with no body.
  - `packs/{digest}`: the canonical archive, immutable, with Range support.
  - `packs/{digest}/index`: the pack's files.
  - `packs/{digest}/files/{sha256}`: one file, so a sensor fetches only the changed files of a new version.
- A sensor reads only digests in its organization's desired set; anything else is `404 content-not-found`. A revocation takes effect within 10 seconds.
- Measured with 3 sensors over 2 runs: a new pack version with 2 of 40 files changed cost 92% less traffic than full downloads.

### Added: organizations' own sensor products and an SDK minimum

- A sensor is judged by what it declares (protocol, SDK, capabilities) against ranges the platform owns, whatever its product (RFC-037 §13, `docs/architecture/sensor-compatibility.md`).
- New `sdk.min` in `versions.yaml` (empty for now): a sensor of any product built with an older sdk-go is degraded with the critical reason `sdk_unsupported`; `sdk_status` gains `unsupported`. SDK checks apply only to sensors built with sdk-go.
- An organization records the latest and minimum release of a sensor product it builds itself: `GET /api/v1/sensors/custom-products` (`sensors:read`), `PUT` and `DELETE /api/v1/sensors/custom-products/{product}` (`sensors:write`, audited, at most 50). Its sensors of that product then get "update available" and "unsupported" verdicts, for that organization only. Names starting with `openctemio-` and products the platform lists are refused. Migration `002913_tenant_sensor_products` (new table).
- A custom product without a recorded release line keeps only the SDK and protocol verdicts.
- **Upgrade note:** nothing to do.

### Added: sensor protocol v3 gRPC binding on port 443 in every setup (ALPN routing)

- The gateway image with the layer4 module routes a TLS connection whose ClientHello offers the ALPN id `openctem-sensor/3` to the API's mTLS listener (passthrough, PROXY protocol v2) on the platform's own port; every other connection is terminated as before. Works with an IP address, a single host name or no DNS at all; no extra port. `OPENCTEM_SENSOR_GATEWAY=alpn` (new, the default of `deploy/docker-compose.sensor-passthrough.yml`); `passthrough` now routes the ALPN id and the dedicated `SENSOR_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME` (SNI). RFC-059 T16 and §5.1 (deployment modes).
- Without `SENSOR_PUBLIC_HOST` the API derives the gRPC endpoint from the platform URL's own host and port (an IP address too), instead of `sensors.<host>`. The self-probe offers the sensor ALPN id; a second probe without it decides whether hello names the endpoint as `grpc_endpoint` (any client) or only as the new `grpc_alpn_endpoint` (clients that offer the id: sdk-go with `client.SensorALPN`). `GET /api/v1/sensors/transport` reports `requires_alpn`; probe metric result `ok_alpn`.
- Behind the stock gateway nothing changes: the probe meets the gateway's certificate and sensors keep the HTTPS binding (logged at info, not as a warning, when the endpoint is derived).
- **Upgrade note:** a deployment that relied on the derived `sensors.<host>` name sets `SENSOR_PUBLIC_HOST=sensors.<host>:443` explicitly (the compose override already does with `passthrough`). Behind the layer4 gateway set `SENSOR_MTLS_TRUSTED_PROXIES` to the gateway's address (the override does).

### Added: sensors reach the gRPC binding on the API's own port without a gateway

- With `SERVER_TLS_CERT_FILE` and `SERVER_TLS_KEY_FILE` set, the API listener terminates TLS itself. A TLS connection that offers the sensor ALPN id `openctem-sensor/3` is served by the sensor gRPC binding on that same port, with the same checks as the mTLS listener (client certificate from the sensor CA, resolved at the handshake and on every call); every other connection gets the configured certificate and the normal API. The endpoint is advertised automatically once the self-probe passes. For an API deployed without our gateway (web served separately, or behind a TCP load balancer), no extra port is needed.
- The certificate files are re-read when they change.
- Unset (the default), the API serves plain HTTP behind a TLS proxy as before.
- RFC-059 §5.1 now has a deployment-mode matrix, with tested nginx `stream` and HAProxy examples for ALPN routing in the architecture doc.

### Added: a new sensor product needs no platform change

- `SENSOR_PRODUCTS_FILE` names a file of extra sensor products, for example your own sensor built on the SDK.
  - The format is the `versions.yaml` product format, and `release_identity` may be `""`.
  - The products are added to the built-in catalog: the Sensors page lists them, the install dialog offers their snippets, and their sensors are judged against their own release line.
  - A file cannot redefine a built-in product or a fixed section. An invalid file stops the API from starting (RFC-094 I2).
- Install snippet templates are product data. They live in one directory per snippet set: `configs/sensor-products/<set>/<format>.tmpl`, with `sensor/`, `collector/` and `connector-tenable/` shipped.
  - Any well-formed `<set>/<format>.tmpl` in `SENSOR_CONFIG_TEMPLATES_DIR` is loaded, so a product's set is added without an API change.
  - `docker.tmpl` is required for each set.

### Added: sensor setup checklist from the sensor's config report (migration 001061)

- Sensors that see the hello feature `config_report` send the results of
  their preflight checks with `PUT /api/v2/sensor/config-report` (at most
  64 KiB) and echo its digest on every heartbeat (`config_report`); a
  different digest gets the heartbeat action `send_config_report`.
- The platform sanitizes every report (closed sets, typed and re-validated
  parameters, bounded plain text, unknown members dropped and listed), keeps
  the latest per sensor, and never stores a setting value even if a sensor
  sends one.
- `GET /api/v1/sensors/{id}/config-report` (`sensors:read`) explains each
  check from the platform's own catalog, with fix snippets for env, Docker
  Compose and Helm; older sensors get a checklist derived from the heartbeat.
- New health reasons `config_check_failed`, `config_check_warning` and
  `config_report_stale`; the sensor list and detail carry `config_health`.

### Added: per-task logs from sensors, kept 14 days and shown on the run page

- Sensor protocol v2 gains `POST /api/v2/sensor/commands/{id}/logs` (feature `logs` on hello, RFC-029 §4.4.1): the sensor holding a command sends what its tool logged, in numbered batches through its outbox. A batch is stored once; a command keeps at most 200 batches and 2 MiB; the platform caps, cleans and redacts every line itself before storing it.
- Logs are kept 14 days (`command-log-retention` controller) and deleted with their command. Migration 001130 (`command_logs`, a new table).
- The run page's task table has a Logs action per task (`GET /api/v1/pipeline-runs/{id}/tasks/{task_id}/logs`, `pipelines:read`); lines are shown as plain text.
- Sensors send logs from sdk-go releases that support the `logs` feature; older sensors are unaffected.

### Added: a sensor's tool options on its Manifest tab

- Each tool on a sensor's Manifest tab lists the options its tool manifest declares, read-only: common options first (request timeout, rate limit, concurrency, retries), then the tool's own, with default, range or values, who may set it (the sensor's configuration only, or a scan too), its safety class (impact, dangerous) and the native flag it maps to. The platform already stores each tool's manifest with the sensor's manifest; nothing new is stored.

### Added: per-sensor tool settings, validated and delivered inside the signed job

- Owners and administrators configure each tool of one of their sensors from
  the sensor drawer's new "Tool settings" tab: a form generated from the
  settings schema the tool's descriptor declares in the sensor's manifest
  (common options first, bounds, defaults, safety tags, effective values).
- `GET /api/v1/sensors/{id}/tool-settings`, `GET .../{tool}/effective`
  (`sensors:read`), `PUT` and `DELETE .../{tool}` (`sensors:write`). Values are
  validated with the CTIS settings contract (`ctis/settings`); non-default
  values of dangerous (T2) options are refused for now. Changes are audited
  as `sensor.updated` with a per-key diff; sensitive values are redacted.
- A sensor's settings for a tool travel in each scan job of that tool as
  `settings_layers.sensor`, covered by the job signature. Settings that no
  longer validate after a sensor upgrade fail the job with
  `TOOL_SETTINGS_INVALID`; save or reset them to clear it.
- Migration `002114_sensor_tool_settings` adds the `sensor_tool_settings`
  table (new and empty; no upgrade step).

### Added: sensor protocol v3 gRPC binding on port 443 by SNI (Compose)

- `deploy/docker-compose.sensor-passthrough.yml` builds the gateway with the layer4 module and passes TLS for `SENSOR_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME` through to the API's mTLS listener with a PROXY protocol v2 header; every other host is served as before. The API believes PROXY headers only from `SENSOR_MTLS_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (the gateway) and closes a connection that sends one from anywhere else.
- **Upgrade note:** nothing changes without the override. To use it: point a DNS name (different from the platform host) at the gateway, then `SENSOR_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME=<name> docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.sensor-passthrough.yml up -d --build`.

### Added: sensor protocol v3 over HTTPS (RFC-059), off by default

- `SENSOR_TRANSPORT_V3_ENABLED=true` serves `openctem.sensor.v3.SensorService` (Connect, gRPC and gRPC-Web) under `/api/v3/sensor`, authenticated by an RFC 9421 signature of a key-bound sensor only (no bearer keys). Every call runs through the protocol v2 routes in-process: same validation, limits and side effects; the v2 rate budgets are shared by both protocols.
- `Subscribe` is a control stream: the doorbell is pushed when a command becomes pending or a held one is cancelled (under a second on one replica), with a keepalive; a revoked key or sensor ends it.
- The v2 hello lists `transport_v3` (HTTPS path, `SENSOR_PUBLIC_HOST`) when v3 is on. The gateway routes `/api/v3/sensor/*` to the API (sensor plane).

### Added: sensor protocol v3 gRPC binding with mTLS (RFC-059)

- With `SENSOR_TRANSPORT_V3_ENABLED` and `SENSOR_PUBLIC_HOST` set, the API serves the gRPC binding on `SENSOR_MTLS_LISTEN_ADDR` (`:8443`): TLS 1.3, HTTP/2 only, a client certificate from the sensor CA required. The certificate's key is resolved through the sensor key table at the handshake and on every request, so a revoked key or sensor is refused without a revocation list; revoking or disabling a sensor ends its live control stream at once.
- `IssueCertificate` certifies a key-bound sensor's registered key (7 days by default, `SENSOR_MTLS_CERT_TTL`); the sensor renews it over either binding. Issuance is recorded on the sensor's timeline.
- The sensor CA comes from `SENSOR_MTLS_CA_CERT_FILE` + `SENSOR_MTLS_CA_KEY_FILE`, or is created once in `SENSOR_MTLS_CA_DIR` (default `/app/data/sensor-ca`, on the `api-data` volume). It is separate from the job signer.

### Added: sensor protocol v3 contract (gRPC + mTLS, Connect/HTTPS fallback)

- RFC-059 and the `openctem.sensor.v3.SensorService` proto (`api/proto`), with the generated Go code in `api/pkg/sensorproto/v3`. Nothing serves it yet; protocol v2 is unchanged.
- API CI runs `buf lint`, `buf breaking` against the base branch and a generated-code drift check (`make proto-check`).

### Added: sensor protocol v3 pushes across API replicas (RFC-059)

- Command and sensor changes on one API replica now wake the control streams held by every replica, through Redis pub/sub (channel `sensor:v3:wake`). The message is a hint (tenant, sensor); each replica re-reads the database. Without Redis, other replicas see a change at their 30-second re-check.

### Added: the transport of each sensor (RFC-059)

- Every heartbeat records how it arrived: `grpc` (protocol v3 over mutual TLS), `https` (protocol v3 over HTTPS) or `v2`, decided by the platform from the listener the call came on, plus the sensor's own fallback reason (sanitized, 256 characters). A heartbeat carried by v3 records protocol 3. Migration 001345 adds `sensors.protocol_binding` and `protocol_fallback_reason` (nullable, no backfill).
- `GET /api/v1/sensors/{id}` and the list return them under `protocol.binding` and `protocol.fallback_reason`; the sensor detail sheet shows the transport and the reason.

### Added: `server -healthcheck` for container healthchecks without a shell

- `server -healthcheck` requests `GET /health` on `127.0.0.1:$SERVER_PORT`
  (default 8080), with no proxy, no redirects and a 3 s timeout. It exits 0
  on a 200 answer and 1 otherwise.
- The API image's `HEALTHCHECK`, `api/deploy/docker-compose.yml` and the e2e
  Compose file use it instead of `wget`, so the API image will no longer need
  busybox. The probe can only reach the container's own loopback listener.
- Upgrade note: the Compose healthcheck now needs an API image from this
  release or later. An older image does not know the flag and reports
  unhealthy, so keep the Compose file and the image on the same release.

### Added: service accounts for integrations

- `GET/POST /api/v1/service-accounts`, `DELETE /api/v1/service-accounts/{id}`
  (`team:members:read` / `team:members:write`): an organization-owned identity
  for an integration (a SIEM export, a ticketing bridge). It starts with no
  role, gets custom roles and teams like a member, and acts only through API
  keys minted for it, which carry at most what it holds.
- It never signs in (no password or federated identity, enforced by the
  database), belongs to one organization only, and can never be an owner or
  administrator or hold full data access (database triggers and the role grant
  guard). Deleting it removes its roles, team memberships and keys at once
  (migration 001586).
- `GET/POST /api/v1/service-accounts/{id}/api-keys` and
  `DELETE /api/v1/service-accounts/{id}/api-keys/{key_id}`: mint, list and
  delete its keys (member and API key permissions together; minting and
  deleting need a recent sign-in). A scope must be held by the person minting
  the key. API keys cannot reach `/api/v1/service-accounts`.
- Settings > Integrations > Service accounts in the web console.

### Added: shared sensor enrollment with a single-use instance enrollment token

- A super administrator issues a single-use token in the console
  (`POST /api/v1/admin/shared-sensors/enrollment-tokens`: super admin, console
  step-up, a reason; valid 5 to 60 minutes; shown once, stored only as a keyed
  hash; console audit row). A sensor that starts pairing with it
  (`enrollment_token`) becomes a shared sensor: no organization, trust level
  trusted, the least-privilege grant. Redemption, approval and confirmation
  are audited in the console log. A malformed, unknown, expired or used token
  gets one `401`; no organization can look up, approve or deny such a request.
- `bootstrap-admin sensor-token` registers the token an install generated for
  its bundled sensor (`-from-env SENSOR_INSTANCE_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN`), or mints
  and prints one.
- A key-bound shared sensor now authenticates its signed requests (its key has
  no tenant and resolves only to a sensor of scope instance); it never gets a
  tenant context.
- Migration 002887 adds `instance_enrollment_tokens` and
  `sensor_pairings.instance_token_id`.

### Added: console page for shared sensors (fleet, queue, audited job view, pause, resume, retire)

- Console > System > Shared sensors (`/api/v1/admin/shared-sensors`). Any administrator sees:
  - the instance sensors: name, region, status, health, version, tools, current jobs, last seen;
  - queued and running shared jobs per tool lane;
  - per-organization counts (organization names only for super and operations administrators; a read-only administrator gets opaque ids);
  - job metadata: organization, type, tool, state, shared sensor, times.
  No payload, targets, result or error text is ever listed.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/shared-sensors/jobs/{job_id}/view` shows one job's targets and logs. It needs a super or operations administrator and a reason, and is rate-limited. A high admin audit row (`shared_sensor.job_viewed`, with the organization and the reason) is written before anything is returned. Results and findings are never shown.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/shared-sensors/{sensor_id}/disable|enable|revoke` needs a super admin, a reason and a route-level step-up, and writes a critical admin audit row before the status changes (if the row cannot be written, the action fails and nothing changes). It only acts on instance sensors (an organization's sensor answers 404). Pause stops new jobs while held jobs finish; retire revokes the sensor, and it cannot be resumed (409).
- No migration.

### Added: shared sensor egress addresses, and the tenant view is called "Shared sensors"

- The instance administrator publishes the addresses shared sensors send traffic from: Console > System > Platform scanning, "Egress addresses" (`GET/PUT /api/v1/admin/settings/shared-sensors/egress`). IP addresses or CIDR ranges for every region and per region. Only public addresses are accepted: private, loopback, link-local, cloud metadata, carrier-grade NAT and other internal ranges (ctis `addrscope`) are refused with 400. Any administrator reads; a change needs a super admin, a reason and a route-level step-up, gets a critical admin audit row (`platform.shared_sensors_egress_changed`), and the other administrators are emailed.
- `GET /api/v1/platform/scanning` returns them as `egress` to an organization that may use shared sensors, so its members can allowlist the scanners. Nothing else about the sensors is shown, and an organization that may not use them sees no addresses.
- Web: "Platform scanning" is now "Shared sensors" (Sensors page card, new-scan and workflow sensor choice, scan detail, run views), and the organization's own are "Organization sensors". The card lists the egress addresses with a copy button and links administrators to the owner's opt-out.
- The API takes ctis at the commit that adds `addrscope`. No migration.

### Added: signing key scripts

- `scripts/signing/init-keys.sh` creates the catalog root key, the release feed key and a separate catalog online key (private files, mode 0600), signs the catalog key set (listing the catalog online key only) and prints only public material and two `gh secret set` commands (`release-feed` and `content-catalog` environments); it refuses to overwrite keys. `scripts/signing/rotate-keyset.sh` re-signs the key set each year. See `docs/architecture/signing-keys.md`.

### Added: sign-up feed and burst alerts in the platform console

- Console > Requests > Sign-ups lists accounts created, organizations created
  and access requests submitted, with daily counts, kept 90 days. Each event
  keeps only the registrable email domain and the client network prefix (/24
  or /48); never the address, a name or a user agent (migration
  `signup_events`).
- When sign-ups of one kind from one network or one email domain reach a
  threshold within a window (default 10 per network, 20 per domain, an hour),
  the API raises one alert: the metric
  `openctem_signup_burst_alerts_total{dimension,kind}` (new monitoring rule
  `SignupBurst`), a WARN log line `alert=signup_burst`, a high admin audit row
  `platform.signup_burst` and an email to the platform administrators.
- A super admin changes the thresholds and the ignored domains with a reason
  and a fresh authenticator code (`PUT /api/v1/admin/settings/signup-alerts`,
  audited critical). Any console role reads the feed
  (`GET /api/v1/admin/signup-events`, `/daily`).
- **Upgrade note:** burst alerts need Redis; without it events are still
  recorded.

### Added: onboarding offers invitations and the organization of a verified domain; join requests

- An account without an organization gets its pending invitations, the organization that claims its
  verified email domain (only when that organization is discoverable and allows joining) and whether
  it may create one: `POST /api/v1/auth/onboarding/options`, `POST /api/v1/auth/onboarding/accept`
  (refresh-token authenticated). Offers carry opaque references bound to the account; no
  organization id or slug is shown. Taking an offer accepts the invitation, joins at once as the
  domain's role (`auto`) or creates a join request (`approval`).
- Organizations decide requests in their own inbox: `GET /api/v1/organization/join-requests`,
  `POST .../{id}/approve` (viewer or member only) and `.../reject`. One pending request per person
  and organization, 5 a day per person, 30-day expiry, purged 30 days after decision. Audited.
- Migration 002830 adds `organization_join_requests`.

### Added: onboarding, domain settings and join requests in the web console

- A signed-in account without an organization sees its invitations, the organization of its
  verified email domain (Join or Ask to join, then "waiting for approval") and the create form when
  allowed. Joining opens the organization at once.
- Settings > Domains (owners change, admins read): who may join with each verified single sign-on
  domain, discoverability, requiring SSO and blocking new organizations for accounts on it.
- Settings > Members shows waiting requests to join, approved as viewer or member or rejected.
- Sign-up refused because the domain requires its organization's SSO sends the person to sign in
  there. All text in English and Vietnamese.

### Added: the sign-up policy is a console setting (System > Sign-up)

- Who may create an organization (`admin_only` or `self_service`, plus whether
  people may request access) is now one platform setting, stored in the new
  `platform_settings` table (migration 001313) and edited on Console > System >
  Sign-up. create-first-team, `POST /tenants` and `GET /auth/providers` read
  it per request; a read failure means `admin_only`.
- Any administrator reads it. A super admin changes it with a fresh
  authenticator code and the version read (409 on a concurrent change). Every
  change writes a critical admin audit row (`platform.signup_policy_changed`)
  and emails the other administrators. Existing organizations, users and
  sessions are never affected by a change.
- **Upgrade note:** `TENANT_CREATION_MODE` now only seeds the setting on the
  first start after this upgrade. Change it in the console afterwards; editing
  the environment variable no longer has an effect once the row exists.

### Added: the sign-up policy decides account sign-up and organization creation separately

- Console > System > Sign-up has two choices: who may create an account (`accounts`: closed, domain,
  open) and who may create an organization (`mode`: admin_only, self_service; self_service needs
  open accounts). Each is limited by `SIGNUP_MODE`: `domain` allows domain sign-up but never open
  sign-up or organizations. The hosted service can keep sign-up open while pausing organization
  creation. `PUT /api/v1/admin/settings/signup` takes `accounts`; `GET` also reports `accounts`,
  `max_accounts` and `effective_accounts`; `GET /auth/providers` reports `signup_accounts`.
- The admission rule gains two outcomes: `domain_account` (the account joins its verified domain's
  organization, never creates one) and `sso_required` (an address on a domain whose organization
  requires its SSO is refused for password and social sign-up, nothing written). Domain policies
  that produce them follow in the next change.
- A stored policy keeps its meaning: `self_service` reads as open account sign-up, `admin_only` as
  closed.

### Added: release images carry a signed SLSA build provenance

- Every image of a release (`openctem-api`, `openctem-web`, `openctem`,
  `openctem-gateway`, `migrations`, `seed`, `admin-cli`) gets a SLSA build
  provenance attestation signed through Sigstore and stored in the registry
  next to the image, recording the workflow, commit and runner that built it.
  Verify with `gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/openctemio/<image>:<tag> --owner openctemio`.

### Added: software inventory captured from scan output

- Ingest now records which products and versions each asset runs (RFC-066): typed CTIS technologies and services, HTTP technology strings (`Name:version`), the HTTP `Server` header, service banners, open-port versions and the operating system CPE.
- Products and versions live once in a shared software catalog (`software_products`, `software_product_aliases`, `software_versions`); a row is global only for public identities (a curated list of about 80 common products), and everything else a tenant observes is private to that tenant. Assets link to versions in `asset_software`, with the location, source, evidence and a confidence score; a newer version at the same location supersedes the old link.
- Migration 001616. No API or UI yet; the vulnerability matcher and the asset Software tab build on it.

### Added: host discovery stage (`discover.hosts`)

- New workflow stage `discover.hosts` (T1): finds the live addresses of addresses and ranges with light probes before deeper scans, and reports each as an `ip_address` with the probe that answered. It is the `cidr → ip` adapter; chunks hold at most 64 targets and 4 096 addresses (RFC-088 step 5).
- naabu runs it only for a step that names the capability; a step that pins naabu without it is still a port scan, and a naabu report that names no capability is still bound to `scan.ports`. Sensors need the naabu with `discover.hosts@1` (sensor release after #233) to claim such steps.
- ctis is bumped to the taxonomy with `discover.hosts@1`.

### Added: signed direct downloads, S3 server-side encryption, storage metrics and a local↔S3 copy command

- `STORAGE_DIRECT_DOWNLOAD=true` (off by default) adds
  `GET /api/v1/attachments/{id}/signed-url`: after the same checks as a
  download, a 60-second signed GET for that one object in an HTTPS bucket,
  forcing an attachment download. Local storage, plain-HTTP endpoints and
  flagged files answer `409` and download through the API. The console uses
  it for file downloads.
- `STORAGE_SSE` (`AES256` or `aws:kms`) and `STORAGE_SSE_KMS_KEY_ID` ask the
  server bucket to encrypt every object written.
- Metrics `openctem_storage_operations_total`,
  `openctem_storage_operation_seconds`, `openctem_storage_bytes_written_total`
  and `openctem_storage_events_total` (quota rejections, purges, scan
  results).
- `bootstrap-admin storage migrate -from local -to s3` (and the reverse) in
  the `admin-cli` image copies the server storage with the same keys,
  verifying each object by SHA-256; repeatable, `-dry-run`, `-tenant`,
  `-verify`. Switching `STORAGE_PROVIDER` without it leaves existing files
  unreachable (see `docs/architecture/file-storage.md`).

### Added: support access in the web app and the admin console

- Settings › Support access (owners and admins): how support access works, a
  "Grant access" dialog for owners (support administrator's email, findings
  and/or assets, 1 to 72 hours, reason, optional case reference; confirmed
  with a re-authentication), the active access with Revoke, and the history
  with status, session count and last access. A link opens the audit log
  searched for support events.
- Every member sees a banner while platform support can read the
  organization's data (who, which data, until when, case), stronger while a
  support session is open, with a link to the page for owners and admins.
- Admin console › Customers › Support access: the grants that name the
  signed-in administrator and a read-only support session opened from one,
  framed with its end time, with Overview, Findings and Assets (only the
  granted scopes), search, filters, pages and a detail drawer. When the
  access is revoked, expires or ends elsewhere, the session view closes and
  says so. The server checks and audits every read; the UI only reflects it.

### Added: the suppression approval preview lists example findings within the approver's access

- `GET /api/v1/suppressions/{id}/preview` now also returns `in_scope_findings` and `sample`: how many of the matching open findings are on assets the caller's data scope covers, and the first 10 of them (title, severity, asset, path). `matching_open_findings` stays the organization-wide count the approval acts on; findings outside the caller's scope are counted there and never listed. The approve dialog shows the examples and how many matches are not listed (en and vi).
- The examples are listed only to a caller who also holds `findings:read`; the counts stay. A secret finding's title (its message can quote the secret) is never listed: its rule id and path identify it.

### Added: approvers clear the review flag of a suppression rule

- `POST /api/v1/suppressions/{id}/reviewed` (`findings:suppressions:approve`) clears the review flag the platform set on a rule that had no end date; the rule keeps its end. Audited as `suppression_rule.reviewed` with the flag before and after; 409 when the rule is not flagged. The rule's detail in Exceptions has a "Mark as reviewed" button for approvers.

### Added: metric for the findings a suppression rule decides

- `openctem_suppression_rule_hits_total{applied_by}` counts the findings an approved suppression rule decided: `ingest` for new findings a rule matched as they arrived, `approval` for open findings it closed when approved. A finding is counted once per rule. The labels carry no tenant, rule or finding id; the per-rule breakdown stays in `finding_suppressions`. Documented in `docs/operations/monitoring.md`.

### Added: System page in the platform console (read-only)
- `GET /api/v1/admin/system` and Console > System status: service health (api, postgres, redis, web, gateway, connected sensors), free space of the configured data volumes and the database size, the last successful backup, sensor CA and TLS certificate expiry, the running version and the version-check result. Readable by every platform administrator role including the read-only one; aggregates only, no tenant data, secrets or paths.
- A system watcher sets `openctem_system_*` metrics and emails the platform administrators when free space falls below 20% (warning) or 10% (critical), the last backup is older than 26 hours, or a certificate expires within 30 days (warning) or 7 days (critical). Configure with `SYSTEM_STORAGE_PATHS`, `SYSTEM_BACKUP_STATUS_FILE`, `SYSTEM_TLS_CERT_FILES`, `SYSTEM_WEB_HEALTH_URL`, `SYSTEM_GATEWAY_HEALTH_URL`, `SYSTEM_WATCH_INTERVAL`.

### Added: a decision on a taint finding is suspended when its source changes

- A false-positive or accepted taint finding whose re-scan reports another source (file and code of the trace's source step) is confirmed again for review; the earlier decision is kept (`finding_decision_suspensions`) and the change audited. A refactor of the steps in between, or a trace-less report, keeps the decision. The trace is never part of the finding's identity.

### Added: team memberships with an end date

- A team (access group) membership can end on a date (`expires_at` and
  `expiry_reason` on `POST /api/v1/groups/{groupId}/members`, and
  `PATCH /api/v1/groups/{groupId}/members/{userId}` to set, move or
  clear it; at most 365 days ahead; `team:groups:members` with the usual
  delegation cap). Teams of type `external` (engagements, audits) require an
  end date for every member but their creator.
- Within a minute of the end date the membership is removed (controller
  `team-membership-expiry`), the member's data scope is recomputed, the
  removal is audited (`member.removed`, reason `expired`) and the member is
  told (migration 001502, RFC-050 W22).

### Added: teams can carry roles

- A custom role can be bound to a team (`GET/POST /api/v1/groups/{groupId}/roles`,
  `DELETE /api/v1/groups/{groupId}/roles/{roleId}`): every active member of
  the team holds it (migration 001543, view `v_user_role_grants`).
- Binding, and changing who is in a team that carries roles, are grants: the
  actor must be able to grant each role and hold the team's assets; nobody
  but the owner adds themselves. Roles with full data access or member, team,
  role, API key, secret store or settings administration are bound, and
  their teams changed, by the owner only with a recent sign-in. External
  members never get full data access through a team. Only custom roles of
  the organization bind; a bound role cannot be deleted.
- Permission changes reach team members at once (cache invalidation), and a
  team membership past its end date stops granting immediately.

### Added: the Tenable.sc connector is on, as Beta

- Tenable.sc integrations can be created again: the connector runs as its own image, `ghcr.io/openctemio/connector-tenable` (v0.1.0), paired like a sensor with the `scan-connector` grant profile. Syncs, scans launched and scheduled from OpenCTEM and licence-aware rolling coverage work; the sync and coverage controllers run. The integration page shows a Beta badge, and its text is translated (en, vi).
- Beta until a run against a real Tenable.sc confirms what only the documentation states. Known: the API states `maxScanTime` without a unit, so Tenable.sc may allow a scan to run longer than asked; the connector stops a scan itself at its maximum duration plus 30 minutes for the import.

### Added: the Tenable.sc connector image and its grant profile

- The Tenable.sc connector now runs as its own image, `ghcr.io/openctemio/connector-tenable` (openctemio/connector-tenable), paired like a sensor; the sensor no longer carries it. The connector dialog shows the run command and points to the image's setup guide (en, vi).
- New sensor grant profile `scan-connector` (or `scan-connector:<tool>`): job types `connector_sync` and `connector_scan`, tier ceiling T1, no credentials, no push ingest, zone-bound. Before it, no profile allowed `connector_scan`, so a connector sensor needed a custom grant. A connector at trust level New receives syncs only until an administrator trusts it. The grant refusal of a connector sync or scan names the profile.
- The connector dialog's text goes through the translations.

### Added: license-aware rotation for Tenable.sc coverage

- A connector's rolling coverage can rotate more assets than the Tenable.sc license holds (`coverage_rotation`: `off` by default, `aging` or `recycle`), behind an administrator's acknowledgement that the customer's license terms allow it (`coverage_rotation_acknowledged`). `aging` waits for Tenable.sc's nightly cleanup of the rotation repository; `recycle` has the connector delete and recreate its rotation repository before the next batch, only after the previous batch was ingested.
- Every batch carries the connector's license guard, so a batch Tenable.sc has no room for is refused before anything is created and retried later; batches are sized from the license numbers reported after each import.
- Coverage batches settle the asset coverage ledger per target (assessed, no reply, unfinished, failed) instead of marking every dispatched asset covered, and the connector's state shows the coverage cycle with progress and an ETA.
- A recycle rotation stalls when a batch fails after it launched; `POST /api/v1/integrations/{id}/coverage/reactivate` (`integrations:manage`, audited) resumes it.

### Added: scan assets now with a Tenable.sc connector

- `POST /api/v1/integrations/{id}/scans/run` (`scans:write`, scans module) scans up to 50 chosen inventory assets through a Tenable.sc connector with its coverage policy, repository and zone, as a manual run of one hidden on-demand scan per connector, so every scan gate applies (act scope, active-probe gate, scan windows, scan approval). Assets of another organization or outside the caller's data scope, and another organization's integration, answer 404. A connector without a coverage policy and repository is refused with a message to set them.
- The web console offers "Scan with Tenable.sc" on IP address and host assets and "Rescan with Tenable.sc" on findings the connector reported; a finding closes after a full rescan only through coverage auto-resolve (`INGEST_COVERAGE_AUTO_RESOLVE=enforce`).
- The connector dialog sets license rotation (off, aging, recycle) with the required acknowledgement and the aging wait; the coverage panel shows the rotation cycle, its progress and ETA, why the next batch waits, and a stalled rotation with a Resume action.

### Added: an organization's data region is fixed at creation

- New `DEPLOYMENT_REGION` (for example `eu-central`): every organization created on the deployment
  gets it and keeps it for its life; it is shown when creating an organization and in its settings.
  Organizations created before have no region. Unset: no region is named.
- Migration 002571 adds `tenants.region`.

### Added: the `not_observed` finding status

- **`not_observed`: not seen lately, not fixed** (owner
  decision O2). Recent scans no longer report the finding, but nothing
  proves the check ran against it. It is an open status: never counted as
  fixed, no `resolved_at`, and its SLA keeps running. Only the platform sets
  it; a sighting reopens it (not counted as a regression), and it reaches
  `resolved` only through a retest or a `findings:verify` holder.
- **Feature-branch expiry writes `not_observed`** instead of `resolved`, so
  "not seen for N days on a branch" no longer counts as a fix in fix-rate
  or MTTR. Migration 000640 moves existing `resolved` / `branch_expired`
  rows to `not_observed` (no other row is touched) and adds a CHECK
  constraint on `findings.status`, which had none.
- Retest runs on `not_observed` findings. The web labels the status
  "Not Observed" and lists it in the "Open" filter group.

### Added: ticket field mapping editor in the console

- Settings → Integrations → Ticket field mapping lists the mapping profiles
  and creates one per Jira project and issue type (findings or remediation
  tasks), from a preset.
- The editor connects OpenCTEM attributes to Jira fields (pick or drag), with
  direction, transform (value map against the field's allowed values, user,
  date, number, labels, join), sync mode and conflict winner per row, a
  sample render for templates, and the problems found against the live
  project.
- The Status tab draws the project's workflow, maps OpenCTEM states to
  workflow statuses (with resolution) and workflow statuses to intents
  (requests marked as needing approval), and simulates both directions.
- Preview of the issue a finding or task would create and of what an
  existing issue would change; version history with diff and rollback;
  import and export; dry run; a check for Jira changes. English and
  Vietnamese.

### Added: ticket field and status mapping profiles

- Per tracker destination (integration, project, issue type) and per object
  (finding or remediation task), administrators map OpenCTEM attributes to
  tracker fields and back, and OpenCTEM states to the project's workflow and
  back: value maps, templates, user, date, number and list transforms, sync
  mode and conflict winner per field. Versions have a draft, publish (checked
  against the tracker's live fields and workflow, step-up) and rollback.
- Preview of the exact fields for a finding or task, inbound preview of an
  issue, a simulator for transition paths and inbound intents, presets,
  suggestions, copy between projects, JSON/YAML import and export, and drift
  detection.
- Security: a tracker change can never set severity, scores or a closing
  status; a due date becomes a request and "Won't Do" a risk-acceptance
  request. Rendered text is redacted after templating. Previews respect the
  caller's data scope. Every change is audited.

### Added: ticket links as their own records

- New `ticket_links` table: one row per link between a finding or a
  remediation task and a Jira issue, with the integration that owns the issue,
  the issue key, the project, the link's role and state (active, unlinked,
  deleted) and who created it (platform or person). The integration, the
  finding and the task are tenant-scoped foreign keys, so a link can never
  pair one organization with another's integration or finding.
- Existing Jira browse URLs on findings and campaign tickets whose site
  matches one of the organization's Jira integrations are copied in.
- Upgrade note: a unique index on `remediation_campaigns (id, tenant_id)` is
  added (a small table).

### Added: published ticket mappings create issues and move their status

- When a Jira destination has a published field mapping, a finding's issue is
  created from the mapping's fields (custom fields, allowed values by id,
  issue type by id), and a status change moves the issue along the mapped
  workflow path, filling the resolution and required screen fields. A path
  the workflow does not allow is reported, never guessed. In dry run the
  mapping is only logged.
- Status sync jobs no longer retry what the tracker refused (4xx) or what the
  workflow cannot do.

### Added: tool availability from the sensors' manifests

- `GET /api/v1/tenant-tools/availability` lists every catalog tool, plus every tool the organization's sensors report. For each tool it gives the sensors that have it (online and total, with their zones and an exclusion reason when the grant or the local policy stops them), the versions and content versions they report, and a derived status: `ready`, `no_sensor`, `offline_only`, `outdated` or `disabled`. `?zone_id=` limits it to one scan zone. Sensor names are listed only to holders of `sensors:read`; the counts go to everyone who may read the tenant's tools.
- `is_available` on the tools-with-config endpoints is now the same answer: an online sensor that may run the tool. `/{toolId}/with-config` used to always return `false`.
- Tools can carry a minimum version (`min_version`, migration 001153), set on custom tools through the custom tool API. A tool whose online sensors all run an older version is `outdated`.

### Added: retest a finding with its own tool's retest handler

- A finding whose tool has a retest handler on a tenant sensor (the sensor reports `retest:<tool>`; sdk-go tool contract retest) is retested by one `retest` command to that tool. Its verdict for the finding settles the retest: `still_present` reopens a resolved finding as a regression, `fixed` resolves it (`retest_verified`), and `unverifiable`, a missing or foreign verdict, or a failed command leaves it unchanged (unknown). Retest now, proof of fix and auto-retest use it whenever such a sensor is online; nuclei findings fall back to the template re-run plus reachability probe otherwise.
- Findings of any tool with a rule id can now be retested when their tool's retest handler is online. Eligibility, limits, gates, activities (now with `method`), SLA restart and announcements are unchanged.
- The `retest` command passes the same active-probe gate as validate commands, names the tool as `scanner` and lists plain addresses, so the claim-time tool predicate and the sensor's local-policy admission apply. Sensors report `retest:<tool>` only for a known tool. Migration 001135 adds the `retest` command type (no long lock on `commands`).

### Added: organization tool defaults, with per-sensor overrides

- Owners and administrators can set, per tool, the values that every one of the organization's own sensors runs the tool with: `GET /api/v1/sensors/tool-defaults`, plus `PUT` and `DELETE /api/v1/sensors/tool-defaults/{tool}`. The routes use `sensors:read` and `sensors:write`. The values are validated against every settings schema that the organization's sensors report for the tool, and every change is audited.
- A sensor's own tool settings now override the organization's defaults key by key, in either direction. A scan, a workflow step or a job can still only lower rate, concurrency and retries.
- Scan jobs carry the defaults that the claiming sensor inherits as `settings_layers.tenant` inside the signed payload. This layer leaves out the keys that the sensor overrides, and it is never sent to shared platform sensors. If the defaults no longer validate against a sensor's schema, that sensor's jobs of the tool fail with `TOOL_SETTINGS_INVALID`.
- The sensor tool settings response adds `organization_values` and `organization_problems`. The effective view and the preview add the source `tenant` and a `chain` of every layer that sets a key.
- Migration `002136_tenant_tool_settings` adds a new, empty table.

### Added: preview a scan's tool options on a sensor; scans and steps checked when saved

- `POST /api/v1/sensors/{id}/tool-settings/{tool}/preview` (`sensors:read`, read-only) resolves a scan's or a workflow step's options over the sensor's tool settings the way the sensor will: every option with its value and source (default, sensor or scan) and the config keys the sensor ignores; 422 by path when the sensor would refuse the options.
- Saving a single-scanner scan, and adding or editing a step pinned to a tool, checks its tool options against the organization's own sensors for that tool: a sensor-only option, a value out of bounds, or a raise of rate, concurrency or retries above what the sensor allows is refused when no sensor would accept it, instead of failing every job later.

### Added: tools show their trust and the tier the platform assigns them

- The tool view (`GET /api/v1/tools?include=availability`) reports, for each tool and each sensor that runs it:
  - `trust`: `builtin`, or `unverified` for a copy the sensor's operator installed;
  - `tier`: the tier the platform assigns a scan with the tool, from the tool contracts the tenant's sensors report (RFC-055 §5).
- The tool's trust is the lowest among its sensors, and its tier the highest.
- The workflow builder's palette, the Tools table and the tool detail show both with one shared badge. An operator-installed copy is flagged "Unverified · T2".
- A sensor whose grant ceiling is below the tool's assigned tier now counts as excluded (grant), the same rule dispatch applies.
- The view reads every sensor's current manifest in one tenant-scoped query. Another tenant's manifests never count.

### Added: trusted organizations — sign in to a sister company with your own company's single sign-on

- **Request and acceptance** (RFC-058 part 2):
  - an organization's owner can trust another organization, named by a domain it verified for SSO (`POST /api/v1/organization/trusts`);
  - that organization's owner accepts (`POST /api/v1/organization/trusts/{trust_id}/approve`);
  - either owner can end it (`DELETE`);
  - every change needs step-up, is audited in both organizations' logs, and both sides are notified.
- **Signing in:** once accepted, external members from the trusted organization can sign in with a session from their own company's identity provider. This also satisfies a host that enforces SSO.
  - It is never weaker than the host's policy: a host requiring 2FA needs MFA evidence from the provider (`amr`, SAML AuthnContext) or the other organization's attestation that its IdP enforces MFA.
  - Password sessions, social logins and third organizations' providers never count.
- **What the trust controls:**
  - a role ceiling (viewer or member; never administrator or owner);
  - whether those members may create API keys (off by default; a key never outlives their access);
  - an optional default end of access.
- **Ending a trust** suspends the host's members from that organization, in the host only.
- Migration 001320: `tenant_trusts`, `sessions.mfa_evidence`.

### Added: every retest is a scan run

- A scan run now has a `kind` (`scan`, `quick`, `retest`, `validation`, `test`,
  `connector`, `system`) and a `subject`. A run that executes no scan workflow
  (a retest) has no `scan_workflow_id`. Migration `001301`.
- Requesting a retest records a run of kind `retest` with one step. Both of the
  retest's sensor commands are tasks of that run, so their status and logs are
  read from the run page. The run ends when the retest reaches its verdict.
  `finding_retests.run_id` links the retest to its run, and the retest API
  returns it as `run_id`.
- `GET /api/v1/scan-runs` takes `kind` (comma-separated) and `include_system`.
  System runs are hidden unless one of these asks for them. Each run in the
  response carries `kind` and `subject`.

### Added: upgrade guide from v0.8.0

- `docs/operations/upgrade-v0.8-to-v0.9.md`: pre-flight checks and read-only inventory queries (checked against the v0.8.0 schema), image, Compose, Helm and environment changes, the two-hop database path through `pre-baseline-001146` with measured durations, the data migrations users notice, removed routes and permissions, sensor upgrade order and compatibility, identity provider changes, verification and rollback. Every step was run on a copy of a v0.8.0 database up to the new API.

### Added: every finding validation is a run

- Validating a finding (re-verify, auto-validation, a ticket rescan) now
  records a run of kind `validation`. Its task and logs are on the Runs page,
  and it names the person who asked. The run ends with the verdict, or fails
  when the sensor fails the check, reports no verdict, or the check cannot be
  queued.
- Like a retest run, a validation run is about a finding. Reading it needs
  `findings:read` and the finding in the caller's data scope (404 otherwise),
  and the Runs list leaves it out for callers who cannot see it.

### Added: software updates in the platform console

- A banner on every console page tells platform administrators about a security release that fixes an advisory affecting the running version (always shown) or a newer release (can be hidden until the next one).
- System > Software updates shows the running and latest versions, the advisories that affect the instance, newer releases with links to their notes, where the information came from and when, the last check's outcome, and, for super administrators, the offline import of the release feed file (RFC-105).
- Organization users see nothing of it.

### Added: version check for new and security releases

- The API reads a signed release feed once a day and the platform console tells platform administrators when a newer release exists or when the running release is affected by a published security advisory (RFC-105, `docs/architecture/version-check.md`).
- The request carries no instance id, no version and no counts: one anonymous download of a static file, compared on the instance. The feed is verified with a root key pinned in the build (Ed25519, the shared signed-feed format); rollback, expired and tampered feeds are refused.
- On by default; `VERSION_CHECK_ENABLED=false` stops the download, `VERSION_CHECK_URL` points at an https mirror. A second feed under an already applied sequence is refused unless its bytes are identical. Air-gapped instances fail silently, back off to weekly and can import the same file in the console (super administrator, step-up, audited).
- New console routes `GET /api/v1/admin/version-check/` (any administrator) and `POST /api/v1/admin/version-check/import` (super administrator + step-up). Migration `002717_version_check_state` (new table, instance-level).
- No usage telemetry is sent; its rules are recorded in RFC-105 as deferred and opt-in only.
- **Upgrade note:** nothing to do. The check stays inert until a release pins the release feed root.

### Added: VEX statements per organization

- `GET/POST /api/v1/vex-statements`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/vex-statements/{id}`: the organization states that a vulnerability does not affect a package (with a justification), affects it, is fixed in it or is under investigation; for every version, listed versions or a version range; on every asset or one asset; with an optional expiry.
- `not_affected` requests a false positive for the open findings it covers (a pending approval by the actor `vex`; the status does not change until approvers decide), `fixed` resolves them; `affected` and `under_investigation` annotate. The statement also covers findings reported later; editing, deleting or the expiry of a statement reopens the findings it closed unless another statement covers them. Findings from pentest, manual, bug bounty and red team sources are never closed.
- `POST /api/v1/vex-statements/import` stores the statements of an OpenVEX, CSAF VEX or CycloneDX VEX document (5 MB, 5 000 statements) for one asset or every asset; `dry_run=true` previews.
- Reading needs `components:read`; writing needs `findings:approve`, the asset in the caller's scope, and full data access for a statement on every asset. Every change, expiry and closure is audited (`vex_statement.*`).
- Migration `001902_vex_statements` adds `vex_statements` and `findings.vex_statement_id` (no data change).

### Added: Software tab, why-this-finding and vulnerability matching settings in the console

- Every asset drawer has a Software tab: products and versions, distribution builds, unrecognised names, last seen, and per product the CVEs that match it with severity, KEV, EPSS, confidence (likely or potential), the affected range, why the confidence was lowered, and whether it is a finding or below the policy; each CVE links to the asset's findings for it.
- A finding the vulnerability matcher created shows "Why this finding" (observed version, range, evidence, confidence) and "Version match" as what found it.
- Settings › Policies › Vulnerability matching (owners and admins): on/off, minimum confidence and severity, distribution builds, internet-facing only, muted products; saves are refused over a concurrent change.

### Added: findings for CVEs that affect the software an asset runs

- The `vuln-match` controller (RFC-066) evaluates each catalog version once against the NVD ranges of its product, then fans the result out to every asset that runs it. A new CVE published today reaches every affected organization without a rescan; an asset whose software changes is re-matched within a minute.
- Matches that pass the organization's policy become findings: technique `va`, tool `version-match`, the CVE, a confidence (80 for a CPE with a full version, 65 for a known product name, lower for partial versions and distribution builds) and the evidence (observed string, version, range). They use the same identity scanners use for that CVE on that asset and port; when a scanner or a person already has the CVE open on the asset, no second finding is made.
- The matcher closes only its own findings that no scanner has reported: `resolved` (version changed) when the software is upgraded out of range, `not_observed` when it was not seen for 30 days, `false_positive` (advisory updated) when the feed narrows the range; it reopens them when the software is back in range. Rejected CVEs are not auto-closed.
- Potential matches (confidence below 80) are capped at P2 unless the CVE is in KEV, and do not enter attack paths. "All versions" statements never become findings.
- Organization policy at `GET/PUT /api/v1/organization/settings/vuln-matching` (owner/admin, audited): on/off, minimum confidence (65), minimum severity (high; KEV or EPSS ≥ 0.1 always pass), distribution builds, internet-facing only, muted products.
- Ingest refuses findings from a report whose tool claims the reserved name `version-match`.
- Migration 001690 (`software_version_vulns`, `vuln_match_queue`, `vuln_match_state`, `software_versions.matched_at`).
- **Upgrade note:** organizations created from now on have matching on; existing organizations have it off until an admin turns it on. Findings appear once the platform imports vulnerability bundles (RFC-066 §5.5).

### Added: chunked vulnerability feed import with a resumable checkpoint

- The vulnerability bundle importer reads bundle format v2 through the sdk-go transfer layer when the release (or `VULNFEED_BUNDLE_DIR`) serves it: retries, Range resume, mirror fall-back (`VULNFEED_MIRRORS`, https only), a verified chunk cache, and each chunk applied in its own transaction with the `feed_checkpoints` row, so a crash resumes at the next chunk. The v1 reader stays the fallback for this release and shares the applied sequence and key-set version.
- Every check is kept: pinned root, key-set version, sequence newer than applied, delta on its base, expiry, size caps, per-record validation, and ranges must name CVEs and products of the same bundle.
- CVE records and ranges carry the bundle sequence (migration `cve_corpus_feed_sequence`: `feed_sequence` and `range_key` columns, table `cve_feed_products`, platform-wide, no tenant data). Replaced ranges are removed when the bundle finishes, where the removal guard now runs.
- The inventory matcher re-evaluates only CVEs whose record or ranges changed.

### Added: import of signed vulnerability bundles

- The `vuln-feed-import` controller (RFC-066 §5.5) imports the daily bundles the collector [openctemio/vulnfeed](https://github.com/openctemio/vulnfeed) publishes into the CVE corpus. The platform no longer needs to call any vulnerability source.
- Before anything is written it verifies the key set against the pinned offline root (and refuses a lower key-set version than one it accepted), the signed pointer and manifests, the sequence (no rollback, deltas only on their base), the 7-day expiry, every file's size and SHA-256, and every record with the platform's own parsers; a bundle that would remove more than 2 % of the stored ranges is refused. Record files are fetched only after the pointer verified, capped at the sizes the signed manifest states.
- Migration 001790 adds the `vulnfeed` threat-intel source, **disabled**.
- **Upgrade note:** set `VULNFEED_ROOT_KEY_ID` (the collector's root key id) and enable the source (`PATCH /api/v1/admin/threat-intel/sync/vulnfeed {"enabled": true}`). `VULNFEED_BASE_URL` points at a mirror; `VULNFEED_BUNDLE_DIR` reads a release's files from a local directory on an air-gapped platform. A warning is logged when no new bundle arrived for three days.

### Added: API descriptions of web origins and their drift

- `POST /api/v1/assets/{id}/api-specs` uploads an OpenAPI 3, Swagger 2, Postman 2.1, HAR 1.2 or GraphQL introspection
  document for a web origin; `GET /api/v1/assets/{id}/api-specs`, `GET /api/v1/api-specs/{id}`,
  `GET /api/v1/api-specs/{id}/drift` (shadow, orphan, zombie, parameter drift) and `DELETE /api/v1/api-specs/{id}`.
- Only the declared operations (method, path, parameter names, deprecated) and the document's digest are stored
  (migration 001299); the document, its examples and captured values are not. No remote reference is fetched.
  Design: RFC-056.

### Added: an asset's coverage on its page

- The asset page and the asset detail sheet gain a Coverage section (from
  `GET /api/v1/assets/{id}/coverage`): per capability the asset's type
  needs, its state (covered, due, running, failed, blocked, paused, not
  applicable), the reason it was skipped, when it last ran and when it is due
  next, the last error, and whether it is a coverage gap. English and
  Vietnamese.

### Added: data freshness on the asset page, a stale filter and the enrichment switch

- Asset detail (sheet and page) shows **Data freshness**: per attribute
  class (DNS records, domain registration, network owner, web service, TLS
  certificate, open ports) its state (live, stale, dead, never observed),
  the tool that last saw it, its freshness window, and the asset's automatic
  enrichment with a link to its run (RFC-075).
- Inventory > Signals: **Stale data** and **Never enriched** filters
  (`?freshness=stale|never`, deep-linkable).
- Attack surface > Monitoring: **Automatic enrichment** switch.
- All new text in English and Vietnamese.

### Added: asset Timeline in the web console

- The asset sheet has a Timeline tab and the asset page a Timeline card:
  changes newest first, grouped by day, filtered by attribute and source,
  with the old and new value, the deciding source and run, the reason, a
  count when a value flipped back and forth, and "Why this value".
- Discovery › Assets › Timeline lists the organization's recent asset
  changes (only assets you can see), filtered by attribute, source and asset
  tag (for example `bug-bounty`). English and Vietnamese.

### Added: Pull request feedback settings in the CI/CD console

- CI/CD > Trust and gate > **Pull request feedback**: install the GitHub App on
  an organization (the console completes GitHub's setup redirect at
  `/ci-cd/github-app/callback`), unbind installations, and connect or
  disconnect GitLab groups with a group access token (masked; never shown
  again). The gate reason for a secret already on the default branch has its
  label. English and Vietnamese.

### Added: the web console reports error kinds for operator alerting

- `POST /api/v1/client-errors` (public, rate limited per client address and overall) counts an error the
  web console hit, by kind only (`chunk_load`, `render`, `unhandled`, `other`), in
  `openctem_web_client_errors_total{kind}`. No message, stack, URL or user detail is accepted, logged or
  stored. A spike raises the WebClientErrors alert (for example the chunk-load errors after a broken deploy).
- The web console reports uncaught errors, unhandled rejections and errors caught by its error boundaries,
  throttled to one report per kind a minute and ten per page load.

### Added: web endpoints API

- `GET /api/v1/web-endpoints` (list query contract), `/web-endpoints/stats`, `/web-endpoints/{id}`,
  `/web-endpoints/{id}/parameters`, `PATCH /web-endpoints/{id}` (state active or ignored, labels; audit-logged)
  and `GET /api/v1/assets/{id}/web-endpoints`.
- An endpoint is visible exactly when its origin asset is: the caller's data scope is part of every list and count,
  and an out-of-scope or other-tenant id answers 404. Design: RFC-056.

### Added: "Add to scope" on an inventory selection

- Select assets in the inventory and choose "Add to scope": each name or public address becomes an exact scope entry in one request (one re-authentication for the batch). URLs and services are covered by their host; private and internal targets (scan zones decide), repositories and cloud accounts are skipped and counted. The result says what was added, what was already in scope and what was refused. Needs `attack_surface:scope:write`. The inventory's Scope column and "In scope" pill are translated (en, vi).

### Added: inventory triage in the web console

- The inventory shows each asset's scope standing from the scan gate ("In scope", "Not in scope · passive only", "Excluded", …) on desktop rows and phone cards, and lists discovered assets by default (RFC-054 §15).
- New filters (scope status, found by) and views (Not in scope, Discovered, Out of scope, New since last visit).
- Bulk actions "Mark out of scope" (exclusions, exact or by rule with a preview, or "Not ours") and "Archive", each with Undo.

### Added: path exclusions and their testing mode on the Scope page (web)

- Scope › "Put out of scope" can exclude only a path (RFC-056 §5): a host
  pattern, a path prefix and the methods it blocks, with a "block only what
  changes state" suggestion so read-only checks still run there.
- Out of scope shows a path exclusion as host + path, the methods it blocks
  and its testing mode (Blocked, Read-only, Allowed with the date it is
  blocked again).
- "Testing mode…" (exclusion approvers only) changes it in two steps: choose
  the mode and an end (required for Allowed, at most 90 days), then review
  what changes. The API asks for step-up, audits the change and notifies
  every administrator; it never widens scope beyond the organization's
  assets, and there is no switch that lifts every exclusion at once.

### Added: report templates page and Word reports in the report dialog

- Settings › Pentest methodology › Report templates lists the
  organization's Word templates, previews each with sample data, downloads
  the file and the starter template; owners and admins upload (with the
  check's warnings shown) and delete them.
- The report dialog offers Word (DOCX) when the organization has a template
  and sends the chosen template with the report.

### Added: review queue address rows explain themselves (web)

- An IP address in the review queue says why it waits ("Names never grant
  their addresses; this IP needs its own scope entry"), which in-scope names
  resolve to it, and the network it sits in (ASN and organization, and
  whether that matches your organization).
- It offers the fixes the server allows the viewer: "Add to scope: <IP>" and,
  when the organization matches, the /24 or /48 around it; a member gets a
  request. Shared CDN or cloud space says it cannot be added and offers
  nothing.
- Evidence from a sensor shows the sensor's name or "platform sensor", and
  "a removed sensor" instead of an id.
- Several scope fixes of one kind now name what each adds.

### Added: decide the review queue a rule at a time (web)

- Discovery › Attack surface › Review shows suggested rules (a wildcard per
  label level, an IP /24 or /48) with how many pending names each covers,
  which stay out and why, and the evidence (verified domain, discovering
  root, network). Shared or CDN addresses are never grouped.
- "Accept as rule" and "Reject as rule" open a preview of exactly what
  changes (names confirmed or marked not ours, names that stay out, the
  approvals the new entry or exclusion needs, step-up) and need a reason;
  the rule is created through the normal scope paths (RFC-054 §6.7).
- The queue filters by the reason a name was queued and shows what covers
  each name; a name nothing covers offers "Add to scope", since confirming
  records ownership but does not let scans reach it.
- The shared "Review changes" preview (`ScopeChangePreview`) is the one diff
  view for scope changes.

### Added: New Scan checks scope while you type, and picks a coverage level (web)

- New Scan and Quick scan send the targets to `POST /api/v1/scope/check`
  (debounced) and show each refused target with its reason and the fixes the
  server offers (add to scope, allow for N days, request access, approve,
  verify the domain, ...). Nothing is dispatched by the preview.
- New Scan has a coverage level: this host only, host and its subdomains, or
  also their IPs. Subdomains and addresses come from the inventory; each added
  target goes through the same scope check (an address needs its own IP
  scope entry).
- A scan create, edit, quick scan or trigger refused with
  `TARGET_OUT_OF_SCOPE` lists `details.refused[]` the same way, with the
  fixes, instead of one long toast.

### Added: scope policy settings page; scope refusals in words (web)

- Settings › Policies › Scope policy shows and edits the organization scope
  knobs (RFC-054 §6.3): widening approvals, one-off entries, their maximum
  length, the default probe tier and auto-join of discovered names. The values
  in effect (approvals needed now, the operator active-proof mode) are
  read-only; nothing turns scope checks off.
- "Add to scope" offers "this name only" or "this name and every name below
  it", permanent or one-off entries with a reason and a probe tier; members
  without the approve permission send a one-off request instead.
- Every scope refusal code, error code and fix action has an English and a
  Vietnamese message.

### Added: sensor grant view, narrowing and trust level in the console (RFC-052)

- The sensor detail has a **Grant** panel: profile, trust level, job types, zones, tools, capabilities, tier ceiling, target network and scope, credentials, results without a job and remote actions, with what applies now while the sensor is New. A list with no limit reads "Any", an empty one "None".
- **Promote to Trusted** (needs `sensors:grant:widen`, confirmed with what New means) and **Set back to New** (`sensors:grant:narrow`).
- **Edit / Narrow**: apply a profile or edit dimensions one by one. The form warns when a change widens the grant; the server decides and its refusal is shown as is. A grant changed by someone else in the meantime is reloaded.
- The sensor list flags **Legacy broad grant** (narrow it) and **New**.

### Added: pair a sensor from the console (RFC-052)

- Sensors → **Pair a sensor**: enter the code the sensor printed, or choose "Expect a sensor" to get a code for `openctemio-sensor pair <CODE>` and wait for it to connect. The dialog shows the fingerprint (three digits and three words), the host facts the sensor reports, the address the request came from and the key fingerprint; **Approve** stays disabled until "the fingerprint matches" is ticked and the step-up code or password is given. The profile list offers only the narrow profiles; the broad legacy grant is never offered. Every miss answers "Code not found or expired".
- Organization settings → **Require key-bound sensor identity**: turning it on needs `sensors:grant:narrow`, turning it off `sensors:grant:widen`. Where it is on, the key-based "Install sensor" flow is hidden and the empty sensor list offers pairing instead.

### Added: the web console asks to confirm your identity before sensitive actions

- When the API answers `403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED`, one shared dialog asks for an authenticator code (accounts with two-factor authentication) or the password, calls `POST /api/v1/auth/step-up`, and retries the action once. SSO accounts without an authenticator are offered "Sign in again". Cancelling leaves the action undone.

### Added: the Web surface page

- Assets > Web surface (`/assets/web`): origins with their coverage gap, endpoints (method and path template) with a
  detail drawer listing parameter names (never values), path patterns across origins, and the change feed.
- Endpoints under a scope exclusion show as "Excluded, untested" with a link to the exclusions, so no findings there
  is not read as safe. Sensitive-path catalog matches and endpoints answering without authentication are flagged.
- Paths render as text and are never opened from the page. `/assets/discovered-urls` now opens the endpoint list.
  Design: RFC-056.

### Added: web surface views, sensitive-path catalog, change feed and incremental template scans

- `GET /api/v1/web-path-patterns` (one path template across origins), `GET /api/v1/web-origins` (endpoints per origin
  with the coverage gap: excluded-untested, sensitive among them, sensitive answering without authentication),
  `GET /api/v1/web-endpoint-events` (appeared, returned, gone, status, auth, new parameter) and
  `GET /api/v1/web-path-catalog`. All within the tenant and the caller's data scope.
- Endpoints are labelled from a platform-curated sensitive-path catalog (`catalog_key`); `/web-endpoints/stats` reports
  `excluded_sensitive` and `unauth_sensitive`, and endpoints carry `exclusion_id` and their catalog entry.
- The change feed table `web_endpoint_events` (migration 001297). Retention: endpoints unseen 30 days become gone, gone
