  for a year are deleted; events are kept 90 days.
- A template step chained after a crawl can take only the endpoints found new or changed in the run
  (`endpoint_selector: new | changed`). Design: RFC-056.

### Added: Settings → Scanning → Tool defaults, and sensor Tool settings as overrides

- A new page, Settings → Scanning → Tool defaults, lists every tool that the organization's sensors report with settings. Owners and administrators edit each tool's organization defaults there, and the page lists any sensor whose tool version refuses them. Members with `sensors:read` see the page read-only.
- In a sensor's drawer, Tool settings now shows overrides only. Each option shows the value in use and where it comes from: the tool default, the organization, or this sensor. **Override** and **Reset to organization default** change that per option. A tool's summary reads "2 overridden". The effective table names the layers that each value overrides.
- The options come from each tool's own settings schema; no tool is hard-coded in the page.

### Added: Scope policy > Scan unclassified assets

- The scope policy form sets `unclassified_scans` (Off, Low-impact by
  default, Full) with a hint for each, and says when Strict scan approval
  keeps it off. Saving goes through the existing re-authentication, audit and
  administrator notice. Shown only when the API reports the setting.

### Added: workflow steps run as capability jobs

- A workflow step whose tool runs capability jobs on the sensor (subfinder, dnsx, naabu, httpx, katana, nuclei, trivy, semgrep, codeql, betterleaks) now names its capability in the command (`capability`, for example `scan.ports@1`). The sensor then checks:
  - that the tool implements the capability;
  - the tool's output against the capability's contract.

  It also records the capability in the result's provenance (RFC-055).
- The step's settings stay in `config`, mapped to the tool's keys as before, so a sensor older than the tool contract runs the step unchanged. Commands for other tools are unchanged.

### Added: see how a workflow step is shared between sensors

- `GET /pipeline-runs/{id}/stages` now gives each stage its chunk counts (total, queued, running, completed, failed) and the sensors that took them. A platform job is listed as platform, without naming the platform sensor.
- In the scan run panel, each stage lane shows "2 of 10 chunks done, 3 running, …" and the share per sensor. The workflow graph shows the chunks done and how many sensors work on each step.
- The workflow preview in the new-scan dialog shows each step's chunk size and how many sensors can work on it at once.

### Added: scan workflow drafts and publish

- The builder saves a draft, and saving never fails because of a problem in
  it: the layout and the edits are kept even when a pinned tool is missing.
  The draft autosaves shortly after each change, and leaving with unsaved
  changes asks first.
- Every issue of the draft is listed in a panel under the header and on each
  node, split into blocking issues and warnings, each with how to fix it.
  Choosing an issue selects its step.
- **Publish** makes the draft the steps runs use. It is refused (422 with
  every issue) while the draft has a blocking issue. Steps keep their ids
  and run history, the version moves on, and the draft is removed.
  **Discard draft** goes back to the published steps.
- Badges: Unsaved, Draft, Published vN.
- API: `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /api/v1/scan-workflows/{id}/draft` and
  `POST /api/v1/scan-workflows/{id}/publish`, gated like the workflow reads
  and writes. Migration 001329 adds `draft`, `draft_issues` and
  `draft_updated_at` to `scan_workflows`.

### Added: two sensors never scan the same host at once for workflow steps

- Now that a workflow step is shared between sensors, the platform keeps them off the same host at the same time. A chunk of an active step (port scan, HTTP probe, crawl, vulnerability templates) records the hosts it hits. While one sensor runs that chunk, no other chunk of the organization that touches one of those hosts is offered or can be claimed, and two sensors claiming at the same moment are serialized.
- A host is free again as soon as the chunk finishes, fails or is released, or its lease runs out. Passive steps (subdomain discovery, DNS resolution) are not limited. Another organization's work never holds yours back.
- Migration `001186_command_host_keys` adds `commands.host_keys` and a partial index. Each sensor's own per-host limit stays as a second line of defense.

### Added: workflow readiness, and a scan refuses a workflow that cannot run

- `GET /api/v1/scan-workflows?include=readiness` (and `GET /{id}?include=readiness`)
  says, for each workflow, whether it can run for the caller's organization
  now and why, per step:
  - `ready`: a tool that runs the step is on an online sensor allowed to run it;
  - `waiting`: such sensors exist but none is online;
  - `ci_only`: code analysis that runs in the CI images;
  - `blocked`: no enabled tool runs the step, or no sensor offers one.
  Each step carries a reason and a fix ("Add a sensor with naabu", "Enable
  httpx", "Set up the CI pipeline integration").
- Readiness is computed in one pass from the sources the dispatch gate reads
  (the tool catalog, the organization's sensors, grants, manifests and zones)
  and the platform scanning offer. Platform sensors appear only as platform
  scanning, never per sensor. The inputs are cached for 10 seconds per
  organization.
- Creating a scan with a blocked or CI-only workflow, or starting one, is
  refused with 400 `WORKFLOW_NOT_RUNNABLE`, naming the steps and why. A
  waiting workflow can be scheduled; a run now still needs an online sensor
  (`NO_SENSOR_FOR_TOOL`). Readiness is checked again when a run starts.

### Added: a workflow's steps read as stages

- The workflow detail sheet and the New-scan preview show a workflow's steps
  as stages computed from its dependency graph, not as a flat numbered list:
  - parallel steps share a stage, labelled "N in parallel";
  - a step that waits for several shows "Waits for: X, Y";
  - each step reads capability first, then how it picks its tool (Any tool,
    Preferred list, Pinned tool).
- A summary gives the most steps that can run at once, set against the
  max-parallel limit, the longest chain, and an upper bound on duration from
  the step timeouts.
- Inline warnings cover:
  - a tool no online sensor offers;
  - a max-parallel limit lower than what the graph allows;
  - unpublished draft changes, when the caller passes them.
- A cycle or a dependency on a missing step is shown as a problem.
- A Stages / Graph toggle opens a read-only graph, with "Open in builder".
- One shared component (`WorkflowStages`), with en and vi strings. Run pages
  can colour its steps by run status.

### Added: copies of system scan workflows are offered the template's later changes

- A tenant's copy of a system scan workflow keeps its lineage: the template it was made from and the template's steps as the copy took them. Copies made earlier get it from the audit event of the copy or from the template's name.
- When the template changes (Network gained Host discovery), the workflow builder shows "Update available: add Host discovery" with a preview of each change: steps the template added, and steps it rewired that the copy still has as they were.
- Applying it (scan workflows write) publishes a new version of the copy and is audited; dismissing keeps the copy and stops the offer. A tenant workflow is never changed on its own.
- API: `GET /api/v1/scan-workflows/{id}/template-update`, `POST .../template-update/apply`, `POST .../template-update/reject`.
- Migration `workflow_template_lineage`: two nullable columns on `scan_workflows` and a backfill of existing copies.

### Changed: the off-box audit sink delivers at least once from a durable cursor

- `ADMIN_AUDIT_SINK`: the administrators' audit rows are sent in batches with their hash-chain position and hash (not the request body or user agent), plus the chain head and the chain verification state; when nothing is new the head is sent every `ADMIN_AUDIT_SINK_HEAD_INTERVAL` (default 15 minutes). Destinations: `https://…` (HMAC-signed POST), `syslog+tls://` (optionally mutual TLS) or `file:///path` (one JSON batch per line).
- Delivery is at least once from a durable cursor (migration `admin_audit_forward_cursor`) that moves only after the destination accepted the batch, with a batch id, exponential backoff and lag, failure and chain-break metrics and logs (`openctem_admin_audit_forward_*`, `openctem_admin_audit_chain_ok`). The cursor controller runs on one replica at a time. The earlier in-memory queue, which dropped events when full, is gone.
- The shipped columns are an explicit list; a test fails when `admin_audit_logs` gets a column that is neither shipped nor withheld.
- Webhook requests carry `X-OpenCTEM-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp and body), `X-OpenCTEM-Timestamp` and `X-OpenCTEM-Batch-Id`.
- Mutual TLS for syslog: `ADMIN_AUDIT_SINK_SYSLOG_CA_FILE`, `ADMIN_AUDIT_SINK_SYSLOG_CLIENT_CERT`, `ADMIN_AUDIT_SINK_SYSLOG_CLIENT_KEY`.
- **Upgrade note:** optional; nothing changes unless `ADMIN_AUDIT_SINK` is set.

### Changed: access requests move to a Requests section in the admin console

- Access requests are now under Requests (`/admin/requests`); the old URL `/admin/organizations/access-requests` is gone.
- The console overview lists waiting access requests (a warning once the oldest has waited two days). `GET /api/v1/admin/overview` returns `requests.access_pending` and `requests.access_oldest_pending_seconds`.

### Changed: the all-in-one image is 30% smaller, its gateway is built with the current Go, and the sensor CA persists

- `ghcr.io/openctemio/openctem` copies the web and API files in once, owned by
  root, instead of `cp -a` + `chown -R`, which stored the web console twice and
  then the web console and API a third time (amd64: 197 MB compressed / 642 MB
  unpacked before, 138 MB / 423 MB after). The runtime user can no longer
  modify the application; `/data`, `/config` and the Next.js cache stay
  writable.
- The runtime base is plain Alpine with node copied from the web image (no
  npm), instead of the node image.
- Caddy (same release, v2.11.4) is compiled with the pinned Go toolchain and
  current `golang.org/x/net` and gRPC instead of copying the released binary,
  which carried an older Go standard library: 20 HIGH advisories fewer in the
  image scan.

### Changed: the API image is distroless (no shell, no busybox)

- `openctem-api` is built on `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot`. It
  contains the four binaries, the OpenAPI spec, migrations, configs, CA
  certificates and time zones, and nothing else: no shell, no busybox
  `wget`, no package manager (42.7 MB compressed, amd64).
- Users, uids, paths, writable directories and the entrypoint are unchanged
  (`USER` is now numeric, `1000:1000`).
- Healthchecks use the binaries themselves: `server -healthcheck` for the API
  and the new `openctem-signer healthcheck` (connects to the signer socket)
  in `docker-compose.job-signer.yml`, replacing `test -S`.
- Debugging: there is no shell to `docker exec` into. Use an ephemeral debug
  container (`docker debug <container>`, or
  `kubectl debug -it <pod> --image=busybox --target=api`) or run the image's
  binaries directly (`docker run --entrypoint /app/bootstrap-admin ...`).

### Changed: the API image's operator commands are links to the server binary

- `bootstrap-admin`, `refingerprint`, `repomerge` and `ci-trust-scope-plan` in
  the `openctem-api` image are now links to `/app/server`, which runs the
  command named by the link. Each was a static binary that linked most of the
  API (17-26 MB each); the image drops from 175 MB to about 97 MB unpacked,
  and the all-in-one image drops its second copy of `bootstrap-admin`.
- Paths, flags and output are unchanged: `docker compose exec api
  /app/bootstrap-admin ...`, `docker run --entrypoint /app/repomerge ...` and
  `go run ./cmd/<command>` work as before. The job signer stays a binary of
  its own.

### Changed: the API image is half the size and its files are read-only to the API

- `openctem-api` no longer stores every binary twice: the files are owned by
  root at copy time instead of a later `chown -R /app`, which duplicated the
  whole application in a new layer (amd64: 87.8 MB compressed / 250 MB
  unpacked before, 45.9 MB / 131 MB after).
- The binaries, OpenAPI spec, migrations and configs are owned by root, so the
  API process (uid 1000) can no longer modify its own code. The writable paths
  are unchanged: `/app/data` (attachments, sensor CA) for the API, and
  `/var/lib/openctem-signer` and `/run/openctem-signer` for the job signer.
- The four binaries are built in one `go build` with `-trimpath` (no builder
  paths in the binaries) and a BuildKit build cache.

### Changed: every list validates its paging the same way

- The latest-N lists (asset merge log, tag suggestions, EASM rules, a
  finding's retests, sensor activity and manifests) read `limit` with one
  shared parser: a value that is not a positive whole number is refused
  with 400 instead of being ignored, and a value above the list's maximum
  is lowered to it. The pentest campaign, finding and template lists and
  the simulation runs list read `page` and `per_page` with the shared page
  parser. A test now fails on any handler that reads paging parameters
  itself.

### Changed: more list endpoints share one page parser

- Attacker profiles, business services and units, compensating controls,
  compliance frameworks, controls and assessments, CTEM cycles, remediation
  campaigns, report schedules, threat actors, threat models and the admin
  console's audit log, target mappings, users and organizations read `page`
  and `per_page` with the shared parser. A non-numeric or non-positive value
  is now refused with 400 instead of silently becoming the first page;
  `per_page` above 100 is capped at 100 (the admin organizations list
  allowed 200).

### Changed: state history and service lists page with page / per_page

- `GET /state-history` (and its views: appearances, disappearances,
  newly-exposed, exposure-changes, shadow-it, compliance),
  `GET /assets/{id}/state-history`, `GET /services` and
  `GET /services/public` take `page` and `per_page` (max 100) and return
  the list envelope (`data`, `total`, `page`, `per_page`, `total_pages`).
  `limit` and `offset` are no longer read (they allowed 1000 rows per
  request). The web's "What changed" page and the asset rename history use
  the new parameters.

### Changed: the remaining page / per_page lists share one page parser

- Twenty-six more list handlers read `page` and `per_page` with the shared
  parser: API keys, asset groups, relationships and types, branches,
  capabilities, CI admin, coverage and pipelines, commands, components,
  EASM review, exposures, finding sources, the sensor fleet, notifications,
  relationship suggestions, scanner templates, scan profiles, scope, sensors
  and sensor results, tools and tool categories, findings and automations,
  and the audit log. A `page` of 0 or a non-numeric `page` / `per_page` is
  refused with 400 instead of being read as the first page; `per_page` is
  capped at 100 (the audit log had no cap; lists with a lower cap keep it).

### Changed: indicators, notification history and CTEM IDs page with page / per_page

- `GET /iocs`, `GET /iocs/{id}/matches` and `GET /iocs/matches` take `page`
  and `per_page` (default 50, max 200) and answer `items`, `page` and
  `per_page`. `GET /integrations/{id}/notification-events` and
  `GET /ctem-ids` take `page` and `per_page` (max 100); the notification
  history answers the list envelope (`data`, `total`, `page`, `per_page`,
  `total_pages`). `limit` and `offset` are no longer read, and a
  non-numeric or non-positive value is refused with 400. The indicators
  panel and the notification history use the new parameters.

### Changed: waiting lowerings of the false-positive settings are shown with their time and can be canceled

- Settings → Finding approvals shows a waiting lower false-positive level and,
  new, a waiting lower second-look share, each with the time it takes effect,
  and a "Cancel the change" button (for members with `settings:write`) that
  keeps the value in force. The form warns that a lower share waits 24 hours.
  English and Vietnamese.

### Changed: the approvals inbox names the requester, is translated and is in the main menu

- `GET /api/v1/approvals` returns `requested_by_name` for each request: the requester's name when they are a current member of the organization (looked up in the caller's organization only); a former member and an AI triage or VEX request have no name.
- The approvals inbox has a Requester column ("You", the member's name, "Former member", or the platform actor), and Approve and Reject are disabled on the viewer's own request with the reason shown (the server still refuses a self-approval).
- Every text on the inbox and the request dialog is translated (English and Vietnamese).
- "Approvals" is a main menu entry under Findings; for approvers it shows the number of pending requests in their data scope.
- The requester of a pending request can remind its approvers from the inbox (at most once an hour; uses `POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/remind`). The inbox shows the request's decide-by date, and the acceptance end is labelled as such.

### Changed: background jobs read a tenant's assets in id-ordered batches

- The relationship-suggestion, graph-enrichment and certificate-monitor jobs
  read every asset of a kind with LIMIT/OFFSET pages of 100-200 and a
  `COUNT(*)` per page, which is quadratic in tenant size. They now page by id
  (`ListAfterID`) in batches of 1,000 without a count. On a tenant with 110k
  assets, one pass over its domains went from 811 queries (345 s of database
  time) to 73 queries (3.4 s).
- Id-ordered paging also no longer skips or repeats an asset created while
  the read is running.

### Changed: the asset header names its state and says whether scans can reach the asset

- The asset drawer's header shows the scan-scope answer next to the lifecycle state ("In scope", "Not in scope · passive only", "Excluded", "Not ours" …), the same answer the inventory's Scope column and the scan gate give. It used to appear only in the Details tab.
- Criticality, exposure and the network zone are named in the header ("Criticality: Medium", "Exposure: Public", "Zone: Internal"). The zone (the asset field `scope`: internal, external, cloud …) is not the scan scope; its tooltip says so. Without names, "Internal" next to "Public" read as a contradiction.
- The drawer's tabs, menu and the badge labels and descriptions are translated (en, vi).

### Changed: asset Properties rendered from the property schema

- The Properties section of an asset follows its type's property schema (RFC-042 §6.3.9). Labels are in the viewer's language (English or Vietnamese) and in schema order. Each address links to its IP asset in the inventory, and URLs open only when they are http(s). An older row's synonyms (`ip`, `resolved_ips`, ...) show once, under "IP addresses". Third-party and custom keys are listed under "Other".
- The property filter and its chips use the same labels. The host and network pages, the export, the external-surface facts and the scope preview read addresses through the one schema helper.

### Changed: clearer labels for HTTP facts and asset sub-types

- The property `server` (synonym `web_server`) is labelled "HTTP server header" (vi "Header Server (HTTP)"): it is the `Server` response header a web probe recorded, and "Server" alone read as the organisation that runs the machine. `title` is labelled "Page title". Registry change only (`api/configs/asset-types.yaml`); no stored data changes.
- The asset drawer's type line shows the sub-type in words ("Host · Workstation", not "Host · workstation").

### Changed: stored asset properties normalised to the property schema (migration 001185)

- Migration 001185 folds the property synonyms of every stored asset into the canonical key: `ip`, `ips`, a plain `ip_address` string, `resolved_ip`, `resolved_ips` and `addresses` become `ip_addresses` (addresses in canonical form, non-addresses dropped; the technical `ip_address` object stays). `nameserver`, `technology` and `san` become `nameservers`, `technologies` and `sans`. It also removes keys that only other classes may hold, such as a port, HTTP status or banner on a domain, host or IP address (RFC-042 §6.3.9).
- `updated_at` is unchanged. The previous properties are kept only until migration 001481 drops the ledger; take a backup before upgrading if you may need them.
- **Upgrade note:** deploy the release that folds synonyms on write (#1311) with or before this migration. Run the migration explicitly; `air` does not run migrations.

### Changed: the console says when a risk score is not computed yet, and why a score is what it is

- An asset that was never scored shows "Not yet scored" and a first score in
  the queue "Calculating…", instead of a score of 0; a queued rescore keeps
  the score with a spinner. The asset's Risk card shows when the score was
  last computed.
- "Why this score?" on the asset's Risk card lists the model's factors
  (findings per severity with exploitable counts, exposure, effective
  criticality, compensating controls) and the open findings that drive the
  score, each linked to the finding.
- Risk level labels follow the organization's bands everywhere and are
  translated: 0 reads "No open risk" and a score below the low band "Minimal"
  (it read "Info").

### Changed: the scan wizard expands coverage with one inventory request

- `GET /assets` takes `under` (comma-separated DNS names, at most 10): the names equal to or below them, with the caller's data scope. The new-scan coverage expansion asks once for every typed domain instead of one search per domain.

### Changed: a repository opens at its asset URL

- The repository workspace (overview, branches and branch compare, findings by branch and scanner, scan settings) is shown at `/assets/{id}` for a repository asset, like every other asset; `/assets/repositories/{id}` is gone, with no redirect. Links from CI pipelines and the rest of the console use `/assets/{id}`.
- **Upgrade note:** bookmarks to `/assets/repositories/{id}` answer 404; use `/assets/{id}`.

### Changed: Attack surface Suggestions tab with a Decide panel

- The Attack surface Review tab is now Suggestions. Each scope decision that
  still needs a person is one card: addresses behind your in-scope names,
  confirmed assets no scope entry covers, and the suggested rules for names
  found outside your scope. The tab and sidebar badge count cards, not rows.
  The overview shows the same cards; "Not now" hides a card there for a week.
- The row list stays one click away under "Show all items". A host row shows
  the services, certificates and web endpoints that follow it. The confirm
  action reads "Ours: add to scope", and the toast names the scope entries it
  added, with Undo.
- An address in a published CDN edge range is shown as shared space in the
  review rows too, and no scope fix is offered for it.
- Every string in the review queue, the overview card, the review reasons, the
  rule dialog and the asset Ownership card now comes from the en and vi
  dictionaries. The Scope settings page has a switch for
  `confirm_adds_to_scope`.

### Changed: automations are named automations in the database and the Go code (migration 001613)

- Migration 001613 renames the automation tables: `workflows` to `automations`, `workflow_nodes` to `automation_nodes`, `workflow_edges` to `automation_edges`, `workflow_runs` to `automation_runs` and `workflow_node_runs` to `automation_run_steps`; the `workflow_id` / `workflow_run_id` columns to `automation_id` / `automation_run_id`; and every index, constraint, trigger and RLS policy named after them. Rows and ids are unchanged. There are no compatibility views.
- The Go packages `internal/app/workflow` and `pkg/domain/workflow` are now `internal/app/automation` and `pkg/domain/automation`; the postgres repositories are `Automation*Repository`.
- The HTTP API (`/api/v1/workflows`), the permission ids and the module id are unchanged by this entry.
- **Upgrade note:** one step. Stop the old api, run the migration, start the new api: an api from before this release cannot read the renamed tables. Custom SQL or BI queries on the old table names must use the new ones. Run the migration explicitly; `air` does not run migrations.

### Changed: the session bootstrap carries the platform announcements

- `GET /api/v1/me/bootstrap` returns the active platform announcements in `announcements` (the same list `GET /api/v1/announcements` returns in `data`; an empty list when none is active). The web app shows the announcement banner from the bootstrap and no longer requests `/announcements` on every page load. `GET /api/v1/announcements` stays for other clients.

### Changed: the Approvals badge comes with the session bootstrap

- `GET /me/bootstrap` returns `badges.pending_approvals`: the finding approval
  requests waiting for a decision, counted as `GET /approvals` counts them
  (the caller's data scope applies). Only for callers with `findings:approve`
  and the findings module on, the same audience the badge had.
- The web reads it from the bootstrap instead of asking `GET /approvals` on
  every page load, and refreshes it after a decision on the inbox.

### Changed: emails, reports, notifications and API pages name the configured brand

- Every text the API writes for people now names `BRAND_NAME` instead of a
  fixed "OpenCTEM": report footers and scheduled report subjects, test
  notifications and their footers, Jira and GitHub ticket comments, CI pull
  request comments, MCP texts, the OAuth error page, the API reference page,
  generated sensor configuration and the admin two-factor issuer.
- Emails carry `BRAND_EMAIL_FOOTER` and, for a brand other than OpenCTEM,
  the "Powered by OpenCTEM" credit unless `BRAND_POWERED_BY=false`.
- Documentation links of sensor configuration checks and the welcome email
  point at `BRAND_DOCS_URL`, keeping their path.
- Technical identifiers do not change (headers, image names, the CI check
  name, protocol and policy identifiers). With no `BRAND_*` set, every text
  is as before.

### Changed: changelog entries are one file per change

- Unreleased entries live in `api/changelog.d/<short-slug>.md`, one file per
  change, instead of the top of `api/CHANGELOG.md`, so pull requests no longer
  conflict on the changelog. The release folds them in with
  `api/scripts/changelog.py release vX.Y.Z`.
- API CI refuses an entry written under Unreleased in `CHANGELOG.md` and any
  merge-conflict marker committed in a tracked text file.

### Changed: CI runs the API and web test suites in parallel shards

- API tests, the least-privilege tests and the web Vitest suite run as parallel shards, and lint runs in its own job, so a push waits for the slowest shard instead of the whole suite.

### Changed: pull request CI survives migration number clashes and skips code suites for docs

- PR CI renumbers, in the runner only, a PR's migrations whose number
  develop took in the meantime, so the DB-backed tests run on the tree the
  merge queue will merge instead of failing on a duplicate version. A
  duplicate between the PR and its base is a warning on the PR; the merge
  queue and pushes still fail it.
- Documentation (`*.md`, `api/docs/**`, agent notes) no longer starts the Go
  or web suites or the API/Web Security workflows; the changelog check moved
  to API CI's always-running `changes` job.
- Docs check cancels superseded PR runs; the secret-scan and workflow-lint
  tool downloads retry.

### Changed: CI snippets and how-tos pin openctemio/ci v0.2.0

- The GitHub and GitLab snippets on the CI/CD integration page and the CI
  how-tos pin `openctemio/ci` v0.2.0 (diff-aware SAST on pull requests, the
  scanned image's digest, `.openctem.yml` gate settings, and OIDC reporting
  from Azure Pipelines, Bitbucket, CircleCI and Jenkins). The v0.9 upgrade
  guide no longer points at the `@v1` ref, which has no matching scanner
  images; pin a full release tag.

### Changed: CI guides pin the sensor image by digest and document the runner's security controls

- The GitLab and GitHub examples in the CI how-tos run a sensor release pinned by digest instead of the moving `latest-ci` tag, with the cosign command to verify a digest before pinning it.
- The GitLab guide's security notes cover protected refs, the run token's least privilege, budgets, secret handling, the minimum runner version, gate enforcement and audit.

### Changed: developers see the CI runs of the repositories their team owns

- A developer sees a repository's CI runs, pipelines and coverage when the repository asset is in their data scope. Making their team (a group) an owner of the repository asset gives them the runs, and leaving the team takes them away. A test covers both. RFC-051 §6.1 documents this, and notes that matching the person who pushed the commit is not built yet.

### Changed: CI gate verdicts link to the run on the CI/CD page

- The `links.run` URL of a gate verdict (printed by the CI job) and the
  break-glass notice now open `/ci-cd?view=runs&run=<run id>` directly instead
  of the retired `/ci-runners/<run id>` path.

### Changed: a task waiting on a few busy hosts starts its other targets

- When a sensor has free scan slots, a queued task of a run step waits whole no longer because a few of its hosts are busy in another task: the claim splits it. The targets on free hosts start at once in the task; the others wait in a new task of the same step and run, which starts when their hosts are free.
- Only tasks with at most half of their targets on busy hosts are split, and a task is split at most 3 times, so a step never breaks into a task per host. Concurrent claims split a task once. The step, its targets' outcomes and its progress count both parts.
- New metric `command_host_splits_total`. Migration: `commands.host_splits` (smallint, default 0; no table rewrite).

### Changed: memory limits for every long-running Compose service

- Postgres (`POSTGRES_MEMORY_LIMIT`, default 4g) and Redis
  (`REDIS_MEMORY_LIMIT`, 1g) get limits like the other services, the job
  signer gets 256m and log rotation, and the API sets `GOMEMLIMIT`
  (`API_GOMEMLIMIT`, 1600MiB, about 80% of its 2g limit) so the Go runtime
  collects garbage before the limit kills it.
- The web console runs under an init process, waits for a healthy API, and the
  gateway waits for a healthy web console.

### Changed: the Compose stack sizes PostgreSQL for its host

- The bundled PostgreSQL in `api/deploy/docker-compose.yml` ran with the
  built-in defaults: 128 MB `shared_buffers`, 4 MB `work_mem` and a
  `random_page_cost` meant for spinning disks.
- It now starts with settings for an 8 GB host: 1 GB `shared_buffers`, 3 GB
  `effective_cache_size`, 16 MB `work_mem`, 256 MB `maintenance_work_mem`,
  `random_page_cost` 1.1, 2 GB `max_wal_size` and a 256 MB `/dev/shm`.
  Override them with `PG_SHARED_BUFFERS`, `PG_EFFECTIVE_CACHE_SIZE`,
  `PG_WORK_MEM`, `PG_MAINTENANCE_WORK_MEM`, `PG_RANDOM_PAGE_COST`,
  `PG_MAX_WAL_SIZE` and `PG_SHM_SIZE` (see `.env.example`).
- Measured on a 525k-finding tenant with 2 PostgreSQL CPUs: an interactive
  mix of list and stats reads at 10 users went from 12.9 to 17.7 requests/s,
  and the median latency from 370 ms to 223 ms.
- Upgrade note: on a host with less than 4 GB of memory, set
  `PG_SHARED_BUFFERS=256MB` and `PG_EFFECTIVE_CACHE_SIZE=768MB` before the
  next `up`.

### Changed: the Compose deployment sends SSO to the public URL; backups and monitoring work out of the box

- The API in `api/deploy/docker-compose.yml` gets
  `OAUTH_FRONTEND_CALLBACK_URL=<OPENCTEM_PUBLIC_URL>/auth/callback` (SSO logins
  went to `http://localhost:3000`) and `METRICS_TOKEN` (empty: metrics off). It
  drops every Linux capability; API, web and gateway have memory limits
  (`API_MEMORY_LIMIT`, `WEB_MEMORY_LIMIT`, `GATEWAY_MEMORY_LIMIT`).
- `versions.yaml`: the newest sensor is v0.11.0 (it said v0.6.4) and the oldest
  supported is v0.9.0 (protocol v1 is retired, older sensors cannot connect);
  the newest SDK is v0.18.0. The Sensors page, install snippets and Compose
  defaults follow.
- New `api/deploy/backup.sh`: `backup` (database, attachments, gateway CA, .env;
  retention; node-exporter metrics for the BackupStale/BackupFailed alerts),
  `verify` (restore into a throwaway Postgres and compare row counts) and
  `restore <dir> --yes`.
- New `deploy/observability/docker-compose.openctem.yml` overlay: monitors the
  shipped stack (network, `web` service, Postgres TLS, Redis over TLS verified
  against the datastore CA). The Postgres monitor role now gets CONNECT, which the
  least-privilege roles revoke from PUBLIC (`pg_up` was 0).

### Changed: the console has one Health page and one Platform scanning page

- Monitoring > Health now holds what Health (`/operations`) and System (`/system`) showed: services, storage, backup, certificates, schema and version, work queues, sensors and background jobs. The duplicated version, database and service blocks are gone.
- Scanning > Platform scanning (`/scanning/platform`) now holds what Platform scanning (`/system/platform-scanning`) and Shared sensors (`/system/shared-sensors`) showed, as the tabs Policy, Fleet, Queue, Zones, Egress and Anomalies. While shared sensors are not available in the release, the page shows one notice and the domain-proof policy instead of empty fleet tables.
- The language of the console can be chosen from the sidebar footer, and the last hard-coded English texts of the console moved to the translation files (English and Vietnamese).
- **Upgrade note:** the pages `/operations`, `/system`, `/system/platform-scanning` and `/system/shared-sensors` no longer exist and there are no redirects; update bookmarks to `/health` and `/scanning/platform`. The configuration overview and the "Needs attention" list link to the new pages.

### Changed: platform console navigation and overview

- The console sidebar groups pages as Customers, Scanning, Security, Settings
  and Monitoring; every scanning page sits under Scanning, and the personal
  security keys moved to the sidebar footer next to the signed-in
  administrator.
- A super admin acting read-only now sees every page; a page that needs a
  higher acting role offers the elevation in place instead of saying "Super
  admin only".
- The Overview's "Needs attention" list now shows services that do not
  answer, volumes running out of space, failed, stale or unreported backups,
  certificates close to expiry and newer releases.
- Lists that are empty without any search or filter no longer suggest
  adjusting one. The console has a "Skip to content" link, and the temporary
  password form and shell messages are translated.

### Changed: the platform console's site defaults to port 8443

- In port mode (`OPENCTEM_ADMIN_SITE=port`, the Compose default) the console's site is `https://<OPENCTEM_HOSTNAME>:8443`; change it with `OPENCTEM_ADMIN_PORT` if the port is taken. The gateway refuses a console port equal to 80, 443 or `GATEWAY_HTTPS_PORT`, and one out of range.
- `setup.sh` sets each console setting on its own: `--admin-site port|host|off`, `--admin-host`, `--admin-port`, `--admin-cidrs`, `--admin-public`, and recommends a host name of its own for production.
- `OPENCTEM_ADMIN_BIND` (optional) publishes the console port on one interface only, such as a private or VPN address: a published container port is not filtered by the host firewall.

### Changed: credential stats in one query

- `GET /credentials/stats` counts by state and by severity with one grouped query instead of thirteen; the numbers are unchanged.

### Changed: the dashboard overview is reused briefly and capped per organization

- `GET /api/v1/dashboard/overview` runs twelve tenant-wide reads. Identical
  concurrent calls from the same session now share one computation, and the
  result is reused for 15 seconds. Nothing is shared between users or
  sessions, so each caller still sees only what its own permissions and data
  scope allow.
- One organization runs at most four overview reads at a time. A burst of
  dashboard loads in one organization queues instead of taking every database
  connection. On a 525k-finding tenant, 50 concurrent loads used to time out
  (and, before the timeout fix, crash the API). Ten cold loads now finish in
  5.6 s and repeat loads in under 100 ms.
- The tenant-wide aggregate endpoints (dashboard metrics, finding and asset
  stats, finding groups, threat-intel stats, attack-surface stats, paths and
  chains) run at most four at a time per organization. Extra requests wait,
  and a request that gives up waiting gets 503 with `Retry-After`.

### Changed: sdk-go v0.19.0 and sensor v0.12.0

- The api builds against the released sdk-go v0.19.0 instead of a pseudo-version.
- versions.yaml: sensor latest v0.12.0 (passive rdap/asn lookup tools, sensor-side scope limits), SDK latest v0.19.0.

### Changed: Documentation of repository scope entries and CI trusts

- RFC-054 §17 covers repository entries, shared code hosts, a CI trust's managed entries, evidence, opt-in proof and the threat table.
- RFC-091 adds the planner rule (a covering repository entry and the organization's own code-host credential).
- The CI runner architecture doc gains a "Trust and scope" section.

### Changed: documentation of what ingest makes of a collector report

- `docs/architecture/sensors.md` ("What ingest makes of a collector report") lists how each field the asset collector sends is stored: relationships, directory identity, last-seen time, owners, private DNS zones, network device matching and complete reports from trusted collectors.

### Changed: documentation for the platform console as its own service

- New architecture page `docs/architecture/platform-console.md`; the Docker deployment guide documents the four console settings, host mode as the recommended production setup, the all-in-one image's console port, and the IdP redirect URI at the console's root. The release image list includes `openctem-console`.

### Changed: the apex exclusions the wildcard rule change made redundant are removed

- When `*.x` meant "the subdomains only", an upgrade added an apex exclusion
  `x` beside every wildcard exclusion `*.x` (created by
  `system:migration-000292`). Since `*.x` covers `x` again (RFC-054 S1), such
  a row is redundant while its wildcard parent is in effect at least as
  long. Migration `001164` deletes those rows: untouched since the upgrade,
  active, and under an active, approved parent that never expires or expires
  no earlier.
- Every other such row (its parent was removed, deactivated, shortened or is
  still pending, or a person changed it) stays as a standalone exclusion,
  with a reason that says so: "Apex of the former wildcard exclusion
  `*.x` (id), kept as its own exclusion when the wildcard rule changed
  (2026-10)", followed by the original reason.
- Nothing that is excluded today becomes scannable. No audit rows are written
  from SQL (the audit log is hash-chained by the application); this entry
  records the change. The down migration restores the previous rows and
  wording.

### Changed: 117 redundant indexes dropped

- Migration 001057 drops indexes that another index on the same table
  already covers: exact duplicates (usually a plain index next to the UNIQUE
  constraint on the same column) and left prefixes of a wider btree index
  with the same predicate. Queries use the covering index instead; writes
  and vacuum get cheaper. No index that backs a primary key, unique
  constraint or foreign key is dropped. The down migration recreates them.

### Changed: the "addresses your in-scope names resolve to" card explains its value and shows evidence

- The card says why it matters (only the names are scanned today, so a
  service on the address without a name is missed) and lists, for each
  address, the open ports seen on it or on its names and the other names
  that resolve to it (`ports`, `other_names`).
- An address inside an announced prefix of the organization's own seeded
  network offers that prefix as one CIDR rule (`prefix_rules`), only when the
  platform guardrails accept it; adding it goes through the scope service
  (step-up, approvals, audit).
- Shared, CDN and hosting addresses stay out of the count, listed as
  "Shared, not offered". "Not ours" records a rejection, so the addresses are
  never suggested or scanned again (undo on the toast). "Not now" hides the
  card on the overview for 30 days, or until it shows a new address, port or
  name. While unclassified assets get low-impact checks, only addresses whose
  network is unknown wait for a decision.

### Changed: discovered services, certificates and web endpoints follow their host

- A service, certificate or web endpoint that discovery left waiting for
  review is now linked to the host it was seen on (by a stored relationship
  of the organization, or by the host in its own name) and carries the
  host's state. Confirming, rejecting or scoping the host decides its
  children too; a person can still decide a child on its own, which ends
  the link.
- The Attack surface review queue lists the host only, with how many
  services, certificates and web endpoints follow it; its count no longer
  counts children.
- Upgrade note: migration `attribution_children_follow_host` adds a nullable
  column and links existing pending children of pending hosts by stored
  relationship. It changes no state and is safe on populated tables.

### Changed: APP_URL alone sets the frontend URLs

- When `APP_URL` is set, the API derives the defaults of `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (the APP_URL origin), `SMTP_BASE_URL` (APP_URL) and `OAUTH_FRONTEND_CALLBACK_URL` (APP_URL + `/auth/callback`); the SSO redirect allow-list follows. An explicit value still wins. Without `APP_URL` the localhost development defaults stay.
- A malformed `APP_URL` (not http/https, or with credentials, query or fragment) now stops startup instead of silently producing localhost links in e-mails.
- Docker Compose: `OPENCTEM_PUBLIC_URL` is optional and defaults to `https://<OPENCTEM_HOSTNAME>`; set it only when browsers use another port. The API service passes `APP_URL` alone.

### Changed: the session and OAuth state secrets are derived; no default database password; no plaintext credentials

- `AUTH_JWT_SECRET` is optional: unset, it is derived from `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (HKDF-SHA256, 64 bytes). Rotating the encryption key then also signs every user out; set `AUTH_JWT_SECRET` to rotate the two independently (docs/deployment/encryption-key-rotation.md). Docker Compose no longer requires it.
- `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` is optional in production too: unset, it is derived from the session secret under its own label.
- **Behaviour change:** `DB_PASSWORD` has no default (it was `secret`). Outside `APP_ENV=development` startup refuses an empty one.
- **Removed:** `APP_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT_CREDENTIALS`. Credentials are always encrypted; the server refuses to start without `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in every environment (a development checkout uses the key in `api/.env.example`). Startup refuses the variable with a hint.

### Changed: the finding drawer says each thing once, in plain words

- The title reads like a sentence: a leading package prefix the scanner repeats is dropped ("django: Django SQL injection" → "Django SQL injection") or moved to the end ("Arbitrary command execution in PyYAML"), a secret is named by its kind and file ("Generic API Key in app/settings.py"), and a SAST finding uses the scanner's message instead of the rule slug. The stored title is unchanged.
- The line under the title names the CVE or rule, the package and version (or file and line) and the asset, instead of repeating the technique.
- The priority appears once, in "Why it matters", which now explains the deadline when it differs from the severity's window ("The deadline follows the priority (P2: 15 days), not the severity (critical: 2 days)"). The remediation-window text is translated.
- Tags show only labels people set (the scanner's tool name, finding type and file are left out); "Occurrences" reads "Seen in N scans"; the finding ID moved to the ⋯ menu ("Copy finding ID").
- The description renders `inline code` from advisories, is collapsed to four lines with "Show more", and no longer flashes the code snippet before the finding loads.
- The SLA window is no longer requested for a nil or free-text asset id.

### Changed: closing a finding needs evidence in proportion to risk; risk acceptance is capped by priority

- A person resolving a critical, P0 or known-exploited (KEV) finding needs a
  retest that confirmed the fix, or the verification checklist completed by a
  second person. A high or P1 finding needs the verification checklist (or a
  confirming retest). Medium and low findings close with a note, as before.
  The status menu and the bulk preview show the reason a resolve is blocked
  (`evidence_required`, `checklist_required`); `PATCH /status` answers 400.
  Evidence counts only when it is newer than the finding's last reopen and
  last sighting: a retest or checklist from before a regression is stale.
- An accepted risk may last at most 30 days for P0 or KEV, 90 for P1, 180 for
  P2 and 365 for P3. A request with no end gets 90 days or the cap when
  shorter; an end past the cap is refused, never shortened. The finding
  response carries `max_acceptance_days` and the approval dialog limits its
  date to it. A finding accepted by a suppression rule ends at the rule's end
  or its priority cap, whichever is sooner.
- Migrations `002541_acceptance_cap_review` and
  `002542_acceptance_cap_review_validate`: accepted findings whose end is past
  the new cap are flagged for review (`acceptance_exceeds_cap`, with a timeline
  entry), not shortened; the migration reports how many.

### Changed: the web console offers the status moves the API allows

- The finding status menu (drawer, properties, remediation task) lists the moves from `GET /findings/{id}/transitions` for the signed-in user. An allowed move can be chosen; a blocked one is shown disabled with the reason, for example "Needs the findings:verify permission" or "Only the assignee, an assigned group member or the asset owner can claim a fix". The menu loads its moves when it opens.
- A bulk status change first runs the dry run (`POST /findings/transitions/preview`), sends only the findings that may move, and reports how many cannot move and why.
- The console's own copy of the transition map (`STATUS_TRANSITIONS`, `AUTOMATED_STATUSES`, `PENTEST_STATUSES`) is removed. The API's transition engine is the only copy of the rules.

### Changed: Findings keep the scanner details they used to drop

- Ingest now stores the rule **family** (Nessus / Tenable.sc plugin family,
  scanner category), the scanner's **exploit-available** verdict as a column,
  **VPR** (display only, no priority effect), the **CVSS version**, **every
  CVE** named on the finding (`cve_ids`) and the vendor **patch publication
  date**. The finding API returns them. Migrations 000688-000689 (nullable
  columns, NOT VALID checks, partial indexes, and a backfill of the exploit
  flag from metadata). Fingerprints are unchanged.

### Changed: the findings list shows the asset and the place on it

- The Location column shows the asset on one line and the place on it (URL path, file and line, port) below, cut from the middle so the end of a path or URL stays visible; the full value is in the tooltip. Two findings of one check on one web application no longer look identical.
- Phone cards show the location too.
- The Source and Created columns are hidden until turned on in View, so location, status and SLA fit at 1280px.

### Changed: the Findings overview cards are page-level and load with one stats request

- The cards above the findings list (Total, Open, Critical open, High open,
  Overdue SLA, In CISA KEV, Awaiting verification) now count every finding the
  caller may see, whatever the state tab, search or filters. Total equals the
  All tab and Open the Open tab. Filter-aware numbers stay in the tab counts and
  the result bar. Each card applies the filter it counts and explains itself in
  a tooltip.
- `GET /findings/stats` adds `open_by_severity` and `awaiting_verification`.
  `kev_open`, `epss_high_open` and `sla_breached` now use the Open tab's
  predicate, so pentest drafts and findings in review are no longer counted.
- The page loads one stats response instead of two, switching tabs sends no
  stats request, the grouped and verification views no longer load the flat
  list, and the saved-views menu loads its list and your groups only when used.

### Changed: faster attack paths, exposure chains and dashboard rollups on large tenants

- The attack-graph node read counts every asset's findings in one aggregate
  over the tenant's findings instead of one index probe per asset.
- A new covering index, `idx_findings_tenant_rollup_cover`, replaces
  `idx_findings_tenant_stats_cover` with six more columns. The tenant-wide
  finding rollups (dashboard stats, executive summary, finding groups,
  attack-graph counts) can now run as index-only scans.
- Measured on a tenant with 110k assets and 525k findings: attack paths went
  from 3-5 s to 0.5 s, exposure chains from 3.2 s to 0.8 s, finding groups
  from 1.4 s to 0.75 s, and the dashboard overview from 4.8 s to 3.1 s.
- Upgrade note: both migrations build and drop the index `CONCURRENTLY`, so
  the findings table stays writable. The build reads the whole table once
  (about 1 s per million findings on the test host).

### Changed: the Sensors page lists CI pipelines (Mode: All, Daemon, Runner)

- The Sensors page switches by **Mode**: All, Daemon (sensor rows, heartbeat, can be offline) and Runner (CI pipelines: one per workflow file of each repository, fresh or stale against its own cadence, never offline). The role filter (scanner, collector) applies to both. Header counts per mode.
- Runner mode shows each pipeline with its provider, repository, workflow, status, last run, default-branch gate and runner version, and a drawer with its runs (paged), branches and gate trend. Archived, revoked and never-run pipelines are hidden behind **Show inactive**; nothing is deleted.
- The CI runners page is folded in: `/ci-runners` opens the Sensors page in runner mode and `/ci-runners/{run id}` (the link in a gate verdict) opens that run. The run-style facet of the daemon list is now **Run style** (`?exec=`); old `?mode=ci` links keep working.

### Changed: the gateway compresses read responses

- The bundled gateway now compresses GET/HEAD responses of text types with
  zstd or gzip, whichever the client accepts. API JSON shrinks 6-13 times: a
  100-row findings page drops from 179 KB to 27 KB, the dashboard overview from
  69 KB to 8 KB, and the SBOM export from 4.8 MB to 0.37 MB.
- Write responses and the sign-in, OAuth and sensor APIs are never compressed.
  Those responses can carry a freshly issued secret next to request-controlled
  text, which is what a compression side channel (BREACH) needs.
- Event streams are not compressed, so they are never held back in a buffer.

### Changed: the layer4 gateway image is built with the pinned Go and ships one Caddy binary

- `api/deploy/gateway/Dockerfile` (the `openctem-gateway` image with the
  layer4 module) compiles Caddy v2.11.4 and caddy-l4 v0.1.2 with the pinned Go
  toolchain and current `golang.org/x/net` and gRPC, on plain Alpine laid out
  like the Caddy image (`/config`, `/data`, `/etc/caddy`, `/srv`, the same
  command and ports). Before, it replaced the binary of the Caddy image, so
  both binaries shipped, and Caddy's build toolchain carried 10 HIGH
  advisories: amd64 39.7 MB compressed / 109 MB unpacked with 10 HIGH before,
  22.6 MB / 63 MB with none after.

### Changed: the API contract files are generated, no longer committed

- `api/api/openapi/swagger.yaml`, `api/api/openapi/routes.txt`,
  `web/src/config/api-route-permissions.json` and
  `web/src/lib/api/generated/api.types.ts` are generated from the Go source by
  `make generate` (or `make generate-docker`, which needs only Docker) and are
  ignored by git, so pull requests no longer conflict on them and the merge
  queue can batch API changes.
- CI generates them on every run. API CI checks the spec against the handlers
  and the router as before; Web CI type-checks the web against the contract a
  change produces, runs the web checks for any API change that alters the
  contract, and reports the contract difference against the base (breaking
  changes, route gate changes, routes added or removed) on the pull request.
- Image builds (`docker-publish.yml`, all-in-one, e2e) generate before building
  the web image. `docker build web` from a plain checkout needs `make generate`
  first (`make allinone` does it).
- **Upgrade note:** a checkout that runs the stack from source (air, `next
  dev`) needs `make generate-docker` after `git pull`: the pull that brings this
  change deletes the committed copies.

### Changed: a step's chunks never wait for each other

- A step cut into chunks puts every target of one host in one chunk: a name with its URLs and services, an address with its `address:port` forms, a range with the addresses of its buckets, and a name with the addresses the inventory says it resolves to. Two chunks of one step no longer hold the same host, so one chunk never waits for its sibling while a sensor slot is free.
- The chunks of a step are evenly filled: 450 targets with a chunk size of 200 are three chunks of 150, not 200, 200 and 50. The number of chunks is unchanged.
- A host with more targets than a chunk holds gets chunks of its own, which run one after the other.

### Changed: a task waiting for its hosts says how many, held by what, and what can start

- In a run's task list, a queued task waiting for its hosts now reads in full, for example "Waiting for 2 of its hosts, held by nuclei (step templates, run 1a2b3c4d); 21 of its 23 targets are on free hosts", instead of a cut-off generic sentence. The holder's run and step are named only when you can read that run. A host is never named.
- The task list (`GET /scan-runs/{id}`, `GET /scan-runs/{id}/tasks`) gives `host_wait` on such tasks (at most 25 per page). `host_wait` in the list and in the task placement answer gains `targets` and `can_start`.

### Changed: a task waiting for its hosts says so, and which task holds them

- The "Why waiting?" panel of a queued task that waits while another task of the organization scans its hosts now reads, for example, "Waiting: 10 of its 10 hosts are being scanned by httpx (step http). It starts when those hosts are free." It replaces "Sensors that can take it: 1 (0 busy). It should start shortly." and links the run that holds the hosts.
- The answer shows host counts only, never host names. A holding task's run and step are named only when the caller can read that run, and another organization's tasks are never counted.
- The run's task list marks such a task "Waiting for its hosts".
- A sensor that hands a task back because its own per-host limit holds one of the hosts is stored as the code `hosts_busy`, and shown as such ("its sensor is still scanning one of its hosts").
- API: `GET /scan-runs/{id}/tasks/{task_id}/placement` adds `host_wait` (`hosts_held`, `hosts_total`, `holders[]`) and the reason `sensor_hosts_busy`. Run tasks add `waiting_on_hosts`.

### Changed: install snippets pin sensor v0.21.1 (sdk-go v0.31.0)

- The console's sensor install commands and the "update available" check now point at sensor v0.21.1, built on sdk-go v0.31.0. Sensors on v0.21+ detect their tools by themselves and free each host as its targets finish.

### Changed: install snippets pin sensor v0.22.1

- The console's sensor install commands and the "update available" check point at sensor v0.22.1: confined port scans reach their targets, a fully refused target reports `egress_refused`, probes accept `host:port` targets, and the signed OpenCTEM rules pack is the default SAST content.

### Changed: install snippets pin sensor v0.23.0

- The console's sensor install commands and the "update available" check point at sensor v0.23.0: nuclei runs in waves of whole hosts and frees each wave's hosts as it ends. The Tenable.sc connector now ships as its own image, `ghcr.io/openctemio/connector-tenable`.

### Changed: one inventory definition; review items say what covers them

- Dashboard asset totals and the EASM surface, new-asset and exposed-service
  counts now count only inventory members (confirmed or unrecorded,
  `dependency`, `monitor_only`), like the Assets list and the attack-surface
  stats (RFC-054 §4.4). Names waiting for review are no longer counted as
  surface.
- Attack-surface "recent changes" items carry `asset_id`,
  `attribution_state` and `in_inventory`, so a discovered name shows as
  "Added · needs review" instead of "Added".
- The review queue (`GET /api/v1/easm/candidates`) filters by `reason` and
  says per item which scope target, seed or verified domain covers it
  (`covered_by`); the EASM summary adds `review_by_reason`.
- `GET /api/v1/assets/{id}/attribution` adds `scope_status` (`in_scope`,
  `out_of_scope`, `internal`, `not_applicable`), `covered_by` and
  `blocked_code`.

### Changed: finding lifecycle caps are organization limits
- The finding lifecycle catalog caps (`lifecycle_sub_statuses`, `lifecycle_schemes`) are limit keys like the others: unlimited unless set. Migration 002890 carries each organization's earlier caps (Free 3 sub-statuses and no scheme, Pro 1 scheme) into operator limits with the reason "migrated from plan". A refused addition answers `LIMIT_REACHED`.

### Changed: more lists keep their page and filters in the URL

- The notification outbox, the notifications page, account activity and the
  admin console organizations and system logs now keep their page, page size,
  search and filters in the address. A link, a reload or Back shows the same
  page of the same list. A guard test keeps every route's main list on the
  shared list-URL hook.

### Changed: the CI/CD, sensor fleet and EASM review lists keep their page in the URL

- The CI/CD pipelines, runs and coverage views, the sensor fleet ("All") and
  the EASM review queue keep their page and page size in the address, and
  the CI runs view keeps its verdict filter there too. A link, a reload or
  Back shows the same page. Switching the CI/CD view, the review queue tab
  or the Sensors page mode starts the new list on page 1.

### Changed: more lists page with `page` and `per_page`

- These lists now read `per_page` instead of `page_size`, through the shared
  parser:
  - `GET /api/v1/credentials`, `/credentials/identities` and
    `/credentials/identities/{identity}/exposures`;
  - `GET /api/v1/findings/{id}/activities`;
  - the notification outbox list;
  - the secret store credentials;
  - the template sources.
- A `page` or `per_page` that is not a positive whole number is answered 400.
  It used to fall back silently to the first page of 20. `per_page` is capped
  at 100; a larger value used to fall back to 20.
- **Behaviour change:** clients that send `page_size` get the default page size
  until they send `per_page`. The console is updated.

### Changed: groups, assignment rules, scope rules and AI triage history page with `page` and `per_page`

- These lists now read `page` and `per_page` through the shared parser,
  instead of `limit` and `offset`. Their responses report `page` and
  `per_page` instead of `limit` and `offset`:
  - `GET /api/v1/groups`, `/groups/{id}/members` and `/groups/{id}/assets`;
  - `GET /api/v1/assignment-rules`;
  - `GET /api/v1/groups/{id}/scope-rules`;
  - `GET /api/v1/findings/{id}/ai-triage/history`.
- A bad value is answered 400 instead of falling back silently. `per_page` is
  capped at 100.
- **Behaviour change:** clients sending `limit`/`offset` to these endpoints get
  the first page until they send `page`/`per_page`. The console is updated.

### Changed: one list paging convention for scans, scan runs and scan workflows

- `GET /api/v1/scans`, `GET /api/v1/scans/{id}/runs`, `GET /api/v1/scan-runs` and `GET /api/v1/scan-workflows` read `page` (1-based) and `per_page` through one shared parser: a value that is not a positive whole number is answered 400 (it used to fall back to page 1 silently), and `per_page` is capped at 100.
- The four lists answer with one envelope, `{data, total, page, per_page, total_pages}`. `GET /api/v1/scans` no longer sends the duplicate `items` key, and `GET /api/v1/scan-runs` and `GET /api/v1/scan-workflows` send `data` instead of `items`.
- `GET /api/v1/scan-runs` takes `scan_id` (the runs of one scan, within the caller's tenant) and `status=blocked`; an unparsable `scan_workflow_id`, `scan_id` or `asset_id` is answered 400 instead of being ignored.
- Console: every Scans list keeps its state in plain URL parameters (`page`, `per_page`, `sort`, `q` and field-named filters); the prefixed `run_page`, `run_per_page`, `run_sort` and `run_status` are gone. A scan's run history pages locally and links to "View all runs" (`/scans/runs?scan_id=`).
- **Upgrade note:** API clients reading `items` from these four lists read `data`.

### Changed: the MCP comment tool needs only findings:comment

- `add_finding_comment` now requires `findings:comment` (split from
  `findings:write`), and its OAuth scope is renamed `mcp:findings.write` →
  `mcp:findings.comment`. An AI application allowed to comment can no longer
  stand on `findings:write` or `findings:severity`.
- Migration `001556_mcp_findings_comment_scope` renames the scope in existing
  connections, pending requests and organization MCP policies, so nothing
  needs reconnecting.

### Changed: MCP tool results mark untrusted text and errors are typed

- Tool results that carry text written by people or imported from tested systems return it under `untrusted_data` with a fixed notice; the tool descriptions and the server instructions say to treat it as data.
- A failed tool call returns `{"error": {"code", "message", "retryable"}}` (`invalid_argument`, `not_found`, `forbidden`, `permission_denied`, `module_disabled`, `not_confirmed`, `unavailable`, `internal_error`) instead of "tool execution failed"; an item that does not exist and one the caller may not read share the `not_found` answer.
- Every tool carries annotations (`readOnlyHint` on the read tools, `destructiveHint: false`).
- `get_campaign` takes `campaign_id`, and `get_finding`, `explain_finding_priority` and `get_pentest_finding` take `finding_id` (`id` is still accepted).
- `get_campaign` sends the campaign's emergency contact, communication channel and escalation procedure to the campaign lead only, and only the known rules-of-engagement keys.

### Changed: AI assistants (MCP) settings are organized in tabs, with a request-and-approve flow

- Settings, AI access (MCP) is now **AI assistants (MCP)** with a status line and tabs: Connect (everyone), Applications, Connections and Policy.
- Applications lists members' access requests (Approve / Decline), the **Approved publishers** (a validated list with Add publisher and Remove, replacing the free-text "Trusted application hosts" box; platform-trusted hosts are shown read only), the applications registered by the organization, and, folded under **Advanced**, "Allow unverified applications", which now asks for confirmation before it turns on.
- Policy groups the settings into Access, **What assistants may do** (read scopes, and the comment-adding scope, off by default, with each comment confirmed by the member) and Limits.
- The consent page of a blocked application offers **Request access** to members and **Allow <publisher> for <organization>** to those who may change the policy.
- All AI assistant pages (settings, connected applications, consent and change confirmation) are translated (English and Vietnamese). Alert titles now wrap instead of being cut off.

### Changed: the members list pages with page / per_page

- `GET /tenants/{tenant}/members` takes `page` and `per_page` (default 100,
  max 500, for pickers of the whole organization) and returns the list
  envelope (`data`, `total`, `page`, `per_page`, `total_pages`). `limit` and
  `offset` are no longer read; a non-numeric or non-positive value is refused
  with 400. The members page and every member picker use the new parameters.

### Changed: MODULE_NOT_ENABLED names the module and the reason

- A request refused by the module gate now carries
  `details: {"module": "<id>", "reason": "disabled_by_admin"}` with the same 403 and code,
  so clients can tell the user the feature is turned off for their organization. Plan
  entitlement reasons follow with RFC-064.

### Changed: one declarative module registry

- `configs/modules.yaml` declares every module: presentation, core flag, release,
  read permission, dependencies, and the REST routes, MCP tools and background jobs it
  owns. `make generate-modules` writes the Go catalog and the web constants; migration
  001460 writes the `modules` rows from it; CI fails on drift (`make modules-check`).
- Coverage tests fail when a route, an MCP tool or a job does not follow the registry.
- Fixed with it: relationship suggestions (`/api/v1/relationships/suggestions`) follow
  the `relationships` module, and the scope join background pass skips organizations with
  `attack_surface` off.

### Changed: neutral wording for modules that are not available

- `MODULE_NOT_ENABLED` now says "This module is not available for this organization" (and "...no longer available for this organization: it is read-only for now" during the grace). The `reason` codes are unchanged. The unavailable-entitlement 503 no longer mentions a plan.
- Enabling a module that is not available is refused with "is not available for this organization".
- The AI triage token-budget error now asks the person to contact their administrator.
- Platform scanning, when not allowed, says "Platform scanning is not available on this installation".

### Changed: New Scan dialogs keep their header and actions in view

- New Scan, Edit scan, Quick scan and Scan these assets keep the title, the step indicator and the actions fixed while the content scrolls; on a phone they open as a bottom sheet with full-width actions.
- Scan these assets offers the scanners of the tool registry instead of a fixed list.

### Changed: New Scan options, and one target picker for Quick scan and Scan these assets

- New Scan Options shows where the scan runs (Auto, your sensors, platform where offered) and the scan profile; job size, timeout and retries are under Advanced. The sensor preference moved here from the first step.
- Quick scan and Scan these assets use the New Scan target parts: per-line format, repeats counted once, the live scope check and removable chips. Pasted targets may be separated by newlines, commas, semicolons or spaces.

### Changed: New Scan target picker

- New Scan, step Targets, is one picker with three tabs: Assets (search, type and criticality filters, page, range and select-all-matching selection, selected only), Groups (searchable) and Paste (each line shown as domain, wildcard, IP, CIDR, URL or host:port; repeats counted once; Clean up). A summary under it shows how many targets, what the scope check says, and the whole selection with remove buttons and the fixes for refused targets.
- Picked assets are sent by id; the API names and checks them.

### Changed: pentest campaign creation wizard, duplicate, status stepper; campaign pages translated

- New campaigns are created in three steps (engagement; scope and rules;
  team and sign-off) with sensible defaults; only the name and client are
  required.
- "Duplicate" on a campaign starts the wizard from its settings, scope,
  rules, team and completion policy (findings, links and test credentials
  are not copied).
- A status stepper shows where the campaign is (planning, testing,
  remediation, archived) and what comes next.
- The campaign list, campaign page and campaign panel no longer show
  English-only text: every string is in English and Vietnamese.
- Design: RFC-086 §7.

### Changed: pentest campaigns record targets, approach, environment, TLP and the authorization letter

- A campaign records several target types (`targets`, from the
  organization's list), the testing `approach` (black, grey or white box),
  the `environment` (production, staging, development, other) and a `tlp`
  sharing level (default amber, printed on reports).
- The signed authorization letter is a file uploaded to the campaign and
  linked with `authorization_attachment_id`. New organization setting
  `require_authorization_before_start` (off by default) refuses to start a
  campaign without it.
- Retired: `campaign_type` (moved into `targets`), `priority`, and
  `client_contact` (moved into the rules of engagement's emergency contact).
  The `type` and `priority` list filters are replaced by `target`.
- Status changes, completion-policy changes and completion sign-offs now run
  under the campaign row lock in one transaction, and the general campaign
  edit no longer writes the status or the completion policy.
- Report data gains `campaign.targets`, `campaign.approach`,
  `campaign.environment`, `campaign.tlp`.
- Upgrade in one step: migration `002054_pentest_campaign_profile` moves the
  data and drops the retired columns.
- Design: RFC-086.
- Console: campaigns show their targets, environment (production stands
  out) and TLP; an "Engagement" card edits the profile and links the
  authorization letter from the campaign's files; the campaign list filters
  by target type; Settings → Pentest gets the authorization requirement and
  calls the list "Target types". English and Vietnamese.

### Changed: CVSS 3.1 and 4.0 calculator, CWE and OWASP pickers

- The finding CVSS calculator handles CVSS 3.1 and 4.0 base vectors: paste a
  vector or pick the metrics. Scores follow the FIRST specifications (the
  4.0 score was an approximation before). The finding records the CVSS
  version of its vector.
- CWE and OWASP Top 10 are searchable pickers; a CWE id outside the built-in
  list can be used as typed.
- A Playwright spec covers creating a finding with a pasted screenshot,
  reordered steps and publishing it.

### Changed: a campaign that takes no new findings says why

- On a completed, on-hold, canceled or archived campaign, the Findings tab
  shows the reason in place of "New finding", the checklist hides "Create
  finding", and a new finding opened for such a campaign keeps its name, shows
  the reason and cannot be saved. Users who may change the campaign status
  (its lead, tenant admins) get the one-step status change the API allows:
  reopen or resume testing, or move a canceled campaign back to planning.
  Archived campaigns have no one-step change.
- The campaign picker says "No campaign is open for new findings" when no
  campaign is planning or in progress, instead of "No open campaign matches".

### Changed: pentest finding editor

- New and edit pages share one editor: sections on the left with a sticky
  section bar, a live summary (severity, CVSS, status, what is still missing)
  and the assignment, deadline, tags and references on the right, one column
  on phones.
- A sticky action bar shows the save state and the actions the campaign role
  allows: save draft, submit for review, and publish for leads and
  administrators (the finding is created as a draft, then confirmed through
  the status endpoint). Ctrl+S saves, Ctrl+Enter runs the main action; a
  shortcuts popover lists them.
- Affected targets and the inventory asset are one control: type a URL, host,
  endpoint or file, or pick an asset. Suggestions list the assets the
  campaign's scope covers first ("In this campaign's scope"), then the rest of
  the inventory with why each is outside the scope. Scope patterns are read as
  in the scope module: "*.example.com" covers example.com and every name below
  it, so wildcard scopes no longer leave every asset "out of scope". Free text
  naming an inventory asset links it.
- A new finding keeps a draft in the browser (with a "kept" indicator) and
  offers it on the next visit; leaving a page with unsaved changes asks first.
- Required fields are checked inline; saving focuses the first missing one.
- Severity is a one-click segmented control. The edit page saves fields
  without a status and moves the status through the status endpoint.

### Changed: a pentest retest's environment has its own field

- `POST /api/v1/pentest/findings/{id}/retests` takes `environment` (production, staging, development or qa; optional) and retests return it; the console no longer writes it into the notes. Reports show it in the retest results, report templates read it as `{environment}` inside `{#retests}`, and the MCP `list_retests` tool returns it.
- Migration `002073_pentest_retest_environment` adds the column and moves existing values: notes that start with exactly `**Environment:** <production|staging|development|qa>` and a blank line lose that prefix and the value goes to the column; other notes are left unchanged. The down migration puts the prefix back.

### Changed: a committed private key is now blocked in CI and by the pre-commit hook

- The Secret Scanning job fails a change that adds a private key block, a key or keystore file, or anything under `data/`; the pre-commit hook runs the same check. Throwaway keys under `testdata/` are allowed.
- `SENSOR_MTLS_CA_DIR` documents that a relative default resolves against the working directory, so run from a source checkout with it pointed outside the checkout.

### Changed: network ranges are scanned in /24 pieces, chunked by address count

- The scan target gate cuts every range target into pieces of at most /24
  (IPv6 /120): a /16 is 256 pieces, recorded one run-target row each, never
  one per address (RFC-088).
- A port-scan step closes a chunk before it would reach more than 1 024
  addresses (a range piece weighs its address count, any other target 1),
  so a /16 is 64 chunks that every eligible sensor shares instead of one
  command on one sensor for hours. Other capabilities keep their target
  counts.
- Politeness knows about overlap: a chunk holding a range and a chunk
  holding an address inside it are never run at the same time by two
  sensors, in either order, by poll, by id or in a batch claim; two
  addresses of one /24 still run in parallel. Host keys stay per tenant.
- No migration and no operator step. Chunks already queued keep their old
  keys (a range string is its own key) until they finish.

### Changed: the priority reclassification sweep writes only what changed

- The whole-tenant sweep, which runs on a schedule and after KEV/EPSS
  refreshes, rewrote every finding it re-examined. It now persists a finding
  only when its priority class, reason, reachability or SLA changed. In a
  10-minute window on a tenant with 525k findings, it rewrote 2,189 of 34.7k
  re-examined findings (before: all 20.9k), and it went through findings 1.65
  times faster.
- A re-confirmed class no longer adds a `priority_class_audit_log` row. The
  log records transitions, as the ingest path already did. Before, every
  sweep added one row per open finding (20.8k rows in 10 minutes).
- The sweep reads the distinct assets of the tenant's open findings in one
  query instead of paging every open finding with a count per page.

### Changed: a task whose sensor skipped some targets ends the run partial

- A sensor with sdk-go #191 removes a scan target that its local policy refuses or cannot check, such as a name that does not resolve or a wildcard pattern. It runs the task on the other targets and completes it with `refused_targets` in its result metadata.
- The platform reads that list, bounded and cleaned. The step ends `partial` (code `TARGETS_SKIPPED`), and so does the run, instead of "completed". Before the sensor change, one unresolvable target failed the whole task.
- A batched step sums the skipped targets of its completed batches.
- Run tasks (`GET /api/v1/pipeline-runs/{id}` and `/tasks`) carry `skipped_targets` (at most 20) and `skipped_targets_total`. The run page shows "Completed with N targets skipped: api.example.com (does not resolve)" under the task status.
- Skipped targets do not roll over to the next scheduled run.

### Changed: sensor and SDK releases reach the platform without a platform release

- The signed release feed now lists the newest release of each first-party sensor product and of the sensor SDK, with the image digest (RFC-037 §12). The instance learns them at start-up, after each daily check or import, and on every replica within the hour: "update available", the SDK status and the install commands follow a sensor or SDK release with no OpenCTEM change, release or restart.
- A learned release only raises the version this platform release was built with (`latest` in `versions.yaml`), never lowers it; `min` and the SDK advisories still come from `versions.yaml`. The install commands pin `image:tag@sha256:...` when the feed gave a digest; a mirror set with `SENSOR_IMAGE` is pinned by tag.
- `GET /api/v1/sensors/stats` products gain `latest_source` (`feed`, `built_in`, `operator`); the Sensors page says when "latest" is only the built-in version. The admin version check view gains `components`, listed on System > Software updates.
- The feed is published every 6 hours from the public release lists of the sensor, connector and sdk-go repositories; those repositories no longer open a pull request here after a release.
- Fixed: the helm and signature-check snippets took the tag from an image reference with a digest wrongly.
- `api/deploy/docker-compose.sensor.yml` now follows `versions.yaml` (it named v0.9.7 for the API image).
- **Upgrade note:** nothing to do. Until a release feed key is pinned in a release, the built-in versions apply as before; an air-gapped instance imports the feed file in the console.

### Changed: a missing release feed is visible

- The version check logs a warning when its outcome changes (feed not published, signature invalid, unreachable, expired) and once at start-up when the build pins no feed key; a 404 is reported as `not_published`. Console > System shows the feed state and the last success time.
- The `Release Feed` workflow fails with an error naming the one-time setup when `RELEASE_FEED_SIGNING_KEY` is missing, instead of skipping with a warning. Setup: `docs/architecture/version-check.md#setup-maintainers`.

### Changed: a running scan frees each host as soon as it is done with it

- A command used to hold all of its hosts until it ended. Now a host is free for other work of the organization as soon as the command's targets on that host settle. For example, the nuclei tasks for the hosts httpx has already probed start while httpx still works on the rest.
- The sensor names the hosts it freed on its heartbeat (`released_keys`, sdk-go with per-target release). The platform applies them only to commands that sensor holds, and only keys of that command. A re-queued or re-claimed command holds all of its hosts again.
