- Older sensors send nothing, so their commands hold their hosts until they end, as before.
- Migration `command_settled_host_keys` adds a nullable column (no rewrite) and replaces `get_next_platform_job` in place.

### Changed: report templates and stored reports move from Postgres to the file storage

- New pentest report templates and stored reports are written to the
  organization's file storage (server storage or its own bucket, failing
  closed); the rows keep the key. Reads are checked against the recorded
  SHA-256 and refused when the file was changed.
- The `report-file-migration` controller moves existing rows (10 per kind
  per minute): each file is written, read back and compared, then the row's
  bytes are cleared. The database and its dumps shrink accordingly.
- Deleting a template or report, directly or with its campaign, removes
  its file (organization deletion erases the whole namespace): a trigger queues it in
  `storage_blob_deletions` and the attachment-retention sweep deletes it.
- Migration `002063_report_files_in_storage` (expand step): `content`
  becomes nullable, `storage_key`, `storage_provider`, `size_bytes` added
  (backfilled), the queue table and trigger. Its down refuses while any file
  lives only in the storage.
- **Upgrade note:** back up the file storage (the `api-data` volume or the
  bucket) together with the database from this release on: report files are
  no longer in the database dump once moved.

### Changed: a task that ends with unfinished targets runs only those again

- When a sensor completes a scan task with per-target outcomes (`target_outcomes`: done, failed, skipped, unfinished) and some targets are unfinished, the finished targets are settled and a new task carrying only the unfinished targets is queued in the same transaction (`commands.retry_of` names the task it continues; migration `002098_command_retry_of`). The step settles with its last task, so it waits for the follow-up and counts its results. A finished target is never run twice because a later one stopped the task.
- Dispatch attempts count per chunk of targets: a run that settled targets leaves the remaining chunk's attempts as they were; a run that settled none adds one. One host that never answers exhausts only its own task, not the targets already done.
- Single-scanner scan tasks now carry their step id (`commands.scan_run_step_id`), as workflow and zone-routed tasks already did.
- Sensors without per-target outcomes are unaffected.

### Changed: retests follow what the sensors report they can re-check

- Auto-retest picks findings of every tool that an online sensor of the organization reports it can re-check. That is either the tool's own retest handler (capability `retest:<tool>`) or the template re-verify rung. Before, only nuclei findings were ever auto-retested. With no such sensor online, nothing is queued, and the next tick tries again.
- `GET /api/v1/findings/{id}/retests` returns `can_retest`, which says whether a retest would be accepted now. It runs the same eligibility checks, target gates and sensor availability as a request, and records nothing. The console offers "Retest now" from it on a finding of any tool, instead of on nuclei findings only.
- The only tool name left in the retest and validation paths is the engine of the template re-verify rung (`validation.ReverifyTool`) (RFC-094 §4.6).

### Changed: stored discovered-URL assets become web endpoints

- Migration 001288 turns every `discovered_url` asset into a GET endpoint under its origin (`http_service`, created
  when missing; origin named `scheme://host[:port]`, default port dropped), keeping query parameter names only, moves
  their findings and exposure events to the origin and deletes the URL assets. Design: RFC-056.
- Upgrade note: the down migration does not recreate the URL assets; the endpoints keep the inventory.

### Changed: the scope model records the attack surface review decisions

- RFC-054 §14.5 records the decisions now in force:
  - a scope entry lets scans reach a pending name;
  - children follow their host;
  - a person's confirmation adds the exact entry;
  - addresses behind in-scope names become one suggestion;
  - the Suggestions tab replaces the review queue;
  - connector assets are in scope by default.
- It also gives the threat model of each decision. R3 and R4 are adopted, and
  the connector default changes from off to on.

### Changed: RFC-055 records how the legacy capability vocabulary is retired

- RFC-055 §10.1 records the OC5 decision.
- Custom capabilities stay as tenant labels, each optionally mapped to one ctis taxonomy capability id, which then drives routing. Tenant rows are never deleted.
- Only the legacy matching columns and the old-sensor name fallback are dropped, one release train after the command-logs sensor release is live everywhere.

### Changed: RFC-055 covers web scope, CTIS 1.6 endpoints and evidence

- RFC-055 and `docs/architecture/tool-contract.md` now describe:
  - the job's `web_scope` and how the SDK and katana enforce it;
  - the `endpoint` record kind and port;
  - CTIS 1.6 `endpoints[]`, `finding.web` and `finding.evidence_items` with marked sensitive spans;
  - retest verdict evidence and the rule that a networked `fixed` needs the attempt's HTTP exchange.
- The RFC index row lists the merged and open pull requests.

### Changed: automations hear about every way a scan run ends

- The `scan_completed` automation trigger now also fires for runs that time
  out or are canceled, including runs the timeout controller ends (past their
  deadline, or no sensor picked them up). `status_filter` accepts `timeout`
  and `canceled` as well as `completed`, `partial` and `failed`. Without a
  filter it still fires on completed runs only, so existing automations behave
  as before.

### Changed: one flow view for a scan run

- The run drawer draws the run's steps as one flow. Each step is a card
  with its state (colour, icon and label), tool, chunk progress bar, outputs,
  findings, duration and the comparison with the last run; text wraps instead
  of being cut. Steps that run side by side are drawn as a laid-out graph
  (left to right or top to bottom, whichever fits) with arrows labelled with
  what flowed along them; a chain of steps, and a phone screen, get the list.
  The separate Stages/Graph toggle of the run map is gone.
- A skipped step says which upstream step it waited on ("Skipped: HTTP probe
  failed").
- A finished step whose targets the sensor's network confinement refused says
  "could not reach N targets (blocked by the sensor's network confinement)"
  instead of "produced nothing", when the API reports
  `egress_refused_targets` on the step's tasks.
- Every step card is a button: click or Enter opens the step's panel (tasks,
  logs, outputs). The run drawer is wider (2xl) to fit three steps side by
  side.

### Changed: scan run lists update from real-time notices

- The scan page and the runs tab refresh when a live run changes, from its
  `run:{id}` notices, instead of polling every 10-30 seconds; they poll only
  while the real-time connection is down, and every 2 minutes to notice new
  runs.

### Changed: a run executes the workflow version it started with

- When a scan workflow run starts, the workflow's settings and steps are saved
  as an immutable version (only when they changed since the last one), and the
  run reads that version until it ends. Editing a workflow while it runs now
  changes the next run, never the running one; before, the running one picked
  up the edited steps and settings halfway through.
- `GET /scan-runs` and `GET /scan-runs/{id}` return `scan_workflow_version`
  and `spec_digest`.
- Migration 001321 adds `scan_workflow_versions` and the two run columns.
  Runs started before the upgrade keep reading the live workflow.

### Changed: scan approval rules read the scan's declared intensity

- The intensity scan approval rules match and approvers approve is the scan's declared intensity (RFC-071), never below what its tool or workflow steps probe. Changing the declared intensity changes the approved definition and needs a new approval (RFC-073 §8).

### Changed: scan refusals and run messages say scan workflow and scan run, not pipeline

- Run refusals (scan workflow not found, disabled, without steps, a step without a scanner), run outcome messages and scan workflow audit messages now use the scan workflow / scan / scan run vocabulary. "Pipeline" is kept for CI pipelines.
- Error codes (`PIPELINE_*`) and the automation action `trigger_pipeline` are unchanged.

### Changed: New Scan review groups refused targets by reason, with one action per group

- The Review step no longer lists every refused target with its own buttons.
  Targets are grouped by reason, with counts (for example "212 need a
  verified domain for platform sensors" or "69 resolve to private addresses
  outside every scan zone"). Each group is collapsible, shows a few examples
  with "Show all", and has one action for the whole group: "Run on your own
  sensor", "Verify <domain>", approve or activate the covering scope entry,
  "Set up a scan zone", or "Remove these targets". There is also a Remove all.
- "Scan the N allowed targets, skip the rest" saves the scan with only the
  allowed targets. The server records the skipped ones with their reasons.
- "Runs on" explains the choice, for example "Auto -> runs on your sensor
  sensor-docker-01, because platform sensors need a verified domain".
- The scope check runs again whenever the Review step opens, and on
  "Re-check".
- A private target reads "Resolves to 10.x.x.x, an internal address:
  scanning it would hit your own network".
- Fixed: the New Scan dialog body scrolled sideways and clipped its content
  when a long list of names was shown (a fieldset was as wide as its
  longest line).

### Changed: the scan trigger decides its targets through the one target gate

- `resolveScanTargets` builds the candidates (direct targets, asset-group members, the scanner type gate, archived members) and calls `ResolveDispatchTargets` once for exclusions, ownership (including the takeover-only exception), the act scope, the private-range rule and the tier ceiling. Its own copies of those checks are removed. Targets, counts, warnings and refusal codes are unchanged, pinned by characterization tests.
- The gate checks the act scope before the tier ceiling on every path: a target refused by both is reported as outside the actor's scope, so an actor learns nothing about the scope entries of what they may not scan.

### Changed: "Inventory in scope" means the internet-facing inventory

- `coverage` is now the share of the internet-facing inventory (domains,
  subdomains, public addresses, services and applications whose attribution
  puts them in the inventory) that an active scope target covers and no
  exclusion removes. Repositories, cloud resources, review-queue items and
  rejected names no longer dilute it; internal names and private addresses
  are counted apart. A URL or `host:port` asset is matched on its host, as
  the active-probe authority does.
- New response fields `inventory_internet_facing`, `inventory_in_scope` and
  `inventory_internal`.

### Changed: scope refusals say why and how to fix it; `POST /scope/check` is a dry run of the whole gate

- A scan request refused for its targets (`TARGET_OUT_OF_SCOPE`) now lists
  every refused target in `details.refused[]` with a code (`no_entry`,
  `rejected`, `needs_review`, `deny_list`, `proof_required`, …), a message and
  the fixes that would let it through (RFC-054 §6.5). Dispatch-gate refusals
  carry the code too.
- `POST /api/v1/scope/check` now takes `{"targets": [...], "sensor_preference",
  "tier"}` and answers, per target, what a scan by the caller would do:
  allowed with what authorizes it (scope target, seed, verified domain; proof
  level; zone), or refused with the code, the caller's own rule (a pending,
  expired or deactivated entry; an exclusion) and the fixes the caller may
  take. It dispatches, logs and audits nothing.
- **Removed:** the old `POST /scope/check` body `{"asset_type", "value"}` and
  its `in_scope`/`excluded` answer.

### Changed: intrusive (T2) scope entries may last longer, up to an owner-set limit

- An entry that allows intrusive (T2) probes was bound by the one-off limit (at most 30 days, 7 by default). It now has its own limit, set by an owner: 7, 30 (default), 90 or 365 days, or permanent. A T2 entry still needs a verified domain for its probes and an approval when it is added or widened.
- `PUT /api/v1/scope/settings/intrusive` (owner, re-authentication, reason; audited at high severity, every administrator told) changes it; `PUT /api/v1/scope/settings` keeps it. `GET /api/v1/scope/settings` adds `t2_max_duration`, `t2_max_days` and `t2_permanent_allowed`.
- The add and edit dialogs offer durations up to the limit, and "Permanent" for a T2 entry only when the owner allows it. Turning one-off entries off no longer blocks an expiring T2 entry.
- New refusal code `INTRUSIVE_TOO_LONG`. No migration.

### Changed: a scoring change sends one summary instead of one alert per finding

- When a scoring model or the organization's risk scoring settings, priority rules or SLA policy change, the open findings it moves no longer send one `finding_priority_escalated` notification each. Once the recompute has finished, one `scoring_change_applied` notification per change summarizes it: findings changed, moved up (and to P0), moved down, and deadlines moved earlier (table `scoring_change_impacts`).
- A finding a scoring change moves into P0 still sends its own `finding_priority_escalated` event (its ticket and workflow start at once); every other move is in the summary only.
- The summary is enqueued in the same transaction that marks it sent, so an outbox failure leaves it pending and the next worker pass sends it.
- The new event is on by default and is turned on for every channel that already receives priority escalations. Its severity follows the most urgent movement, so the channel's severity filter still applies.
- Priority escalations for any other reason (new findings, intel, asset context, controls) are unchanged.

### Changed: EPSS and KEV refreshes recompute only the findings whose CVE changed

- After the daily threat-intel refresh, only open findings whose catalog EPSS crossed a threshold the classifier or one of the organization's priority rules uses, or whose CVE entered or left KEV, are queued for a new priority and SLA deadline. Before, a KEV refresh queued every finding of each touched organization and EPSS changes reached no finding at all.
- Daily EPSS drift that crosses no threshold no longer causes a recompute; closed findings are never recomputed.
- The stored EPSS score and percentile of every open finding now follow the catalog after each refresh (a batched column update per organization), whatever the change. The CI gate's `epss_threshold` judges the stored score, so a finding whose EPSS rose above the gate's threshold now fails it the next day; before, the stored score only changed when a recompute happened to run.

### Changed: risk scoring settings show their whole-organization impact before they are applied

- `POST /settings/risk-scoring/preview` scores every asset with the new settings, the way the background worker will, instead of a 100-asset sample. It returns the score changes, band moves and the largest changes; assets outside the caller's data scope are counted but not named. When the ownership floor changes, it also returns the open findings that would change priority, the deadlines that would move earlier and the findings with a linked ticket.
- The console's Save opens this review; the settings are applied only from it.
- Saving no longer rescores in the request: the response is `{"config", "recompute": "queued", "scoring_version"}` and the workers recompute in the background. `POST /settings/risk-scoring/recalculate` queues every asset and answers `assets_queued` (was `assets_updated`).
- The preview is limited to 6 per minute per organization (429 with Retry-After): it is a dry run over every asset and open finding.

### Changed: the api depends on no sensor SDK module

- The chunked feed transfer (fetcher, bundle format, writer and consumer) comes from the contract module `github.com/openctemio/ctis/transfer`, where it moved unchanged from `github.com/openctemio/sdk-go/pkg/transfer` v0.1.0; bundles are byte-identical. The api no longer requires any `github.com/openctemio/sdk-go` module, so SDK releases and the SDK dependency graph never reach the api build (RFC-094).
- CI job "Platform depends on contracts only" fails when `api/` or `web/` requires, imports or vendors the sensor SDK or a sensor.
- The dev container builds from the `go.mod` pins with `GOWORK=off`, like CI and the release image: it no longer writes a `go.work` for a mounted `sdk-go` checkout, and such a mount is ignored and can be removed.

### Changed: the security ack survives base-branch merges and rebases

- `security-gate` records a digest of the pull request's security-sensitive
  lines when `security-ack` is added and keeps the label while that digest is
  unchanged. Merging `develop` in, rebasing, or pushing changes to other files
  no longer drops the ack; changing a sensitive line or adding a sensitive file
  still does, and a mismatching digest blocks the merge queue.

### Changed: security.txt names the disclosure policy by default

- `/.well-known/security.txt` now carries `Policy: https://docs.openctem.io/security/vulnerability-disclosure/` while the contact is the default security@openctem.io. An operator who sets `SECURITY_CONTACT` gets no default `Policy` line and sets their own with `SECURITY_POLICY_URL`.
- `SECURITY.md` matches the published disclosure policy: GitHub private vulnerability reporting as a second channel, fix targets by severity, testing rules for services we operate, and the safe harbor.

### Changed: the seed image is a psql client (114 MB to 9 MB) and runs as non-root

- `ghcr.io/openctemio/seed` is Alpine with the PostgreSQL 18 client and the
  seed files, instead of the full `postgres:18-alpine` server image (amd64:
  114.5 MB compressed with 1 CRITICAL and 24 HIGH advisories before, 8.9 MB
  with none after). It runs as uid 65532: psql needs no privileges.
- Usage is unchanged: `docker run --rm -e PGHOST=... ghcr.io/openctemio/seed:<tag> psql -f /seed/seed_required.sql`.
  The image no longer contains a PostgreSQL server or its entrypoint script.

### Changed: the sensor CLI snippet starts the sensor without deprecated flags

- The built-in CLI install snippet now starts the long-running sensor as a bare `./openctemio-sensor` (add `-verbose` for debug logs). Sensor v0.21.0 and later run the daemon with platform commands by default, and `-daemon` / `-enable-commands` are deprecated there.
- The `config.commands_disabled` setup check explains that platform commands were turned off (`-enable-commands=false` or `sensor.enable_commands: false`) and its fix says to remove that setting, instead of asking for the deprecated flags.
- Migration: none. A sensor started with `-daemon -enable-commands` behaves the same; sensors older than v0.21.0 still need both flags.

### Changed: sensor heartbeat maximum follows the command lease; jittered Retry-After

- The longest heartbeat interval the platform advises is now derived as
  `min(offline mark / 2, SENSOR_COMMAND_LEASE / 3)`;
  `SENSOR_HEARTBEAT_MAX_INTERVAL` can only lower it. Raising the lease, the
  offline mark or any heartbeat setting can no longer let a sensor that holds
  a command heartbeat too rarely to renew its lease, which re-queued the
  command and ran it twice. The defaults are unchanged (45 s).
- When the doorbell query is slow (platform under load) the doorbell advises
  that maximum interval.
- A 429 from the sensor routes now carries a `Retry-After` computed from the
  refused bucket's refill time plus up to 50 % jitter, bounded to 1 s - 5 min,
  instead of a constant 1 s, so refused sensors do not all retry in the same
  second. Limits themselves are unchanged.

### Changed: sensor install snippets mount one data volume

- The docker run, Compose and Kubernetes snippets mount ONE volume at
  `/var/lib/openctem` (the sensor's `state/`, `outbox/` and `content/`)
  instead of three; the Kubernetes manifest has one 8Gi PVC
  (`<sensor>-data`), and the Helm snippet sets
  `sensor.data.persistence.enabled=true` (chart 0.19.0+). Sensors installed
  with three volumes keep working; the sensor README has the migration.
- The setup checklist explains the sensor's new `storage.outbox_persistent`
  check (an outbox off any volume loses undelivered results when the
  container is recreated), and the state and key-renewal fixes point at the
  data volume.

### Changed: the templates directory layout

- **Upgrade note:** the default `SENSOR_CONFIG_TEMPLATES_DIR` is now `configs/sensor-products`. If you mounted edited templates over `configs/sensor-templates`, move them to the new layout:
  - `<format>.tmpl` goes to `sensor/<format>.tmpl`;
  - `collector-<format>.tmpl` goes to `collector/<format>.tmpl`;
  - `connector-tenable-<format>.tmpl` goes to `connector-tenable/<format>.tmpl`.
- Files left in the old layout are ignored, and the built-in templates are used instead.

### Changed: sensor install snippets and fix-it snippets use the SENSOR_ names

- Install commands, configuration templates and the configuration checklist's fix snippets set `SENSOR_API_URL`, `SENSOR_API_KEY`, `SENSOR_REGION` and `SENSOR_KEY_AUTORENEW` (the sensor release that ships with this version refuses the old `API_URL`, `API_KEY`, `REGION`, `PLATFORM_KEY_AUTORENEW`).
- **Upgrade note:** rename those variables on existing sensor hosts when upgrading the sensor.

### Changed: sensor install snippets no longer list tools

- The built-in sensor install snippets (config file, environment, docker run, CLI, Compose, Kubernetes, Helm) no longer set `SENSOR_TOOLS`, `-tools`, `sensor.tools` or a `scanners:` list. The sensor offers the tools it finds (a registered tool whose binary is installed), so the image variant defines the tool set; narrow it with the local policy's `tools.allow`. Re-emitting the tools a sensor last reported pinned a reinstalled sensor to its old tool set, so an upgraded image's new tools were never offered.
- The one-shot examples still name one tool (`-tool <name>`).
- The setup checklist fixes for "no scanner available", "scanner not installed" and "scanner not offered" now point at an image that ships the scanner and the local policy's `tools.allow` instead of `SENSOR_TOOLS`.
- Migration: none required. Deployments that set `SENSOR_TOOLS` keep working; it narrows the detected set (newer sensors treat it as a deprecated narrowing filter). To let a sensor offer every tool its image ships, remove `SENSOR_TOOLS` (Helm: leave `sensor.tools` empty).

### Changed: one session read per page load instead of six

- `GET /me/bootstrap` now also returns the caller's profile (`user`, as
  `/users/me`), their organizations (`tenants`, as `/users/me/tenants`), the
  organization policy (`tenant_creation_mode`, as `/auth/providers`) and the
  badge counts (`badges.unread_notifications`, `badges.easm_review`). Each part
  is the caller's own data; the review count is data-scoped and only sent with
  `assets:read` and the attack surface module, like `/easm/candidates`.
- The web console reads these from the bootstrap instead of asking each
  endpoint on every page load, so a hard load of any page sends five fewer
  requests, and `/auth/providers` (which shares the sign-in rate limit) is only
  asked on the sign-in pages.
- The bootstrap response is `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

### Changed: settings are grouped by what they protect, and search finds individual settings

- The settings area has eight groups: My account, Organization, Security (Authentication, Domains, Trusted organizations, SSO approvals, Support access, Audit log), Access (Members, Teams, Roles, Directory sync, API keys, Service accounts, AI assistants), Findings & assets, Scanning, Scanner content and Integrations. Page URLs are unchanged.
- Search in the settings rail, on the Settings page and in the command palette finds the settings inside a page (for example "IP allowlist" or "interactsh"), opens the page at that setting and outlines it.
- The sensor scan-job controls (private targets, out-of-band callbacks, custom templates, tool User-Agent and TLS, sensor identity and key binding, shared sensors) moved from Authentication to the new Scanning › Sensor job safety page. They are still saved in the security settings and still change only for the owner.
- Settings forms on General, File storage, Authentication, Sensor job safety and Modules save through one sticky bar shown while there are unsaved changes, with Ctrl/⌘+S, and ask before you leave with unsaved changes.
- Authentication and Sensor job safety list the changes that weaken protection (for example two-factor no longer required, an emptied IP allowlist, callbacks allowed) and ask for confirmation before saving, and show who changed them last.
- General has one danger zone (transfer ownership, delete the organization); only the owner can edit the URL slug, as the API already required.

### Changed: the release feed is signed by one pinned online key

- The version-check release feed is signed directly by one online Ed25519 key whose public key is pinned in the binary (`releasefeed.PinnedKeys`, up to two entries for a rotation overlap); the offline root and the feed key set are gone. Rollback and sequence protection, the 45-day expiry, the link allowlist, https and the offline import are unchanged, and the check stays inert while no key is pinned. The release feed key signs only the feed and is never listed in the catalog key set.
- `cmd/release-feed`: `keyset` is removed, `build` no longer takes `-keyset`, `verify` takes `-key <public key hex>`. The migration drops the unused `version_check_state.keyset_version` column. The admin error code `no_root` is now `no_key`.
- The content catalog keeps root, key set and its own online key; its key set may be valid up to 365 days. The maximum key set validity is now per feed type (`feedsign.KeySetType.MaxValidity`): 365 days for the catalog, 180 days for the program feed and the vulnerability bundle (unchanged). `feedsign.MaxKeySetValidity` is removed.

### Changed: capability contracts come from the ctis capability taxonomy

- The scan-stage catalog now reads each capability's contract from `github.com/openctemio/ctis/capability`, the copy the SDK and the sensor also read (RFC-055). That covers the ports, the standard params, the tier floor and the required-output rules. The literal contracts in `stage/contract.go` are gone.
- The catalog keeps only platform data:
  - the stored asset pairs each port carries;
  - the implementations and their defaults;
  - the fan-out caps;
  - the display names of the required fields.
- At start, the API refuses a catalog stage whose tier differs from its capability's floor, or a capability the taxonomy does not know.
- `GET /api/v1/scans/stages` adds `phase`, `ctem_stage`, `attack` (MITRE ATT&CK) and `d3fend` to each capability.
- Three planned capabilities are listed: `discover.cloud`, `sbom.generate` and `import.file` (cross-cutting).
- `verify.finding` gains its standard param `mode` (`retest` or `exploit_check`).
- Existing fields of `/scans/stages` are unchanged for the 22 capabilities it listed.

### Changed: a task is stalled only when nothing moves, and its sensor hands back what it finished

- The heartbeat's per-command progress also carries liveness counters (`records`, `output_bytes`, `cpu_ms`; migration `002099_command_liveness`). A running task is stalled only when none of finished targets, records, output bytes or CPU time (by at least 2 s since it last counted) moved for its stall window, so a slow but working batch tool (a large httpx list, naabu, nuclei) is never cut. This replaces the rule that a task was stalled only after it finished a target.
- A stalled task is no longer re-queued at once: its sensor is asked to stop it and hand back what it finished (`stop_command_ids` in the heartbeat answer). The task completes partial and only its unfinished targets run again. With no answer within 5 minutes (a sensor that cannot stop it) it is re-queued as before. A task that stops with nothing finished is re-queued, not failed.
- The overrun cap (twice the task budget plus 5 minutes) is unchanged and applies whatever the signals say: they are hints that can delay a stall decision, never the overrun cap or the run's deadline.

### Changed: suppressed findings are dispositions, not fixes

- **A suppression rule marks a finding `false_positive` or `accepted`,
  never `resolved`** (owner decision O9). A false-positive
  rule gives `false_positive`; accepted-risk and won't-fix rules give
  `accepted`. The resolution stays `suppressed` and `finding_suppressions`
  names the rule. Fix rate and MTTR therefore count real fixes only.
- Migration 000751 moves existing `resolved` / `suppressed` rows to the
  disposition of their recorded rule (same tenant), only when that rule is
  certain; rows with no recorded rule or conflicting rules stay as they are.
  The relabel is not counted as a regression.

### Changed: approving a suppression rule moves findings through the transition engine

- Closing the open findings a newly approved suppression rule matches is now decided, finding by finding, by the transition engine with a new `rule` actor. Only a rule may move matching open findings straight to its disposition (false positive or accepted); no other actor gets this. The timeline entry of each finding records the rule id and `actor_kind: rule`. The acceptance cap by priority and the rule's scope are unchanged.

### Changed: rotation off rescans what the license already counts

- With rotation off, assets the connector assessed before are rescanned without using license headroom, and new assets are added only while the license has room.

### Changed: a Tenable.sc scan's unfinished targets are recorded on its run

- When a `connector_scan` result carries per-target outcomes (sensor with the Tenable.sc tracking change), the targets it left unfinished end the step `partial` with "N target(s) not finished" and are recorded on the run's unfinished targets, so the next scheduled run plans them first and coverage never reads them as covered. Targets are read against the command's own targets; a sensor cannot add one. Results without outcomes (older sensors) behave as before.

### Changed: the Tools page shows what your sensors really have

- Settings > Scanning > Tools lists the tools your sensors report, with a status per tool: Ready, Offline only, No sensor, Outdated or Disabled. It also shows the sensors that have each tool (n/m online, with zones), their versions, the last report and the organization's on/off switch. "Show full catalog" adds every catalog tool. The install details moved into the tool detail, under "How to add this tool to a sensor". The card view is gone.
- The scan builder, the quick scan and the workflow tool pickers disable a tool no online sensor can run and say why. The sensor detail marks a tool its grant or local policy refuses. The Capabilities page says which tools are ready.
- Custom tools can set a minimum version.

### Changed: shorter guidance text on assets, findings and CI/CD pages

- Assets overview and duplicate review no longer mention the internal
  "correlator"; the duplicate-review title is in sentence case.
- Finding data flow: the explainer banner and the three-step "to enable"
  box become one line each; the empty state is titled "No data flow"
  instead of "No Attack Path Data".
- Exposure type overview: the fallback no longer says the breakdown "needs a
  newer API version".
- CI/CD integration, CI runs and CI trust: subtitles no longer list six CI
  providers, and empty states say what to do in one line.
- Touched strings are now translated (en, vi).

### Changed: shorter guidance text on prioritization and insights pages

- Attack paths, exposure chains, CTEM maturity, data quality and program
  health: page subtitles cut to one short sentence, the explainer under each
  ranked list no longer repeats the subtitle, and empty states say what to do
  in one line. These strings are now translated (en, vi).
- The priority-rule dry run no longer tells you to start a reclassification
  sweep from the Cycles page: saving a rule already reclassifies the matching
  findings.
- CTEM maturity no longer shows the internal "maturity aggregator" name when
  it fails to load; compensating controls drop a note about what the
  percentage "does not currently" do.

### Changed: shorter guidance text on scan settings and the admin console

- Scanner templates, capabilities, scan zones, clone scan, new scan and the
  system-template copy notice: subtitles and hints cut to what you need;
  internal wording removed ("stored in database", "extend the tool
  registry", "scans dispatch as before").
- Admin console target mappings: the empty state no longer names the
  internal "smart filtering".
- Touched strings are now translated (en, vi).

### Changed: shorter guidance text on scoping, cycles, reports and automations

- Cycles: the same "a cycle binds the charter…" sentence appeared as the
  subtitle, the empty state and the scoping overview card; the empty state
  now just says to create one.
- Attack surface review: subtitle cut to the ownership-versus-scope point.
- The review queue no longer shows the raw `assets:write` permission code;
  cycle fields no longer guess that a module "may be off".
- Finding remediation, scheduled and executive reports, create automation:
  filler sentences removed ("cron cadence", "board decks", "consult the
  documentation").
- Touched strings are now translated (en, vi).

### Changed: shorter guidance text in settings and account pages

- Asset lifecycle: the subtitle and the card no longer explain the same
  thing twice; the permission notice no longer shows the raw `team:update`
  code, and the load error no longer guesses that "the lifecycle endpoint may
  not be available on this environment".
- Vulnerability scanners: the paused-connector notices drop internal wording
  ("scanner runner", "no runner any more").
- SLA policies, AI access (MCP), Jira ticketing, account activity, create
  team and notifications: subtitles and hints cut to what you need to act;
  a subtitle that only repeated the title is gone. Touched strings are now
  translated (en, vi).

### Changed: sensor latest v0.14.0, SDK latest v0.20.0

- versions.yaml and its consumers: sensor v0.14.0 (protocol v3 transport selection, self key bind, adaptive per-host scan rate with coverage gaps), SDK v0.20.0.

### Changed: sensor v0.15.0 and sdk-go v0.21.0 are the latest versions

- The install snippets pin sensor v0.15.0 (gRPC on the platform port through ALPN routing; keeps protocol v3 across platform restarts). sdk-go latest is v0.21.0.

### Changed: sensor v0.17.0 and sdk-go v0.23.0 are the latest versions

- Install snippets pin sensor v0.17.0, which reads the SENSOR_-prefixed names (`SENSOR_API_URL`, `SENSOR_API_KEY`, `SENSOR_REGION`, `SENSOR_KEY_AUTORENEW`); the snippets use them again (re-land of #1860).

### Changed: install snippets pin sensor v0.22.2; SDK v0.32.0 is the latest

- The console's sensor install commands and the "update available" check point at sensor v0.22.2: one refused target no longer fails a whole scan task (the others run and the refused one is listed with its reason), and `host:port` targets are checked on their host.
- The newest SDK is v0.32.0, so a sensor built with an older SDK shows "SDK outdated". Sensor v0.22.2 is built with it; sensor v0.22.1 (an earlier sdk-go build) shows "SDK outdated" and "update available" together, both pointing at v0.22.2.
- `versions.yaml` names Helm chart 0.23.3, the newest published chart for v0.9.5 (it said 0.4.1).

### Changed: the vulnerability feed verifies with the shared signed-feed package

- pkg/vulnbundle uses pkg/feedsign for its key set, envelopes and strict decoding instead of its own copy; the checks and limits are unchanged.

### Changed: CI/CD integration has its own page; the Sensors page opens on the sensors

- New page **Discovery > CI/CD** (`/ci-cd`, `scans:ci:read`, `scans` module): CI pipelines, their runs and repository coverage, plus a **Trust and gate** tab (trust configurations, gate policy, break-glass) and links to the GitHub Actions and GitLab CI guides.
- The Sensors page opens on the sensors in your networks (daemon mode) and links to CI/CD with the number of active pipelines; the Runner and All modes stay available.
- `/ci-runners`, `/ci-runners/{run}` and the old runner-sensor list `/runners` redirect (308) to CI/CD. The settings entry is renamed **CI/CD integration**.

### Changed: dialogs keep their title and actions in view while the form scrolls

- Dialogs, confirmations and side sheets share one frame: a fixed header (title, description, close), a body that is the only part that scrolls, and a fixed footer with the actions. The Add finding dialog uses it first; the other dialogs move onto it in follow-up changes.
- On phones a dialog opens as a bottom sheet that stays above the on-screen keyboard and brings the focused field back into view; the footer clears the home indicator. A dialog without its own height limit can no longer grow past the screen.
- Dialog widths are presets (`size`: sm, md, lg, xl, full) instead of per-dialog values. A governance test fails on a dialog that sets its own scroll, height or width.
- The Add finding and Import results buttons on the findings page have accessible names on phones, where they show only an icon.

### Changed: the finding's data-flow tab is labelled "Data flow"

- The finding page tab that shows the source-to-sink trace was labelled "Attack path". It is now "Data flow" (Vietnamese "Luồng dữ liệu"). Its link key stays `?tab=attack-path`, so existing links still open it.
- The finding page's not-found state, SLA callout and tab labels are translated (English and Vietnamese).

### Changed: asset detail and list screens are fully translated

- Owners, direct access, overview sections, classification badges, duplicate review, linked assets, facet panel and the inventory page header now take every label, toast and message from the English and Vietnamese dictionaries.

### Changed: asset screens are fully translated

- Inventory table and bulk actions, identity, findings, attribute sources, TLS cells and asset forms now take every label, toast and message from the English and Vietnamese dictionaries.

### Changed: the Exceptions page is translated

- The Exceptions page, its suppression rule form, detail drawer and reject dialog, and the suppression type and status labels read their text from the translation catalog in English and Vietnamese (new `exceptions` namespace) instead of showing English only.

### Changed: finding screens are fully translated

- The finding dialogs, tables, drawer and detail cards now show their text through the translation files, so they follow the chosen language (English and Vietnamese).

### Changed: finding detail tabs are fully translated

- The finding detail page cards and tabs (overview, evidence, remediation, related, retest, properties) now show their text through the translation files, in English and Vietnamese.

### Changed: the sensor Manifest tab and the asset overview, stat strip, row actions and Add relationship dialog are translated

- The sensor drawer's Manifest tab (sections, tool contract, history, ignored items, resources and concurrency text), the asset overview cards and hints, the inventory stat strip, the inventory row and bulk actions (Scan, Sync from source, Copy, their toasts) and the Add relationship dialog now read their text from the translation catalog in English and Vietnamese instead of showing English only.

### Changed: sensor pages are fully translated

- The sensor list, detail drawer, install, pairing, key rotation, grant, local policy, content and fleet screens now go through the translation catalog in English and Vietnamese.

### Changed: the web image ships node only, and its files are read-only to the server

- The `openctem-web` runtime is Alpine plus the node binary: npm, npx, the C
  headers and the glibc shim are no longer in the image at all (before, npm
  was deleted in a later layer, so its bytes still shipped in the base layer).
  amd64: 83.9 MB compressed / 282 MB unpacked before, 76.8 MB / 253 MB after.
- The application files are owned by root, so the Next.js server (uid 1001)
  can no longer modify its own code; `.next/cache` stays its only writable
  directory (with `/tmp`), as the read-only Compose deployment already assumes.
- The image no longer has the node image's `docker-entrypoint.sh` entrypoint;
  the command is still `node server-with-ws.mjs`.

### Changed: the invite dialog explains what will happen, and roles show their risk

- The invite dialog takes one primary role (built-in, then custom roles) and optional additional roles. As you type the address it previews what will happen: whether the person is outside your organization or uses a personal address, whether you will confirm your identity, whether they will need two-factor authentication, and an end of access only for someone outside. A policy refusal is a translated sentence under the address, and sending is disabled; server errors are shown as translated messages, never raw text.
- The role list no longer scrolls inside the dialog, so no card or focus ring is clipped. Every role shows a risk tier and what it views or changes, instead of a permission count, in the invite dialog, the role editor for a member, the roles table and the role details.
- Role details show "Template update available" with what the update adds and removes, and apply it on request. Creating a role from a template records the template.
- Pending invitations show "Outside" and "Two-factor required"; a resend sent too soon says so.
- Settings › Authentication: "Who can be invited" (anyone, verified domains only, verified and allowed domains) and "Require an end of access for people outside".
- The dialog, the role picker and these settings are translated (English and Vietnamese).

### Changed: the web console caches each endpoint once, and an organization switch clears the cache

- Pages that read the same endpoint (the dashboard, threat intel, validation,
  scoping, exposures, sidebar badges) now share one cached answer instead of
  fetching it again under a second cache key.
- Switching organization drops every cached answer before reloading, so no
  data of the previous organization stays on screen while the new one loads.

### Changed: the asset Ownership card says what each choice does, and whether scans may reach the asset (web)

- The card is now "Ownership and scope". It answers two questions side by
  side: is the asset ours (state, confidence, evidence), and may scans reach
  it (the scope entry, seed or verified domain that covers it, or "Out of
  scope" with an "Add to scope" action).
- The decision buttons have plain labels ("Ours", "Not ours", "Ours, on
  third-party infrastructure", "Watch only", "Undo the decision") and the
  consequence of each is written next to it, not only in a tooltip.
- The card states that confirming ownership does not authorize scanning
  (RFC-054 §4.2): a scope entry decides what scans may reach.

### Changed: pentest settings and the finding library are translated

- Settings › Pentest methodology (campaign types and methodologies), the
  finding library (list, new, edit, detail) and the shared finding form
  cards (classification, steps, impact and remediation, tags, references,
  asset and workflow) now show every text in the user's language (English
  and Vietnamese), including template categories, severities, toasts,
  validation messages and button labels. Unused template dialogs were
  removed.

### Changed: the pentest workspace is translated

- The pentest findings list, retest queue and retest dialog, evidence
  uploader, OWASP checklist, campaign dashboard, campaign and finding badges,
  SLA indicator, finding section navigation and the module error page show
  every text in the user's language (English and Vietnamese). The retest
  dialog's hints name the current finding statuses (resolved, fix applied,
  in progress), and the checklist's emoji note buttons are icons.

### Changed: pentest console follows the campaign phases

- The campaign page, quick view and list offer the phase actions in words (Start testing, Finish testing, Deliver report, Close campaign; Back to testing, Reopen testing with a reason, Put on hold, Resume) to the campaign lead and to org admins who are members; the stepper has five steps and a "Ready to start" mark for planning campaigns (dates, authorization letter, lead and tester, scope).
- New finding is offered per phase (testers while testing, reviewers while reporting) with the reason when it is not; the campaign picker lists campaigns in testing or reporting; list metrics and filters cover Reporting.
- Mark as duplicate (lead, reviewer) picks the finding of the same campaign it repeats; retests can be recorded as "Unable to verify" with a reason. English and Vietnamese.

### Changed: the web console polls only while it can change something

- The permission sync no longer polls every 2 minutes while the real-time
  connection is up; role changes still apply on the next request.
- Scan pages refresh their run lists every 10-30 seconds only while a run is in
  progress, and every 2 minutes otherwise.

### Changed: the web console revalidates reference data instead of downloading it again

- The `/api/v1` proxy forwards `If-None-Match` and passes back the API's `ETag`
  for responses the browser may keep, and answers `304 Not Modified` without a
  body. The asset type registry (about 107 KB) is no longer downloaded again on
  every asset page load.

### Changed: the web console sends one request per identical GET in flight

- Two parts of a page that read the same URL at the same time (under different
  cache keys, or a direct read racing a hook) now share one request. In
  development, a GET sent twice at once or repeated within a second logs a
  `[request-budget]` warning naming the URL.
- A guard test (`request-hygiene-guard.test.ts`) counts raw `fetch` of the API
  outside the API layer, `[url, tenantId]` cache keys and polling sites; the
  counts only go down (page-load request budget).

### Changed: the scan list shows each scan's real last run, and a schedule switch only where there is a schedule

- The Scans list's Status column (the configuration's Active/Paused flag, read as a run state) is replaced by **Last run**. It shows the latest run's real state (Running with its progress, Completed, Partial, Failed, Blocked with the reason on hover, or Never) and when it started. Clicking it opens the run. The scan page and the scan drawer show the same chip.
- The on/off switch moved to the **Schedule** column as "Schedule on/off" with the next run. Only scans with a schedule have it; manual scans have none. The scan page and drawer offer **Run now** on any enabled scan, paused or not, and "Schedule on/off" only for scheduled scans.
- The **Type** column shows what the scan runs: the workflow's name or the single check's tool, instead of "Single Scan" on every row. Results count blocked runs. The Runs tab can filter blocked runs, and a blocked run's drawer says why it was refused.
- A **Show one-off scans** filter lists the quick scans that are hidden by default.
- **New scan > Targets:** a wildcard pattern (`*.example.com`) given to an active scanner offers two fixes. One is "Discover subdomains of example.com", which switches to subfinder with the root as the seed. The other is "Scan the N known assets matching *.example.com".

### Changed: the assets table asks the server whether each asset is in scope (web)

- The Scope column comes from `POST /api/v1/scope/check` (one call per page)
  instead of matching scope patterns in the browser, which read `*.x` the old
  way and only saw the first 100 entries. The client-side matcher is removed.

### Changed: Scoping › Boundaries is now Scoping › Scope at /scope (web)

- The page moved from `/scope-config` to `/scope` with no redirect; every
  link and the navigation use the new URL.
- No inline status switches: activating an entry (a widening that may wait
  for approval) and lifting an exclusion are labelled row actions.
- Kinds are detected from the pattern (domain, IP address, IP range, URL,
  repository, cloud account); `subdomain` is no longer offered and older
  rows read as Domain.
- "Added by" shows the person (or the system action in words), never a raw
  user id or `system:...` string (shared `ActorChip`).

### Changed: Scope page with In scope, Out of scope and Approvals (web)

- Scoping › Scope lists what scans may touch on three tabs: In
  scope (entries), Out of scope (exclusions, which always win) and
  Approvals, one list of every entry and exclusion waiting for a second
  person, with who asked, why, what it covers, for how long and the approvals
  so far. Several changes can be approved at once; the requester never can.
- "Put out of scope" adds an exclusion with a detected kind, a required
  reason and an optional end; it waits for another approver.
- Widening row actions say so ("Activate (may need approval)", "Extend by 7
  days (may need approval)", "Lift (scans may reach it)"); there are no
  inline toggles.
- An empty In scope tab shows the three steps to get started (add your
  domain, prove it, discovery finds the rest), worded for the operator's
  active-proof mode.

### Changed: sensor Tool settings as a collapsible, searchable list

- The sensor drawer's Tool settings tab shows each tool as a collapsed row
  with its version and a summary ("All defaults", or "3 changed: rate-limit
  300, timeout 20, …"); tools with changes come first, then by name.
- A search box filters by tool or option name and opens the matching tool at
  the matching option. The open tools are remembered per sensor in this
  browser.
- Inside a tool the common options are open and the other groups are
  collapsed with their changed count; impact options keep their badge and get
  a short warning.
- Each changed option has a marker and "Reset to default"; "Reset tool" clears
  every option. One save bar per open tool appears only with unsaved changes
  (sticky at the bottom on a phone). Saving every option back to its default
  removes the stored settings. The save endpoints and permission checks are
  unchanged.

### Changed: the Sensors health metrics count every sensor that needs a look, and filter on click

- "Needs attention" now counts enabled sensors that are not connected (stale, offline or never connected). It also counts sensors that fail or have not sent their setup check, and sensors whose identity was cloned. The page used to drop the setup-check and cloned-identity reasons the API sends.
- "Fleet health" filters the list to the sensors that are not connected when there are any. Needs attention, Updates, Zones and protocol v1 filter or group as before. Jobs stays a number.
- The "Run style" filter shows only while the organization still has a one-shot sensor.

### Changed: toasts show at the top on phones

- On phones, toasts appear at the top of the screen, below the notch, instead of at the bottom. Dialogs are bottom sheets there with their actions pinned at the bottom, and an error toast used to cover the button needed next. Larger screens keep toasts at the bottom right.

### Changed: every remaining API read in the web console is cached under its URL

- Threat intelligence (sync status, EPSS, KEV, CVE enrichment), asset (full
  view, repository, tags) and exposure (detail, history) reads share the cache
  with every other reader of the same endpoint, and `mutate(url)` reaches them.

### Changed: checking a scan workflow draft reports every issue, by step

- `POST /api/v1/scan-workflows/verify` returns 200 with every issue of the
  draft, each anchored to its step and field (`node`, `field`) with a `fix`.
  It used to stop at the first step problem with a 400, so the builder showed
  nothing while the user edited a step with a bad setting. `errors` block a
  save; `warnings` do not.
- New warnings: a pinned tool no online sensor offers (`TOOL_UNAVAILABLE`),
  and a capability none of whose tools (the preferred ones when listed) is on
  an online sensor (`NO_SENSOR_FOR_CAPABILITY`).
- The builder shows errors and warnings on each node, and the step inspector
  lists them with their fixes. Settings outside the capability contract (a
  template's tool-native keys) are listed there and can be removed.
- A refused step is logged at debug level (it is user input, not a fault).
- Messages say "scan workflow" instead of "pipeline" (log fields
  `service`/`handler=scan_workflow`, conflicts, not found, run messages).
  An unknown tool reads `tool "x" is not installed in this organization`.
  Error codes are unchanged.

### Changed: the workflow edit form shows stages and fixes old-format steps

- The Steps tab of the workflow form groups steps by stage, from what each
  step runs after ("Stage 2 · 2 steps run in parallel · waits for Stage 1"),
  numbers them 1, 2a, 2b and shows the steps of one stage side by side.
- Each step has a "Runs after" choice; a step that already waits for it is
  disabled (no loops). Dragging a step onto another stage moves it there by
  taking that stage's dependencies, and refuses a move that would make a loop.
- A step in the old format (a tool without its catalog capability) offers a
  one-click "Use capability ... (tool implements it)" fix that keeps the tool
  pinned; a banner fixes every such step at once.
- Step changes made in the form save to the workflow's draft and publish only
  through "Save and publish", like the builder: the version scans run is never
  changed in place. A workflow with a draft is edited from its draft.
- The New Scan starter cards summarize steps by stage ("DNS resolution + HTTP
  probe (in parallel)") instead of a flat chain.

### Changed: New Scan shows which workflows can run here

- The New Scan wizard asks for each workflow's readiness. The ones that can
  run come first; a workflow that is only waiting for a sensor carries a
  short note.
- A workflow that cannot run here stays visible but is off and sorted last.
  A starter card is greyed with the reason and a link to the fix (add a
  sensor, enable a tool, set up the CI pipeline). In the workflow select,
  such workflows sit under "Not available" with their reason.
- The workflow list shows the same badge ("No capable sensor online",
  "Runs in your CI pipeline", "Not available").

### Changed: a workflow step runs on every eligible sensor

- A workflow step is no longer pinned to one sensor when it is queued. Its commands go to the run's zone, the platform queue or the organization's own sensors, and any sensor there that has the tool and whose grant admits the job may take them.
- A large step is cut into chunks, so several sensors share it. The chunk size comes from the step's capability (for example 200 targets for an HTTP probe or DNS resolution, 50 for a port scan, 25 for vulnerability templates). The step finishes with its last chunk: it fails only when every chunk failed, and ends partial when some did. When a sensor stops renewing its lease, its chunk goes back to the pool for another sensor.
- A workflow scan with several targets is no longer warned that only its first target is scanned.

### Changed: scan zones are documented as the sensor pool

- The scan-zones architecture doc states that the sensors assigned to a zone
  share its work (any of them may claim a command routed to the zone), and that
  zones (infrastructure) are kept apart from asset groups and scan targets
  (scope). No behaviour change.

### Fixed: admin-cli image size budget

- The release image check allowed the admin CLI image 30 MB; it is 34 MB since console sign-in gained WebAuthn and TOTP, which blocked publishing every v0.10.0 image. The budget is now 40 MB.

### Fixed: page-size selects no longer show empty on lists paged by 25

- Tables and pagers now always offer the page size in use (the console Users and Content packs lists open at 25, which was missing from the choices).

### Fixed: the admin console no longer lists or counts the internal System organization

- `GET /api/v1/admin/tenants` leaves the platform system tenant out of its rows and total; `include_system=true` lists it.
- The console overview no longer counts it as an organization, nor as one without an owner.

### Fixed: the deadline admission log reports whole seconds

- The "step not started: the run's deadline is too close" log line reports
  `left_seconds` and `need_seconds` as integers (code scanning flagged the
  durations as log input derived from user settings).

### Fixed: the all-in-one image starts again
- The all-in-one image now includes the gateway's `admin/` site snippets that the Caddyfile imports, so the gateway no longer exits at start with "File to import not found: admin/off.tenant".

### Fixed: the all-in-one image keeps its sensor CA on the data volume

- `SENSOR_MTLS_CA_DIR` now defaults to `/data/sensor-ca` in the all-in-one
  image. Before, the CA the API mints for sensor mutual TLS was written inside
  the container filesystem, so a re-created container (an upgrade) minted a
  new CA and every sensor's client certificate stopped being trusted.

### Fixed: the all-in-one image is published again

- The publish workflow downloaded the all-in-one digests with the pattern `digests-openctem-*`, which also matched the `openctem-api`, `openctem-web` and `openctem-gateway` digests, so the multi-arch manifest named digests of other images and v0.9.0 and v0.9.1 published no `ghcr.io/openctemio/openctem` image. The all-in-one digests now use their own artifact prefix.

### Fixed: the API images serve the OpenAPI spec again

- `openctem-api` and the all-in-one image generate the OpenAPI spec during the
  image build (it is no longer committed), so `GET /openapi.yaml` and `/docs`
  work on image installs instead of answering 404 / an empty page.
- The spec declares the project licence (GPL-3.0-only) instead of MIT.

### Fixed: the approvals list names each finding

- Findings > Approvals showed the first characters of the finding id. The list (`GET /api/v1/approvals`) now returns `finding_title` for each approval, read within the organization, and the page shows the title linking to the finding.

### Fixed: the approvals list filters by status and counts within the data scope

- `GET /api/v1/approvals` takes `status` (pending, approved, rejected,
  canceled, expired; without it every status is listed) with `page` and
  `per_page`, and returns `status_counts`. It used to return pending
  approvals only, so the Approved, Rejected and Canceled tabs of
  Findings > Approvals were always empty.
- For a restricted member the list, `total` and `status_counts` are filtered
  in the query to approvals whose finding is in their data scope (the total
  used to count every pending approval of the organization).
- The Approvals page reads each tab from the server, pages through it, and
  shows Cancel only on the caller's own pending requests (the server refuses
  anyone else).

### Fixed: every asset fact is visible, and structured properties read as tables

- The "+N" after a chip list (IP addresses, CNAMEs, open ports, technologies, labels) is now a button that opens the full list, with a "Copy all" button, on click, tap or keyboard. It used to be a hover-only tooltip, so the hidden values could not be reached on touch screens or inside the asset drawer.
- The asset drawer's facts list every value instead of "+N".
- Asset properties render by shape: DNS records, open ports and other record lists as compact tables (type, name, value, TTL; port, protocol, service, product, version), objects as labelled values, deeper values as pretty-printed JSON in a collapsible block with a copy button, timestamps as local dates with the relative time. They used to print as one long JSON line.
- The property list gets a search box when it holds more than eight values, and labels of keys outside the registry keep their acronyms ("DNS record count", not "Dns record count").

### Fixed: a closed dialog no longer loads the whole asset group list

- A disabled asset group list (the closed Edit scan dialog, a group scope rule
  dialog on another rule type) sent `GET /asset-groups` anyway, so the Scans
  page and every page holding such a dialog paid one extra request on load.
  It now sends nothing until the dialog needs the list.

### Fixed: the asset lifecycle worker demotes assets ingest stopped seeing

- The stale pass required a row in `asset_sources` before it would demote an
  asset. Nothing writes that table, so an enabled worker never marked any
  discovered asset stale. It now decides from the asset itself: the clock is
  `assets.last_seen` (moved only by ingest and integrations) and the
  provenance is `assets.discovery_source`, mapped to the categories of the
  "excluded source types" setting (manual, import, integration, scanner; an
  asset with no discovery source counts as manual). A raw discovery source
  (for example `cert_transparency`) can also be excluded on its own.
- Tenants that enabled the worker will see ingest-discovered assets that were
  not re-observed within the threshold go stale on the next run. Run the
  dry-run first to preview the count. The worker is off by default.

### Fixed: asset risk scores follow their findings

- An asset's risk score was recomputed only by the manual recalculation, so
  findings that arrived by CI upload, sensor ingest, import, bulk triage or
  auto-resolve never moved it (a repository with 81 open findings showed 0).
  Database triggers now queue an asset whenever an input of its score changes
  (its findings, criticality, exposure, data context, business units and
  services), and a background worker rescores queued assets per organization
  every few seconds, one rescore per asset however many findings changed.
  A daily reconcile rescores everything as a safety net.
- Assets in the API carry `risk_scored_at` (absent = never scored) and
  `risk_score_pending` (a rescore is queued).
- Migration `002153_asset_risk_queue` adds the queue, the triggers and the
  column, and queues every asset once.
- **Upgrade note:** nothing to run. After the migration the worker rescores
  the whole inventory within minutes; watch
  `openctem_asset_risk_queue_depth` fall to 0.

### Fixed: asset counts, tags and asset details answered 404

- The asset component routes were mounted at `/api/v1/assets/{id}`, which captured every one-segment asset route (`/stats`, `/tags`, `/facets`, `/overview`, `/changes` and `GET /assets/{id}`) and answered 404: the inventory KPI strip showed 0 while the list below had rows. Each component sub-path now has its own group.

### Fixed: technology detections removed from asset software

- A migration copies the technologies existing assets show into the asset technologies list; a
  background job (`asset-technology-backfill`, once per organization) gives them their category and
  removes the software component links earlier ingest created for detections that have no version and no
  CPE. A versioned or CPE-backed link is never removed, and each removed link is recorded. The first run
  only reports (a count and a sample in the log); set `ASSET_TECHNOLOGY_BACKFILL_REPORT_ONLY=false` to
  delete. Batches of 500 rows, no long locks (RFC-112).
- Upgrade note: migration `asset_technologies_backfill` reads `assets` and writes only the new tables.

### Fixed: "Assign to owners" skips closed findings and changes status only along the lifecycle

- `POST /api/v1/findings/actions/assign-to-owners` assigned resolved, false
  positive and accepted findings to their asset owners. Closed findings are now
  left alone.
- It tried to move a `new` finding straight to `in_progress`, which is not a
  lifecycle edge (the error was dropped). A `new` finding is now assigned and
  stays `new`; a `confirmed` finding moves to `in_progress`. The response
  reports how many started (`started`).

### Fixed: stuck, hung and failing automation runs end

- Automation runs that a restart left pending or running are failed with their
  open steps. The `automation-run-reaper` controller does this on start and every
  15 minutes, for runs over an hour old.
- The 30-second per-step limit is applied. A hung step fails, and the run goes on
  to its next step.
- An automation whose latest 20 runs all failed is switched off (audited, reason
  `consecutive_failures`).
- When a run finishes, it no longer switches back on an automation that was
  switched off while the run was executing.
- A manual automation run now records the finding or asset it was started on as its subject.

### Fixed: a batch of new findings starts one automation run per finding

- A `finding_created` automation now runs once for every new finding that
  matches it. Before, it ran once per ingest batch, for the first matching
  finding only: with 40 new critical findings, "critical → ticket" filed one
  ticket.
- The same event never starts an automation twice: runs carry their subject and
  an idempotency key (migration 001222, `workflow_runs.subject_id`,
  `workflow_runs.idempotency_key`).
- Runs are bounded where they are created: 200 per automation and 5,000 per
  organization per hour. Over the limit, events are dropped and one `THROTTLED:`
  run per hour records it in the automation's history. Up to 100 runs per
  automation (500 per organization) may wait. They run 10 at a time per
  organization, and a run waits for a free slot instead of failing at once.

### Fixed: runs say when an automation or a retry started them

- A scan run started by an automation's `trigger_scan` step now has
  `trigger_type` `automation` (it said `manual`). Its run context names the
  automation, the automation run and the step (`automation_cause.node_key`).
- A run started by the retry of a failed run has `trigger_type` `system`
  (it said `manual`).
- Migration 001309 allows `automation` and relabels earlier automation runs
  (`triggered_by` `workflow:<id>`).

### Fixed: the Automations canvas shows and saves only what runs

- The visual builder no longer opens on a hard-coded demo graph. A new workflow starts with one manual trigger, and a stored workflow opens as saved.
- Selecting a step opens an inspector for its settings: the trigger, the action or the notification channel, a saved scan for "Trigger scan", tags as a list, and JSON for other settings.
- The API refuses a workflow graph with a cycle, a step no trigger reaches, an edge into a trigger or a condition edge without a yes/no branch (400, `WORKFLOW_GRAPH_CYCLE`, `WORKFLOW_GRAPH_UNREACHABLE` or `WORKFLOW_GRAPH_EDGE`). It refuses before anything is written, so a bad save no longer leaves the stored graph half-replaced. The canvas refuses the same connections while you drag and lists the steps that are not connected.
- The `run_script` action, which always failed, is refused on write (400 `UNSUPPORTED_WORKFLOW_FEATURE`) and is no longer offered. The `finding_status_changed` trigger, which the finding service already fires, is now accepted and offered.
- Workflow validation errors carry their code in the response `code` field.

### Fixed: database passwords with URL characters, and the first owner's link when e-mail fails

- `bootstrap-admin`, the all-in-one image's start-up migrations, `scripts/migrate.sh`
  and the development entrypoint built the database URL from `DB_*` without
  escaping it, so a password with `@ : / ? #` or `%` in it failed to connect
  or connected with the wrong value. User, password and database name are now
  percent-encoded. A `DATABASE_URL` / `DATABASE_MIGRATE_URL` you set yourself is
  used as given: percent-encode the password in it.
- `bootstrap-admin -org-*`: when sending the new owner's set-password e-mail
  failed (for example an unreachable relay), the link was neither sent nor
  printed. It is now printed once on standard output with a warning that it is
  a secret; it is never written to a log.
- Docs: `AUTH_JWT_SECRET` is optional everywhere (derived from
  `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` when unset); the READMEs and the Kubernetes page still
  listed it as required.

### Fixed: creating a remediation campaign works again

- Creating a campaign failed with an internal error after the campaign version column was added (the insert sent one value more than it named). Campaigns are created at version 1.

### Fixed: remediation campaign dates accept a date alone and refuse anything else

- `start_date` and `due_date` on `POST` and `PATCH /api/v1/remediation/campaigns` take an RFC 3339 timestamp or a date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, UTC). A date alone is the start of that day for `start_date` and its last second (23:59:59 UTC) for `due_date`.
- A value in any other form is answered 400; before, create dropped it silently.
- `PATCH` with `"due_date": null` (or `start_date`) clears the date; before, null was ignored.

### Fixed: a remediation campaign page lists the findings its count counts

- New `GET /api/v1/remediation/campaigns/{id}/findings` (remediation:read and findings:read): the findings the campaign tracks, from its finding filter, remediation key or linked findings, any status, on the caller's in-scope assets. Its total equals the campaign's `finding_count` for the same caller.
- The campaign page lists those findings, so a campaign scoped by a filter or a remediation key no longer shows "Findings (0)" next to "8 findings linked" in the list. Unlink is offered for explicitly linked findings only.

### Fixed: remediation campaign saves no longer undo each other

- Saving a campaign checks its `version`: a save made on a stale copy (a second tab, or the progress reconciler after someone paused or canceled the campaign) is refused with `409 Conflict` instead of silently reverting the change. `PATCH /api/v1/remediation/campaigns/{id}` and `/{id}/status` accept the `version` the caller edited; responses carry it.
- Reading a campaign (`GET`) never writes it any more; the reconciler and `POST /{id}/refresh` store the counts, through an update that never touches status.
- Completing a campaign of 1,000 or more findings no longer fails: the risk fields stored finding counts in `numeric(5,2)` columns. They are widened and left unset until campaign risk is measured; the counts they held are cleared (migration `remediation_campaign_version`).
- The reconciler no longer starves campaigns beyond its batch: it takes the least recently reconciled first and stamps each one it visits.
- A campaign is overdue only after the end of its due day (UTC), not from its first minute.
- Priority must be `critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low` (API validation and a database CHECK); stored `urgent` values become `critical`. An empty name is refused on update.

### Fixed: an organization admin who is on a campaign team keeps their campaign role

- An admin who is the lead (or another member) of a pentest campaign got "You do not have permission to access this resource" when opening the campaign (the test credentials list) and could not sign off its completion: campaign routes skipped resolving an admin's campaign role. The role is now resolved for admins too; admins who are not members still pass the campaign role checks as before, and still cannot read test credentials or sign off without joining.

### Fixed: the CI/CD page explains access, break-glass and empty lists instead of dead-ending

- A developer who opens a pull request's gate link for a repository outside their access sees why: the run is not in their access, the PR comment lists what blocked it, and an administrator can grant access. Before, it said only "CI run not found".
- Empty pipeline and run lists no longer claim "No CI pipelines yet" to readers who cannot see the pipelines. A verdict filter that matches nothing says so. The empty pipeline list offers only "Connect a pipeline".
- After a break-glass, the console says to re-run the pipeline on that commit: its next run passes and the check turns green.
- The setup sections can be linked (`/ci-cd?tab=setup&section=feedback`). After installing the GitHub App, the callback returns to Pull request feedback.
- "GitHub App guide" is a link. The run list shows the verdict next to the repository, so it is visible on a phone. Pagination nouns and the Sensors page's CI runner strings are translated.

### Fixed: CI coverage, pipeline details and status labels are translated

- The CI/CD coverage view, the pipeline detail sheet (overview, runs,
  branches, retire dialog), pipeline status and freshness labels, gate reason
  badges and cadence ("every 6 hours") now use the console's English and
  Vietnamese catalogs. The guard test also checks every key built from a
  status, reason, capability or tab value.

### Fixed: the CI/CD page's pipelines, runs and OIDC banner are translated

- The CI/CD page header and tabs, the pipelines view (metrics, columns,
  search, empty states), the runs view and run details, the "Require OIDC for
  CI" banner and the Sensors page link card now use the console's English and
  Vietnamese catalogs. Copy no longer names only two CI systems or tells
  people to run the sensor in a CI job; the header links one CI integration
  guide. A test checks that every CI/CD key exists in both catalogs.

### Fixed: CI trust, gate policy and break-glass settings are translated

- The CI/CD page's Trust and gate tab (trust configurations and their form,
  the sample-token check, pipeline snippet, gate policies and break-glass
  overrides) now uses the console's English and Vietnamese catalogs. The
  "always on" note says accepted risk and suppressions are honored while they
  apply.

### Fixed: a repository's CI gate policy follows it on merge and goes with it on delete

- `ci_gate_policies.scope_id` is replaced by `repository_asset_id` and `business_unit_id`, each with a foreign key. Before, merging or deleting a repository left its gate policy pointing at nothing. The API is unchanged (`scope_type` + `scope_id`). Policies whose repository or business unit no longer exists are removed by the migration.

### Fixed: the gate check and pull request comment are no longer lost or marked final too early

- Storing a run's verdict queues its GitHub or GitLab decoration in the same
  statement. Before, a failure of a later step left the verdict without a
  check, and branch protection waited for one forever.
- A failed post is retried up to eight times with a backoff (30 seconds,
  doubling, at most 30 minutes apart). Before, five attempts ran within about
  75 seconds. A GitHub rate limit (429, or 403 with Retry-After or no
  requests left) is retried instead of being final.
- When GitHub recomputes a pull request's merge commit because the base
  branch moved, a run that judged the same head (one of the merge commit's
  parents, as GitHub reports them) still posts its check on the head.
  Before, it was skipped as "newer commits".
- The check is `action_required` when only a scanner failure failed the gate.
  Findings the policy lists in comment mode are notice annotations, marked
  "not blocking" in the comment.

### Fixed: a CI provider outage or key rotation no longer refuses CI jobs

- The CI provider's discovery document is now served stale (up to six hours,
  like its keys) when the provider cannot be reached. Before, every CI token
  exchange failed once the one-hour cache expired, even with the keys still
  cached. Concurrent refreshes wait for one fetch, and a failed fetch is not
  retried within 30 seconds.
- A token whose keys cannot be fetched (the provider is unreachable past that
  bound, or it has just rotated to a key not yet fetched) now gets `503
  CI_ISSUER_UNAVAILABLE` with `Retry-After: 30`, and nothing is claimed, so
  the job retries the same token. Before, it got the same `401` as a forged
  token.

### Fixed: GitLab merged results pipelines get the gate status and the merge request note

- A merged results pipeline runs on the commit GitLab makes by merging the head into the target, never on the
  merge request's head, so its verdict was always skipped as "the merge request has newer commits": no status
  and no note. It is now posted when the run's pipeline is the merge request's head pipeline and its commit is
  the run's verified commit; the status is attached to that pipeline (`pipeline_id`), which the merge request
  shows. Merge train pipelines are still not decorated.

### Fixed: an approved exception covers the finding it was requested for

- The CI gate applies approved, unexpired suppression rules when it judges a run, so a rule approved after the finding was first seen (an `.openctem.yml` exception) no longer leaves that finding counting. Ingest still stamps only new findings; the gate decision is read only.

### Fixed: the CI/CD page's GitHub and GitLab snippets run the CI scanner

- The pipeline snippet of a GitHub or GitLab trust configuration ran the
  sensor's former CI image (`sensor:latest-ci`) with flags the sensor no
  longer has (`-auto-ci`), so a pipeline copied from the console failed. It
  now uses the openctemio/ci reusable workflow (GitHub) or template include
  (GitLab), pinned to a release: one job per capability (SAST, SCA, secrets,
  IaC) with the job's OIDC token and one gate job. A trust configuration with
  its own audience passes it (`oidc-audience`, or each GitLab job's
  `id_tokens`).

### Fixed: CI jobs joining one pipeline run at the same moment all get the run

- When several jobs of one pipeline run exchanged their tokens at the same moment, one of them could fail with
  a database unique violation and get no run, so its results never reached the platform. The insert's
  conflict target and an older unique index both matched the new aggregate runs; the older index now covers
  only the runs opened before the pipeline-run key. Migration `ci_aggregate_open_index_legacy_only`.

### Fixed: CI runners are judged against their own release line

- The token exchange compared the CI runner's version (openctemio/ci, `openctem-ci/v0.2.0`) with the sensor minimum (`SENSOR_MIN_VERSION`, v0.9.0). Every released CI runner was refused with `RUNNER_OUTDATED`, and every pipeline showed as degraded with "below the minimum".
- CI runners now have their own settings, `CI_RUNNER_LATEST_VERSION` (default v0.2.0) and `CI_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` (default none). They come from the new `ci` entry in `versions.yaml`, which also sets the release the console's pipeline snippets pin.

### Fixed: a CI run whose gate job never ran no longer stays "Running" for ever

- A sweeper concludes a CI run that is still running after its 6-hour pipeline window with the verdict `fail` and the reason `not_judged` (the run view shows "Never judged (the gate job did not run)"). Before, a cancelled pipeline or a skipped gate job left no verdict, so nothing blocked the merge. Findings the run uploaded are kept; a run judged in the meantime keeps its verdict.

### Fixed: the CI upload idempotency marker outlives a slow ingest
