- The in-flight marker of an `Idempotency-Key` upload now lives at least as long as the run token (15 minutes) or the request deadline when later, so a slow ingest is not replayed in parallel. A finished request overwrites or releases the key only while the stored record still carries its own body hash, so it never clobbers another request's record. A store failure between the two lookups is logged.

### Fixed: a large CI upload is no longer taken for a failed upload

- The response to a CI report upload listed every result of the report that already carries a decision
  (`known`), so it grew with the report. Past about 95,000 decided results it was larger than what the CI
  runner reads (8 MB), and a report the platform had stored counted as a failed upload: the gate then failed
  with "not uploaded". `known` now lists at most 10,000 results (lowest indexes first, about 1 MB); the new
  `known_total` counts them all and `known_truncated` is true when some were left out. Older runners keep
  working: they read `known` as before and show the results left out of it. The gate on the platform judges
  every finding either way.

### Fixed: connecting a pipeline twice no longer dead-ends, and the GitHub snippet starts on the pinned release

- When a trust configuration already admits the organization, "Connect a pipeline" reuses it and shows its snippet. It no longer fails with "name already exists" or the plan limit.
- The wizard asks for the default branch. The GitHub snippet scans pushes to that branch, not always `main`, and tells you where to save the file.
- The GitHub snippet grants `security-events: write`, which the openctemio/ci reusable workflow needs to start. The Azure Pipelines, Bitbucket and CircleCI snippets run the pinned release image instead of the moving `edge` build.

### Fixed: `command_claims_total{mode="claim_n"}` was never incremented

- The poll's claims (claim-N, the path every current sensor uses) are now counted, one per command handed out.

### Fixed: a new collector sensor gets the collector grant, and its refused reports say why

- A sensor created with type `collector` (create API, or a pairing approval with no profile chosen) now gets the `collector` grant profile (collect and connector_sync jobs, passive tier, no target network, push ingest on) instead of `internal-network-scanner`, which had push ingest off and refused every report. Migration 002075 changes the insert trigger only: existing sensors keep their grant.
- Trust is still never automatic: a new collector stays at trust level New and its reports are refused until an administrator promotes it. The install flow offers **Trust this collector to push asset reports** (off by default; `"trusted": true` on `POST /api/v1/sensors`, collector only). It needs `sensors:grant:widen`, is checked before the sensor is created, and is audited and notified like any promotion.
- `PUSH_INGEST_NOT_GRANTED` (protocol v2 item error `push_ingest_not_granted`) now names what is missing, the grant or trust, in its message and detail; the sensor timeline event and `sensor.push_refused_grant` audit entry carry `missing`. The sensor's Grant section explains a refused collector and links the fix.
- **Upgrade note:** a collector created before this release on `internal-network-scanner` keeps being refused. Change its profile to `collector` and promote it to Trusted on its Grant.

### Fixed: a collector's install commands run the asset collector

- The install commands of a sensor of type Collector rendered the scanner image with a local policy. They now run the asset collector (`SENSOR_COLLECTOR_IMAGE`, default `ghcr.io/openctemio/asset-collector:latest` until the collector tags a release) with its own settings: `SENSOR_API_URL`, the API key and vendor passwords as files (`SENSOR_API_KEY_FILE`, `*_FILE`), one data volume at `/var/lib/openctem`, a `doctor` check before `-daemon`. docker run, Compose and Kubernetes are covered; Helm says the chart bundles the scanner only.
- The docker run snippet's comment now describes the one data volume it mounts (`state/`, `outbox/`, `content/`), not three volumes.

### Fixed: owner resolution only names active members

- The owner-resolution job matched an asset's `owner_ref` email to suspended and offboarded members too; it now names only active members of the asset's organization. An owner that matches no member stays text on the asset, and no account or invitation is created for it.

### Fixed: task logs keep every attempt of a command

- A command released (sensor restart, lease expiry) and claimed again lost
  the logs of its new attempt: the sensor numbers each attempt's batches
  from 0 again and the platform took them for replays of the first
  attempt, answering 200 without storing them. Batches are now keyed by the
  command's lease epoch, which the platform reads from the command (the
  sensor never sets it), so every attempt's lines are kept (migration
  `command_logs_per_attempt`; existing batches get their command's current
  epoch).
- A batch with the seq of a stored one but other lines in the same attempt
  answers `dropped` instead of `stored`, is logged and is counted in
  `openctem_command_log_batches_dropped_total`; batches over the per-command
  caps are counted there too.
- A log batch that states a lease epoch (`X-OpenCTEM-Lease-Epoch`) the
  command is no longer held under is refused with 409, never filed under the
  new attempt.
- The task logs dialog reads lines oldest attempt first and marks where each
  attempt starts when there was more than one.

### Fixed: trivy components get their ecosystem instead of "other"

- A component reported with a package URL and no ecosystem label (trivy fs) takes its ecosystem from the PURL type (npm, golang, pypi, maven, cargo, nuget, gem, composer, hex, cocoapods, swift, pub, cran); more trivy package types are recognised as labels (uv, bun, rustbinary, jar, pom, sbt, dotnet-core, packages-props, gemspec, composer-vendor, mix-lock).
- Migration `001361_component_ecosystem_from_purl` corrects the components and asset components already stored as "other" whose PURL names an ecosystem. OS packages (deb, apk, rpm) stay "other".

### Fixed: the Compose stack pulls the images a release publishes

- `api/deploy/docker-compose.yml` defaulted the web console to
  `ghcr.io/openctemio/ui`, a name v0.9.0 is not published under, so
  `docker compose up` from a clean checkout failed. The API, web, job signer
  and gateway now default to `ghcr.io/openctemio/openctem-api`,
  `openctem-web` and `openctem-gateway` (the gateway also falls back to the
  file's release when `OPENCTEM_VERSION` is unset). API CI fails when the
  stack names an image the release workflow does not publish.
- The sensor gRPC overlay (`docker-compose.sensor-passthrough.yml`) no longer
  builds a gateway locally: the published gateway image has the layer4 module.
- **Upgrade note:** drop `API_IMAGE`/`UI_IMAGE` from `.env` if you set them to
  the new names; set them only to run v0.8.0 or earlier with this file.

### Fixed: large uploads and feed imports no longer fill a 100 MB tmpfs

- The API's `/tmp` was a 100 MB in-memory tmpfs, but finding imports (up to
  110 MB) and form uploads are spooled there and feed bundles are staged
  there. It is now the `api-tmp` volume (on disk, not counted against the
  memory limit).

### Fixed: destructive actions in the console ask before they act (part 1)

- Deleting a dashboard or a saved view, deleting an automation workflow, cancelling a scan run,
  disabling scans in bulk, resolving findings or exposures in bulk, unlinking a finding from a
  remediation campaign or task, cancelling an invitation, revoking an authorization letter, and
  suspending or ending a program now open a confirmation that names the object and the
  consequence. One click no longer changes data.
- Deleting an automation workflow from its row menu works again: the delete fired before the
  workflow id was set and was refused.
- The shared confirmation dialog: Cancel has the focus (Enter on open cancels), both buttons stay
  disabled while the action runs, Escape cannot close it mid-request, and its text (including
  "Type ... to confirm") is translated. Erasing a member's personal data and bulk deletes of ten
  or more scans ask the user to type the email or the count.

### Fixed: destructive actions in the console ask before they act (part 2)

- Unlinking an asset from a business unit or service, removing an asset from an asset group
  (quick view and the add-assets dialog), removing a member from a role, disabling a sensor,
  deleting a CI gate policy, revoking a break-glass override, merging duplicate assets, rejecting
  a scope change, and (platform console) removing an organization's limit override or blocking
  an AI application everywhere now open a confirmation that names the object and the consequence.
- Deleting or revoking a sensor from the sensor list asks for its name, and a bulk sensor delete
  asks for the count, as the sensor dialog already did.

### Fixed: settings confirmations name what they delete and are translated (part 3)

- Confirmations for API keys, service accounts and their keys, SCIM tokens, secret-store
  credentials, SIEM, ticketing, SCM and notification integrations, the notification outbox,
  finding templates, SLA policies, roles, module resets, sessions, MCP connections and
  applications, trusted organizations, verified domains, identity providers, SAML, report
  schedules, SSO change approvals and organization deletion now name the object, state the
  consequence and are translated (English and Vietnamese).
- Revoking or deleting an API key, deleting a service account or one of its keys, revoking a SCIM
  token and deleting a secret-store credential now ask the user to type its name. A bulk delete of
  ten or more finding templates asks for the count.
- Delete-role and the report-schedule delete use the shared confirmation (Cancel focused, no
  double submit) instead of their own dialogs.

### Fixed: discovery, scoping and scanning confirmations name what they delete and are translated (part 4)

- Confirmations for assets (single and bulk), asset owners, relationships and access grants,
  asset groups (delete, bulk delete, remove assets), business units and services, attacker
  profiles, crown jewels, priority rules, scope entries and exclusions, domain proofs, scanner
  integrations, SCM connections, template sources, tools, scanner templates (delete, deprecate),
  scan profiles, scan zones and workflow steps now name the object, state the consequence and
  are translated (English and Vietnamese).
- Bulk deletes of ten or more assets or asset groups ask the user to type the count. Deleting a
  business unit says its sub-units become top-level units (they are kept).

### Fixed: validation, remediation and access-control confirmations name what they delete and are translated (part 5)

- Confirmations for pentest campaigns, findings, reports and evidence, campaign members,
  controls, suppression rules, remediation tasks, finding approval requests, evidence notes,
  threat actors, indicators, comments, teams (delete, remove member, remove asset, remove role),
  assignment rules, scope rules, capabilities and CI pipeline retirement now name the object,
  state the consequence and are translated (English and Vietnamese).
- Deleting a pentest campaign, which deletes its findings, asks the user to type its name; bulk
  deletes of ten or more pentest reports ask for the count.
- The team, assignment-rule, scope-rule and evidence-note deletes use the shared confirmation
  (Cancel focused, no double submit) instead of their own dialogs.

### Fixed: platform-console confirmations name the object, repeat the verb and are translated (part 6)

- Platform-console confirmations for administrators (reset two-step verification, deactivate,
  reactivate, change role, break-glass mark/unmark/test, unbind the identity provider), target
  mappings, the platform identity provider, access requests and audit-chain rebaselining now name
  the object and are translated (English and Vietnamese). The administrators dialog's confirm
  button repeats the action ("Deactivate", "Reset") instead of a generic "Confirm".
- The visual workflow builder's step delete and discard confirmations are translated.

### Fixed: every new organization gets the deployment region

- Organizations created together with their owner (the console, self-service sign-up and approved access requests) were stored without the deployment region; only the other creation path stamped it. Existing organizations keep what they have (the region never changes after creation).

### Fixed: the coverage ledger no longer deadlocks with asset updates

- Inserting a ledger row takes a key-share lock on its asset (the foreign
  key). The coverage reconcile took those locks in arbitrary order in one
  statement per rule, while the asset business-context update locks the
  same assets `FOR UPDATE` in id order: the two deadlocked on live. The
  reconcile now reads assets in batches of 500 in id order (keyset, one
  short statement each, no wide transaction), inserts only missing rows in
  id order, and retries a statement once after a short jitter if PostgreSQL
  still reports a deadlock. The foreign key stays.

### Fixed: a refused coverage batch is blocked, not retried every minute

- The coverage loop left the zone routing to the scan trigger, so one target
  no scan zone could place refused the whole batch (`NO_ZONE_COVERAGE`) and
  the loop retried it every pass. The scope gate now routes zones for a
  coverage batch, so such a target is refused on its own (`zone_none`,
  `zone_no_sensor`) and blocked in the ledger while the rest runs. A batch
  the trigger still refuses as a whole (a domain refusal: zone coverage,
  approval, a scan that may not run) blocks its pairs with the code, checked
  again after 6 hours; any other error leaves them due.

### Fixed: Coverage-scoped auto-resolve no longer reads a missing coverage_type

- **Coverage-scoped auto-resolve no longer reads a missing `coverage_type`
  as full** (safety; CTIS spec 4.5, owner decision Q5).
  A scan command's run closed findings it no longer reported when its
  report declared `full` *or nothing at all*, while the report-level
  (repository) path already treated an absent value as no auto-resolve.
  Now only an explicit `full` qualifies; an undeclared report is refused
  with reason `coverage_undeclared`. **Upgrade note:** sensors whose sdk-go
  predates openctemio/sdk-go#150 send no `coverage_type`, so their scans no
  longer close findings on this path (fail safe; the mode defaults to
  `dry_run`). Sensors with that change send `full` only for completed runs
  and `partial` for runs that stopped part-way.

- **A finding's occurrence count grows with every sighting** (RFC-043 P0).
  Re-ingesting an existing finding wrote back the count it had loaded before
  the merge, so `occurrence_count` stayed at 1 however often a scan saw the
  finding, and concurrent ingests overwrote each other. The update now adds
  one to the stored value in SQL.
- **A finding another ingest just created is no longer reported as new, and
  keeps its ticket links** (RFC-043 P0). Ingest checked which fingerprints
  existed and then inserted the rest; when two ingests raced on one new
  finding, or one report named a finding twice, the second insert still
  counted as created and ran the new-finding steps (workflows,
  notifications, assignment rules, remediation keys, exposure bridge) under
  an id that was never stored. Its `ON CONFLICT` update also replaced the
  stored ticket links (`work_item_uris`) and metadata with the empty values
  of the incoming row. The upsert now returns the stored id and whether it
  inserted; only inserted rows count as created and run those steps, a
  repeated finding in one report is folded into the first, ticket links are
  never taken from the incoming row, and metadata keeps the stored keys.
- **Asset stats and facets respect data scope.** `GET /api/v1/assets/stats`
  and `GET /api/v1/assets/facets` counted every asset of the organization,
  so a member restricted to some assets (access groups) could read totals,
  breakdowns and property values of assets they cannot list. Both now apply
  the same data-scope filter as the asset list: a scoped member's numbers
  equal what their list shows, and in an organization where members without
  an access group see nothing, such a member gets empty stats and no facets.
  Administrators and unrestricted members see the same numbers as before.
  The facets query is also bounded: it reads the 5,000 most recently
  updated assets in scope, expands at most 50 elements of an array property
  per asset and returns the top 20 values per key from the database. On a
  larger inventory the facet counts are counts within that sample.

- **Findings keep the port they were found on.** CTIS `Finding.Network`
  (port, transport, service) was used only inside the network-VA dedup
  fingerprint and then dropped, so no stored finding knew its port. Ingest
  now stores it in `findings.network_port`, `network_transport` and
  `network_service` (migration 000377), and the finding API returns
  `network_port`, `network_transport` and `network_service`. A re-sighting
  fills a missing value and never replaces a stored port, so the port does
  not flip between scans for a finding whose fingerprint does not include
  it. Fingerprints are unchanged. Existing findings get the value on their
  next scan.

- **Scope exclusions apply on every path that scans or discovers, not
  only at scan trigger** (RFC-042 F16). Four paths ignored them:
  - `POST /api/v1/pipelines/runs` and the `trigger_pipeline` workflow
    action passed `context.targets` straight into the step commands. The
    run's targets now get a scan's checks: excluded targets are dropped
    (every target excluded: `ALL_TARGETS_EXCLUDED`); a private address
    outside every scan zone, loopback, link-local or metadata address, or
    a target zone routing cannot place refuses the run (400
    `TARGET_REFUSED`); a caller's `scan_zone_id` is ignored and set from
    the routing. These starts also crashed on a nil scan id before
    creating the run; they now work and are limited per pipeline.
  - The Tenable rolling coverage dispatcher sent its batches unchecked.
    Excluded or refused assets are now skipped for that rotation, a batch
    stays in one scan zone and its command is stamped with it.
  - Certificate Transparency discovery no longer queries an excluded
    domain or raises exposures for an excluded host.
  - Ingest no longer adds a new asset (or a root domain or resolved IP
    derived from one) that matches an exclusion by name, repository URL
    or address. It is counted as `assets_skipped_excluded` and named in
    the warnings; its findings are skipped, never attached to another
    asset of the report. Assets already in the inventory are not changed
    or deleted.
  A failed exclusion lookup stops each of these paths (fail closed).

- **Group scans resolve members as assets and skip archived ones.** A scan
  of an asset group matched scope exclusions against each member's name
  only, so a host whose address was in an excluded network was scanned. It
  also scanned archived members. Members are now read by asset id (only
  assets of the scan's tenant), exclusions are tested against the member's
  name, addresses (`ip_addresses`, `ip`) and repository URLs, and archived
  members are skipped and counted (`archived_target_count` in the run
  context, and a warning). **Behaviour change:** archived assets in a group
  are no longer scanned, and a member whose address matches an approved
  exclusion is now excluded. Stale and inactive members are still scanned.

- **A pipeline step's settings reach the sensor.** Step commands carried
  the step's config as `step_config`, which no sensor reads, so every step
  ran with its tool's defaults (a naabu step with `ports: "80"` scanned the
  top 100 ports). The payload now carries it as `config`, the key the
  sensor SDK reads. Needs sensor with sdk-go per-scan settings (naabu:
  `ports`, `top_ports`, `exclude_ports`, `rate`, `retries`; nuclei: `tags`,
  `exclude_tags`, `severity`). Saving a step now checks these keys against
  the sensor's rules (`INVALID_STEP_SETTING`): a port list that is not one,
  a flag-like tag, an intrusive tag (`dos`, `fuzz`, `fuzzing`,
  `intrusive`), ports together with top_ports. `allow_interactsh` is refused
  on a pipeline step. A stored step with such a value fails when its run
  queues it, with the reason.

### Fixed: the coverage ledger settles each asset from its own target

- A run's step can end with more tasks than chunks (claim-time splits,
  follow-ups of unfinished targets). The coverage loop settled every pair of
  a run from the run's overall status, so one failed task failed every pair
  and a run that completed covered targets nobody ran. It now settles each
  pair from its target's own outcome across every task of the run: done
  covers it, a failure keeps its class (unreachable, timeout, tool error,
  egress refused), a skip blocks it with the reason, a task that failed
  whole fails its targets with its error, the run's unfinished targets
  (a connector's included) fail as unfinished, and a target no task carried
  fails as not dispatched.

### Fixed: credential leak counts were wrong past 100 credentials

- The cards and status counts on the Credentials page are counted by the server
  for every credential you can see, instead of from the first 100 rows. They do
  not change with the filters.
- The page loads only the view shown: the list, or the identities.

### Fixed: pages knew who you were only until a reload; the member list refused status=all

- The members page, Account › Activity, the pentest campaign list and the
  pentest campaign and finding sheets read the signed-in user from the auth
  store, which is empty after a reload (the session lives in an httpOnly
  cookie). They treated you as someone else: your own activity did not load,
  "is it me" checks failed, and the pentest member picker listed nobody. They
  now use the profile API (`useDisplayUser`), and a test fails on any new
  reader of the store's user outside the shared hooks.
- `GET /api/v1/tenants/{tenant}/members?include=user&status=all` (and
  `status=offboarded`) answered 400 "unknown member status filter": the
  handler and the repository accepted them, the service did not. They agree
  now.

### Fixed: a duplicate dashboard name is answered 409, not 500

- Creating or renaming a personal dashboard (`/api/v1/me/dashboards`) to a name you already use now answers 409 with the reason instead of 500.

### Fixed: dashboard numbers say what they count

- `findings.overdue` in `GET /dashboard/stats` is now computed (open findings
  past their SLA, equal to the executive summary's `sla_breached`); it was
  always 0.
- `findings.total` and `findings.by_severity` count open findings; they counted
  every status. `findings.by_status` still lists every status.
- `sla_compliance_pct` (executive summary) is the share of open findings that
  carry an SLA and are not past it, and is `null` when none does; it was 100
  for an organization with nothing to measure and counted findings without an
  SLA as compliant.
- `mttr_critical_hours` and `mttr_high_hours` (executive summary) and
  `overall_hours` (MTTR analytics) are `null` when nothing was remediated, not
  0. New: `mttr_{critical,high}_median_hours`, `..._p90_hours`, `..._sample`
  and `overall_median_hours`, `overall_p90_hours`. MTTR analytics leaves out a
  severity or priority bucket with no remediated finding. **Upgrade note:** API
  clients must accept `null` in these fields.
- New `kev.tenant_open_count` in `GET /threat-intel/stats`: the tenant's open
  findings in the KEV catalog. The CTEM loop shows it instead of the size of
  the catalog.
- Weekly velocity is computed with two range scans over the window instead of a
  join of every week with every finding, with the same result.
- Console labels match their formulas: open findings, open within SLA, time to
  fix (median with the 90th percentile), crown jewels with open findings,
  crown jewels on an attack path, and connector dispatch freshness for the
  scan-coverage row. A figure that is not measured shows a dash.

### Fixed: a DAST finding re-sighted by a newer sensor is no longer a new finding

- A sensor that reports the HTTP method in the CTIS web location (instead of a `method` or `request` property) made every re-sighted DAST finding a new one, and its triage stayed on the old one. Ingest now reads the method from the web location too, and a missing method counts as GET, so a field a producer stops sending never forks a finding again. A fuzzed parameter in the web location now counts as well.
- A fixed-path detection template that matches several of its own request paths on one target (for example `/wp-json/wp/v2/users` and `/?rest_route=/wp/v2/users`) is one finding, keyed on the target the producer names in `source_extra.target`. Endpoints given as targets and fuzzed parameters keep one finding each. A finding keyed on its matched URL before is re-keyed on its next sighting, keeping its triage.

### Fixed: the tool catalog lists a tool without an install method

- A tool row whose `install_method` is empty no longer makes the tools list fail with an internal error.

### Fixed: default sensors run retests

- "Retest now" on a finding waited out its 30-minute deadline and ended with
  no result on every sensor with a default grant. No grant profile listed the
  `retest` job type, so the dispatch gate never offered the command.
- Every grant profile that may scan now also lists `validate` and `retest`
  (RFC-052 §5.2), with the same zones, target network, target scope and tier
  ceiling. Migration 001263 adds them to the default grant a new sensor gets
  and to every grant still on one of those profiles. A grant an administrator
  edited (profile `custom`) keeps its job types; `retest` can be added to it on
  the sensor page.
- A retest is rated at the tier of the detection it repeats: the scan tier of
  the finding's tool, under the contract the sensor reported. The retest of a
  T1 finding is T1, and only a T2 detection retests at T2. A sensor at trust
  level `new` is still capped at T0 and gets no T1 retests until it is
  promoted.

### Fixed: remediation task counts use fix_applied only

- Remediation task counts no longer reference the retired `validated_fixed` status; a fix claimed and awaiting verification is `fix_applied` only (the validation result is its own field now).

### Fixed: restore stops the console too, sensor and SDK pins, MANAGED_SERVICE text

- `backup.sh restore` now also stops the `console` service while it replaces
  the database and volumes, so the admin console cannot write during a restore.
- `versions.yaml` pins the newest sensor (v0.23.2) and SDK (v0.34.0), so the
  install snippets and the "update available" verdict use the current releases.
- The `MANAGED_SERVICE` description names its value (`true`).

### Fixed: documentation and in-app links from the API

- The sensor setup checks linked to `docs.openctem.io/sensor/troubleshooting`,
  a page that does not exist: they now open the matching entry of the setup
  check reference on `/sensors/troubleshooting/`.
- In-app notifications for scope changes opened the removed `/scope-config`
  page (now `/scope`), CI break-glass alerts opened the removed
  `/settings/scanning/ci` page (now CI/CD, Trust and gate), and member
  lifecycle notices go to `/settings/members` directly.
- CI checks every docs.openctem.io and GitHub file link in code against the
  docs site and the repositories (job "Docs links" in `docs-check.yml`).

### Fixed: the environment variable reference renders prose defaults

- A default that is a sentence with its own code spans (the `CI_RUNNER_*`, `SENSOR_*_VERSION` and database URL rows) was wrapped in another code span, which Markdown cannot nest, so the cell rendered broken. The generator (`make env-docs`) writes such a default as is; a plain value stays a code span.

### Fixed: the environment variable reference shows what to do with a retired name that has no replacement

- `docs/configuration/environment-variables.md` printed "rename it to ``" for
  retired names without a replacement (such as `SCOPE_ACTIVE_PROOF`); it now
  prints the same note the API gives at startup. A replacement that contains
  `|` no longer breaks the table.

### Fixed: a scan no longer waits as "should start shortly" behind a scan of the same hosts

- Every command now gets its host keys when it is created, whatever path built it: quick and single-scanner scans, zone fan-outs, validate, retest and platform jobs, not only workflow chunks. The keys come from the same politeness function the sensor uses, and are sent in the payload.
- A command whose hosts another task of the organization is scanning is no longer offered to a sensor that would hand it back ("its hosts are busy on this sensor") again and again. A free slot takes other work instead, and the task shows "Another task is scanning one of its hosts".
- A follow-up of unfinished targets holds only the hosts of its remaining targets.
- Pending commands queued before this change get their keys on start (the stored keys only; their payloads are not rewritten).
- A local filesystem path (a code scan of `.` or `/src`) is on the running sensor's own disk and holds nothing back.

### Fixed: an ended risk acceptance reopens the finding in one transaction, with a new SLA clock

- The hourly acceptance expiry now ends each accepted finding whose
  `acceptance_expires_at` has passed in one transaction: the finding returns
  to `confirmed`, a new SLA clock starts at the reopen (the policy deadline
  for its priority, on track), its approved requests are marked `expired`,
  and the timeline records `acceptance_expired` and `sla_restarted`. Before,
  the request was expired first; a failed finding update left the finding
  accepted for good, with no timeline entry, the old breached deadline and a
  junk resolution text.
- Every accept path records when the acceptance ends: an approved suppression
  rule (its expiry, else 90 days), ingest suppression and re-link to another
  rule, merges that inherit an acceptance, and pentest acceptances.
- Migration `002166` gives accepted findings that still had no end the 90-day
  default from the day it runs, with a timeline note.

### Fixed: an accepted risk always ends, and the CI gate stops honoring it at that end

- A request to accept a finding's risk gets an expiry of 90 days when it names none, and is refused with an expiry in the past or more than a year ahead. A false-positive request no longer takes an expiry.
- Approving the acceptance writes the end to `findings.acceptance_expires_at`, which the CI gate reads; a finding accepted by an accepted-risk suppression rule takes the rule's expiry. The column is cleared whenever the finding leaves `accepted`.
- The web request dialog asks for the acceptance end (90 days ahead by default, at most a year).
- Migration `002117` adds the clearing trigger and fills the end for findings already accepted through an approval or a suppression rule.

### Fixed: finding approval requests have a decide-by time, one pending request per finding, and approve in one transaction

- A false-positive or accepted-risk request now has a decide-by time (14 days),
  separate from the end of the acceptance it asks for. A pending request past
  it can no longer be decided and the hourly approval expiration job marks it
  expired, with a timeline entry and an audit row (`finding_approval.expired`).
  Before, a pending request waited forever. The database enforces it too
  (approve and reject claim no row past it), and any writer that names no
  decide-by time (VEX and AI-triage requests) gets the 14-day default.
- A finding holds at most one pending request (from a person or a platform
  actor); a second request answers 409. Older duplicates are cancelled by a
  migration (newest pending request kept), with a timeline entry.
- Approving writes the request, the finding's status and the timeline entry in
  one transaction: two approvers at once cannot both apply it, and a failure
  leaves the request pending and the finding unchanged.
- A request can only be made for a finding inside the requester's data scope.
- The approval API returns `decide_by`.
- Migrations `002419`–`002422` (`finding_approval_decide_by`,
  `finding_approval_decide_by_backfill`, `finding_approval_pending_dedupe`,
  `finding_approval_one_pending`); safe on a populated table (the table is
  small; new column nullable, backfill touches pending rows only).

### Fixed: last seen branch and commit, and the technique of trivy misconfigurations and secrets

- A finding seen again kept the branch and commit of its first sighting as "last seen" forever; they now follow the latest scan.
- A trivy report from `openctem-ci` names its capability in `metadata.properties`; ingest now reads it there, so the IaC job's findings are IaC instead of SCA. A report without a capability files trivy misconfigurations as IaC and secrets as secret detection by the finding's type. Migration 002215 relabels the existing misconfiguration and secret findings filed as SCA.
- A concurrent first sighting by a different tool no longer pairs that tool's version with the first reporter's name.

### Fixed: closed findings get their close date from the timeline

- Migration `002191` gives closed findings that have no close date
  (`resolved_at`, read by MTTR and close-date filters) the time of the latest
  timeline entry that moved them into their current status. Findings with no
  such entry keep no date; none is invented. Idempotent.

### Fixed: finding import accepts files up to its 110 MiB limit and writes in batches

- `POST /api/v1/findings/import` now applies its own 110 MiB body limit. The
  global 10 MiB request limit ran first, so every file above 10 MiB was refused
  with a misleading "larger than 110 MiB" error.
- An import no longer makes three database round trips per finding. The
  priority audit entries are written in one statement per 1,000 findings, SLA
  policies are loaded once per batch instead of once per finding, and the
  version-2 identity re-key runs only for findings that still hold a version-1
  key. A 17.7k-finding nuclei file went from about 213k to about 160k SQL
  statements and imports about twice as fast on the same host.
- A rescan no longer rewrites every finding's source interop data when it is
  unchanged. On a 17.7k-finding rescan, that update went from 9.3 s writing
  17,721 rows to 0.28 s writing none.
- The fingerprint existence check takes the keys as one array parameter, so a
  report above 65,535 findings no longer exceeds PostgreSQL's bind-parameter
  limit.

### Fixed: decisions the old taint-source check reversed are restored

- Migration `002217` restores each finding that a changed taint source moved
  from false positive or accepted back to `confirmed` (resolution
  `decision_suspended`, before migration `002173`) to its latest suspended
  decision, with a timeline entry (reason `decision_restored`) and an open
  review flag (`taint_source_changed`), in the finding's own tenant. A
  restored acceptance ends 90 days later. Idempotent.

### Fixed: the SLA status follows every status change, with one warning definition

- `sla_status` is now recomputed on every status or deadline change, whatever
  path makes it (trigger `trg_findings_recompute_sla_status`, migration
  `002181`): false positives, accepted risks and duplicates are
  `not_applicable`; a resolved finding is `on_track` when fixed by the
  deadline and `exceeded` otherwise; an open finding past its deadline is
  `overdue`. Before, it was only computed when a deadline was set, so closed
  findings kept `overdue` and dispositions showed `exceeded` in lists, filters
  and exports.
- One warning definition: the SLA escalation job's policy threshold, now
  measured from the reopen for a regression's restarted deadline (it flipped
  to warning at once). The domain's own 24-hour warning is removed.
- The migration recomputes stale values in place.

### Fixed: only accepted-risk requests expire, each with a timeline entry and an audit row

- The acceptance expiry job's sweep of stale requests (their finding had
  moved on) now expires only approved accepted-risk requests; an approved
  false-positive request that carries an end date is left alone. Each expired
  request gets an `approval_canceled` timeline entry on its finding and an
  audit row in its tenant, in the same statement.

### Fixed: one definition of open, fixed and dispositioned findings

- Every count and job now asks "open?" and "fixed?" through one shared set
  (`pkg/domain/vulnerability/status_sets.go`), replacing about twenty
  hand-written status lists that disagreed. Open is `new`, `confirmed`,
  `in_progress`, `fix_applied`, `validated_fixed` and `not_observed`; fixed is
  `resolved`; false positives, accepted risks and duplicates are
  dispositions, never fixes.
- The daily risk snapshot no longer counts accepted, false-positive or
  duplicate findings as closed today or in MTTR, and no longer counts pentest
  drafts as open.
- Asset and asset-group finding counts, the has-findings filter, repository
  branch counters, scan severity counts and branch comparison count open
  findings only (before: accepted, false-positive and duplicate findings were
  counted). Active CVEs and the grouped view now include `fix_applied`,
  `validated_fixed` and `not_observed` findings instead of dropping them.
- Risk velocity counts a fix in the week of its close, not of its last edit;
  validation coverage counts duplicates as closed and windows on the close date.
- Migration `002150` adds `is_open_finding_status(status)`, the same set in
  SQL, rewrites the branch counter trigger with it and recounts the branches.
- A test fails when code hand-writes a new finding status list.

### Fixed: every automatic status move is on the finding's timeline, in the same transaction

- About fifteen platform moves wrote no timeline entry, or wrote it after the
  move in a separate write: template drift, feature-branch expiry, CI
  pipeline stale and retired, VEX in scan reports and VEX documents, the
  software vulnerability matcher, correlation link and release, taint-source
  suspension, suppression re-link, validation verdicts, the IOC correlator,
  workflow `update_status`, auto-assign to owners, bulk verify / reject by
  filter, coverage auto-resolve and scan re-detection.
- Each now writes one entry per moved finding in the same transaction as the
  move, with the old and new status, the previous resolution, a reason code,
  the actor and the evidence behind it (scanner, scan, pipeline, rule,
  statement). Migration `002180` adds the trigger
  `trg_findings_record_transition` that writes it for a writer that names
  itself for its transaction.
- A workflow's status change is recorded with the actor `workflow:<id>`;
  before, its entry failed on an invalid actor id.

### Fixed: undoing a resolve is not a regression

- A person moving a finding back from resolved (the drawer's Undo, a
  correction, a bulk status change) no longer sets `is_regression` or counts
  in `reopen_count`, so the reopen rate counts only fixes that evidence shows
  did not hold (a scan sees the finding again, a retest fails, a fixed VEX
  statement is withdrawn). Migration `002205` updates the regression trigger.
- The drawer no longer offers Undo after a resolve; reopening is a deliberate
  move from the status control.

### Fixed: the findings list opened for an asset no longer jumps or sends a bad request

- Opening the findings list from another page (an asset's "View findings", for example) sent one list request with the previous page's sort and without the asset filter, which the API refused with 400, and then the real request. The page now waits until its own address is in place before it asks for anything, so it sends one request with the right filter.
- The active context filters (asset, scan, CVE, rule and the other group drill-downs) now sit in their own row under the table toolbar, so the toolbar keeps one height and its controls (state tabs, saved views, grouping, export) no longer move when a filter is set.
- The overview cards above the list (Total, Open, Critical open, ...) now count the findings of that context (for example the one asset) instead of every finding, so they agree with the list and the state tab counts. Facet filters, search and the state tab still leave the cards unchanged.
- The cards and tab counts keep their numbers while new ones load instead of blanking.

### Fixed: grouped findings apply every filter of the list

- Grouping the findings list (by CVE, rule, asset and the other dimensions) now runs the list's own filter: search, priority, CISA KEV, reachable, SLA status and the asset, scan, CVE, rule, family, type, component and owner filters. Before, only severity, status, source, "assigned to me" and the lens reached the groups, and a note said the rest applied to the ungrouped list. The search box is shown in the grouped view too.

### Fixed: "Awaiting verification" on the Findings page always showed 0

- It read a status count the stats response never carried; it now reads
  `awaiting_verification`.

### Fixed: a scan workflow's settings do what they say

- The workflow **timeout** now applies. A run started without a scan, or from
  a scan that has no timeout of its own, ends at the workflow's
  `timeout_seconds`. A scan's own timeout still wins, and 24 hours remains
  the ceiling.
- Editing a workflow in the form no longer rewrites its steps. The form
  showed a few fields of each step, and saving replaced the rest (preferred
  tools, conditions, step configuration). Steps of an existing workflow are
  edited in the visual builder only.

### Fixed: a chained template stage gets each web service once

- In a workflow, the vulnerability template stage received the same web
  service twice (the HTTP probe's origin URL and the port scan's bare
  `host:port`) plus the name it is served on, and open web ports the probe
  found no HTTP on. A stage that takes web origins now gets each one once,
  as the `http_service` origin; non-web open ports still reach a stage that
  declares open ports (network templates). What is dropped is counted as
  `covered_by_origin` on the stage plan. A chain without an HTTP probe is
  unchanged.

### Fixed: a scan waiting for its hosts is no longer ended as "no sensor picked up this run's work"

- A run whose work waits while another task of the organization scans the same hosts is no longer failed after an hour (four for a scheduled run) as unclaimed with NO_SENSOR, a reason that is never retried. Once its hosts are free, the usual rule applies again.

### Fixed: an HTTP probe creates web origin assets

- The recon converter names an `http_service` by its bare host. Ingest used
  that name, which is the name of the subdomain or address the origin runs on,
  so the probe's result was folded into that row and no web origin asset was
  ever created: crawling, templates and DAST had no web target. Ingest now
  identifies an `http_service` by its URL (`https://app.example.com`,
  `http://203.0.113.7:8080`), so every probed origin is its own asset and the
  subdomain or address keeps its type.
- Existing inventories: the next HTTP probe creates the missing origins. No
  backfill: the folded observations carry no port, so an origin rebuilt from
  them could be wrong.

### Fixed: switching organizations works with AUTH_PROVIDER=hybrid

- In hybrid mode `POST /api/v1/auth/token` was answered by a deprecated OIDC
  stub (200 with an identity-provider URL and no token) instead of the local
  tenant token exchange, so a local user could not switch organizations. The
  local exchange now serves the route in local and hybrid mode.

### Fixed: a refused legacy-name copy no longer stops a release

- The copy of `openctem-web` to the old `ghcr.io/openctemio/ui` name was
  refused by the registry, which failed the publish job. v0.9.0 therefore has
  no all-in-one image, no cosign signatures, no SBOM attestations and no
  Docker Hub mirror. The copy is now best effort and warns.
- Release images carry `org.opencontainers.image.revision`, `created`,
  `title`, `description` and `licenses` labels. The gateway image has a
  `HEALTHCHECK`, and the image guard no longer exempts it from the non-root
  check (it runs as uid 1000).

### Fixed: import uploads honour their documented size limits

- The web console now streams import uploads to the API instead of reading
  them into memory, up to each route's own limit: finding import 110 MiB,
  SBOM import and asset CSV import 50 MiB, campaign Burp/CSV import 50 MiB.
  Before, every upload above 12 MiB was refused by the console although the
  finding import accepts 110 MiB. Other requests keep the 12 MiB cap.
- `POST /components/import`, `POST /assets/import/csv` and
  `POST /pentest/campaigns/{id}/findings/import` declare their body limit on
  the route, which replaces the global 10 MiB limit (`SERVER_MAX_BODY_SIZE`).
  Before, they refused every file above 10 MiB although they document 50 MiB.
  The permission gate still runs before any of the body is read.
- Multipart forms (attachments, campaign import, credential CSV import) keep
  at most 1 MiB in memory; larger file parts are spooled to a temporary file.

### Fixed: a report delivered late no longer undoes newer asset data

- Ingest uses the time a report's source saw the asset (the report timestamp, never later than now) instead of the arrival time: `last_seen` keeps the newer observation, and an older report's property values only fill gaps (RFC-069 §5.6).
- A delayed older port scan no longer closes a port a newer scan saw open.
- A stale asset that a scan reports again is saved active. Before, the asset history said "recovered" while the asset stayed stale.

### Fixed: an ingested asset's type no longer contradicts its name

- A DNS name reported as `ip_address` (for example a recon tool's target type) was stored and shown as an IP address. Ingest now stores it as a `domain`, and an IP literal reported as `domain` or `subdomain` as an `ip_address`. Other types are left as reported. Rows already stored with the wrong type are not rewritten; re-ingesting the asset does not move them either, so correct them by hand or delete and rediscover.

### Fixed: two sensors that use the same report id no longer block each other

- Protocol v2/v3 segment jobs were keyed by the report id the sensor chose, under an idempotency index that is per organization, not per sensor. If a second sensor of the organization used the same report id with the same bytes, its segments and commit failed with `500` until the report expired. That happened by accident, or deliberately when a compromised sensor copied a sibling's id. Jobs are now keyed by the stored report's own id, which is unique across sensors.

### Fixed: the Jira client and its mapping come from the same integration

- With several Jira integrations, the outbound client was the first connected
  one whose credentials worked, while the mapping (project, priorities,
  status maps, routing) was read from the first connected one even when its
  credentials did not. Tickets could be filed with another integration's
  mapping. Both now come from the same integration.

### Fixed: inbound Jira webhooks work with stock Jira

- Inbound Jira status sync required a custom signature header and timestamp that Jira never sends, so every real delivery was refused. Each Jira integration now has its own webhook URL, `/hooks/jira-integrations/{integration_id}`, verified with Jira's own `X-Hub-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256 of the body) under that integration's secret.
- Replays are refused by body hash and by delivery id (`X-Atlassian-Webhook-Identifier`) for 24 hours, and by the payload timestamp (at most one hour old); a delivery that fails to process is released so Jira's retry is processed; per-IP and per-integration rate limits apply.
- The secret is set in Settings > Integrations > Ticketing > Inbound webhook: generated (shown once) or entered from Jira, stored encrypted, never returned.

### Fixed: a Jira delivery whose sender disconnects is processed on retry

- When processing a Jira webhook delivery failed after the sender had
  disconnected, its replay keys were released with the request's canceled
  context, so they stayed held and Jira's retry was dropped as a replay. The
  keys are now released on a context that outlives the request.

### Fixed: system workflow templates no longer pin tools that may be missing

- The older system templates (Subdomain Enumeration, Port Scanning, Full
  Reconnaissance, Web Vulnerability Scan, API Security Testing, Continuous
  Monitoring) now use capability steps with "Any tool", like the starter
  templates: each step names its capability and the platform picks an
  available tool. A copy made from one used to fail to save on an
  organization without one of the pinned tools.
- Steps no catalog capability runs (dalfox, sqlmap, kiterunner, ffuf, report
  and rate-limit steps) are removed; the steps that waited for them no longer
  do. Settings keep only the capability's standard params (`top_ports: "1000"`
  becomes `top_n: 1000`).
- Only system templates change (migration 001322). Organizations' own copies
  are untouched. The down migration restores the previous steps.

### Fixed: sensors on the tool contract register their capabilities

- Sensors from v0.11.0 report each tool's capability from the OpenCTEM taxonomy (`vuln.templates`, `scan.ports`, `scan.ports@1`) next to the older words. The platform only knew the older words and ignored every taxonomy id as `unknown-capability`, so the manifest registered with "6 items ignored".
- Capability names are now also accepted when they are in the taxonomy (`ctis/capability`), with or without their major version. The older words stay accepted until they are retired (RFC-055 §10.1).
- A name in neither list is still ignored.

### Fixed: the comment-adding AI scope can be allowed in the organization policy

- The policy refused `mcp:findings.comment` as an unknown scope shape, so no organization could let AI applications add (person-confirmed) comments to findings. It is accepted now.

### Fixed: AI-drafted pentest summaries match the delivered report

- The `exec_summary` and `attack_narrative` MCP prompts read the delivered report's findings only (no drafts, findings under review, false positives or duplicates) and count their statistics from the same set.
- `list_campaign_findings` filters by severity, status and search in SQL before paging (`page`, `limit` up to 50, `has_more`, `next_page`); it no longer cuts at 100 rows before filtering. `list_retests` is paged.

### Fixed: every permission can be granted from the role editor

- The role editor listed permissions under modules through a hand-kept map to module ids
  that do not exist (`validation`, `campaigns`, `risk`), so pentest, SLA and remediation
  permissions were hidden even with their modules on; and the API dropped permissions
  whose module was empty or retired (`ctem:*` cycles, business services, attacker
  profiles, compensating controls, priority rules; `attack_surface:scope:*`), so they
  could not be granted from the console at all. Migration 001524 files every permission
  under a live module and the editor compares real module ids. The roles list counts
  every permission a role holds.

### Fixed: every module preset applies, including "minimal"

- Applying a preset whose diff touches more than 50 modules (for example
  "minimal" on an organization with every module on) failed with "too many
  module updates (max 50)". The preset update set is built on the server from
  the preset catalog, so it is now applied as one set without the per-request
  cap; a caller-supplied toggle batch is still capped at 50.

### Fixed: a module switched off is off on every surface, on every replica

- MCP: the tools and prompts of a module the organization has off (pentest, compliance,
  attack surface) are no longer listed and answer "This module is not enabled for your
  team", as their REST routes do.
- AI triage: `/api/v1/findings/{id}/ai-triage*` and `/api/v1/findings/ai-triage/*` follow the
  `ai_triage` module (403 `MODULE_NOT_ENABLED` when off), and auto-triage does not start.
- Automations: events start no automation for an organization with the `workflows` module
  off. The background remediation progress pass leaves the campaigns of an organization
  with `remediation` off untouched (no counts, no auto-complete, no ticket sync).
- A module toggle reaches every API replica at once through Redis (`modules:changed`);
  before, other replicas kept the old state for up to a minute.
- Console: the sidebar, the route guard and every module check follow a toggle at once,
  in every open tab, without a reload (they read the session bootstrap, which a toggle did
  not refresh).

### Fixed: New Scan target limits, all asset groups, tier-aware scope preview

- New Scan no longer drops targets past the first 1,000 without a word: the Targets step says how many are selected and what to do. Validation errors now show their reason (for example "targets must be at most 1000 items") instead of "Validation failed".
- Every asset group can be picked: the list loads 100 groups by name with a search box (it showed only the first 20).
- Selected assets keep their names after going back to the Targets step.
- The live scope preview of a single check and of a quick scan checks at the scanner tier, so an intrusive scanner shows the targets the scan would refuse. `POST /api/v1/scope/check` accepts `scanner_name` for this.

### Fixed: New Scan offers workflows only when the scan workflows module is on

- With the scan workflows module off for the organization, New Scan no longer offers the starter workflows or another workflow (the API refused them at the end); the scan is a single check. Editing an existing workflow scan still shows its workflow.

### Fixed: security and lifecycle notices reach the in-app inbox again

- Seven notification types were declared and sent but refused by the type check, so every such in-app notice was dropped with only a warning in the log: sensor grant changes (`sensor_security`), scope changes (`scope_change`), CI security (`ci_security`), member lifecycle (`member_lifecycle`), scan approvals (`scan_approval`), scan window overrides (`scan_window_override`) and attack surface digests (`attack_surface_digest`). They are accepted now, and a test keeps every declared type valid.

### Fixed: panicking requests, rate-limited requests and URL paths in the HTTP metrics

- A request that panicked was never counted in `http_requests_total` and left `http_requests_in_flight`
  one higher for good; it is now counted as the 500 it returns. Requests refused by the global rate
  limit (429), the concurrency limit and the body limit are now counted too.
- **Behaviour change:** the `path` label of `http_requests_total`, `http_request_duration_seconds` and
  `http_response_size_bytes` is the matched route pattern (`/api/v1/assets/{id}`), or `unmatched` when no
  route matched. It was the raw path with ids replaced, which carried names and hosts from the URL into
  the label and let any caller create a new series per random path. Dashboards that matched raw paths
  must use the route pattern.

### Fixed: an organization that owns a repository with components can be deleted

- Deleting an organization (and so erasing its data) failed with
  "insert or update on table asset_repositories violates foreign key
  constraint" when it owned a repository asset with two or more components or
  branches: the count triggers updated the repository row after the cascade had
  removed its asset. The triggers now skip a repository whose asset is gone
  (migration 001260). `TestDeleteTenantAndUser_EverySchemaTable` passes again
  and a new test deletes committed rows the way a real database holds them.

### Fixed: the sidebar organization card shows the organization's real plan

- The membership list (`GET /api/v1/users/me/tenants`, the session bootstrap) and `GET /api/v1/tenants/{id}` reported every organization as "free" from a leftover placeholder, while Settings > Plan & usage, the console and limit enforcement read the stored plan. All of them now read `tenant_plans`; an organization with no stored plan (the one bootstrap-admin creates, one created in the console or from an approved access request, one older than plans) is Enterprise everywhere, as it already was for limits.
- A self-service organization's Free plan is now stored in the same transaction as the organization. Before, a failed write after the organization existed left it with no plan, and so without the Free limits.
- A plan change in the console is audited with the plan it replaced (`from`).
- No data change: limits were already enforced from `tenant_plans`, so no organization's limits change.

### Fixed: a CI upload no longer deletes another import's package list for the same lock file

- A CI SCA report carries only the vulnerable packages of a lock file and the packages on their paths. Its package snapshot replaced every package stored for that lock file on the repository, so the full list from an SBOM upload or a code-host connector shrank to the CI subset on every run.
- A report now prunes only the packages its own channel listed. A CI list refreshes the packages it names without taking them over, so the next SBOM upload still owns and prunes them; a finding import only adds.
- Package links stored before channels were recorded are pruned only by a full inventory, never by a CI list.

### Fixed: password forms state the server's password policy

- `GET /api/v1/auth/providers` reports `password_policy`: the minimum
  length, the required character classes and how long a forgot-password link
  stays valid (`reset_link_valid_minutes`), from `AUTH_PASSWORD_*` and
  `AUTH_PASSWORD_RESET_DURATION`.
- The register, set-password, reset-password and change-password forms (and
  the platform console's temporary-password change) state and pre-check that
  policy instead of their own copy: change-password said "at least 8
  characters" while the server requires 12 by default, plus an uppercase
  letter, a lowercase letter and a number.
- The forgot-password confirmation said the link lasts 24 hours; it now
  states the configured lifetime (1 hour by default).

### Fixed: campaign clients edit and delete their own comments and react on pentest findings

- Clients (usually organization viewers, without `findings:comment`) could post a client-visible comment on a pentest finding but not edit or delete it, nor react to comments they can read. New routes `PUT|DELETE /api/v1/pentest/findings/{id}/comments/{comment_id}` and `POST|DELETE /api/v1/pentest/findings/{id}/comments/{comment_id}/reactions` (`?emoji=` to remove) need `pentest:findings:read` and authorize by campaign role: a client reaches client-visible comments only, only the author edits or deletes, non-members and other findings get 404. The web console uses them for every campaign member on a pentest finding.

### Fixed: campaign clients read and download delivered pentest reports

- A campaign client can now list, read and download the reports delivered to their campaign (`GET /api/v1/pentest/campaigns/{id}/reports`, `GET /api/v1/pentest/reports/{id}`, `GET /api/v1/pentest/reports/{id}/download`). Access is read-only.
- Reports that are not delivered stay invisible to the client. The client also cannot generate a report on the fly, deliver one or delete one.
- The client's view leaves out the generation options. Every download stays audited.
- The client's campaign page no longer offers what the API refuses them, so they get no permission errors:
  - no Generate report or Export;
  - no Checklist tab;
  - no campaign stats cards.

### Fixed: comments and activity on pentest findings work for campaign members

- `GET /findings/{id}`, its comments, reactions and activity, and the MCP per-finding tools and prompts returned 404 for campaign members who are not org admins. They checked the asset data scope, and pentest findings usually have no inventory asset.
- For pentest findings, campaign membership (a client: published findings only) now replaces the asset data scope.
- New `POST /api/v1/pentest/findings/{id}/comments` (`pentest:findings:read`) lets every campaign member comment, clients included.
- The web finding sheet shows the visibility choice and a badge on each comment.
- The activity panel says when loading failed instead of "Nothing yet".
- Discussion stays open on a completed campaign.

### Fixed: a new pentest finding keeps the status it is created with, or is refused

- `POST /api/v1/pentest/campaigns/{id}/findings` honours `status` `draft` (default) or `in_review`; it was always stored as `draft`.
- Any other status on create is answered 400: a finding is published (confirmed, resolved, ...) by a later status change, through the campaign role gate.

### Fixed: the Findings tab note agrees with the campaign phase and never gives a client reopen advice

- In remediation the note said testing was complete and that a lead could reopen testing, to clients too, while the remediation banner says fixes and retests continue. It now says fixes and retests continue and that a new finding needs testing reopened, which only the campaign lead can do. A campaign client never sees reopen or phase advice: the note says the pentest team adds the findings (in reporting: the lead and reviewers), that each appears once published, and in remediation that the client can request a retest once a finding is fixed.

### Fixed: a campaign's "New finding" opens the finding in that campaign

- The new pentest finding page read its `?campaign=` link from the address bar
  on its first render. After the in-app "New finding" click on a campaign's
  Findings tab the address bar still showed the campaign page, so the form
  opened with an empty campaign field. It now reads the router's query.
- The same first-render read is fixed for a channel's "View events" (the
  notification events page opened the first channel) and for a link to one
  scan run (`/scans/runs?run=`, the run drawer did not open).

### Fixed: pentest finding form: campaign, markdown toolbar and step order

- A new finding opened from a campaign shows that campaign by name, even when
  it is not on the first page of campaigns, and the campaign can still be
  changed. The picker searches the campaigns a finding may be added to
  (planning or in progress) and says when the campaign does not exist, is not
  visible to the user, no longer takes findings, or the user's campaign role
  cannot add findings.
- The edit page shows the finding's campaign as read-only text with a link:
  a finding does not move between campaigns.
- The markdown editors keep their toolbar on one row: buttons that do not fit
  move into a "More" menu. Formatting keeps the browser's undo. Screenshots
  and files pasted or dropped into the description, a step or the proof of
  concept upload as evidence with progress and are inserted where the caret is.
- Steps to reproduce reorder by dragging the handle, by keyboard on the
  handle, or with move up / move down buttons; steps can be duplicated,
  inserted and deleted, and a delete can be undone.

### Fixed: pentest finding status transitions come from one state machine

- The pentest finding status transitions were defined twice and disagreed: the
  legacy pentest finding path refused `verified -> remediation` (a regression
  reopen) that the unified findings path and the campaign role gate allowed.
  There is now one state machine (`pentest.FindingStatusTransitions`); both
  paths validate against it, and tests pin it to the campaign role gate.
- The web status menu on a pentest finding now offers exactly the transitions
  the API accepts. An administrator was offered every status, including ones
  the API refuses (for example `confirmed -> verified`); a reviewer was
  offered `draft -> false_positive` and `verified -> false_positive`, which
  the API refuses, and was not offered `false_positive -> confirmed`, which
  it allows.

### Fixed: a campaign's Findings tab counts every finding, not the first 100

- The Findings tab metrics (all, critical, high, medium, in progress, resolved) were counted from the first 100 findings loaded. They now come from `GET /api/v1/pentest/campaigns/{id}/stats`.
- Campaign clients may now read that endpoint; their counts cover published findings only (no drafts, no findings in review, no retests of those). The team's counts are unchanged.

### Fixed: pentest retest evidence and retest results

- Retest evidence (`context_type=retest`) can be attached while remediation is open, including on a completed campaign, by the members who may submit the retest (lead, reviewer, the owning tester); it is refused on a canceled or archived campaign and for observers and clients. Finding evidence stays frozen on completion.
- Campaign stats (`GET /api/v1/pentest/campaigns/{id}/stats`) return `retests_passed`, `retests_failed` and `retests_partial` from the recorded retests. The web's retest success rate is now passed / (passed + failed + partial); findings closed as false positive or accepted risk no longer count as failed retests.
- The web no longer crashes on a finding or campaign status it does not know, and the finding sheet of a completed campaign explains that remediation continues instead of asking to reopen the campaign.
- **Upgrade note:** migration `002070_pentest_legacy_import_drafts` returns pentest findings left in status `new` by the earlier import to `draft` (a reviewer publishes them again), gives untitled ones their message as title, and replaces empty fingerprints. Its down migration is a no-op.

### Fixed: Vietnamese and other non-Latin text appears in PDF reports

- PDF reports used the core PDF fonts, which cover cp1252 only: Vietnamese
  (and any other non-Latin-1) text in campaign names, findings and
  descriptions was dropped. The PDF is now set in DejaVu Sans, embedded in
  the API and subset into each report.

### Fixed: pentest reports contain what the report dialog asked for

- The report dialog sent its options in a form the API ignored: unticking
  "Proofs of concept" still put exploit code in the report, and the severity
  and status filters did nothing. The dialog now sends the API's options
  (`include_poc`, `include_unpublished`, `severities`, `statuses`,
  `classification`, `watermark`), and the toggles the server cannot honour
  (sections, timeline, appendix) are gone. The fake progress bar is replaced
  by a real wait; a failed generation keeps the dialog open and says why.
- **Behaviour change:** a report holds published findings only by default.
  Drafts, findings in review, false positives and duplicates are left out
  unless `include_unpublished` is set or `statuses` names them. Unknown
  statuses or severities are refused (400).
- Findings are ordered most severe first (then CVSS score, then age); the
  summary counts describe the findings in the report; CVE ids appear; retest
  results are listed only for reported findings; a campaign above 2,000
  findings is refused instead of cut at 500.
- The live download (`GET /pentest/campaigns/{id}/reports/download`) accepts
  the same options as query parameters. The dialog offers PDF, HTML and JSON,
  and every generated report is stored in the campaign's report list.

### Fixed: retest buttons follow the viewer's campaign role

- The Retest button on a campaign's Retests tab and on the Retest queue, and the finding sheet's "Submit retest" and "Request retest", now follow the same campaign role checks the API makes. A campaign client or observer no longer sees a Retest button that the API refused with 403 when their organization role allowed retests; a client still requests retests. A tester sees Retest disabled, with the reason, on a finding they neither wrote nor are assigned, and everyone sees it disabled on a canceled or archived campaign. The API stays the only gate; no API change.

### Fixed: a retest that cannot save the finding's new status says so

- Submitting a pentest retest result that moves the finding (passed → resolved,
  failed → in progress) ignored a failed save of the finding: the API answered
  success and the retest claimed a status change the finding never got. The
  retest is recorded first, then the finding is saved, and a failed save is
  returned to the caller. A result that does not move the finding no longer
  writes it.

### Fixed: the Retests tab and the Retest queue reach every finding awaiting a retest

- A campaign's Retests tab read one page of the campaign's findings (20) and the Retest queue the first 100, then filtered them in the browser: on a large campaign some fix-applied findings never appeared there and the counts were short. Both now ask the server for the pending (`in_progress`, `fix_applied`) or closed statuses and page through the result; the counts are the server totals. The validation overview's "Retests due" count is fixed the same way.
- `GET /api/v1/pentest/findings` and `GET /api/v1/pentest/campaigns/{id}/findings` take `status` and `severity` (comma-separated or repeated, at most 20 values; unknown values answer 400) and `search`, applied in SQL before paging. Visibility is unchanged and applied first: a campaign client never gets drafts or findings in review, whatever statuses it asks for.

### Fixed: campaign clients no longer see the team's next-step advice

- The campaign status stepper showed clients the team's phase advice ("Next: Close campaign…") and the planning readiness checks. Clients now get a neutral line on where the campaign is (in remediation: fix the findings, then request a retest) and no readiness checks.

### Fixed: published pentest findings get their SLA deadline

- Pentest findings never received an SLA deadline (deadlines were computed
  only for ingested findings), so SLA tracking, warnings and breach reports
  missed them. When a pentest finding is published (leaves draft or in
  review for a status other than false positive or duplicate), it gets the
  deadline of the organization's SLA policy, counted from publication. A
  deadline already set is kept; a policy error does not block publishing.

### Fixed: migrations and the sensor upgrade check run on PostgreSQL 18

- Migration 001483 (`drop_dead_columns`) stopped on PostgreSQL 18 and left the
  database dirty: its safety guard, which refuses to drop a column another
  constraint still uses, also counted the column's own NOT NULL, which
  PostgreSQL 18 records in `pg_constraint`. The guard now ignores NOT NULL
  constraints; nothing changes on PostgreSQL 17 or for a database that has
  already applied 001483.
- The post-upgrade sensor rename check (run at every server start) no longer
  reports `<table>_user_agent_not_null` on PostgreSQL 18 as a leftover.
- API CI applies every migration to PostgreSQL 18 as well.
- **Upgrade note:** a PostgreSQL 18 database left dirty at 1483 is unchanged
  (the failed migration rolled back). Run `migrate ... force 1481`, then the
  migrations of this release (`migrate ... up`).

### Fixed: saving a pipeline no longer erases the history of its runs

- Saving a pipeline in the builder deleted and re-created every step. Step runs were deleted with their step, and the chaining inputs (`scan_step_outputs`) with their step run, so one save erased the step history of every past and running run of that pipeline.
- Steps are now updated in place and keep their ids (matched by the step `id` the builder sends, then by `step_key`). A removed step's step runs are kept: `step_runs.step_id` becomes NULL and the step run keeps its key, plus the step name and tool copied onto it when it was created (new columns `step_runs.step_name` and `step_runs.tool`, backfilled). Migration 001159.
- A change to a pipeline's steps is refused with `409 PIPELINE_RUN_ACTIVE` while a run of that pipeline is pending or running, so a running run is never changed under it. Every step write (full save, add, update, delete) is one tenant-scoped transaction.
- The step run response adds `step_name` and `tool`; `step_id` is omitted for a removed step.

### Fixed: nuclei templates written with a `tcp:` block were refused as having no execution block

- The template validator now counts `tcp` (nuclei v3 network templates) as an execution block, for custom templates and content packs.

### Fixed: sensors no longer hand back work the platform has just offered them for a "busy" host

- The per-host politeness keys are now defined once, in `github.com/openctemio/ctis/politeness` (the CTIS contract, so the platform does not depend on the sensor SDK), and used by both the platform and the sensor runtime. Every workflow chunk of a catalog stage carries the keys the platform holds for it in its payload (`host_keys`; an empty list for a passive stage), and a sensor on sdk-go v0.26.0 or later admits the chunk under exactly those keys. On live, 32 of 34 requeues in 30 days were "released by sensor: its hosts are busy on this sensor", caused by the two sides keying hosts differently.
- Behaviour change: address keys are canonical (`::ffff:10.0.0.5` and `10.0.0.5/32` hold `10.0.0.5` and its bucket), so a mapped or `/32` form of an address now waits for the address like any other form.

### Fixed: names in a private DNS zone are not internet-facing

- A domain or subdomain reported with `zone_visibility: private` (the cloud DNS collector sends the visibility of the zone each name is in) is created with exposure `private` and not internet-accessible, instead of the public default of a DNS name, and its exposure claim for attribute reconciliation is `private` (a person's decision still wins on an existing asset).
- A root domain that only private-zone names of a report name is created `private`; a root that a public-zone name also names stays public.

### Fixed: Word and Excel downloads open again

- The web API proxy decoded every response that was not on a short list of binary types as text, which corrupted DOCX and XLSX files: the pentest starter template, uploaded templates, template previews and Word reports downloaded from the console did not open. Only JSON and text responses are decoded now; every other type is passed through byte for byte.

### Fixed: Quick Scan accepts wildcard targets

- A Quick Scan of `*.example.com` (or an inventory-mode range) is no longer refused with "in the scanner settings is a pattern, not a host". The typed targets are stored as the scan's targets only, so each run expands them to the known in-scope assets like a saved scan; they are no longer copied into the scanner settings.

### Fixed: recon properties belong to their asset types

- Ingest warned "report asset properties outside the asset type schema" for
  keys the recon converter writes. They are now part of the schema of the
  asset they land on: `open_port_count` (addresses), `dns_record_count`
  (domains and subdomains), `discovery_method` (subdomains: the passive
  source that reported the name), `fingerprint` and `is_host_mismatch`
  (certificates; `host_mismatch` folds into it), `cdn_type`, `favicon_mmh3`
  and `tls_fingerprint` (web origins). They become filterable and shown
  with labels in English and Vietnamese.

### Fixed: registering again with an unverified address emails a set-password link

- A user whose verification email was lost or expired had no way back:
  registering again gave the usual answer and sent nothing, and sign-in said
  "Email is not verified". Registering again with an address whose password
  account never verified now emails that address a set-password link (the
  forgot-password link). Following it verifies the address and replaces the
  password. The answer and its timing stay the same as for any address.
- Security: the account cannot be kept by whoever registered the address
  first with their own password (account pre-hijacking): the owner's link
  replaces that password. A verified account and a new address get nothing new.

### Fixed: lint and code-scanning debt

- Sanitise user-influenced values (errors, names, codes) in a few log lines; tidy formatting, a repeated string constant and one SQL fragment so the release lint and code-scanning gates see no new findings.

### Fixed: a release checkout installs its own version

- Before, `versions.yaml` `platform.release` was bumped only after tagging, so
  the `vX.Y.Z` tag's `api/deploy/.env.example` and `docker-compose.yml`
  defaulted to the previous release: `setup.sh` on a v0.9.0 checkout installed
  v0.8.0 images. The release branch now carries its own version, synced into
  every default, and the tag is refused otherwise.

### Fixed: the remediation key backfill keeps campaigns that track a key

- `refingerprint -remediation-keys` now follows its key changes in the campaigns that track a remediation group (`finding_filter.remediation_key`): a campaign moves to the new key when all of its old key's findings land on that one key and no other finding does (so a campaign never widens), with its version bumped and one audit entry per campaign. A campaign whose findings split over several keys, share the new key with other findings, or that tracks a key no finding has, is printed as a warning with its finding count and left alone.
- Per tenant, idempotent; the dry run reports what it would retarget and changes nothing.

### Fixed: remediation groups are built from the fix, not from a package id or shared advice text

- A package group is now the package and the version that fixes it (`upgrade:pypi:django:4.2.30`, titled "Upgrade django to 4.2.30"): two installed versions that one upgrade fixes form one group, and no title is a raw id.
- A leaked secret is grouped only with findings of the same secret (by its fingerprint). Secrets were grouped by their advice text, so different secrets on different assets could share a group and be resolved together.
- Solution-text groups need specific text (a version or an id, not generic advice) and are kept per source.
- Keys are now derived for re-sighted findings, CVE-matching findings, findings a person creates and license findings, not only for findings a scan creates; a finding that no longer has a key leaves its group.
- **Upgrade note:** existing findings keep their old keys until the backfill runs. Dry run: `refingerprint -remediation-keys` (read-only, prints per-tenant counts); apply: `refingerprint -remediation-keys -apply`. It is idempotent and works one tenant at a time (`-tenant <id>` for one). A remediation campaign that tracks an old key (`finding_filter.remediation_key`) keeps the old key and counts nothing after the backfill; re-create it from the new group.

### Fixed: resolving a remediation group or campaign marks its findings fixed

- Group and campaign "resolve" failed for every finding that was not already
  `in_progress` (on most groups, every finding), with no reason shown. It now
  takes each finding through the legal steps (`new → confirmed → in_progress
  → fix_applied`), with the note, for the caller's own findings, and queues a
  proof-of-fix re-check per finding, like the dedicated fix-applied action.
