- A finding already `fix_applied` is skipped instead of being rewritten.
- The response names every finding not updated and why
  (`updated`, `skipped`, `failed`, `validations_queued`, `rows`); the web
  shows them in one shared "mark fixed" dialog (English and Vietnamese).

### Fixed: remediation task pages (validator, paging, priority, permissions, edit scope)

- The validator picker chose a person, but a task's validator is a group: every
  save failed. It now lists groups and sends the group id.
- The task list read only the first 50 tasks: metrics, the board, search and
  "add to an existing task" were wrong beyond that. It now reads every page.
- Priority uses the API's values (critical, high, medium, low); the web no
  longer sends `urgent`.
- Write controls (new task, bulk move, row status actions, every edit in the
  task drawer) show only with `findings:remediation:write`.
- Editing a task keeps its other scope conditions and never adds linked
  findings to a task tracked by a fix.
- Priority, status and validator labels in English and Vietnamese.

### Fixed: databases that skipped three migrations are repaired

- Three migrations (content catalog, verified-domain sign-up policy,
  organization join requests) were merged with numbers below versions already
  applied, so databases upgraded across them never ran them. A new repair
  migration re-applies exactly their schema and seed rows idempotently: a
  no-op where they exist, complete where they were skipped. No action needed.

### Fixed: a renamed repository keeps its asset, and repository import and CI share one asset

- CI found a repository asset by name, so renaming or transferring a repository made a new asset: the
  findings, branches, baseline, gate policy and coverage expectation stayed on the old one, and every pull
  request of the renamed repository was blocked for lack of a baseline. Repository import named assets
  `org/repo` while CI named them `github.com/org/repo`, so one repository was two assets. Both now find a
  repository by its code host and immutable repository id (GitHub repository id, GitLab project id, Bitbucket
  repository UUID) first; a renamed repository keeps its asset and takes the new name; repository import
  names new assets `host/path` and adopts an asset CI created.
- Existing duplicates are merged by `repomerge` (separate change).

### Fixed: the retest queue counts the asset a pentest finding is linked to

- The retest queue and the pentest finding sheet count the linked inventory asset together with the free-text affected targets; a finding linked to an asset no longer shows "0 assets".
- A pentest finding without a linked asset no longer answers an all-zero `asset_id`.

### Fixed: a retest re-runs the template against the origin, not the matched-at URL

- A retest passed the finding's matched-at URL (`https://host/wp-admin/js/theme.js`)
  to the template as its input. The template appends its own path to the input,
  so the re-run requested the path twice, got a 404, "did not match", and the
  finding was resolved as fixed whether or not it was. The re-run now targets
  the origin (`scheme://host[:port]`) of the matched-at URL.
- Migration 001175 voids those outcomes: every finding resolved by such a
  retest, and unchanged since, returns to the status it had before the retest;
  the retest reads "unknown" with a `voided:` reason. Retest those findings again.

### Fixed: stored assets typed against their own name are corrected

- Migration 001151 retypes an `ip_address` asset whose name is a DNS name to `domain`, and a `domain`/`subdomain` asset whose name is an IP literal to `ip_address` (the rule ingest now applies). The sub-type is cleared and each change is reported as a NOTICE (id, old type, new type); no audit rows are written, since only the app extends the audit chain. A row whose target name already exists in the tenant is skipped with a NOTICE. The down migration is a no-op.

### Fixed: the run map was empty on the run sheet

- The run sheet read the run's step runs as `step_runs`, but the API sends
  `scan_run_steps`, so the run map never showed. The web now reads
  `scan_run_steps`, its run types are checked against the generated API
  contract, and the run sheet is tested on a fixture the API writes from its
  own response.

### Fixed: a running task is no longer taken back before the deadline its sensor was given

- The platform re-queued a running scan task at twice its time budget even when its step allowed it more time (the step timeout, for example one hour), while the sensor was still working within that timeout. Each re-queue threw the task's progress away and counted a dispatch attempt, so a slow but healthy task (an HTTP probe over 71 hosts) was restarted three times and then failed with "Max dispatch attempts exceeded".
- The overrun re-queue now waits for the deadline the sensor enforces: the step's timeout when the task carries one (at most 24 hours), else twice its time budget, plus the 5-minute grace. The stall rule (nothing moves within the stall window: the sensor is asked to stop and hand back what it finished) is unchanged and still catches a hung task.
- Hand-backs that only mean "not now" (hosts busy on this sensor, no free slot) and a task waiting for its hosts never count a dispatch attempt; tests now pin this.

### Fixed: SBOM export is a valid CycloneDX 1.6 or SPDX 2.3 document built by the server

- New `GET /api/v1/components/sbom?format=cyclonedx|spdx[&asset_id=]`
  (`components:read`) returns CycloneDX 1.6 JSON (default) or SPDX 2.3 JSON
  of the components the organization's assets use, or of one asset, with
  the licenses the organization's assets report (SPDX ids where they are
  one) and the vulnerability count per component. A restricted member gets
  only components of assets in their data scope; an asset outside it is not
  found. Above 10000 components the export is refused (export one asset at
  a time) instead of being cut short.
- The Components > Export SBOM page downloads that document. It used to
  build a file in the browser after a simulated 1.5 s wait that was not
  valid CycloneDX or SPDX (and offered XML and options it did not apply).
- Removed: `GET /api/v1/components/export` (the browser-side builder's
  source).

### Fixed: automations can react to failed and partial scan runs

- The `scan_completed` automation trigger now also fires for scan runs that end
  `partial` or `failed`, for automations that ask for them with
  `trigger_config.status_filter` (`completed`, `partial`, `failed`). Without a
  filter it still fires on completed runs only. An unknown outcome in the filter
  is refused on save (400 `INVALID_TRIGGER_CONFIG`).
- The run-a-scan, run-a-scan-workflow and request-AI-triage actions now fail when
  their backing service is not available, instead of reporting a successful step
  that started nothing.

### Fixed: a scan of picked assets alone can be created

- `POST /scans` with `asset_ids` and no `targets` or asset groups was refused with 400 by the handler before the server could name the assets, so New Scan could not save a scan of assets picked in the inventory picker without also typing a target. It is accepted now; a request with no targets, assets or groups is still refused.

### Fixed: editing a scan with a cron or RRULE schedule

- The Edit scan wizard showed a cron or RRULE schedule as "weekly" and sent it back that way, so every save of such a scan (a rename included) was refused for a missing day. The wizard now shows the stored expression and keeps it unless you replace it with a daily, weekly or monthly schedule.

### Fixed: editing a scan's targets and asset groups

- The Edit scan wizard let you change a scan's targets, assets and asset groups, but the API had no such fields and dropped the change while reporting success. `PUT /api/v1/scans/{id}` now takes `targets`, `asset_ids` and `asset_group_ids` (omitted = unchanged). New targets pass the same checks as a new scan's, as the editor (target validation, act scope, ownership, intrusive proof, scope tier); another organization's asset group is not found; a scan must keep a target or a group. A governed scan needs approving again after its targets change. The wizard sends them only when you changed them, and shows the groups by name.

### Fixed: typing a scan's max duration or retry backoff

- The New and Edit scan wizards clamped the max duration and the retry backoff on every keystroke, so typing 3600 saved 30600 and typing 120 saved 1020. The fields now keep what you type and apply the limits when you leave the field.

### Fixed: one-off quick scans no longer clutter the scan list

- Quick scans created before quick scans became ad hoc (RFC-046 D10) were stored as ordinary configurations named "Quick Scan - YYYYMMDD-...", so they kept showing in the scan list. Migration 001154 marks them ad hoc: the default list hides them like every later quick scan, and "Save as scan" restores one as a configuration. Only manual scans that still carry both the generated name and the generated description are matched.

### Fixed: a scan can be edited and cloned from its page and drawer

- Edit and Clone were only in the scan list's row menu. The scan page header now has Edit and Clone buttons, and the scan drawer's menu has both, for members who may change scans.

### Fixed: a refused Run now shows its blocked run at once

- When Run now is refused (no sensor online with the tool, targets out of
  scope), the API records a blocked run, but the scan page kept showing
  "No runs yet" until its next poll. The run history and the scan list now
  refresh after a refusal as well as after a start.

### Fixed: cancel a scan run from its run drawer

- A run in progress could be canceled only from its scan's page. The run drawer (opened from the Runs list, a scan page or a notification) now has Cancel run in its menu for members with `scans:write`, after a confirmation.

### Fixed: a scan's last run, run count and results come from its runs

- A scan's `last_run_id`, `last_run_at`, `last_run_status` and run counters are now recomputed from its runs after every run change (start, finish, cancel, timeout, unclaimed abort, refused trigger). Before, a refused scheduled trigger moved `last_run_at` with no run behind it and runs were counted only when they finished, so a scan could read "Last run: today" beside "Runs: 0". `total_runs` now counts running and blocked runs too.
- Migration 001157 recomputes every scan's summary once.

### Fixed: scan runs work for tenants without the scan workflows module

- `/api/v1/pipeline-runs` (the Scans Runs tab, a scan's run history, task
  logs, run stages and run cancel) was gated on the `scan_pipelines` module.
  The `minimal`, `asset_inventory` and `compliance` presets switch that
  module off, so those tenants got 403 `MODULE_NOT_ENABLED` on every scan
  run. The run routes now follow the core `scans` module; the permissions
  are unchanged. The scan workflow templates (`/api/v1/pipelines`) keep the
  `scan_pipelines` gate.

### Fixed: a workflow scan can be saved or scheduled while its sensor is offline

- The New Scan wizard disabled Save and Schedule for a workflow scan whose sensors were only offline at that moment, although the API saves such a scan and its runs wait for a sensor. It is now a warning when the scan is saved for later or scheduled; a scan set to run now is still stopped, and a step no sensor has at all still blocks.

### Fixed: a scan scheduled to run once, later, now runs

- New Scan, Schedule for later, Once: the scan used to be saved as a manual scan that never ran, while the confirmation said it was scheduled. You now pick the date, time and timezone of the run, and the scan runs once then. The API takes `schedule_type: once` with `run_at` (a minute to a year ahead) and returns `schedule_run_at`. Migration 001694 adds `scans.schedule_run_at`.
- Scheduled times are in the timezone you pick, your own by default. The wizard did not send a timezone, so every time was read as UTC.
- Monthly schedules run on the day of the month you pick (it was always the 1st). A shorter month runs on its last day.
- Cloning a scan keeps its recurrence rule (an rrule clone had none and never ran).
- **Upgrade note:** run migrations (001694).

### Fixed: a refused scan run says why and what to do

- A run start refused for its targets (`ALL_TARGETS_UNCONFIRMED`, `NO_COMPATIBLE_TARGETS`, `TIER_EXCEEDS`, `INTERNAL_TARGET_OUTSIDE_ZONES`, `NO_RESOLVING_TARGETS`, `INTENSITY_EXCEEDED`, `LIVENESS_NEEDS_HOST_DISCOVERY`) answered with the generic `BAD_REQUEST` code, and a governed scan waiting for approval answered a bare 403 with no message. They now keep their code (and the approval refusal its message: `SCAN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, `SCAN_APPROVAL_PENDING`, still 403), and the console's "Run now" toast adds what to do (en, vi).

### Fixed: scan buttons match what the API allows

- Quick scan now needs `scans:write` and `scans:execute` in the console, as the API does; it showed for `scans:write` alone and always failed.
- The workflow editor and the workflows list no longer offer Save draft, Publish, Discard draft, step changes, the enable switch, Edit, Clone or Use template to members without `scan_workflows:write`; the editor opens read-only for them.

### Fixed: a wildcard pattern is no longer sent to an active scanner as a target

- A target such as `*.example.com` is a set of hosts, not a host. It was accepted as a scan target and dispatched as is, so an active scanner (nuclei) received a name it could not resolve and the sensor refused the job.
- Creating, editing, quick-scanning or triggering a scan whose active tool would receive a wildcard pattern is now refused with `WILDCARD_TARGET`. The message names the way forward: run a discovery scan seeded with `example.com`, or scan the known assets that match the pattern.
- A discovery (passive) tool such as subfinder takes the pattern as its root domain: the run hands it `example.com`. A workflow takes the pattern when every step that starts the run is a discovery step. The stored scan keeps the pattern as written.

### Fixed: creating a scan workflow needs the scan workflow permission

- The "New scan workflow" button on the scan workflows page was gated on the
  automations write permission, so a member allowed to write scan workflows
  saw it disabled and a member allowed only to edit automations saw it
  enabled (the API refused them). It is now gated on
  `integrations:pipelines:write`, the permission the API checks.
- The scan page names the scan workflow a workflow scan runs and links to it,
  instead of showing a raw ID. The New scan help text no longer points to a
  "Workflow mode" that no longer exists.

### Fixed: deleting a scan workflow keeps its run history

- `DELETE /api/v1/scan-workflows/{id}` used to delete every run of the
  workflow, along with their steps, outputs and stage plans (ON DELETE CASCADE).
  A workflow that has runs is now **retired** instead. It leaves the workflow
  lists, and it can still be read by id with `retired_at`, so its runs keep
  their graph. It cannot be edited or run (409 `WORKFLOW_RETIRED`, also for a
  scan that uses it), and its name can be used again. A workflow without runs
  is still deleted.
- A delete while a run is pending or running is refused (409
  `PIPELINE_RUN_ACTIVE`).
- `scan_runs.scan_workflow_id` no longer cascades, so no delete can remove a
  run again. Migration `001296`.

### Fixed: expired invitations, admin sessions and reviewed quarantined results are purged

- Three deletes existed with no caller, so their rows stayed forever: unaccepted invitations past their expiry (an email address and a token hash), platform-admin console sessions past their absolute expiry (IP address and user agent; they were only swept when an administrator signed in again), and reviewed quarantined sensor results (the full report payload).
- New controllers `invitation-purge` (hourly), `admin-session-purge` (hourly) and `sensor-result-quarantine-purge` (daily, deletes items reviewed more than 30 days ago; pending items are never purged). Each holds its controller lease, so with several API replicas one runs it at a time, and each is exported under the usual `openctem_controller_*` metrics.
- Settings: `INVITATION_PURGE_INTERVAL` (default `1h`), `ADMIN_SESSION_PURGE_INTERVAL` (`1h`), `SENSOR_RESULT_QUARANTINE_PURGE_INTERVAL` (`24h`), `SENSOR_RESULT_QUARANTINE_RETENTION` (`720h`).

### Fixed: the API starts again (empty route pattern in the GitHub App routes)

- `GET /api/v1/ci/scm-apps` was registered with an empty pattern inside its group, which chi refuses with a panic at start-up. It is now `/`. A test fails any empty route pattern in the route files.

### Fixed: the Scope page says "Add to scope" when a member's entry applies at once

- Members without the approve permission saw "Request access" on the Scope
  page, on the scope check's fix buttons and in the rule dialog's summary even
  when scan approval is Off or On, where their entry takes effect immediately.
  These now say "Add to scope" (or "Allow for N days" for a one-off); "Request
  access" appears only under Strict scan approval. Under Off and On the button
  also shows when the organization does not accept member requests, since
  nothing is requested.

### Fixed: adding a scope entry that already exists names the existing one

- Adding an entry or exclusion whose pattern the organization already has answers `409 SCOPE_ENTRY_EXISTS` / `SCOPE_EXCLUSION_EXISTS` with `details: {id, status}` of the existing row (tenant-scoped lookup, never another organization's row). The add dialogs say what the existing row is (waiting for approval, deactivated, expired, rejected, in effect) and offer the fitting action: approve or put in effect, activate, renew, or open it. Review-rule previews return the same code with `existing`.

### Fixed: Add to scope picks a duration the policy allows
- The add and edit scope entry dialogs offer a compact duration choice (7 days, 30 days, 90 days, 1 year, Permanent, Custom date) that fits a phone screen and shows the date the entry expires on.
- The default is the longest duration the organization allows: an intrusive (T2) entry defaults to the owner's limit (30 days unless an owner changed it) instead of Permanent. Permanent is offered disabled, with a link to the owner setting, when the organization does not allow it; a member request never offers it.
- No error is shown before the user acts: a neutral line says what will happen (approvals needed, expiry date), and the dialog names the tools each tier runs and offers "Verify domain" when domain proof is needed.

### Fixed: a target behind a pending scope entry shows what is left, never Approve to the requester
- The scope check rows (New Scan preview, target picker, refused scans) show, for a target whose scope entry waits for approval, every remaining blocker with its action: the approval (who can approve, named only for people who may see the members; Remind approvers; Approve for another approver; self-approval with an authenticator code for the only owner when nobody else can approve), a tier the entry does not allow, and domain proof with Verify domain.
- The person who asked for the entry no longer sees an Approve button that the server would refuse.
- `POST /api/v1/scope/check` also returns `tier`, the probe tier the targets were checked at.

### Fixed: a pending scope entry has no approval time

- A scope entry waiting for approval no longer reports `approved_at`; it is set when the entry is approved (or at creation when it needs no approval).
- Migration `001362_scope_pending_not_approved` clears the approval time stored on pending and rejected entries.

### Fixed: a malformed scope target pattern is answered 400, not 500

- `POST /api/v1/scope/targets` (and `/preview`) with a pattern that does not fit its type, or an unknown target or exclusion type, now answers 400 with what is wrong instead of 500.
- A bare 12-digit AWS account id as a `cloud_account` pattern is refused with the accepted form, `AWS:<account id>`.
- Pattern refusals no longer echo the submitted pattern back, except the AWS hint.

### Fixed: the scope entries list no longer shows a probe ceiling that does not apply

- Entry tier ceilings limit probes only under Strict scan approval. Outside
  Strict the "Deepest probe" column now says "Set per scan", with a note and
  a link to the scan approval setting, instead of showing a default "T1 safe
  active" that meant nothing; the default-tier setting says the same. Strict
  keeps the ceiling and its edit.

### Fixed: a base64 APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY no longer stops the API at start-up

- Configuration accepts `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` as 64 hex, 44 base64 or 32 raw
  characters, but the secret store decoded only hex and used a base64 key as its
  44 raw bytes, so the API exited with "encryption key must be 32 bytes". The
  Helm chart generates a base64 key, so a default chart install never started.
  The secret store (and `rekey`) now decode the key the same way configuration
  validation does.

### Fixed: a run's seed targets name their inventory asset

- A stage plan recorded its seed targets (`scan_run_targets`, origin `seed`)
  without the asset they are, so a run could not say which assets it
  covered. The seed now names the tenant's asset of that name (an open port
  seed `host:port` matches `host:port:tcp`), in the same transaction. Seeds
  nothing in the inventory names (wildcards, ranges, unknown literals) stay
  without an asset. Rows recorded before this change are not rewritten.

### Fixed: program jobs with a required identification reach sensors again

- The heartbeat and manifest sanitizer kept only known sensor-wide
  capabilities and did not know `http.identity@1`, so it was dropped from
  every sensor report ("ignored capabilities[N] \"http.identity@1\":
  unknown-capability" in the sensor log). Jobs on targets of a bug-bounty
  program that requires headers or a User-Agent wait for a sensor reporting
  it, so they were withheld from every sensor. It is now kept.
- **Upgrade note:** a sensor that registers a manifest sends its
  capabilities only with the manifest, which it registers at start; restart
  such sensors after upgrading so the platform records `http.identity@1`.
- Every sensor-wide capability dispatch gates on (`validate`,
  `scope.limits@1`, `net.confined@1`, `http.identity@1`) now comes from one
  list, with a test that a sanitized report keeps each of them.

### Fixed: sensor install snippets keep the baked nuclei templates and a paired identity

- The docker run, Docker Compose and Kubernetes snippets on the Sensors page no longer mount empty directories over `/home/openctem`, `/scan`, `/cache` and `/config`. They hid the nuclei-templates release baked into the sensor image, so a sensor had no templates until its first download (and none at all on a host without internet access); under Docker those directories were not even writable by the sensor's user. Only `/tmp` is writable now, and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` / `XDG_CACHE_HOME` point the scanners' settings there.
- The Kubernetes snippet sets `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch`. With the default policy every pod start made the state volume's files group-readable, and the sensor refuses an identity key its group can read.
- The Helm snippet asks for chart 0.15.0 or later.

### Fixed: the platform keeps a sensor's reach probe instead of ignoring it

- Sensors since v0.20 report their built-in reach probe (tool `reach-probe`, capability `reach.probe@1`). It had no tool catalog row, so every manifest logged `ignored tools[N] "reach-probe": unknown-tool` and the platform dropped it from the sensor's inventory.
- The reach probe is a sensor service the platform requests (RFC-089 §4.3), not a scan tool tenants choose. The platform now knows it without a catalog row and keeps it, and its capability, from a sensor's heartbeat and manifest. Tools missing from the catalog are still dropped.

### Fixed: a service follows its host in scope, review and dispatch

- A service is stored as `host:port:proto` (for example
  `example.co.uk:443:tcp`), but the scope code read host names with a
  `host:port` parser that fails on three parts. So a service under a
  permanent scope entry stayed in the review queue instead of joining the
  inventory (RFC-054 S4), and the scope authority did not see its host.
- One parser, `asset.SplitServiceName` / `asset.HostOf`, now reads every form
  (`host:port:proto`, `host:port/proto`, `host:port`, `[v6]:port/proto`,
  `[v6]:port:proto` and the stored `v6:port:proto`) and is used by the scope
  join, the active-probe authority and ownership gate, exclusions, internal
  target detection, the scan stamper, retests, ingest and sensor grants. A
  network (`203.0.113.0/24`) is never cut to its first address.
- A service on an IP address still joins only through an IP, range or CIDR
  scope entry: a name grant never becomes an IP grant.
- The stored form is unchanged (`host:port:proto`, written by the inventory
  normalizer), so no data migration is needed. The scope-join run at start-up
  confirms the services left in review.

### Fixed: honest settings copy and states

- Authentication no longer mentions a session length setting, and General no longer mentions localization: neither exists.
- File storage shows an error when its settings cannot be read instead of showing "Local filesystem" as if it were saved, and reports the server's reason when a save fails.
- The pages are translated into Vietnamese.

### Fixed: info is reported everywhere severity is counted

- `GET /findings/stats` reported informational findings under the key `none`,
  so the console, scheduled reports and the MCP stats tool showed 0 Info.
  It now reports `info` (info + none).
- Dashboard, trend, MTTR, component and pentest counts fold `none` into `info`;
  the dashboard severity maps always carry all five keys. Vulnerable
  components report `info_count`; MTTR analytics report an `info` average.
- Jira tickets for informational findings default to priority `Lowest`
  instead of the `Medium` fallback.
- A priority rule on severity `info` also matches `none` findings.

### Fixed: an asset can be saved as Not rated

- `assets.criticality` accepted `none` everywhere except the database CHECK,
  so saving an asset as Not rated failed. Migration 001180 adds it. The
  findings `asset_criticality` filter accepts `none`. New assets still default
  to `medium`: Not rated adds no criticality weight to risk, so it stays an
  explicit choice.
- The web console reads both scales from one source (`@/lib/severity`,
  `@/lib/criticality`): Info and Not rated appear in every filter, facet,
  summary, chart and mapping, and a guard test fails on a new hand-written
  list. The findings list has a saved "Hide informational" toggle.

### Fixed: the sign-in screens follow the user's language

- The second sign-in step (2FA code, recovery code, forced 2FA setup), the
  set-password and reset-password form, forgot-password, team selection and
  the sign-in form's labels and notices are translated (English and
  Vietnamese). They were English-only.

### Fixed: the console states SLA windows from the organization's SLA policy

- The priority-class badge, the finding "Why it matters" panel and the
  priority explanation said P0/P1/P2 = 7/30/60 days and P3 "opportunistic",
  which matched neither the platform defaults (2/5/15/30 days) nor a
  configured policy. They now show the window of the finding's asset (its
  override, else the organization's default policy, else the platform
  defaults), read from the API.
- The pentest finding forms suggested a deadline of 7/30/90/180/365 days by
  severity; the suggestion now uses the severity window of the asset's SLA
  policy (none for informational findings with no SLA).
- A new SLA policy starts from the organization's current windows as the API
  reports them; the web keeps no copy of the defaults.
- `GET /api/v1/sla-policies/default` and `GET /api/v1/assets/{id}/sla-policy`
  return the platform default windows with `is_platform_default: true` and an
  empty `id` when no policy is configured, instead of 404.

### Fixed: the release smoke test works on images without a shell

- `smoke-image.sh` read the binary's ELF header and the OpenAPI spec through a
  shell inside the image, so the distroless `admin-cli` image failed its smoke
  test and the release's `admin-cli` build job could not pass. It now copies
  the files out of a stopped container with `docker cp`.

### Fixed: a batch tool is no longer re-queued as stalled before it finishes a target

A scan command is called stalled only after it has finished at least one target and then stopped making progress. Tools that write their output only when they exit (httpx, naabu) report no finished target until the end, so they were re-queued at every stall window and the command was exhausted after three attempts (`COMMAND_EXHAUSTED`). They are now bounded by the task's overrun limit only.

### Fixed: workflow runs no longer hang when a step's wake-up is missed

- A chained step waits until its predecessors' reports are ingested. If such
  a report failed or expired, nothing woke the step, and the run stayed
  "running" until its timeout. A failed report now wakes the step at once.
- If the platform stopped between saving a step's plan and creating its
  tasks, the step never started. The new `stalled-run-repair` controller runs
  every minute and handles both cases:
  - it re-plans such a step after 2 minutes;
  - it advances any running workflow run that has a step left to start but
    nothing queued, running or being ingested for 2 minutes.

### Fixed: scans on a starter workflow can be created and run

- The New scan wizard offers the starter (system) workflows, but creating
  a scan on one failed with "Scan not found": the scan's workflow was looked
  up only among the organization's own workflows. Starter workflows are now
  usable, read-only, by every organization when a scan is created, edited,
  quick-started, run on schedule or pinned to a version; another
  organization's private workflow stays out of reach, and changing a starter
  workflow still needs "Duplicate to edit".
- A missing workflow is now answered 404 "Scan workflow not found" (code
  `SCAN_WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND`) instead of "Scan not found"; a disabled one is
  refused with a 400 that names it.

### Fixed: step failures keep their reason and class; doomed runs are not retried

- Every step failure code has a class: config, scope, placement, policy, transient, tool, timeout or canceled. Step runs in scan run responses carry `error_class` next to `error_code`.
- Failures a retry cannot fix are never retried, as a step or as a whole run: the queue-time codes (`NO_MATCHING_TOOL`, `STEP_CAPABILITY_AMBIGUOUS`, `INCOMPATIBLE_TARGETS`, `STAGE_NOT_CHAINABLE`, `NO_SENSOR_FOR_TOOL`, `STEP_TARGETS_REFUSED`) and policy refusals now join the permanent ones. Transient failures (a lost lease, an exhausted or expired command) stay retryable.
- Sensor protocol v2: `POST /commands/{id}/fail` takes an optional `error_code` (`SCANNER_NOT_FOUND`, `TARGET_REFUSED`, `NO_TARGETS`, `POLICY_REFUSED`, `TOOL_EXIT`, `PARSE_ERROR`, `TIMEOUT`). The step records it instead of the flat `COMMAND_FAILED`; any other value, including a platform code, is recorded as `COMMAND_FAILED` and the message is classified as before. A structured policy refusal that was not re-queued is `POLICY_REFUSED`.
- A run whose command lost its lease and went back to the queue is no longer aborted as "no sensor ever took it" (`NO_SENSOR`, never retried): the reaper now also counts dispatch attempts.

### Fixed: a finding a suppression rule decides at ingest raises no alert

- A new finding that an approved suppression rule marks false positive or accepted at ingest no longer fires the finding-created workflows (notifications, tickets), no longer gets an SLA deadline and is not promoted into the exposure store. The other findings of the same report are unchanged.

### Fixed: tabs and URL filters update on the first click
- Switching a tab on AI assistants (MCP) settings, an asset group, or opening a saved view on Findings no longer needs a second click: every write to the address bar now reaches the pages that read it.

### Fixed: taint traces reach the finding for every producer, and a re-scan replaces a changed trace

- SARIF `codeFlows` are now stored as the finding's data flow (ctis maps them; before, they were dropped). semgrep and opengrep traces were already mapped and now share the same bounds and path rules.
- Data flows are stored for re-sighted findings too, not only for new ones. A re-scan whose trace differs from the stored one replaces the finding's flows in one transaction. An identical trace is not rewritten: migration `002120_finding_data_flow_trace_hash` adds `finding_data_flows.trace_hash`. The migration also adds `finding_data_flows.commit_sha`, the commit the trace was reported for; `GET /findings/{id}` returns it on each trace (`data_flow.traces[].commit_sha`), so a step can link to its exact lines. A report without a trace keeps the stored one. The per-finding caps (50 flows, 100 steps) still hold.
- Ingest normalizes every received trace again (`ctis.NormalizeDataFlow`), whichever producer sent it. Paths become repository-relative: absolute paths of the scanning machine and paths leaving the repository are dropped. Credentials in step snippets are masked, and the bounds hold.
- Sanitizer steps are kept in step order. They were dropped before. End line, end column and the function of a step are stored too.
- The trace never feeds the finding's fingerprint.
- The API's unused SARIF code-flow converter and the data-flow repository methods without a tenant filter are deleted. Every flow query now joins `findings` and filters on the tenant.

### Fixed: the task Logs dialog says why a refused task has no logs

- A task that a policy refused before any tool started shows "This task was refused before it ran" with the refusal reason. Before, it showed "No logs from this task". A task that failed before its sensor logged anything shows its error the same way.

### Fixed: a Tenable.sc sync or scan the sensor's grant refuses fails at once with the reason

- A connector sync or scan whose sensor grant does not allow it (the default profile of a paired scanning sensor allows neither `connector_sync` nor `connector_scan`; a sensor at trust "new" receives no T1 scan; targets outside the grant) was queued and then withheld at every claim until it expired, leaving the sync pending and the run running for hours. "Sync now", scheduled syncs, scan runs and coverage batches now check the grant first and refuse with `CONNECTOR_GRANT_REFUSES` (HTTP 409 on "Sync now") naming what to widen. The claim still checks the grant and fails closed.

### Fixed: leave flow reachable by members, honest settings copy, ownership-transfer read

- "Leave organization" moves to My account, Organization membership, so members and viewers can reach it; the only owner sees it disabled with the reason.
- The Authentication and General settings descriptions no longer promise a session length or localization setting that does not exist.
- `GET /api/v1/organization/ownership-transfer` answers 200 with `null` when no transfer is pending instead of a 404.
- The scan-profile "Set as default" action is hidden from members, who cannot use it.

### Fixed: a request reaching its timeout always gets the 504

- At the deadline the handler and the timeout path both saw the cancelled context, and a handler that wrote first answered its own status (200) instead of the 504. A write after the deadline is now refused when nothing was written yet, so the timeout response wins. Found as a flaky test on develop: 21 failures in 300 runs before, 0 after.

### Fixed: the TLS expiry alert no longer fires on the gateway's internal CA

- With `OBS_PUBLIC_PROBE_MODULE=http_2xx_internal_ca` the gateway serves 12-hour certificates that it
  renews itself, so `TlsCertExpiringSoon` fired permanently against the 14-day threshold. The probe
  target now carries its `module` label: public-CA certificates keep the 14-day/3-day thresholds,
  internal-CA certificates alert at 2 hours/30 minutes left (renewal stopped). Alerts carry a `ca`
  label and show the time left as a duration.

### Fixed: switching off a tool the organization never configured

- `POST /api/v1/tenant-tools/bulk/disable` (and `bulk/enable`) did nothing for a tool without a tenant config row, and a tool without a row counts as enabled, so such a tool could never be switched off. The switch now creates the row. Only platform tools and the organization's own custom tools get one; any other id is ignored.

### Fixed: a v0.8.0 database upgrades without failing, and its crawled URLs become web endpoints

- Migration 001290 failed with a unique violation on a database that held two legacy `path` exclusions of one rule where the one to drop already carried the new pattern (`/api/*` next to `*/api`, `https://x/admin/*` next to `https://x/admin`). The duplicates are now deleted before the kept row is rewritten. A database that already ran 001290 is not affected.
- Migration 001317 converts the crawled URL assets that v0.8.0 and older stored under a garbled name (`https:::host:path`, every crawler and API-created `discovered_url` asset of those releases) into web endpoints under their site, like 001288 does for URL-named ones: the URL is read back from the name, findings and exposure events move to the site (its garbled `http_service` asset when there is one), pending duplicate reviews that named the URL asset are removed, and the URL asset is deleted. 001288 matched only names starting with `http(s)://`, so on an upgraded v0.8.0 database it converted none of them. A URL whose site name belongs only to a deleted asset is left as it is. About 6 ms per URL asset.

### Fixed: audit actions read as sentences, not as Title-Cased ids

- The organization audit log and account activity labelled an action by Title-Casing its id ("Sso Change Requested") while the sensor activity used a separate label list. All three now use one label source: "SSO change requested", "Organization settings updated", "API key created". Resource types in the audit log read the same way ("SSO change", not "sso_change").

### Fixed: identity providers are named, never shown by their id

- A pending SSO change (the approval card, the owner notification and e-mail, the audit message) said "add the google_workspace identity provider" and "change identity provider <id>". It now reads "add the Google Workspace identity provider \"Corp SSO\"" and "change the Google Workspace identity provider \"Corp SSO\" (client ID)". Changes proposed before the upgrade read "change an identity provider (...)".
- The account page and sign-in error messages name the sign-in method ("Google Workspace", "GitHub", "Email and password") from one label map.

### Fixed: asset and pentest finding breadcrumbs name the record

- The asset page and the pentest finding edit page now name their record in the header breadcrumb (the asset name, the finding title) instead of the record kind.

### Fixed: breadcrumbs name records instead of showing their ids

- The header breadcrumb showed a shortened record id on most detail pages ("dcdc3001...") and the full id when the record was in the middle of the path (a template edit page). Cycle, asset group, scan, scan workflow, pentest campaign, remediation campaign and pentest template pages now name their record, and before the name loads the crumb says what the record is ("Scan", "Template"), never the id.

### Fixed: email verification links and dead links in the console

- The email verification link pointed at a page that did not exist. It now
  opens `/verify-email` (token in the URL fragment, never sent to a server),
  which verifies the address; the welcome email links to `/login` instead of
  `/auth/login`, and the dead `/support` links are gone from the emails.
- Documentation links in the console come from one module
  (`web/src/lib/docs-links.ts`) and point at docs.openctem.io: the CI/CD
  guides and the scanner content help now open the docs site.
- A web test fails when a literal in-app link points at a route that does not
  exist (removed the dead `/unauthorized`, `/settings/appearance`,
  `/settings/display`, `/help-center` and `/dashboard/*` targets).

### Fixed: "Create ticket" shows only to who may create one

- The create-ticket action on the findings list, the finding drawer, the
  finding page and a remediation task's findings now needs the integrations
  module and `findings:write` (the API's gate) everywhere, through one hook;
  the findings list and the task page showed it to everyone. The label is
  translated (English and Vietnamese).

### Fixed: the finding's data-flow tab shows the whole trace with its code

- The tab lists the steps of the trace in order from the source to the sink, sanitizer steps included (they were dropped), with each step's code (it was never shown: the console read a field the API does not send), file and line, function and class.
- Each step links to its file and line at the commit the trace was reported for, when the repository's web URL is known. The link never points at a branch or at the finding's latest commit, which could show other code.
- All text is translated (English, Vietnamese). A finding without a trace says "This scanner did not report a data flow".

### Fixed: review actions show only to people who may use them

- Assets > Suggestions shows Scan, Approve all, Approve, Dismiss, the bulk
  approve bar, row selection and the relationship type editor only with
  `assets:write`, the permission the API checks on those routes. Readers see
  the queue.
- Credentials: "Mark resolved" shows only with the credentials write
  permission the API checks on `POST /credentials/{id}/resolve`.

### Fixed: date fields fit their column on iPhone
- On iOS Safari, date and time fields ignored their column width (they overflowed the form, for example in the new campaign dialog) and grew taller when empty. They now size like every other field, in every form.

### Fixed: the OpenCTEM wordmark no longer overlaps on machines without the brand fonts

- The full logo on the sign-in, admin sign-in and legal pages drew its letters with the operating system font. On a Linux desktop without the requested fonts the letters came out wider, ran into the C and were clipped at the edge. The letters are now outlined paths, so the logo looks the same everywhere and needs no font download.

### Fixed: the MCP connection key no longer offers "Never" expiry

- Settings > AI access (MCP) offered a key that never expires; the API
  requires every `oct_` key to expire within 1 to 365 days and refused the
  request. The page now offers 30 days, 90 days (default) or 1 year, the same
  choices as the API keys page (one shared list).

### Fixed: the console follows the organization's modules the way the API does

- A beta module switched off stayed in the sidebar and led to a refused page.
- Exceptions follows the `suppressions` module (its API) instead of `findings`.
- Asset relations, the dashboard attack paths card, its exposure chains and the
  "Assets reachable" widget follow their modules (`relationships`, `attack_surface`):
  hidden or shown as turned off, never asked for and left empty.
- A page whose module is off says "Turned off for your organization" and offers
  administrators Settings > Modules, instead of "not included in your current plan"
  (plans do not gate modules).

### Fixed: New Scan custom targets accept Enter

- In New Scan and Edit scan, step Targets, pressing Enter after a custom target now starts a new line. It used to be dropped, so the next target ran onto the same line and failed validation.

### Fixed: icon-only buttons on phones have a name, and the campaign dialog's buttons stack

- On a phone, buttons whose text is hidden to save space (New campaign, Add finding, Export, Refresh and about 20 more) showed only an icon and had no accessible name. Their text now stays readable by screen readers.
- The new campaign dialog's Next and Create campaign buttons stack full width on a phone, like Cancel and Back.

### Fixed: the pentest retest dialog and activity feed use the current finding statuses

- A passed retest is described as Resolved (retest verified) for leads and
  reviewers and Fix applied for testers, a failed one as In progress, with the
  labels taken from the shared status registry; the activity entry reads
  "Retest verified" instead of the retired "Verified" status.

### Fixed: a path exclusion no longer refuses POST and other methods on the whole host

A web job whose scope only denies paths now lists every HTTP method. The sensor read an empty method list as GET, HEAD and OPTIONS only, so a single path exclusion refused every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE request on every path of its hosts. nuclei counted those refusals as host errors and skipped the hosts as unresponsive (`breaker_open`). A rule that blocks only some methods still limits the job to GET and HEAD.

### Fixed: scope list filters were ignored (web)

- The scope entries and exclusions lists sent `target_type` / `status`; the
  API reads `types` / `statuses`, so the type filter never filtered.

### Fixed: a web-scoped step a sensor cannot keep to fails once, with its own code

- A scan step whose job has a web scope (the tenant excluded a path on a target host) and whose sensor's tool cannot keep to it now fails with `WEB_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED` (class `placement`) and the sensor's message, instead of the generic `COMMAND_FAILED`, and is never retried: the same sensor would fail the same way. The run ends `partial` when other steps completed, as for any failed step.
- nuclei keeps to a web scope from sensor releases that include it, on sensors whose tool sandbox confines the network (the sensor container started with the seccomp profile in the sensor's `docker/seccomp`).

### Fixed: scrolling lists stay inside their box

- In New Scan, step Targets, the Individual Assets list no longer runs over its pager, Custom Targets and the selected-targets summary: it scrolls inside its own box. The shared scroll area now honours a maximum height, which also fixes the asset group wizard lists, the capability and template dialogs, the pentest report builder and the finding evidence and code-fix blocks.
- Long names in those lists truncate again instead of pushing the type badge out of view.

### Fixed: page content no longer shifts when a scrollbar appears

- The page scroller always reserves its scrollbar gutter, so content keeps its
  width when a page becomes long enough to scroll. The scrollbar thumb is
  shown only while scrolling; wheel, trackpad, keyboard and touch scrolling
  are unchanged, and forced-colors mode keeps the system scrollbar.

### Fixed: organization URL fields show this console host

- Settings > General and the create-organization form showed a fixed product domain before the organization slug, and the notification template preview linked its sample finding to that domain. They now show the host the console is served from.

### Fixed: an expanded tool in the sensor drawer's Tool settings is no longer cut off on a phone

- On a phone, opening a tool in a sensor's Tool settings scrolled the drawer frame itself: the expanded tool was cut off mid-card, a blank band appeared under it, and the rest could not be scrolled to. Opening a tool now scrolls only the drawer's body.
- Sheet, drawer and dialog frames clip their overflow instead of hiding it, so no script can scroll a frame out of place.

### Fixed: the workflow form saves what a step does, not "scan"

- The scan workflow form is capability-first, like the builder: a step picks
  what it does ("DNS resolution", "Port scan") and runs on any tool, preferred
  tools or one pinned tool. Picking a tool instead gives the step the
  capability the tool implements (or asks when it implements several). The
  form used to save every step as `capabilities: ["scan"]`, so a DNSX step
  was refused ("capability 'scan' is not supported by tool 'dnsx'").
- Step capabilities accept both catalog keys (`resolve.dns`) and the older
  words (`dns`), mapped onto each other through the catalog. A refusal names
  the step, what the tool can run and how to fix it.
- Step keys are made from what the step does (`resolve-dns`, then
  `resolve-dns-2`), edited under "Advanced", and checked for format and
  uniqueness. Renaming a step never changes its key, and a key change moves
  the dependencies on it. Once a workflow has runs, the API refuses a change
  of a saved step's key: run history and data hops refer to it.
- Editing a workflow in the form shows its steps again and sends them only
  when they changed, and then every field (id, tool preferences, retries,
  condition, settings, layout); the builder sends every field too.
- A step position from the builder canvas may be fractional or negative: it
  is stored rounded. A non-finite or out-of-range position is a 400, not a
  500 (`invalid input syntax for type integer`).
- New steps from an adapter suggestion run on any tool that implements the
  capability instead of pinning its default tool.

### Fixed: a workflow scan whose first step cannot start fails at once with the reason

- A workflow scan run whose first step could not be queued (no tool for the capability, no compatible target, no sensor for the tool) answered 201 and stayed `running` until its deadline, up to 24 hours. The other first steps now still start, the run is re-evaluated at once, and a run in which nothing can run settles `failed` immediately.
- A failed scan run's message names the first failed step, its reason and its code (for example `Step "Port scan" failed: ... (NO_MATCHING_TOOL)`) instead of "Pipeline completed with failures".
